text: Let me tell you a little story, about how a little troll came to be. Having recently relocated from Denver, I went in search of a new salon to make my own. Having walked and driven by Gloss on a daily basis for over a month, I decided to make the call. I spoke with a pleasant man and described in detail that I had just moved to the area, was in need of a cut and color for my THICK hair, and wanted to know rates and such. He was very accommodating and made adjustments to get me in the same evening. He had initially quoted me approximately $140 for the cut an color, for this particular stylist. I was very excited and was hopeful that I could find a stylist to meet my needs and support local business. Fast forward four hours later. After speaking with the stylist about the weight of my hair, she decides to "thin it out." I get the color, I get the cut, some minor highlights, along with some really great tips on what to do in this city. After four hours in a chair I failed to notice my hair but almost choked when I got the bill which was $60 more than I was quoted. The next morning when I looked in the mirror, and having slept on it for 8 hours the cut as my boyfriend put it "looks like a pencil troll." Fast forward 3.5 months later. After every product, every curler, flat iron, and even going back to the same stylist, I have resigned myself to a rubber band for the next few months. This will make a total of 6 months that I look like a pencil troll freak. Even my friends from out of town did not believe me until they saw it with their own eyes. I finally broke down, as my ends started to break from all the "texturizing" of my thick, wavy hair, and drove to Great Clips for a trim. A $12 trim and a pep talk (and explanation) of how this could have occurred put me on the right track to look somewhat normal again. Needless to say, can honestly say that hands down this was the WORST haircut I have EVER had in my life (and the most expensive) and was based on someone not knowing how to cut thick wavy hair. I am giving the Salon one star because she did do a good job on my color and was very personable and likable. But if I had to choose between putting a bowl on my head and having my blind grandpa cut my hair or heading back in to Gloss for a cut, I would breaking out the bowl. Save yourself some money on your next cut. Go to Great Clips for a $12 (good) cut. FYI the cut I received is called the Emo cut. You can ask for it by name should you dare to venture into Gloss.
label: NEG

text: I really enjoy ballet and I've taken classes on and off at a few different places since I was a teenager. I was psyched by the concept of Koresh - a studio that specialized in adult classes. I signed up for a few beginner classes and was disappointed. There's a sizable crew of advanced dancers who attend as many classes as they can, regardless of the actual level of the class. And they're not a friendly bunch. They openly discuss the appearance and skills of the other dancers (horrifying to those of us who aren't exactly happy to be wearing a leotard in public), tattling or sniping at dancers who don't follow proper studio etiquette, and monopolizing the instructor. The final straw for me was when a dancer told me I was at her spot at the bar. Even more disappointing is that the instructors give these dancers an unfair amount of attention. Once an instructor took 3 or 4 minutes of class time to discuss the toe box of a dancer's pointe shoe while the rest of us just stood around in our little leather slippers. Many a sickled foot or stuck-out butt went unmentioned - corrections that would actually be useful to the whole class. They often adjust the class to be far too challenging to a beginner or casual dancer. I mean, I've been doing this for a long time and should probably move up to an intermediate class, but I've really struggled with the combinations. I've been there once or twice when this crew wasn't there, usually during semester breaks, and the classes are fun, the students are more colloquial, the teachers are instructive and encouraging, and everyone is just more relaxed. Too bad it can't be like that all the time. I've heard great things about their hip-hop classes, and the dancers seem to really enjoy them, but they do seem pretty crowded.

I've never ordered the lunch specials, though the bulgohgi special seems popular. I usually order one of the Korean dishes, such as the tofu chigeh (tofu in a spicy broth), ja jang myun (traditional noodles with a , or today, the duk mandu gook. I tend to end up here by myself, and I'm always impressed with the fact they still bring out all the banchan. One of the features of Korean food is all the small side dishes - in this case, you get kimchee (pickled cabbage), pickled radish, radish/carrots, chap chae (a noodle-based side), and a fish cake of sorts. So, even before you get your meal, there are 6 small bowls of sides in front of you. The Korean food is solid - not the best I've had, especially compared to K-Town, in Los Angeles, but definitely tasty. During the day, there's a Korean waitress, who's awesome, but in the evenings, I've had a mix of staff, and they're not as familiar with the Korean food. text: This place deserves kudos for having a fairly decent set up for being a total scam. I had booked a massage for myself and my girlfriend as a precursor to Valentines Day, which was thankfully saved by the always dependable James Restaurant. Dependable, a word the personnel at this establishment have yet to add to their vocabulary. I decided to take a chance and try a massage therapy salon I had never been to before since the ones I have tried in the area were good and sometimes great but never extraordinary. Never again... this is the main reason you should never rely on AOL City Guide or city search as both gave this place high marks. I asked for two female massage therapists for a 90 minute Swedish massage. We arrive to an empty salon and are greeted by a bubbling crew that appeared to not only be stoned (not the good stoned... they probably had just huffed the hair glue) but had that weird pyramid scheme vibe about them. They took us back to one room with two benches. First, I hadn't asked for both of us to be in one room although this was obviously not a problem for us, but the room was so small that while being massaged the masseuse kept shoving my bench across the floor with me on it to get from one side to the other. The bench didn't have head support and gave me a throbbing migraine that consumed my concentration. There was an oddly placed shower in the corner of the room that looked like it hadn't been used for years and was blocked by my bench. There was nowhere to place personal items or clothes so we had to end up folding them and putting them under the benches. After waiting for over 15 minutes, the massage therapist came in. As I said earlier, I asked for two females but I guess this didn't matter as one of them was a male whom of course picked my girlfriend to massage. My masseuse was a gigantic Russian female, oddly enough, with the strength of a phantom limbed quadriplegic. I'm pretty sure she didn't speak English, as she never asked me any questions about what pressure I wanted or if the wretched massage was going well. I guess she doesn't like criticism and tries to avoid it in any way she can. Then the music, which has got to be the easiest part of running a massage clinic... slap in some nature crap with a mix of ancient Chinese flute and you're golden. Not here, they prefer heavy drum elevator tunes with a mix of sexual moans blasting through distorted speakers. Now to the massage... neither one had obviously ever received a degree in massage therapy or even been given a massage. Their idea of a relaxing Swedish massage consisted of spritsing some low grade oil on their hands and spinning circles on your back as if they were an impatient Mr. Miyagi. And if that wasn't bad enough, they continuously stopped massaging to make gestures at each other and giggle, which had me paranoid as to whether my manhood was everything but in Russian standards or if they couldn't believe we fell for thinking they were an actual massage therapy clinic... the K in clinic should have given it away. To top it all off, the crappiest massage ever last all but 50 minutes... yep, we were charged for 90 each. NEVER GO HERE... my suggestion is Toppers... ask for Elaine.

text: I despise Macy's and since the location I'm reviewing is in Mid Rivers Mall (which I think is where stores go to die and rot in hell), it doesn't help it any. AND, they had both in stock so I got to take them home with me that day (rare). I thought I'd hit the jackpot. Wrong. China: same price. Flatware: TEN DOLLARS MORE! I could have overlooked the price (since I had the gift card anyway), but then homegirl at the cash register decides to lay on the Macy's-guilt that I didn't register there and have subsequently "missed out" on their 15% off "sales event!!" for newlyweds. Um? What good does this information do me now? You already know I'm married, so why are you making me feel bad for the inability to go back in time and register for my china at Macy's in hopes of attending the elusive "sales event." (Bed Bath and Beyond gave us 20% off, by the way, you dumb cow). She literally stopped scanning my items (as if in shock) when she heard I didn't register at Macy's for them. Like it makes a bit of damn difference? I'm spending almost $200.00 here now! And just in case any brides are trying to gather some info about registering at Macy's in comparison to Bed Bath and Beyond, here's my two cents. BBB will carry all of the china patterns you like at Macy's but for less money - PLUS you can get ALL of your other household stuff there for way less money. But in case you need more convincing, here's why I didn't register there: In February (shortly before my future husband and I registered) I went to Macy's to get a gift for a friend's wedding. I waited in line for TWENTY FIVE minutes (behind ONE customer) to have the sales woman (we'll call her Sales Associate #1) pull a registry for me. I had another sales associate (we'll call her #2) approach me TWICE and ask if there is any way she can help me. I said BOTH times, "Well, I just need to pull a registry." And both times she gave me a blank stare which made me want to stab her with my Kate Spade flatware. Not to mention, the rest of the time, #2 was aimlessly wandering around the sales floor looking lost and bewildered as if she'd recently escaped from a nearby convalescence home. Once I got in front of the customer who felt the need to use #1 as her personal shopper for what could only have been 10 different weddings, the associate informs me that she CAN'T pull a registry (which I am still sure is absolute B.S.) and that I have to get it at the self-serve kiosks. I guess I could have looked around for it, but they have it stashed behind the wall and I really didn't see it, plus, you'd like to think #2 would have informed me when I told her not once, but TWO TIMES what I was standing in line for. Long story short, my friends registered for a bunch of really expensive crap (and I'm poor). So instead of giving them a gift card from Macy's, I got them one to Bed Bath and Beyond. They should have registered there to begin with. And thus, I decided not to put my wedding guests through the same circus. So don't register there, and unless you have a high threshold for pain and annoyance - don't shop there either.

The lunch specials include soup & salad (with four salad choices, soups include tortilla and shrimp and crab bisque), pizza and salad, and triple combo (soup, salad, half sandwich), all for $10.95 or less. Save room for dessert and you will be very pleased. The flour-less chocolate cake topped with pieces of Heath bars is almost literally death by chocolate to me. The berry cobbler streusel is delicious as well, and I've heard great things about the tiramisu and creme brulee. Dessert menu also includes key lime, wedding cake, and after dinner mint martinis. I haven't always had the best service during busy times, which is somewhat understandable, but lunch service is very friendly and quick.

text: How odd that I've never reviewed my favorite park in St. Louis. Yes, I love Forest Park as well, but TGP is the one less traveled, and...well, you know the rest. I am a fan of the winter months, and I love walking through TGP with its bare trees and brown grass covered with leaves. It's quiet, clean (a big thumbs up to the TG parks department, who busts their asses to keep this place clean and well kept), and provides a solitude that you can't always get at Forest Park. My favorite spots aren't really big features. The cypress grove near the east side, where the main road splits, is especially nice in the early fall. There is a carpet of cypress leaves/needles that acts like a soft carpet. The small woodland pond and benches also on the east side is a little oasis. And of course, any place where the ducks and geese are hangin' out. I like to bird watch too--strictly amateur--and TGP has plenty of birds to observe. Today I saw a great horned owl, and a hawk who was feasting on a squirrel in the high branches of an oak. He dropped it as I came down the path, and I almost got blasted by squirrel guts. Awesome!

text: This is my second favorite venue in Nashville after the Mercy Lounge. It carries the same intimate atmosphere but even more so as it is about half the size of Mercy Lounge. It is literally a basement, and to be more specific, the basement of popular record store Grimey's. The Basement is owned and operated by the people that run the acclaimed record store upstairs, so the quality of the performers is pretty much guaranteed to be fantastic. The Basement is one of those few places that works well for both acoustic and amped up performances. The crowd's always seem into the performers and its common to see people dancing and openly enjoying themselves unlike in other clubs around town. The people there are eclectic, anywhere from college kids to industry professionals to other musicians and the place showcases local as well as touring bands. It is kind of out of the way, and very hard to find if you don't know what you're looking for. Also parking is limited, the parking lot is ultra tiny (I'm talking like 5 or so cars) so you usually have to park on the street in the residential neighborhoods behind the building.

Good, not great....but chalk that up to opening night. Service was super slow at the outset but than recovered nicely to be, well, super. The bill came to $150, for some wine and not a lot of food. I was just a touch underwhelmed and probably wouldn't go back, except for a drink at the lively bar. I hate to review a restaurant on opening night, but they've had plenty of time to get everything down. The square will benefit by this new eatery...I'm just wondering if a Parisian would look on this place the same way I look at the wonderful little eatery in the ninth arrondisement called "American Burger Joe." text: Prior to going to Bern's I was told it was the best steak house in the world. Those are BIG words and hard to stand up to especially if you eat out a lot. Upon driving up to Bern's, the outside was quite simple. Not sure what I was expecting but with a statement like "best in the world" I was expecting not only a great steak but a rich setting. I pulled under the overhang to drop my car at the valet which was the only parking option and when my husband opened the door the first words out of my mouth were "The Madonna Inn". Then I realized that the people we were with were already inside and I hoped they hadn't heard me. Have you been to the Madonna Inn in SLO, CA? Bern's was a bit old fashioned and gaudy. I saw rooms with metal rental chairs, the kind you see in an old Italian restaurant with red and white checkerboard table cloths and in another room I saw white rod iron chairs that are usually outdoors. I ordered the filet of course because I had to try the steak and this is my favorite cut. With the steak was a small cup of French onion soup which was really good, for my salad I ordered the Macadamia Vanilla Bean Vinaigrette on the side since the waitress didn't recommend it and I got the Maple Dijon also on the side. Good choice because the Mac Vanilla bean dressing was more like dessert vs. dressing. With my steak came veggies that I left alone, a baked potato and Steak Fried onion rings. I could have ate a whole plate of these fried onions. They were thin shoestring onions that were lightly breaded and lightly fried. Don't forget to order some mushrooms on the side and if you like mushrooms, order your own because you won't want to share. Now the steak was very good don't get me wrong but it is not the best steak I've ever had and I wouldn't rate it the best in the world because I have yet to hit all the best possibilities. My favorite steak has a bit more seasoning and a touch of melted butter. A few surprises and treats were the kitchen tour. It was immaculate and beyond reproach. There are a ton of restaurants and probably a few of my favorites that I wouldn't want to know what goes on behind the scenes. This place definitely had something to show off. The second treat was the desert room. There is an actual room you go to, that has individual Booth's surrounded by walls with just a doorway on each end. I have never seen anything like this. It made dessert really special. If you have never been to the desert room, save room next time and have this experience. The atmosphere was wonderful, not to mention the deserts. I had the Creme Brule but since I'm a purest when it comes to this dessert, it wasn't my favorite. I like a crisp sugar topping and this had a sort of cookie crust. Good but not what I expect. But the Macadamia Nut Sundae was to die for and I'm not an ice cream fan so if you are, ORDER IT.

text: Lil' Abners est un restaurant quasi-légendaire à Tucson, en Arizona. Situé en dehors de la ville, à l'ouest de l'autoroute I-10, il m'a fallu deux voyages pour le localiser. J'ai entendu parler du lieu pour la première fois par Stephen, un ami de San Diego qui, apprenant que je me rendais à Tucson, m'appela spécialement pour me dire : "Tu vas à Tucson ? Il faut absolutement que tu ailles dîner chez Lil' Abners. C'est un steak house perdu au milieu de nulle part dans le désert, à l'écart de la ville. Tu y accèdes par un chemin de terre, ils sont en contrebas d'une colline. J'y ai été manger il y a 30 ans, ils avaient deux plats au menu : steak et steak. Le vrai "cowboy steak", il n'y a pas mieux !" Armée de ces indications un peu approximatives, j'ai cherché l'endroit sur Google Maps, qui m'a donné une vague idée de comment ne pas me perdre dans le désert. Lil' Abners n'a pas de site web, apparemment les patrons se fichent pas mal de se faire de la pub. Hélas, de ma première équipée je suis rentrée piteusement bredouille. De chemin de terre, point. De collines, des tas. Laquelle choisir ? Pas d'enseigne visible. Le numéro "8501" n'était pas affiché en lettres de néon sur les cactus ! De toutes évidences, les lieux avaient changé en trente ans, et la route avait été asphaltée. La description de mon ami avait perdu de sa fraîcheur d'antan. Quelques jours plus tard, armée d'un GPS, je suis retournée sur Silverbell Road. Et cette fois fut la bonne. Mais le bâtiment est si discret qu'il m'a fallu passer 3 fois devant, au ralenti, pour ne pas le manquer. L'enseigne Lil' Abners n'est visible que lorsque vous roulez sur Silverbell Road vers le sud. Si vous allez vers le nord, le restaurant est sur la gauche, et son enseigne est cachée. Vous ne pouvez le repérer que par un pilône au sommet duquel est perché un petit signe "A1", célèbre marque américaine de sauce pour steak. Mon ami Stephen avait tout de même conservé une image assez fidèle du restaurant lui-même. La route n'est certes plus le chemin de terre d'autrefois, mais le bâtiment n'a pas changé. Tout au plus s'est-il entouré d'un mur qui le dissimule partiellement au yeux des dineurs désespérés de le trouver. La bâtisse date de 1905. C'était un "trade post" qui servait de rendez-vous aux cowboys, aux indiens, aux Mexicains et aux pionniers de la petite bourgade de Tucson. Construite en simples briques peintes, elle est de plain-pied, sans étage. Sa porte d'entrée m'a tout l'air d'être la porte originale, une solide porte en bois étroite, avec un guichet protégé par des barreaux de fer. Un "trade post" en américain, une "posada" en mexicain. Lil' Abners n'est devenu restaurant qu'en 1947, lorsque la famille qui possédait le trade post avant la guerre le transforma en steak house. Au menu : steak et patates. La philosophie du lieu : offrir aux "patrons" (les clients) des steaks de qualité à un prix abordable. Il m'est arrivé à plusieurs reprises de mentionner le nom de Lil' Abners à Tucson. Toutes les personnes avec qui j'en discutais m'ont dit connaître le restaurant et y avoir mangé. Toutes avaient un bon souvenir de la place et disaient y retourner au moins une fois par an. Vote unanime sur la qualité du steak. D'aucunes regrettaient simplement que le prix du steak ait tellement augmenté... en 20 ans. L'intérieur est résolument western. Rien de prétentieux là-dedans. Poutres en bois, simples tables de bois recouvertes d'une nappe de Vichy, éclairage intimiste pour ne pas dire sombre. En face de vous, en entrant, le bar. Au fond à droite, une énorme cheminée de pierre au dessus de laquelle est suspendu un fusil du Far West. A gauche, une salle moins stylisée, avec aux murs des enseignes néon de diverses bières. C'est la salle de droite, la principale, qui est la plus remarquable. Les murs sont totalement recouverts des plaques d'immatriculation et des graffitis des gens qui sont passés par là. Cela me fait penser aux livres d'or du Bagdad Café (oui, le café du film) sur la Route 66, près de Newberry Springs. Ou bien encore aux murs graffités et décorés de billets d'un dollar de Krabby Bill's à Indian Rocks, en Floride. Les gens adorent un endroit, ils le décorent, ils en font un lieu culte. Lil' Abners est de ceux-là. Avec un parfum Wild West, des miroirs anciens, et les photos de Calamity Jane, Wyatt Earp et Jesse James. En 30 ans, la carte n'a guère changé, mais elle s'est étoffée de deux ou trois plats supplémentaires. Du poulet rôti, par exemple. La serveuse est très accueillante, avec un bel accent du sud-ouest des Etats-Unis. J'ai commandé un steak accompagné d'une pomme de terre. Rapidement servi, 5 à 6 minutes plus tard, le plat est arrivé avec une grosse patate, et un énorme steak avec une bonne odeur de viande grillée. Les steaks sont préparés sur le grill, à l'extérieur. Le steak était délicieux. Vraiment à la hauteur des dires de Stephen et de mes anticipations. Cuit exactement comme je l'avais demandé (en

text: Can I give negative stars? I can't even begin to express how poorly my mother was treated here. She had a scratch on one of her lenses, so she took it back to be replaced under warranty. They sent it out to the lab, and she finally received them back 3 weeks later. She had been getting headaches wearing her glasses so after awhile she thought her eyes got worse and her prescription needed to be updated. When she went to her eye doctor, the Dr. said that one of her lenses was incorrect. The lense had been replaced with a lense for myopic patients. Luckily, except for the headaches, it didn't do any damage to her eyes. Now, unless the lense is a bifocal, who can tell the difference? No layman that's for sure! Only the Dr. who puts the lense in a machine! So my mom went back to Absolutely Optical who told her that the lenses are only guaranteed for 6 months and they refused to replace it! They said it was the lab's mistake. Now, I understand not replacing the lenses after 6 months if the patient's rx changed without the fault of the company. However, the lab put in the wrong lense! It's not like her rx got worse and she's expecting them to update her rx for free. What kind of company outsources work and doesn't check to make sure it's correct before giving it to the customer? Especially when it's something that has the potential to hurt or harm another human being? Luckily, this particular type of lense had the correct strength and did not do any harm except for the headaches, but what if it had? Eyesight declines naturally as you age. We don't need irresponsible people to help that along. Of course, my mother was upset! But instead of admitting fault and making a long term customer (who has brought business from both herself and my father to them) happy, they told her to take her business elsewhere! Can you believe the audacity? Some people have no morals. Yes, this place is conveniently located at the mall, but that doesn't give them the right to treat their customers poorly. Avoid them at all costs. Bring your business to people who treat others with respect and descency.

text: On my recent trip to Nashville, we ran into some trouble finding places to eat/drink. I combed over Yelp extensively, even posted a talk subject hoping to find some help with my specific needs. (I don't like country music, don't care for touristy spots, and wanted to find genuinely good food for a decent price, much like I can at home.) After all the searching, we ended up hitting a few well reviewed spots, and I am beginning to think my taste buds must be really different from everyone else's. We went to Eastland on our second night in town. The space was very cute, home-y with an open kitchen. We opted to sit outside (in the backyard, if you will...) The weather was nice, and even though our server looked to be busy, he greeted us promptly. We both ordered a glass of wine, me a sparkling, him a red. His was much better than mine, I must say. (Believe me, it's hard for me to admit. I am used to being the ordering professional.) There was something odd about the wine list, though. The prices were actually in favor of ordering by the glass opposed to ordering by the bottle. (Only a few dollars more, but at every other restaurant, you save a little by ordering the bottle. That way, you not only spend more, but the restaurant saves by not having open bottles sitting around for too long.) Since we had a late lunch, we opted to order three appetizers and a side to share, plus the complimentary bread, served with the odd but acceptable combination of traditional dipping oil infused with cilantro. We got the pizza, the goat cheese brulee, the crab cake, and the jalapeno mac and cheese. Mediocrity seemed to be the running theme. The crab cake tasted just like every other version (except for Blais' at Home....I don't think I need to go into that again, but my mouth is watering just thinking about it.) It had way too much filler, not nearly enough crab. The pizza was decent, competently done, with accurate flavors, but it wasn't something I would recommend. The goat cheese brulee was odd. It was a lump of goat cheese on a plate, then hit with a torch and covered in honey and a balsamic glaze. It was served with what looked to be the pizza crust, sliced with no toppings, roasted red peppers, yellow peppers, and tomatoes. A bite of just the crust and the goat cheese was way too sweet, but pairing it with the roasted tomatoes overpowered the other flavors. (I liked the tomatoes, their flavor was just too rich for the goat cheese.) The mac and cheese was the saving grace of the meal, though it was so hot and bubbly we couldn't even eat it until we were full from everything else. (I know that isn't a real problem, but I want to be able to eat things within twenty minutes of them hitting the table. This was too hot to do even that.) After a couple of bites of the perfectly spicy and rich pasta, we took that last piece of pizza and the mac and cheese to go, and paid the bill, which came to $50. Reasonable in the price, but we didn't order main courses. Bottom line is, I would probably enjoy sitting at Eastland's bar and having a cocktail, but wouldn't choose to go back for dinner.

Then came out Ika salad (fried calamari), steamed pork bun, and sichuan pork dumplings. The ika salad was really good, lightly breaded and matched perfectly with a sweet balsamic vinegar sauce. The bun and dumplings were so so. They said the dumplings were suppose to be spicy, but they weren't at all and the sauce wasn't flavorful. Our dragon boat finally came after watching a table of 4 sit and leave after finishing their meal. I would advice you now, do NOT order sushi from here. Our boat has tuna, white tuna, yellowtail tuna, salmon, mackerel, chilean sea bass, and tilapia sashimi, tuna and spider rolls, a california roll with spicy tuna on top and a cooked shrimp sushi. It seems like a lot, but they were not fresh. The chilean sea bass was so chewy I thought my teeth would fall off, which made it very fishy tasting. The salmon was mushy, like it's been dead for months. Yea... GROSS. The spicy tuna on top of the ca roll did not make it better, it's like adding fish puke to fake crab meat. I'm sure the standard for sushi around here makes this place the best sushi place in the world, but I would never come back for the sushi.

text: I had brunch here with my sister today. We've only stopped by to get pastries or cakes here, so we were excited to try the meal today. However, we ended up feeling disappointed with our brunch experience, and we ended up cheering ourselves with a fruit tart and a cookie at the front. La Bonne Bouchée is a small, quaint place with a cute outdoor sitting area, and you're greeted by tempting pastries and cakes that are too sweet and delicious to pass. My sister and I were the first two people waiting to be seated. We had to wait five minutes to be seated. We miss the busy lunch crowd, so waiting to be seated for five minutes is unacceptable, especially when we saw more than three tables opened at the restaurant. We took a seat inside close to the entrance. We were rudely greeted by our server with long black frizzy hair with an European accent. Actually scratch that. There was no greeting, just "what do you want to drink?" We kindly told her that the water was fine, and she tossed us our menu and responded "I'll be back" with a sour attitude. WTF- What the French! My sister ordered a petit portion of Adriatic Chicken Salad and I ordered the Quiche du Jour. After our rude server took our order with an attitude, we watched her waltz around table to table. A couple minutes later a table with three people were being seated near us. My sister and I watched our impolite server take their order. We were shocked to see how quick her attitude changed. It was like seeing a whole new different server. She greeted them with a smile and "how are you." Also recited the Soup of the Day and the Quiche of the Day. My sister and I were very confused and irritated. Enough about our rude server, more importantly the food: My sister's Adriatic Chicken Salad looked like something any dummy can make it at home. It's just grilled chicken breast over some greens, tomato, olives, red onions, feta cheese, and balsamic vinaigrette. The salad had way too much feta cheese. More cheese than lettuce. The salad was average, but it wasn't worth the $8.80 (a full is $11.75). I ordered the Quiche du Jour which came with the vegetables and the choice of a side salad or a soup. I ordered the Soup du Jour which was a vegetable and noodles soup. The soup and the quiche wasn't too bad. The soup was mediocre. Overall, the experience was horrible. The service was horrible. The food was mediocre. We tipped probably less than 15 percent. I am a server and I've always treated every customers with a smile even if they are down-right rude to me. We did not want to order desserts from our server, so we went up to the bakery to order it ourselves and ate it outside because the weather was beautiful today. The dessert was delicious. I had the petit fruit tart (strawberries and kiwi with cream on top of the tart) and my sister had an oatmeal cookie. I don't know I'll ever go back to eat a meal there again, but maybe I'll make a quick stop once in awhile for a pastry.

text: Let me start by saying that we live in the neighborhood and that this was our favorite go-to bar for years. We would come here with friends from out-of-town, after a really late night at work for dinner, and sometimes on a random afternoon for a cold drink on a hot and sweaty day when we were too gross to go anywhere else. We had made this place part of our lives. My father-in-law had been here back in the 80's and was thrilled to see new ownership. My best friend (raised by a bar-owning family) had given it approval way before the Philly Weekly did. Reasons we loved it back then: blackened green beans, fries like at Monk's when you don't want to deal with the wait there, great beer selection, unpretentious, perfect amount of dive and grime. But we had a inconceivable experience about a year and a half ago and have never been back. And I think that other people should skip it as well. January 1, 2009. I know it was a holiday and bad manners can sometimes be excused by the stress that comes with it, but bear with me. My cousins and brother are in-town and we are headed to the Poconos the next day for our annual, under-40, family ski-day. We drop by Grace's for a low-key dinner and some beers. It's not that crowded and we get the big round table without much wait. My cousin, who has learning disabilities and is also a bartender, goes to order a beer he had never heard of before and has trouble pronouncing it (I know you have all had this problem with imports somewhere). He tries to order the beer and the bartender snaps at him because he can't understand what he said. My cousin becomes flustered and apologizes and says he didn't know how to pronounce it. The bartender snarls, "If your mouth wasn't full when you were trying to talk, I could hear what you were saying." My cousin wasn't eating. My cousin then proceeds to says that he is sorry, he has dyslexia, points to the menu, and asks how to pronounce it. The bartender essentially calls him a liar. At this point in time, I talk my slightly inebriated kid brother out of starting a honor fight on his cousin's behalf and we (now unhappily) finish our dinner and our round and go to leave. I've had conversations with this bartender before. He's given me samples, offered beer education, mentioned his favorite books. I figure he is having an off-night. On the way out, I approach the bartender and tell him about how we are regulars, about how my cousin does have disabilities, and that I am upset by how he treated my family. He essentially tells me to go fuck myself. Again, I have to talk my kid brother out of a brawl. And that is why I have given up blackened green beans.

text: Reputation trickles down in the very best way possible at SideBern's, the irreverent sibling of the ever present and highly acclaimed Bern's Steakhouse. "One World Under Food" is it's philosophy, with an eclectic menu that changes every day, flying in the face of Bern's staid demeanor. Once you are seated you are handed not one but two menus, the regular, cutting edge cuisine from around the world and a smaller, Dim Sum menu featuring smaller portions of items ranging from dumplings to scallops. It's a beautiful thing that SideBern's gets to share in the enormous wine collection that Bern's Steakhouse has had for over 50 years, because you get a choice from over 30 different wines by the glass if you are not ready to spend the money on a bottle. I had the beet salad to start, a geometrically designed plate featuring two small piles of layered beet, goat cheese and black truffle goodness with small streaks of a raspberry and Dijon vinaigrette. Then I had a Peking style duck breast with cabbage, black beans and snap peas. The flavors all worked quite nicely together, none of which overpowered the others. The one problem I had was the portions. The mini salad and the huge entree seemed like a pretty drastic contrast. While my dining partners decided to to take the light fare route by getting apps for both courses, they agreed. They were also a but put off by the trendiness of the space. Yes, all the beautiful people were stationed at the bar, and the bulkiness of the aluminum menus kept knocking over the glassware on the way-to-small table. And the last small inconvenience was the service, which was adequate but a bit clumsy and unpolished. But those little things did not diminish the over all experience though. The dining room is beautiful, with polished wood and arching, spider-like chandeliers over the bar and lounge. Everyone from the hosts to the service staff were knowledgeable and friendly. Yes it's trendy and yes you will pay for it when the check is dropped, but don't let that stop you, the food will keep you coming back for more.

text: This joint currently holds the record for 'Worst Greek Food Ever Served in a Restaurant,' and I've had some junk more Grease than Greece. Ordered the Gyro Sandwich w/ Greek Salad. Unable to verify Kim B.'s comments on the bread because our flighty waitress declined to bring us any. Also, final bill for two (two gyros and two sodas) was around 25 with a decent tip. I wasn't kidding before, it really tasted like a Chalupa with Greek-themed filling. Unfortunate, esp. given Tarpon Spring's reputation. Already pleased with the ambience, I was looking forward to a great experience with my date. And then came the cornbread muffins--a great conversation starter and to die for, folks! text: I don't know what it is about Jazmine. I think they put some sort of addictive additive in their food. The food, at first glance, isn't so impressive. I mean that- at a glance- literally. Their summer rolls- the fried ones- those are good too. 2. Tasty Pho- if a bit americanized. This one is easier on the anise than other tastes in the city. The beef pho is great here because they use a nice flank cut of the steak, and it comes out very rare (to be cooked in the soup, o'course). No thai basil, but the cilantro makes up for it. Yum. They also have a chicken pho, for those who aren't fans of red meat. 3. My Favorite Bun- okay, they call them "noodle salad" on the menu here, but we all know what they're talking about. My favorite is the sesame steak noodle bowl, but I've also had a love affair with the tuna noodle bowl and the vegetarian tofu avocado bowl at one time or another (the later is something like a giant, bowl-filling version of their veg. spring roll). These bowls come with a cup of lemongrass soup, which my best friend became addicted to and led me to try to recreate. I failed, but the salty little blend is exciting and aromatic. They redesigned the interior here a year or so ago. It looks ritzier inside, but the flavors are the same, and the prices are still good. To be honest, it made me a little sad- based largely in the fact that renovation meant almost a month of no Jazmine They've also added to the menu. I have yet to taste one of the new poboys, but I've heard other customers sing their praises. okay, I may have said to much already. try it- you'll like it!* *don't try it on monday- on monday, they are closed

text: I find it funny that people think that it's about a logo. Lacoste has been around much longer than the logo craze, 1933, and the crocodile has been there the whole time. I have four Lacoste shirts (French ones) that are twenty-six years old and I can still wear them. I can't think of anything from A&F that would keep it's shape, fit and style for that long. You're paying not for a crocodile, but for quality: taped seams, long fiber twisted cotton and clothes have even gotten better over twenty years. These shirt have worn in with character and the cotton has gotten silky soft. I'm amused that now you can buy the shirts "distressed" from the store, apparently, twenty years of my washing them is distressing enough. It is true that they're Euro-sized; they come from Europe, so some North American sized customers are going to find them hard to fit, but that's true of clothing in Europe, period; it's not a Lacoste conspiracy. I still fit my twenty+ year old shirts, so it's not impossible. Lacoste suffered a bit of a setback in North America when it licensed it's brand to Izod. They eventually withdrew from that agreement over quality issues with Izod and disappeared from North America for a while. Even though, I'm a bigger fan of Fred Perry, their British competitor, I'm glad to see them back and available from the boutique in Edmonton. Get past the logo. You're buying quality clothes, classically styled so they're of use to you over many years not just a season or two. Buy them the way the French do, one or two items when you can afford it, supplementing your wardrobe, not trying to replace it every season.

text: Steakhouses are generally predictable, wildly-overpriced, you get nothing with your steak forcing all but the most passionate carnivores to order "side" dishes which average about $8.00 a piece. This was an exception to those generalities. The steak was prepared generally the way I asked for it (if unevenly) and actually comes with side dishes. And for once, I wish it hadn't. First, I have never seen a more phallic presentation of food on a plate. A circular steak on one end of the elliptical plate, a good portion of "smashed" potatoes on the other, and down the center aimed squarely at me was a single, HUGE carrot. It was so bizarre, I actually laughed out loud. There was another problem with the uber carrot (apart from the challenges of cooking something this big evenly); it is coated in what has to be the single worst idea for a sauce I've EVER tasted in my life. While they refer to it as "glazed", what they should call it is "frosted" (as in mini wheats, pop tarts, etc.) If there is an ingredient in this nightmare sauce apart from sugar and allspice(?), I'd be surprised because it tasted iike nothing else. Rather than a savory steak, it smelled like a Christmas cake or, worse, fruitcake. It overpowered everything else on the plate and made even a round Cabernet Sauvignon taste "wrong". It was vile. Bizarre. Even if you could avoid the flavor of the sauce, the smell was enough to destroy your interest in the meat. What happened next is what really defines a restaurant's "self-awareness" to me... When I asked our server to A) Bring me a replacement carrot minus the sauce and B) PLEASE take away the offending versions from the table, her response was, "Yeah, people either love it or hate it." What? Okay, maybe it was just her. I also mentioned it to the lightly defensive but eventually sympathetic manager that a culinary train wreck of "I'm not coming back here again" proportions had taken place, his response was "Yeah, people either love it or hate it." Uh, how many people need to hate this before you think "hey, maybe this isn't such a great recipe" and stop serving it? People who seek out a steakhouse aren't looking for an adventure, they're looking for a steak and most likely a bottle of Silver Oak (if they're on an expense account). Reading the other reviews, "upper-end restaurant"? No, not even close. In those restaurants, a good chef will come out to the table to inquire as to why TWO ENTIRE SERVINGS were sent back. As for the carrot cake being a disappointment, given the above story, I can't help but marvel at the irony. Perhaps their efforts went into making a carrot taste like a cake rather than making cake taste like a carrot. If you want a steak, make the drive to Flemming's or, if necessary, Sullivan's. You'll leave a bit poorer, but you won't feel robbed.

text: It feels weird to be writing a Yelp review for the place that I've basically lived in for the past few years, but I can't say enough for this school. The education I've received has been challenging and engaging, and although I've grown bored of schooling in general, UCSB has kept me engaged and invested in the university. The school has a great atmosphere, an unbeatable location, amazing people, and I've met very few people who have regretted attending this university. Educationally, the majority of classes are great. Professors are, for the most part, really here for the students, and will go out of their way to help a student out. Class sizes range from gigantic (500+ in Campbell Hall for some intro level classes) to tiny (12 students and a professor in super specific classes). I came in with a great idea of what I wanted to study, but after taking great classes in random departments, seriously considered changing my major, so I highly recommend checking out a handful of classes just for the hell of it. Isla Vista. The good comes with the bad. The place has more community and culture than any neighborhood I've ever lived in, but you'll get reamed by the cost of living. The place has a certain reputation, which I've found to be blown way out of proportion by those who don't live here. Sure, there is a party atmosphere, but most of the people who get out of control are visiting from out of town and expect IV to be some kind of lawless epicenter for the debauch. Those who live here are generally respectful and kind, and a pleasure to live around. As someone who doesn't consider himself a partier, I've loved my time living in Isla Vista. I was hoping for more since my seafood experiences have been generally more positive and a few co-workers had provided positive feedback. I read their menus online before heading over and was looking forward to trying out a few items. I got there for their happy hour specials and since I was on my own, sat down at the bar. The server didn't seem happy about handing me the HH menu and I had to ask for it specifically. I ordered 3 dishes and it seems they didn't time it very well but wanted to wait for all 3 to be ready before bringing it out. It resulted in my over-cooked truffle fries sitting out for about 10 minutes before it was brought to me. Piping hot fries are tasty, slightly over-cooked, hardened fries, not-so-much. The mini-burger was the best of the bunch. My mussels weren't fresh as 2-3 were still closed, and one had a cracked shell but the flesh was stuck to the top and bottom of the shell meaning someone just tried to crack it open. Anyhow, the servers seem to focus on the male guests at the bar more... maybe they tend to drink more and tip more, who knows. All I know is that I wasn't impressed by the food and the service didn't add anything to the overall experience.

text: As the other reviews here indicate, this place is huge hassle on Saturdays and Sundays, and frankly, the Morning Glory isn't amazing enough to merit all that trouble. (Few places really are.) But check out Morning Glory on a Tuesday. Without the long wait, you can appreciate the warm, neighborhoody feel of this place and enjoy the food. When it's not packed, the waitstaff still cultivates an air of hip surliness, but at least they're not rushing you out the door. Go for the fritatta; the kitchen staff excels with eggs of all styles. My foodie sister-in-law is still talking about the goat cheese fritatta she had here over a year ago.

text: I love the downtown YMCA. I love the class varieties and options they have to offer. I like the aerobic teachers. I love the machines, especially the elliptical with the t.v.'s! My recommendations for classes would be Body Pump with Connie. If you want to feel the burn hours/days after your workout, she can provide. I also like her kickboxing class. Deep Dance is a nice way to burn 600 cals an hour without ever looking at the clock. There are plenty of other classes to check out too. All the classes are included in your membership fee, so it's like a one stop shop. They also have a really nice swimming pool with slides and a kiddo area. My only compliant would be the parking situation outside. Not a lot of spots and they are kinda tight to get into.

text: I stayed here last week for a meeting. It's a very large hotel with a Las Vegas feel considering the size of it. It's great if you are one of those people who never want to leave the hotel. There are eight places to eat, seven bars/night clubs, a spa and fitness center, and a shuttle to take you to the Opry Mills mall. Sounds amazing right? Wrong. I am a more picky traveler than most, but I was not impressed by the rooms or the food. The rooms are standard three to three and a half star rooms. The mattress was lumpy and uneven. Also, for two night in a row, my room key did not work after 12:00 AM. I had to walk to the lobby which was an 1/8-1/4 of a mile twice each night to get into my room because they wouldn't fix it the first time. The next day the key worked fine. It's as if the mechanism had been turned off. The food I had was prepared for a large number of people, but I still thought it lacked flavor. Maybe lots of hotels are the same way, but I tend to avoid hotel food when I travel unless the restaurant has received notable reviews. There were none of those restaurants in Opryland. The fitness room was spacious and had a decent number of machines which are relatively new. This was the best part of the hotel for me. Also, the hotel is in the southeast part of town so if you want to go to downtown it's a bit of a drive. You are not in the heart of the city. It's in the burbs. I would not stay at Gaylord if I returned to Nashville. For a minimum of $189 a night, you can find a better hotel.
label: NEG

text: Well... I think Miss J. is a much better writer than me 'cause she nailed this one right on the head. Something was just off about this place. Indeed, the valet is ridiculous (although we did not need to pay on a Friday night... just a tip) and the waitstaff was pathetic. The one thing that Miss J. left out was the unbelievably ridiculous dessert cart they had to manhandle around the restaurant. The thing made Noah's Ark look like a dingy. It probably took 2 or 3 redwoods to get enough wood to build it. Worst of all, they serve you the dessert right off of it. It's been sitting by the front door and then lugged around the place for hours sucking up everyone's sneeze particles and then, wham! You get to enjoy your lovely tiramisu served right off of it. My Penne Bolognese was pretty good though. Perhaps a pretty pricy at $18, but tasty nonetheless. The search for decent, affordable Italian in the area continues...

text: Aritzia is mostly too rich for my blood, but I can't stop myself from shopping here. Sometimes I have to force myself not to go in, because it's all downhill for my bank account from there. I usually take medium-sized coats but this one is small and fits perfectly, so the psychological power of this coat was enough to swallow the cost - over $400. text: I absolutely LOVE this place. Lots to see and lots to EAT! My brother and I were in Philly for a wedding and I had to visit this place to eat at DiNIC's! Seeing this place from Man V Food was my source of finding out about this place and the PORK! O-M-G So much to see and so much to eat at Reading Terminal, but this review will cover DiNICs. When we first walked up to the counter we saw mounds of delicious pork behind the window! You can see perfectly cooked pork just sitting there waiting to be someone's meal! This was heavenly and awesome...i think i was drooling the whole time in line and I was in some sort of hog trance...lol. You can see the oven in the back they use to cook the pork and also the awesome dripping from the pork they use as gravy when they dip the pork again when they make that sandwich. I got mine with the green spinach-type pork sandwich. That first bite was out of this world. You don't get this in Texas for sure. This place definitely made up for Geno's and Pat's. Philly to me is not known for the philly cheese steak (i think texadephia here in Texas is a thousand time better), but for that awesome pork sandwich at DiNIC's! I will definitely be back! Enjoy!

Their food very good...and their bar, EXCELLENT. Their espresso martini, to die for! I highly recommend this place if you're in the KOP area in need of a steak, but make reservations!

text: I've been to Smokehouse on Shelby twice now. The first time was a decent meal in a cool building, but nothing terribly memorable. The second time (Saturday of this past weekend) was definitely memorable . . . and terrible. I had friends in town and we were seeing a show in Fountain Square, so I took them to Smokehouse beforehand to take in a little bit of the area. We were treated horribly by the waitstaff from the moment of our arrival. The hostess couldn't be bothered to seat us, despite the sign that said "Please Wait to Be Seated". Instead, she yanked out a chair and told us to pull it up to a booth because we couldn't have a table (there were MANY tables available, only one in the entire place being used and not a reserved sign to be seen). We then had to wait an extremely long time just to put in our drink orders (and, I should mention, there was hardly anyone in the restaurant - no reason for such slow service). When our drinks came, three of us had ordered iced tea. It was awful. It was as clear as the water our other two companions ordered and tasted like some watered-down sweet tea packet. When we complained (politely - everyone in the party has worked in food service and we know how taxing it can be), the server was sarcastic, rude, and treated us like we were stupid for saying anything. When we complained to another employee about this server, she offered little better. When the food came, it was all right, but certainly not worth the trouble we went through to get it. We hardly ever saw our server and when we did, we were treated badly. Long story short: avoid this joint like the plague.

text: We used Lenora last December. Our belongings had to be stored overnight and unloaded the next day. Lenora came in with the lowest bid, so we hired them. Here is my dilemma. The movers were excellent! They worked hard and were impressively fast. However, they were 3 hours late to load and 2 hours early to unload (we were still closing on our new place when the truck arrived and the clock started ticking) Additionally, the company assured us that they take Major Credit Cards as a form of payment. Unfortunately their story changed when they loaded the truck. If you every purchased a house before, you would understand that looking for an extra 1K in cash on your closing day in not what one would call "stress free". Bottom line: I would recommend Lenora if you are paying cash ONLY. Unfortunately I will have to give 1 star, since I did not receive the service that I was promised and I will not use this moving company again for that only reason. Sorry, Lenora. You lost me as a customer.

text: At Bywater BBQ there was no smoke to be found, neither by sight nor smell. I found this even more disturbing as my self-guided tour revealed an outdoor patio and yard, but still, no smoke. I think any of you who might be a part of my smoke-loving brethren would find this equally disconcerting. Consider yourself warned. I ordered the ribs and was looking forward to some hands on, tactile rib gnawing, but instead I received an enormous serving that tasted more like they'd been cooked in a slow cooker. The meat fell off the bone when nudged with fork, which is fine, but definitely not what I was expecting. More alarming were the sides. I can't be sure and I hate to make this claim unconfirmed, but I suspect that the baked beans may have come from a can. Furthermore, the collard greens were cooked without any kind of meat (horrors), and as a result, tasted a bit like feet. However, there were some plusses, they just weren't food related: 1) Complete with an outside patio and bar, the locale is exceptionally adorable 2) Our waiter was sweet and endearing - a little slice of heaven 3) Dos Equis on tap!!

text: Griffin Plaza Art Supply is a fantastic art supply store in Nashville, TN. This store has a few locations in the Midwest and in the Northeast, but this is the only location in Tennessee. The store is huge and the prices are incredibly reasonable. They have a full line of supplies whether you draw, oil paint, use acrylics, sculpture, screen printing, framing, it sounds cheesy, but if you can imagine it Plaza Art Supplies will find a way for you to create it. (They do not really carry photography materials, though). They usually carry 'starter' versions of all their supplies and also a higher end professional version of the materials. The staff can point you in the right direction if you give them the details about what you are trying to accomplish. I visited the shop when I wanted to embark on a screen printing project. The sales person got me setup with everything I needed, in the quantities I needed. Also, the cashier got me set up with their shopper's card. All you have to do is give them your email address, and you get %15 off every time you shop! That's a pretty good deal, considering their prices are really good to begin with.

text: Wow. I have not seen this bad quality in food in a really long time. This review only refers to the hot pot, not their other stuff. However, I will not return to try anything else. We also for the clams and the beef to go with the order. First of all, the lettuce that they brought out (which they call bok choy- it's really iceburg lettuce), was so old that the veins in the lettuce were turning that red color. We asked them to change it out for us, which they did reluctantly. Then the clams came out. They were a bunch of little frozen clams that were already out of the shell. A little suspicious, but since they were frozen, I thought maybe they were just trying to keep it fresher longer. That's fine.. But then we dipped those in the broth for a little, and then bit into the fishiest, oldest tasting things we've ever tasted. We sent those back as well, but the server argued that we cooked the clams too long. Too long doesn't equal fishy and old, buddy. I'm so glad that the broth was super boiled because I have a lurking suspicion that was old and a half, too. Save your health, go somewhere else.

Poached shrimp, served in broth cappuccino-style The palate cleanser was a lovely spiced-port panne cotta with beads of fresh pear. All the courses were wonderful, but the Peking Duck Breast was especially memorable. Souffles were also a delight. text: Hellas (emphasis on the 2nd syllable) ... me being from Northern Cali, i at first thought it was accent on the 1st, like Hella Good. text: It was a Saturday night and market st in Philly was swarming with people. My friends and I checked 2 restaurants but they both had over an hour long waits. The wait at Anjou? Non existant. That should have been a red flag right there but we were starving and they had couscous on the menu, April's fave. The menu wasn't cheap but the food sounded good. Marco and Karina ordered the "Chilean Sea Bass w/ Tarot puree, heart of palm salad, atop a miso glaze [26]". April ordered the "Pan Seared Red Chile Norwegian Salmon, Sweet peas & couscous in a sun dried tomato, red pepper sauce [22]" because again, she was seriously craving couscous. A fourth companion, Megan, ordered the "Bi Bim Bap- A medley of vegetable & egg julienne, served with two traditional Korean sauces and a bowl of miso soup (available without beef) [16]." I opted for the "French Cut Chicken Breast, Wasabi gnocchi, wild mushrooms, & asparagus in a sweet garlic ginger sauce [22]." All sounds delicious doesn't it? Yeah, we thought so too. First problem. A chip in my glass that was sharp enough to cut a lip. I didn't get cut but I could have! Did I mention the plastic shard at Cheesecake?? The waitress apologized and gave me a fresh glass. Fine, no biggie. Second problem. They ran out of gnocchi for my chicken and tried to push the mashed potatoes. Hey, I can make that at home for a dollar. No thanks. So they said they can do risotto. Fine, no biggie. Third problem. A very, VERY long wait. For a restaurant that wasn't very busy, they sure like to take their time. Maybe they were trying to lure other unsuspecting people from the outside by pretending that they have a full happening place like the rest of them but my friends and I had no interest in being part of their marketing gimmick. We just wanted to be fed! The food had better be worth the wait.... Fourth problem. We finally received our entrees and I immediately recognized a problem. April, the poor innocent patron who had ordered the salmon because of the couscous received, before her, a plate looking very barren with a piece of salmon the size and shape of a sleeve of laffy taffys, 6 or 7 halves of asparagus, and NO COUSCOUS. BIG BIGGIE. "Where's her couscous?!" I blurted out. That's when we noticed that nearly all our dishes were missing crucial elements from the menu. The chilean sea bass was NOT served with mashed taro and hearts of palm salad. just a ring of MASHED POTATOES. Maybe I should have asked what "french cut" meant because now I know that it means "slice a chicken breast as thin and flat as possible to try to cover the plate and keep down costs." My wild mushrooms must've gone loco because they were nowhere on my plate. Maybe they were partying it up with my asparagus because they were also m.i.a. My risotto? Oh it was there all right, resting on my plate like a pale, sticky dome of something that resembled MASHED POTATOES! Since when is it okay to be able to scoop risotto with an ice cream scooper?? We were not happy campers. We went on a hunger strike. The host went back to the kitchen to find out what happened. He came back and informed us that "they ran out of the couscous, and the mashed taro" AND the gnocchi??? And the wild mushrooms??? What do you have back there, a 50 lb bag of instant MASHED POTATOES??? The rest is blur. I remember telling the host/waiter/customer service you can't just change an order without asking the patron if it's fine with them. He agreed and took care of the drinks that we had ordered. That much they did right. We still left a tip for the waitress because we felt horrible that she has to tell family and friends that she works there. We left. Still hungry and livid. The waitress was outside crying and smoking a cigarette. Poor girl, I hope she moves on to a decent establishment like Hooters or Fudruckkers. I wish her well. The 5 of us went down the street to Soho Pizza and scarfed scrumptious slices for 2.50 a piece. And when I ordered the mushroom and broccoli pizza, both mushrooms AND broccoli appeared on my slice. See, other people can do it, why can't Anjou? Unless you want mashed potatoes, don't go here. EDIT 1/19/10- It has come to my attention that this dreadful place is now CLOSED. VICTORY!!!!
label: NEG

text: Yes, this place is a wee bit pricey.. but if every single gift I ever receive for the rest of my life comes from this store, I will be a happy woman. Just peek in the window and you'll see what I mean. Necklaces made out of antique typewriter keys, earrings of unusual but lovely shiny semi-precious stones dangling on silver wires, eclectic collections of tiny photographs laminated and chained into bracelets... The jewelry here is right in the sweet spot between gold with diamonds and rash-inducing-mystery-metal with plastic: not the kind of thing you're going to find on jewelers row (i.e. not the kind of thing you can only wear when you're getting all fancy) but not the kind of thing you get for $3 at Target either. Not that there's anything wrong with getting jewelry for $3 at Target. That's my favorite place to buy earrings. Anyway, the various accessories are a little too expensive for a gal like me to spring for them whenever I want, but they're just right when I'm looking for an extra special gift for my sister... or for myself... They also have great handbags, a few unique greeting cards, the occasional scarf or pair of gloves, etc. If you ever need to kill a few minutes on your way to meet friends at Capogiro, this is the place to stop.

text: this airport basically sucks. However, unfortunately, I do have to use it frequently, so it gets a couple of stars. Here is important info: If you are flying US AIR domestic (USA only), then you could be in Terminal C or F. Before you get to the airport, figure out which terminal you are flying out of. Next, if you are flying Southwest, know if you are in Terminal D or E. Knowing this info will help figuring out where you need to check bags, etc. getting from terminal to terminal inside the secure areas is tricky at PHL. You are better off just going to the correct terminal. You could walk from terminal to terminal on the roadside...but, it will be a long walk!! Parking in the airport is VERY expensive (short-term and long-term). So, if you are poor and have to drive, then use an off-site lot (8$ to 12$ per day) or the Economy lot. Food choices inside most terminals SUCK badly (except Terminal C). So, bring your own food if you want. Drinks, etc is very expensive, but you have no choice than to buy them here or not have a drink at all. Toilets can be hit or miss. Best used minimally. Flight delays are very common and are a rule with US AIR. Weather is often bad and low ceilings are common. The SEPTA train runs through each terminal and connects to downtown and other destinations. SEPTA rail costs $7 to downtown and $10 to Jenkintown. (one way). People (staff) are generally not friendly, since this is the northeast. You might luck out. Continental airlines usually have reasonably good staff. I fly this airline most of the time. There are not enough chairs for the number of people (especially in terminal D). This is not fun. Also, almost non-existent power outlets. There are some by the restrooms, if you want to sit close to the nasty smells. Overall, ok airport....this is going to be as good as it gets for Philadelphia. It wont be better until USAIR becomes bankrupt and stops flying. Then, we could get a different airline as a Philly hub which might improve facilities. Oh, Be VERY careful when exiting off of I-95 to the airport. Thanks to senseless road-designers, they made the airport exits as dangerous as they possibly can. Best to just take the train if you dont live here.

text: I love hotel bars. The good ones are warm and inviting and when they serve and are named after the official drink of New orleans. And they are not joking about official ... its in the charter-- The Louisiana House of Representatives made a historic decision Monday: In a 62-33 vote, legislators proclaimed the Sazerac -- the famed mix of rye whiskey, bitters and absinthe that originated in the bayou -- New Orleans' official cocktail. The drink's origins date back to the 1830s, when a Creole apothecary named Antoine Peychaud concocted a potent recipe at his pharmacy in the French Quarter. Peychaud combined his family's secret recipe for bitters with cognac and began serving the drink to friends. Although the Sazerac can be found across New Orleans' drinking establishments, Peychaud's bitters remain the key to creating this iconic cocktail. NPR's Robert Siegel prepares a Sazerac under the strict guidance of Lu Brow, bar chef at the Swizzle Stick Bar in downtown New Orleans. Brow calls the Sazerac a "wonderful, complex" cocktail and adds, "If ever there was a city that deserved an official drink, it was New Orleans." Needless to say the drink was amazing and the bar is worthy of the name.

The legs were great, though they are not for the squeamish, esp if you like frogs. They look very leg like, as opposed to chicken wings, for example, and you can easily make out the little webbed feet. You've been warned vegetarians. For the main event, I had the blackened drum. Apparently the chef won the Iron Chef with this dish and I can see why. The drum fish (white, flaky, fluffy, great cut) is pressed with a delicious mix of cajun spices and is really infused with the flavors. The result is an outstandingly tender filet, with a perfect mix of spice and flavors, served under cajun butter. there's a roasted vegetable rataouille on the side, which is nothing out of this world, but a great accompaniment. The final step is a creamy mashed potatoes which soaks up the spicy butter perfectly. TRY THIS DISH. Dessert was a panoply; the chocolate molten cake was a halloween special, so you will not find it, but try is cousin if you can. The best was the bread pudding, YOU MUST have this, it's absolutely amazing.

text: New to Philly, I went to the Mexican Post based on a glowing recommendation from someone showing me around town. It was the biggest mistake in the brief history of my Philly food experience. I could go on about the frozen ingredients and horrible chile relleno. Instead, I will say that this is my first Yelp review despite having an account for over a year. Yes - the food at the Mexican was so bad, the experience so frustrating, that I was motivated to post a review warning potential visitors. You've been warned - stay away from the Mexican Post.

text: Dave carries the BEST meat and seafood available in the Treasure Valley..wine selection is also A-one. A great place to grab lunch and all sorts of sauces, oils etc. They also have salads, sweet things, pasta, beer..have been frequenting this place for the past 5 years and it is the saving grace for many a dinner at our house. Most recently we purchased Kobe prime rib to cook for Christmas..WOW. It costs a little more than supermarket shopping but is completely worth it.

text: I think I mentioned wanting multi grain crust at least two or three times while we were ordering and when the pizza came I was convinced they had screwed up and given me extra bleached white doughy crust. But apparently there were a few grains in the dough if you looked close enough but it was the whitest "multi grain" I've ever seen! The toppings were alright, but not the fresh and flavorful toppings I love....overall I was not impressed. Oh and especially with the pitchers! My friends ordered a pitcher because it was two dollars cheaper than getting two beers, but the pitcher was about the size of one beer mug!! We almost asked for one each with an accompanying straw... This pizza just does not compare to a good wood fired pizza or even pizza I make at home.

text: Meh. I don't have high standards for my Mexican food. I usually end up at Las Palmas or La Hacienda. I used to be a regular at Rosepepper until the food quality dived. I was happy there was a close Mexican place, Taco Mamacita, until we visited and I left underwhelmed. We were seated promptly at a relatively clean table. At least three servers came to tell us our server would be with us shortly. We waited about five minutes for water, which was fine. If you're underage, I'd give you a 99% chance of getting a drink here (I say this half sarcastically and half jabbing at the GM to educate his servers about misdemeanors and fines). I ordered a sangria and my date ordered a margarita. I had already pulled out my ID and she said, "I'm only checking this because you have it out." And then she turned to my date, "Guess I should see yours too, if you want." I kept my eyes peeled as others were seated after us and not a single person was carded, and most looked 14 (probably 21, but definitely not 40). The sangria had no punch, and tasted pretty watery. It was only three dollars though. The chips were nice and crispy and the mango salsa was ok. If I ever go back, I'll probably stick to the regular tomato. The tortilla soup was refreshing and they pour the broth into the bowl at the table; great because you can see the portion sizes of the fillings, which were good, and the tortilla strips were in a container on the side, so they stayed crispy. The tacos were larger than I expected, but again, underwhelming. The California Club had good flavor the first few bites and I could pick it up and put the whole circumference in my mouth. The Taco Royale is much bigger though and for lack of creativity, I cut it up. We skipped dessert. My bill for a $3.00 sangria, soup, chips, and two tacos with side was $20.00. I'm not really sure how to improve food; I just eat it. If a friend said a crowd was going, I'd probably go back and eat chips, but I don't see myself getting the urge to return anytime soon.
label: NEG

text: Dee. Lish. Us. We were literally wandering the neigborhood, trying to figure out where to eat. We happened upon Warsaw Cafe, which we'd noticed before but never visited. It was the perfect choice. We started with a couple of Okocim Porters, a Polish beer with a sweet flavor. I'd enjoyed the lager at other places, and the porter did not disappoint. We each had soup. The borscht, served hot, was the only restaurant borscht to compare to that of my Polish grandmother's. The chilled berry soup, with orange crushed peanuts, was divine. Next we shared a few sausage and kraut pierogies. They were good, but not the best pierogies ever. But the entrees were excellent. The beef stroganoff was served with egg noodles and a bit of asparagus. The beef was flavorful and tender. The sauce was great. The other entree, eggplant cakes, was served with a creamy dill sauce. It too was incredible. The atmosphere at Warsaw Cafe is casual and homey. There are Eastern European travel posters on the wall. The room is small and warm. There was Billie Holiday playing. Simply wonderful.
label: POS

text: Why don't we have a Target? I thought K-Mart was going out of business. Well not this one, this miserable son of a bitch refuses to die. They had the audacity to try to update it. It reminds me of Jack Palance its old, tired, and smells funny, but it ain't going know where. I wish a shiny new Target would come along and stab this relic of a store through the heart with its superior retail sword. I have experienced on no less than 5 occasions of a product being labeled as on sale only to be charged full price at the counter. Then I have to stop the line to back to the aisle and grab the sign to show it to the cashier. Once I bought a beach chair here, well my wife saw the dopeness of said chair and wanted to copy me. I return to the store the next day (happened to be 80 degrees and sunny) and those SOB's raised the price of the chair $10. I was pissed yo.

text: Nothing makes me happier than being able to add an extra star on Chuck's Alibi. I like this place so much, that despite my moving about 30 minutes away I decided half way through my meal that I'll be making the trip back often! So with a bit of mental preparation we stopped by Saturday night and were pleasantly surprised to find EVERY ONE of our previous issues had been addressed! We arrived toward the end of what I would call dinner hours (they serve late into the evening though) and the ambiance was very pleasant. Frank Sinatra serenaded us at a ear friendly volume as we went to town on our Dungenous crabs. Late in our meal the clock did click passed 9 and the music got a tad louder and went to typical bar music, but still no where near the ear splitting level of before. In fact, I didn't see the guy that was running things on our last visit, and this time the manager in charge (an obvious seasoned veteran of the service industry, and an obvious positive influence on the business) made a point to go around to all the tables to check on things. The temperature problems seemed to be worked out too. If you haven't been, do yourself a favor and give them a try. text: It's slim pickings at this Value Village location. Considering most items are used and not in pristine condition, some of them are overpriced. I saw toys in their original packaging that are about the same prices as normal retail stores. Isn't the point of going to Value Village to get a bargain deal on stuff, i.e. to get things for cheaper? They have lots of selection, but it's not worth browsing through for long. text: For post number ONE HUNDRED I would like to give my recommendation to the El Rancho Drive in! The last time I went to the drive in was when I was very young, and my parents would make up a bed for me in the back seat of the car so that I could sleep while they watched a movie. Now that I'm dealing with my own antsy toddler, I thought I'd give this a try. HOW MUCH FUN IS THE DRIVE IN?! SO much fun! Okay, you certainly give up a lot in the way of picture and sound quality--no THX at the drive in--but what you gain is the convenience of being able to hang out in your own car with your own food! Just kick back in your pajamas if you want to! The El Rancho is really well-maintained and clean, and I was quite impressed with the whole experience. I can't wait to go back! text: Let me start by saying dinner is a three hour affair. Do not try to cut it short, you are only punishing yourself. I have been to most of the great steak houses in the country and this is #1. I have had steaks as good (not better) but this is also about the experience, service and ambiance. Steaks are dry-aged, cut to order and cooked to perfection over charcoal. Your waiter will ask if you want a tour of the kitchen and wine cellar, the correct answer is "yes" You will not see the entire wine cellar but you will see about 90,000 bottles (less than 20% of the total) and the kitchen is amazing. The wine list is the largest in the world and is overwhelming. The first time in my life I have been intimidated by a wine list. Fortunately, they have three very qualified sommeliers on staff who love to help. I think the wine prices are a good value. About an hour and a half into your dinner, you will be asked if you would like to make reservations for dessert. There is only one correct answer.

text: I always tire of people who mention Roselena's and expensive in the same sentence. They're missing one important facet - the scrumpdiddilyumptiousness of it all. Don't let the Victorian look or the fact that there's nothing resembling spaghetti and meatballs on the menu. This one's an Italian restaurant in a league of it's own, best gone down on when you have time to spare. The pacing here is old world, while the food is so of the new. Need I say more than Mocha Java encrusted pork chops. And as for dessert, the best on East P'unk. Trust me - the Passyunk Smore, mon ami!
