text: I love Jasmine! Being a Medford native, I have been going there for years with both my friends and family. My fondest memory of Jasmine is when my two best friends and I went for dinner, and my one friend had raved about how good the cold sesame noodles were. To his dismay when he ordered them they said they could not make them because he was the only one who ordered them that night (I guess they make them in big batches only) and because of the difficulty or something, I don't know. Well anyway he was really disappointed and hard pressed to pick another dish, so when they came back to take our order the owner came out with our waiter and informed my friend that they would be making the noodles special for him. He was so happy, let me tell you. And as always, they were delicious. So in summary, really good Chinese food, super friendly owner and wait staff, very accommodating and attentive. Even their non-Chinese dishes are delicious. I recommend the Vietnamese Hot and Sour Soup and the Vietnamese Style Vermicelli if you're in the mood for something different. Yummy!
label: POS

text: It is an ok sandwich/salad shop which specializes in various kinds of cheese. Nothing to rant or rave about in my opinion. Ambiance: I didn't really care for the outdoor seating by the front door. Something was missing - at least for me. I would much rather go to Cafe Rani or Martinique Bistro for alfresco dining. Enough already about the ambiance... Food: Nothing special. I am not a cheese gourmet though. I had the Ploughman's lunch which included a small side salad along with a piece of English pork pie, four slices of various cheeses, a couple of wedges of multigrain bread and some chutney spread. The best part of the lunch was the chutney spread on the bread with some parmesan cheese. My wife had a ham & brie sandwich on a baguette with chips on the side. She didn't care for hers either. In my opinion there are lots of better choices - even within walking distance of the Cheese Co. Crepe Nanou, Upperline, and Creole Creamery to name a few. Overall 2 1/2 stars.
label: NEG

text: When I'm feeling like eating something greasy, or I need to reassure myself that I'm a MAN with capital letters, I head over to Big Ed's. I sit down, order myself a beer and a BusterBurger. Then, I slowly but carefully consume a big piece of meat with cheese, ham, eggs, lettuce, onions, pickles and bell peppers between two pieces of bread. When the plate is gone, I look in the mirror and see a smile, and the extra cholesterol-induced sparkle in my eyes, and all is well in the world. The rest of their food is just as awesome, but I'm a believer in measuring places by their most "potent" dish, and this is definitely a contender.
label: POS

text: The staff was very courteous, the room was clean and well kept. There is free wi-fi and a mini fridge. The inn is located right off of the freeway and is within 5 mins of a Vons.
label: POS

text: Great BBQ! The line was outrageous when we stopped by for lunch but the wait was well worth it. I got the ribs and they were soooo tender and delicious. It's been a while since I've had BBQ that good. They were smoked to perfection. For sides, I got the sweet potato fries which where good and the green beans. Let me tell you, you got to try the green beans! They are seasoned to perfection and not over cooked. Eating at Pappy's was definitely one of the highlights of my trip to St. Louis.
label: POS

text: OK, let me qualify the previous reviewer by quoting her: "In fact, I hated pizza for a long, long time." Only a communist could HATE pizza...C'Mon! How can she possibly be reviewing a Pizza joint???Anyhow, this is quite possibly some of the worst pizza in the area. I've had worse, but Grotto's (rhymes with Grosso's) really ranks up their with some worse of the worse. And I know MANY in Delaware who would agree with me. I am somewhat of a pizza snob and believe that good pizza must...MUST be cooked in a stone oven. Grotto uses a conveyor belt in all of their operations. They certainly had much better pizza back in the 1970's when they were a 1 shack operation on the boardwalk in Rehoboth Beach, but as soon as they institutionalized and corporatized and started dumping new sites on every corner in the state, quality went right down the tubes. If your out for pizza in Delaware, then save your money, you'll really need it if you eat here cuz they are WAY over-priced. Take your business to any of the mom and pop pizza joints around the area and make sure you check for the classic stone oven (it's stainless steel and has the door that pulls down in the front), or better yet, a wood fired oven.
label: NEG

text: Tiny greasy ribs. Staff seemed more involved with playing grab ass behind the counter than they did serving and seating. This place is always barren. Oh, also don't buy the boneless wings as an appetizer...it was like eating little pieces of cat and dog. Salad was good and huge. I was able to split it with my wife. If you had to choose between this place and a vasectomy, go with the vasectomy. You can reverse a vasectomy.
label: NEG

text: Holy crud bad service! I checked out the menu online and found something I really wanted to try. We went and it was no longer on the menu. I asked the server if they could still make it (they had all the ingredients from other dishes and just had to sub out the meat on one torta) and she said absolutely no substitutions. I asked why and she said because the cook doesn't speak english, she can't communicate with him and was very rude to us for assuming we could change things up. So I can't get a meal how I want it here? I ended up with a pretty bad burrito and feeling a bit sick because the server couldn't pass on "no queso" (NOT the chefs fault at all, the server was incompetent). Ridiculous. The chips were ultra salty and stale and salsa was okay at best (pretty much what I had for lunch, thanks).
label: NEG

text: Some of Tucson's very tastiest pizza, but wow the calories. Swimming in cheese and a good dose of grease. Service is renowned for being extremely slow. Great selection of beers. The inside seating is dirty and burned out. Lots of off-the-street patio seating, which is surprisingly lacking in Tucson. Beware the parking -- it doesn't fit the web site's categories. During the day, you either park at expensive meters or hike a long ways away from unpermitted residential street parking. At night, you can park for free in the University of Arizona's permitted parking lot, same location as the meters. Park illegally at your own risk -- they patrol like crazy.
label: POS

text: I missed their Monkey Knife Fight on tap, so I opted for the Grog; a very good session beer, a bit malty and smooth. My wife & I split the muffaletta sandwich..glad we did as the portion was massive. Although not quite what I remember other muffalettas to be, Nodding Head's was tasty nonetheless. The roll that it was served on was interesting, kind of like a bun made of pizza dough, soft and chewy with a bit of crunch on the crust. I loved the pesto and cured meat as well. Fries were 'meh' but served with a spicy cajun mayo...nice touch.
label: POS

text: Their carwash is fine, but overpriced, however the real disappointment came when we took our Subaru in for detailing. As I paid, I looked the man in the eye and said, "Does this mean that the chocolate milkshake goo that's stuck to the plastic around the seatbelt buckle will be gone?" and he said "of course!" The next day, we started a road trip to Boston and lo and behold, there was the milkshake residue on the white plastic. It had been wiped and was about half gone, but it was still there. That's just representative of our $130 experience. I will go elsewhere next time.
label: NEG

text: I used to live right next door, and lived in the same complex with the owner. and even though I moved on to better Pizza Joints at The Italian Market I really miss being so close to this place. Peter and his crew always offered top of the line service with a smile. The Pizza is better then most that I've had, and always comes with fresh ingredients. they make a lot of pies throughout the day so you'll get it fresh from the oven on most occasions too. they also make sandwiches, fries, and the usual pizza joint staples. but trust me go with the pizza even if your not big on pizza. it should give you a higher opinion of it. Cravings is also open late night on Fridays and Saturdays. So I couldn't think of a better place to satisfy that hunger craving your bound to have after a few beers.
label: POS

text: I went in here after coming over for some business in the area. It was around 2:30-3pm when I got in and I was hungry. I ended up getting the shawarma sandwich. It came out fairly quickly. The vegetables in the sandwich were pretty good and tasted like they were fairly fresh(They had that nice crunch you get with freshly prepared vegetables). The shawarma meat was plentiful, but it was bland and pretty overcooked. Gonna have to find another place to get some good Middle Eastern food around here. This isn't going to cut the mustard.
label: NEG

text: Purchased 3 premium suits from this location and they all had to be ordered and I was told they would take a month. A month came and went with no contact from the retailer, I called in and they said it would take a week longer. I began to receive small postcard like mail from Jos A Bank and it informed me that individual parts of my order were on back order and that they would be automatically canceled if I did not mail a 'keep order' request. I had to call in for each one of the four postcards in order to prevent my order from being auto-canceled. Another month rolls by and the suits are not in. I finally got a call that said that 2 of the jackets and 2 of the pants were in (not 2 full suits) and that the final pieces should be in soon. Two and half months after my original order, I was able to come in and try on the suit and get fitted. Turned out that none of my original purchase included the tailoring (which I wasn't told) even though the pants were not tailored at all (size 38 pant was about 60 in long) and did not have a finished end. So a $200 pair of pants HAD to have another $50 of tailoring. Paid another $220 to get all three pairs of pants finished and this took another 2 weeks. Suits seem good quality but no where near the price tag of $650 each and $200 per pair of pants and the high price luxury service failed to deliver again and again. No apologies were made for the missed deadlines and I have already attended an event that I purchased the suits for. The staff was simply happy to take my money on two occasions and make no amends for very poor service.
label: NEG

text: I would have given the purveyor of these little pockets of Polish potato paradise a higher rating, but consistency has become an issue. As a neighbor of the Kitchen you can imagine the number of times laziness has pulled me down the block to score some pierogie action, and once they started offering sandwiches that amount just multiplied (which is how I began to notice the discrepancies). Come here and order just pierogies and you will always be happy (they deserve five stars), but ordering the stacker may leave you feeling very disappointed; many a sandwich has been served to me with super dry/ uber charred meat, and the extra grease only makes it worse. Still, I am much more happy living next to some Polaski eating than I ever was with the ice cream shop that dwelt there before it. p.s.- very limited drink selection
label: POS

text: If you are in the New Orleans are it is a must to visit the Napoleon House. Get off of Bourbon St. and make your way to this little gem in the French Quarter. Its a tad bit off the beaten path but well worth to give it a try. The bartenders all are funny and have a good sense of humor and if you are a history buff this is the place to go. Originally built to house Napoleon Bonaparte, this is now a converted bar and cafe. The inside is a blast from the past with its decor and all original interior. Definitely worth a visit if you make it to the New Orleans area. When I was there I didn't get a chance to try the food (only spirits) but will definitely the next time I am down there.
label: POS

text: When it first opened it was pretty tasty and great and I was working in the neighborhood. However, be careful. Order stuff they have to cook and prepare for you for a few extra bucks. Do not order from the already prepared food! I have gotten sick of it and so have friends! Also just run down to the old nelsons for a drink while they cook up your food, they have a more extensive drink selection and it can get cramped/tight in there while you wait!
label: NEG

text: I never thought I would be saying this. But here it goes. The last two visits to the hut were terrible! They really need to hire some help. The service is so bad. There is an older waiter who is very nice but also a very bad waiter. The man juts can't multi task! I'm sorry, but you can't wait tables without that ability! So anyways, back to my last visit. My friend and I walked in craving curry puffs, the best thai appetizer ever!! We sat down and ordered them and he ran away before we could order drinks. Yeah, we waited about 15 minutes before we could track his slow ass down and get some thai tea. about 10 minutes later he brings us gross, overly sweetened tea and told us he was sorry, but o curry puffs today! We walked out. I won't be returning. =[
label: NEG

text: This is the Hot spot in town? wow. I wasn't expecting much, but i guess I should have expected nothing. In its defense, The DJ was spinning good music, current and older hip hop. Thats a star. Drinks were cheap ($3/ bottle). Another star. I ordered couple buttery nipple shots. YUCK! all curled and sour. I have had many of these and these were bad. So i told the lady that the milk might have been bad, She said it was frozen, gave me 2 more on the house. These were even worse. I threw them out. I know the difference between frozen and rancid. This milk's gone bad! Dance floor.. open. no one was dancing so the DJ came out of his dj booth area and went MIA a lot. maybe this place used to be good. Or is good in the summer time? It has potential, tsk tsk.
label: NEG

text: Food was pretty good here. Particularly liked the complimentary salsa, better than most places. Service was shiesty! At first it wasn't even that bad. But about halfway through the meal our waitress disappeared. She'd occasionally re-appear, but never by our table. We needed two tortillas and some re-fills. My brother ultimately walked up to the counter and politely asked. About twenty minutes later the other waitress came by and helped us out. She took off one of the meals of the tab, which was sweet. I agree with other posters that one stop should be enough.
label: NEG

text: This was my third visit here, because the previous two were so good and memorable. This time was a let down. The calamari appetizer was too salty and the combination of different flavors and textures was weird; it just didn't work. The skate wing with crab cake was well done. The surf and turf, though, was the dish that didn't work out. There was a BIG piece of beef brisket which was just slightly overcooked, but it needed a sauce; without which made it boring. It was served over hominy with lobster, which was very good, but an odd contrast with the lump of brisket sitting on top. All of it accompanied by a slaw. Fusion cooking alive and well! The hostess was great, but the server all but disappeared after we expressed reservations about the calamari appetizer. He barely swung by to drop off the check just moments after we asked for.
label: NEG

text: If you've never had Indian food before, then eating here might not be a problem. It's pretty bad if you know what the food should taste like. The only thing I like (and enjoyed quite a bit actually) are the samosas. The rest is pretty bland. There are ways to compromise to make the food cheaper, but it could at least be a bit better than this. Nonetheless, it's in IV and gets a lot of customers whose state of inebriation doesn't allow them to care what their food tastes like anyway. I wish there were somewhere else to get boba in town. Their boba drinks could be much better too (things with powder get gritty and it might be best to just go with a plain green tea), but I'll give them credit for having an expansive menu. You get a bit less than what you pay for.
label: NEG

text: The heart and soul that Rita's never had. ATTN TEENAGERS ON A DATE: The gazebo to the right of the back of the building is an absolutely fantastic date spot. Many a first kiss and first relationship breakup have been had there. Use it wisely, for it is sacred ground.
label: POS

text: Ok, ok, 700 club. The original hipster destination. I can't see how a person can't like this place. It probably has something that appeals to everyone. If you like good beer, they got it. If you like cheap beer, they got it. If you like dancing, they got it. If you like waiting in lines for the bathroom, they got it. If you like places without covers, they don't have one. Ok so first floor is a bar. They have a nice big chalkboard with a ton of beers listed. They don't have all of them in stock all of the time, but the hit rate is pretty good. I've enjoyed a couple pints and conversation there a few times. Nice bartenders and the price isn't bad for the good stuff. Second floor is a trip. Imagine if your grandmother had a really old living room with really old and busted furniture, crazy wallpaper, a dj above a toilet (who knows why they left the toilet) and a cash bar in the back. In the summer, it gets toasty but the music keeps going. The tracks change up all night and people seem to let loose there. Good times. The only real issue is catching a cab on 2nd & Fairmount when you're all done. It can a little bit of a hassle. Still, you gotta love good beer and good prices in a club type atmosphere without the club type bs. I suppose you could always ride your bike...
label: POS

text: I only go to this Cosi as an absolute last resort for lunch or coffee. The reasons? 1. It's totally overpriced given the quality of the food 2. Service swings dramatically from good to horrible 3. They changed the recipe for the pizza bread, so now it's practically cracker thin, and the pizza sauce just makes it like a wet thin cracker (gross) 4. Salad greens are not always fresh 5. It's always packed with tourists (and they really bog things down for the lunch rush sometimes) If I absolutely need something to eat in a hurry, it is convenient, especially since they take credit/debit cards. But with a new Subway just an extra two minute walk down 4th Street, I find myself rarely going inside Cosi anymore.
label: NEG

text: A recent trip back to Tucson to see the friends I miss most, landed me at the Guadalajara Grill. When I lived in Tucson I lived around the corner from it's original location and I am kicking myself for never trying it before. The table side salsa is a nice touch. While most people love it because they can spice it up, I loved it because I could get the perfect medium blend heavier on the garlic. My friend prompted me to order the bandera margarita and seriously I could of drank 10 more. It is a tri colored frozen margarita with lime, strawberry, and melon and it was delicious. Sticking to my bandera theme I ordered the enchiladas banderas and was not disappointed. The tortillas really are excellent and the food was fresh and prompt to our tables. the atmosphere makes you feel like you are someplace else and there really is an experience to be had here.
label: POS

text: Decided to get some sushi take out today. I was REAALLLYYY looking forward to the sushi and trying it from a sushi place I had never been to before. Service was wonderful, restaurant was clean. The only good things :-( . . . I was there at 12:30 to pick up my sushi (ell roll, salmon roll and spicy tuna roll). There was 2 people at the sushi bar and that was it. = ouch! The sushi rolls were SO small (how small you ask?), they were the circumference of a nickle AND they all tasted the same.
label: NEG

text: I'd been fishing all day and when it was finally 12:32am, I just needed food. My body needed it all; proteins, fats, and carbohydrates. For the carbs, I wanted beer. My friends were at a bar nearby that doesn't really serve food, so I needed to find an option for the fats and protein. Fried chicken. Grabbed a 3 piece box consisting of a wing, thigh, and breast from Lincoln just a few blocks away. I'm here to tell you that I'm sorry that I did. I live near a CFC (Crown) and they serve a good bird. I thought all of these loosely similar but independently-owned chicken joints had a similar recipe, or even quality control. Boy was I wrong. When I got to the bar and slugged two city specials, I was ready to eat. I wish I had stopped by a Wawa on the way back from fishing. The seasoning, or lack-there-of, was paltry. The breast piece had to have been sitting under a lamp for at least 8 hours. My jaws still kind of hurt from chewing and gnawing. Of course I ate it all, I was hungry. But the fact that I was so hungry and kinda drunk and am still complaining just tells you how bad the chicken was. This pretty much dispels my previous thought that the eerily similar red-and-white-with-sometimes-KFC-infringement-named fried chicken slingers had a cohesive recipe and quality. They don't.
label: NEG

text: For a Trader Joe's (which are usually "knock your socks off" good, this one isn't all too great. My biggest complaint is the quality of produce. I bought fruit once that was completely molded over by the next day. Generally, the produce does not last longer than three days. And for someone that eats a great deal of produce and lives in a city without a car, this is a major issue. Another problem is that it is generally extremely crowded at all hours of the day. The staff does a great job diffusing the circumstances with witty banter over the loud speaker though. For a big fan of Trader Joe's, this store is a let down.
label: NEG

text: I haven't been to the shop, my experience is with a dress inquiry via email. I emailed the store to see if they carried a sample of a Maggie Sottero gown I found online because the designer's website listed them as a local retailer. On the plus side, they did get back to me relatively quickly (within a few days). On the negative side, all the email said was "We do not have a sample of this dress." They didn't offer to help me find another in the line, they didn't offer to borrow one from another store so I could try it on. They didn't explain or appologize and they didn't seem too interested in my business. I'll keep looking. Bridals by Sandra in Nazareth (a little ways away...) offered me all kinds of help and I've had good experiences with them before for bridesmaid's dresses. I'm not going to waste my time with Coronet, I'd rather drive to Nazareth to get quality customer service!
label: NEG

text: Tortillas were great and the service was friendly but why did it take 20 mins for 2 tacos? The pork tasted very familiar with the hint of cloves. Does this ring any bells? Alittle like Chipolte i would go back for the tortillas alone
label: NEG

text: I was debating whether I should give two or three stars, but I've decided on two just because I was so disappointed with my experience this time & want others to beware. The last time I was in New Orleans, over a year ago, we went to Bennachin and the food was AMAZING. It was my first time trying African food of this variety, and I was very impressed. The food was delicious, and although it took quite a while to get to us, it was definitely worth the wait. This time I had the opposite experience. The food arrived quickly, but there was nothing good about it. I ordered the okra and beef stew with rice. It was over cooked and mushy and had very little flavor. The beef had clearly been prepared separately and did not have any of the tenderness it had had the previous time when it had obviously simmered in the broth of the stew for hours. There was also a large amount of rock salt all over my food, which made for crunchy, salty unpleasantness. The two other people I was dining with shared a vegetarian curry, which was also tasteless. They said that the store-bought roll was the best part of the meal. Sad.
label: NEG

text: This place struggles with its dual identity as a dive bar and venue in a way that the Khyber juggles the two seemlessly. This is probably due to the fact that the locals at Mill Creek are crotchety old drunk dudes and the locals at the Khyber are microbrew/Highlife swilling hipster kids. So whereas at the Khyber there is no real tension between the venue-goers and the drinkers, at the Mill Creek it can go down gangster style. Not that I've ever seen this happen, but it could. This conflict of interests is also evident in the way they book their gigs. Whoever does the booking has this annoying tendency to put Grateful Dead coverbands with indie-kid bands and it just does not jive. Add that to the fact that it is infested with Penn Students the way in which a two-star hostel becomes infested with scabies, and you have it. Two stars. Also- nothing stunning on draft. The Jameson is reasonably priced for the area but it's not keeping me coming back for more.
label: NEG

text: I don't like talking crap about any place, but I had a horrible experience... My B.F and I went here to have Sushi and celebrate the start of our new life in STL. I don't remember what day it was, but I believe it was a weekday cuz the place was empty. The hostess sat us on 2 seaters table on the very end of 2nd Fl. Sushi was WAAAY overpriced for what we get and techno music was so loud , but it was our happy day, so we were ok until..... Then, the hostess sat 2 college gals RIGHT NEXT TO US. HELLOWWW?! The place is EMPTY!!!! Why don't you at least skip one table b/w us and them?! Of course these too girls are like "Oh my GOD, I totally love this place oh, you should totally try this roll! Tthis is totally miso and totally blah blah blah blah". They were even louder than the techno music. STL has so many great places with courtesy. You can not only try to be hip and cool without any efforrt. The waiter was a nice guy, but the hostess was an idiot. I was just so disappointed. We'll never go back to this place.
label: NEG

text: Among the best American Italian restaurants I've been to. We had bruschetta, chopped salad, and spaghetti with meatballs. Huge portions and we (=2) almost finished it all, even though we were full after two-thirds. We'll be back! Indeed, we were back, and went for the same (minus bruschetta) with the same result: though this time I took one third of the pasta home for dinner two days later. :-)
label: POS

text: I have not had such a horrible experience at a bar in a LONG time! I went with my boyfriend and 6 others - and I think none of us will return. You must order your food from a waitress, but drinks from the bartender - so I was forced to swipe my card and tip twice. My dinner was less than par, and the chips that accompanied the wrap were def scraps from the bottom of the bag - about 1/4 cup of crumbs. I ordered a diet coke - taking a night off from the beer - and it was never refilled. My boyfriend had to wait about 10 min to be offered a new pint each time his glass was empty. The service wasn't exactly friendly service either. There was a live band, which, once they started playing were too screachingly loud that we could no longer continue our conversation. I vow never to return here again!!
label: NEG

text: Gambino came out on an "emergency" call ($250) and told me I needed $7,600 worth of work. They did nothing on the emergency call except write up the $7,600 work order. They came out the next business day and rippled up a 50 foot section of my driveway and left the asphalt for me to clean-up. They replace my meter box with a used box which looks like something they had laying around their shop (weather, dented and dirty). The kicker is when I called a asphalt contractor to repair the driveway, I was told that Gambino shouldn't have backfilled the trench with the dirt that was removed, but rather clean stone, and I would be wasting my money to repair the driveway unless all the backfill was removed, by hand, and replaced with packed clean stone. When I called Gambino to discuss, I was up on hold for 30 minutes and then my call was terminated. When looking for an electrician, look past Gambino.
label: NEG

text: Good place to see local music and grab a drink. If you want extremely high quality music, go to Snug Harbor. If you want extremely quality drinks, go to DBA. If you want good drinks and decent music, La Maison is totally adequate. There are no less than three stages at this place. You can watch music on the two downstairs stages for no charge (generally). There is an upstairs stage that charges a cover independent from the main door. So beware. I'm not sure what possessed me to order one of their "special" drinks - rum punch. Basically something mixed up in a huge jug. Juice and grain alcohol. It didn't even begin to get me drunk! Rip off! Stick to beer or drinks mixed in front of you and you'll be fine. Support local music!!
label: POS

text: I make it a point to try and never buy produce at the grocery store unless I am feeling extremely lazy or I don't have another option. Sue's is one of the few produce markets I often frequent. I would agree with the other posts, sue's is not always the cheapest but it's fresh and if you play your cards right you can get some really good deals. I usually stick with certain veggies (almost never fruits because I know I can get them cheaper other places) but sometimes I delve into the fridges of local cheese and yogurt. The quality of product they sell here is great and their produce lasts ridiculously long periods of time. I visit Sue's on an almost weekly basis at times and their produce is a lot better than some of the other places in the area. I can usually leave here with two huge bags of fresh veggies and only spend around 12 dollars. If you buy all your produce at trader joes, or whole foods make a better choice and try out sues. Be sure to bring cash though as they do not take cards.
label: POS

text: Went here a couple weeks ago and really enjoyed it. The chili cheese fries are unbelievable. Seriously - try it. The pretzels are fantastic too - big hunks of pretzel with beer cheese soup and some kind of peppercorn ranch. I think I had a burger for my meal which shows that the entree wasn't as memorable as the appetizers. The dirty martini I ordered wasn't bad either. Decent for a lower end place. Love that it's smoke free. Under 21 crowd allowed until 9pm. Also, we had a decent size group and there was no grumping about splitting the bill.
label: POS

text: Not a good place. Room had no smoke detector, most of the outlets did not work, toilet was not bolted down. When we asked for money back was charged anyway even tho we were there less than 30 minutes
label: NEG

text: Mental Note....if you name a restaurant after a dish you prepare....prepare it *#&@ing delicious. The prime rib was fatty and lacked flavor. The other dishes we ordered were mediocre. The only redeeming value was the interesting atmosphere. Has a cool old style "supper club" feel. Definitely dressy (guys bring your suit jacket) with a more conservative and older crowd. If you have a Tommy gun, you'll feel right at home here.
label: NEG

text: No, no, and no....I love O charleys rolls, but nothing could get me to come back to this establishment. First time wonderful, waiters were great, food was lovely. After that it all went down hill. 2nd trip the rolls they were making them so fast they had not given them proper time to rise, they were flat, doughy, and gross. 3rd time, my lettuce in my salad was rotten, and there was a hair in my appetizer. I will not be back under any circumstances.
label: NEG

text: One of the best thing about Freebirds is they are open 24 hours. It doesn't hurt that they are located in IV and right next to the UCSB campus. They also have an open salsa bar and free fountain drink refills. Other than the qualities listed above, there is really nothing else going on for Freebirds. I used to LOOOOVE this place... especially after a night of drinking and partying. However, over the years, I seen a steady decline in the quality of the food and service. text: Sushi is an art! That means: A sushi chef should know how to craft his art , with the right ingredients and portions, and display with pride. Mochi is a very basic Asian -Vietnamese restaurant, which serves sushi, it's not a Japanese restaurant. With all do respect , calling Mochi a Japanese restaurant is a grave insult! There is nothing Japanese about the menu, it's very Americanized with the typical -fusion-meals like the all mighty Teriyaki bowls and Tempuras. We ordered 4 different rolls only to be disappointed with the content and portions for the price we paid. The taste- AHI was nowhere to be found, it was in such small portions that made me almost send it back, but I didn't. Another one of my favorite rolls= SPICY AHI, which was nowhere near the pepper, not enough fish, not enough flavor, I had to reluctantly ask for Sriracha on the side, even with the big lump of wasabi! The Wasabi was very MILD! Hamachi Kama, which is usually succulent and prized was brushed with teriyaki sauce, what a disgrace! Tempura roll- tiny shrimps didn't qualify for the roll itself. Miso soup tasted like the ones I buy in store, packeted. Nigiri- very SMALL and dry. We ordered one of the special rolls which had minute amount of nori and rice, and even smaller amount of ingredients! Anyhow, not so surprisingly, they have a Vietnamese menu as well. Maybe , they should just stick to calling MOCHI a VIETNAMESE restaurant and not a Japanese one!!! Although I shouldn't expect a lot from Midwestern sushi places , I was still a little disappointed with the Mochi sushi makers! They are doing the sushi experience Injustice! THE SERVICE: was slow, and kind of confusing. The server didn't seem to understand the menu ... maybe she was new, or ? I know nothing beats the real -deal in Hawaii , where Japanese food is #1.

text: I'm a sucker for nostalgia. You know, tiny whispers of the things that used to be, trying hard to cast a glow on the dizzying sheen of modernization. text: Carry-out (order at the counter) or sit-down-and-order-from-the-menu (waiter will take your order). This is _not_ a cookie-cutter strip-mall Chinese place. text: I really can't believe this place hasn't been reviewed yet, as it seems to be something of Tampa institution... though not necessarily one that's well-loved by everyone. Having been to the Press Box a few times now with my coworker, I decided it was time we tried the restaurant NEXT to it, that sometimes seemed bustling & others empty. Last Friday Matt & I ventured in & it was pretty full, but we were promptly seated -- at a window no less! (Granted, the window didn't look out onto anything but the parking lot & the back of the Press Box, but sunlight is always nice.) We started with a draft beer (him) & glass of sangria (me), & while the waiter checked our IDs Matt poked fun at me for being younger than him ("Are you even 21?!"). The sangria was fine, not great, not bad, just fine. Being an oyster lover, I could hardly pass up a half-dozen steamed oysters on the half-shell to start, & decided on the lunch menu's seafood po'boy, while Matt had the grouper sandwich. The oysters came out pretty quickly with some melted butter to dip them in and a lemon to squeeze over them, & were warm & creamy & just delectable. I'm still searching for a place that *grills* them on the half-shell like they did in Hiroshima, though... but as it seems it's either raw or fried everywhere you go, I was happy for the compromise with the steaming. Our food came out about 10 minutes later. My sandwich was on a long roll with just the fried bits of fish, shrimp, & clams on it; no lettuce or tomato or slaw (though there was cole slaw on the side, so I heaped that on), & a side of fries. There was some kind of sauce on the side that was AWESOME; it was sort of a BBQ mayo with some cayenne in it, maybe? In any case I LOVED it, & since I couldn't finish my food I asked the waiter for extra sauce to take home with the rest of it. Matt said his grouper sandwich was pretty good; for $10 he wondered whether it was really grouper, but he said it tasted like grouper, so do with that what you will. We split tabs & I had the oysters put on mine (which Matt argued about, but I let him pay both our tips) & my bill came to $18. Not bad for a Friday lunch with sangria & oysters, I say!

text: I'd file this review under Live and Learn. I took my car here a few years back because it needed some major work (yet was new enough to just be out of factory warranty) and I knew a mechanic whom I trusted and who had worked on the car before had just started working here. You would think the owners would be thrilled to have a new customer thanks to their new mechanic's reputation, but when I asked for him to work on the car, they came across as offended, and bordering on hostile. They said anyone there could do as good of a job as the person I requested and I didn't understand the hostility. I realize now maybe they thought they could get more money out of me if I was more "in the dark" about things. Basically what ended up happening was that the quote I got was about $500 over the cost of the part and I had to specifically request several after-market parts and off brand to save myself money. My old shop did this without asking as a general business practice in their quotes. If there was a reason to have a branded or new part, then fair enough. But not in this case. I'm not sure how they justified the huge mark up on the parts, but when I questioned them, it was just a bunch of hemming and hawing and then all of a sudden, their computer "crashed" and they had to get back to me....which they never did, but miraculously gave me a new quote for more reasonable prices. I did have the work done there and it was done perfectly, but again, this was because there was someone there who knew what they were doing. In addition to the questionable mark ups, they immediately added my home address to their mailer list, and I would get a ton of discount mailers every month. To me, this is a red flag. I don't want a discount, I want a fair price to begin with. The best places don't offer discounts, they just charge a reasonable price. My other gripe is that several times during this work, I was told my car was ready to pick up (the work was done in several intervals so my car was given back to me a couple of times) and when I got there, the car was NOT ready, it was being washed or it needed to be moved from behind several other cars. I waited about 30 minutes each time. I mean, it's great if they want to wash your car, but I'd rather have a car on time than a clean car a half hour late. This place was just a mess.

text: We strolled up to Pizzicato looking for a place to just relax, have a drink, and get something small. It was fairly slow at the time, so we were a bit surprised by how slow our server was. I'm not normally a fruity drink kinda gal, more the craft beer type with an occasional interest in red wines, but this relaxing afternoon called for something special. I can't say how it compared to other like drinks, but it was far too sweet for me. Liquor was definitely present, but for as small as the drink, was the $10 price was a shocker. Since our server was nowhere to be found, we had to ask another employee for some olive oil. My husband got the spicy filet and langoustine salad and loved it, though he switched up the dressing, choosing citrus vinaigrette instead of the menu-listed soy vinaigrette. I got the mixed green salad minus the gorgonzola. Little did I know that the gorgonzola was the only thing that gave the salad flavor. The dressing, a roasted garlic vinaigrette, tasted like nothing more than oil. The menu-listed balsamic onions and roasted red peppers were flavorless. After my husband had nearly finished his salad and mine remained nearly untouched, waiting for the server to return, we finally stopped another server to ask for more dressing. When ours returned with more citrus dressing (assuming it was for my husband), I asked if they had a balsamic vinaigrette dressing, she said yes then brought out plain balsamic vinegar. Our table lacked a pepper grinder, so we grabbed the one off the nearest table (since our server never bothered to ask if we needed anything). It didn't actually grind the pepper, just spewing out near whole peppercorns. We borrowed one from the neighbor's table but had the same result. These were crappy pepper mills, the clear plastic kind that stores salt on top (and allowed whole peppercorns out when I attempted to get some salt) and they must be replaced. In spite of our experience, I actually might return. Their pastas look pretty good, and I wouldn't mind giving them a try. The bar stool were a bit awkward and uncomfortable. 2. It seems to be a place to be seen not for food. Very Ra like and Ra is about being seen not the sushi. 3. None seemed to be older than 25. No one was Japanese or Korean. The age was more of a concern than the ethnicity. It takes years to become a sushi chef and it showed in the quality of fish given out and the cutting skills of the chef. 3. The fish. Our chef accidentally gave us a spicy yellow tail instead of spicy salmon. He told us to keep the Yellow Tail. So we tried it and he broke one of the biggest rules in sushi -- Never serve fishy smelling sushi. This turned me off the rest of the night. Its morning now and my stomach seems to be OK but I doubt I'll be back any time soon. Two stars for being there with its specials but I don't go to sushi bars to be seen, I go there for the sushi and that is where On a Roll fails.

text: Kent: You know what the best part of this place is? Me: What? Kent: It's a steak house that's actually in a house! Me: I'm going to use that in my Yelp review. ---- It was last Wednesday night. Steak had been on my mind since my friend mentioned Citizen Kane's as being his favorite restaurant - mind you, I had watched this friend order fried rice and specifically asked for 'no vegetables.' It had to be good, right? A meat aficionado recommended it. The first thing you notice when you get out of your car is the smell... Delicious. Roasted. Meaty. Mmmm... My friend (Kent C.) and I were seated immediately (I had made a reservation about an hour before). Our waiter (Matt) was fabulous. I ordered the ribeye, which was touted as being a bit fattier (so the cut was more generous), but more flavorful than the house specialty (the NY strip) my companion ordered. As I ate my salad (with the Mayfair dressing - basically a richer, creamier caesar-style dressing) and Kent dipped bread in his beef and cheddar soup, we watched the happenings around us. Kent: Oh my god. Me: What? K: I think that's the ribeye... Me: Oh my god. When our steaks got to the table, the first thing Kent did was stick his face in it (well, close to it). It smelled amazing. Me: Your steak's so big. It's the size of a fetus. My creamed spinach was so creamy that it was more cream-colored than spinach-colored. My steak was... beyond words. Kent's steak was good, too. A little denser, if that's your thing. It was cooked just as asked (a true medium-rare). I smiled all through the next day just thinking about it. I'm smiling now. Yum... Can't wait to go back. Maybe this week...

text: As someone else mentioned, I wish we could rate half stars. I'd likely throw El Camino Real a 3 1/2, but given the option it leans towards that 4th star. Visited about 11 pm on a Thursday night, and surprisingly still found it well over half occupied. Sat down in a not altogether comfortable but perfectly suitable wooden chair, with the welcome sound of Johnny Cash bouncing around overhead. Not too loud to drown out my conversation but not quite quiet enough to speak at a normal level. Having read some other reviews I had no doubt where to start - the fried pickle chip appetizer. Yummy, spicy little bites. I wasn't sure if it was the breading on the pickles or the spicy chili mayo that was giving them such a kick. My friend, who is not quite a fan of things so spicy ate two and gave up. Trying them separately, I'd say it was the mayo that was really heating things up. Moving on to dinner, I chose the brisket sandwich while my friend went with the cactus & potato burritos. My brisket was quite tasty, with a subtle tanginess. The Texas toast it came on was about what you would expect, though I do have to admit it was nicely toasted. Not too soft, not too hard. The cactus & potato burritos were a nice change of pace over the normal options. Of course I snuck a bite (or two) and while I found cactus doesn't exactly have a ton of flavor, it all worked well together. As if I wasn't already in the midst of stuffing myself beyond comprehension I also ordered the mac n' cheese. Jalapeno breadcrumbs? How could I resist?! Overall, I'd say this last dish was the only one I'd skip the next time around. While interesting, it wasn't enough of a twist to warrant the high price. Not to mention, along with my friend's spanish rice, it was served rather lukewarm, which I found odd since it came in a small cast iron bucket which could have been preheated to retain the warmth. While not normally much of a desert fan, the S'mores Bread Pudding was too difficult to resist. This in itself is reason enough to drop by ECR. Warm, gooey chocolate bread pudding, delectable marshmallow ice cream, and a few graham crackers to chop up and mix in... Including a few local Kenzingers and a zesty watermelon margarita, we left about $80 lighter, the lingering sounds of David Bowie drifting out the door behind us. Would I go back? You bet, but not until I run through a few more recommendations from our fellow Yelpers.

text: I have never understood how this place stays open. It's always kinda busy, never packed, never dead. The service is terrible- slow, inattentive, and many times, rude. Last time I was there, we sat on the patio outside, our waitress berated us for the table we sat in, because it was in a place that was "hard for her to reach." She punished us the rest of the meal by not refilling waters, only coming back (after about 30 minutes) to take our order, and bring the food. Never asked us how the food was (cold and slimy) never refilled our drinks. Of course, when the check came, she was our best friend again. I have eaten here probably 20 times over the years and never once had a great meal or decent service. Once, I ordered a club, which was "grilled" but came to me cold, as if it had been stored in a refridgerator. It has the grill marks on the sandwich, but it was ice cold and slimy. How does that happen? Oh yes, and it took them an HOUR to bring it to me. Not to say that the service is always in your face offensive- I have had plenty of service there that was simply indifferent. If you are in the mood for a beer and some pub food, do yourself a favor and walk the four blocks to the piper pub on the balcony at the corner of 8th and main streets. The food is good, the service is good and they actually act like they want your business. Crazy!

text: There's an old expression I was told when I started work at Camden's waterfront office park that I'd like to preface my review with...."If you're not at the aquarium ...your life may be in danger" Yet for those of us who dodge the possibilty of a BMX bike crashing into your car or a methadone induced stampede outside the train station, there is a jewel of a pizza place within this city's deadly embrace. Headed up by an amazing staff that will shout your order out to the dining area as you sit into what some people call the safest place in Camden...The reason being, your probably ordering or eating with Camden's finest in da house! Not to mention the dining area is like an art gallery filled with old amazing pictures of this fair city. My favorite is the before and after picture of the establishment with picture 1 looking like a scene out of the movie New Jack City and number 2.......well on to the food! You have salads loaded with a choice breaded or unbreaded chicken in huge bowls, you have pizza that actually tastes like it's coming from NY with a great crust (ask for extra crispy) And then there's the sandwiches made to your order, like chicken parm, cheesesteaks, roast pork with provolone...You got wings, chicken fingers..etc.. It's an amazing lunch! And lastly, you want a great deal? You got that great deal and service Thanks come again? You GD right I will!

text: This location of Gold's Gym is the best one I've been to. This one is so much cleaner than the Gold's at West Edmonton Mall. It should get 4 stars for that fact alone. It's probably because this one is much newer, but it's still great to have a clean gym - old or new. I love the bug climbing "wall" they have. It's actually a huge cylinder at the front of the gym. It's pretty cool. There is a lot of room in this gym and it's never very crowded. It's great if you are like me and want to go to work out without having to wait for machines or deal with crowds. I also like a women's only area, which they have too. They also have a lot of classes. They have your typical gym classes (spin classes) but they also have some super cool ones like fencing! They are getting a juice bar in right away so that will be a great addition to the gym. They already have a nail and tan salon attached to it. I'm not a fan of having the tanning and nail salon attached but it's probably a smart business move so who am I to say anything?! It's a good gym. Check it out!

text: Great beer list, terrible food, service, and everything else. I really try to love this place, because they get a lot of good, interesting beers in stock, don't charge too much, and did a heck of a job rehabbing part of the Lemp Brewery complex. That said, I can't love it, because the food and the service suck. We've been here 4-5 times and each time is exactly the same. Yays: - Beer list - 36 taps, with a lot of rare beers and beer geek beers, plus their own. - They make their own liquor! Rum, Gin, Grappa, and some kind of Brandy. - The place is beautiful. It's in a historic building (the stables from the brewery), and has been lovingly restored. - The house salad is pretty awesome. I highly recommend getting it with your meal. Nays: - The service is awful. Expect a meal to take more than 90 minutes, 15 minutes to get drinks, and so on. - Our order has been wrong twice that we've eaten there. Last night we ordered a pizza grinder and had a chicken parmesan sandwich delivered. I would have complained except no server to be found. - It is incredibly loud. Deafening, even. Very annoying that I couldn't hear my fiancee across the table. - The food, frankly, isn't any good. They've gone through a couple chefs and ways to envision the food - too bad both chefs have pretty much sucked. If I owned it, I'd sack them and find someone who can cook. Overall, it's great for a beer, but don't be in a hurry, and definitely, don't go hungry.
label: NEG

text: So, ladies (and some gents), you know that body waxing is an experience that's on par with a regular tooth cleaning; necessary (for some) but entirely unenjoyable and uncomfortable no matter how you slice it. Body Restoration is like my dentist of 14 years. Dependable, reasonably charges for services rendered and makes the experience as pleasant as it can possibly be within the circumstances. I go to Body Restoration exclusively for all my waxing needs. Pam and Jennae are the best, thorough and so friendly. Like my dentist, they chat to you during the process as to distract you from what's going on. I've also gotten massages and facials here, and they've both been top-notch (and super relaxing). Waiting area is lovely and soothing. They provide comfy robes and flip flops and 2 change rooms. My only gripe are the size of the rooms. Aside from the typical waxing room, the massage and facial treatment rooms and the change rooms are quite small - I wish they were bigger and airier. Also, as it's been mentioned in almost all reviews, getting to Body Restoration is a bit of a mystery and the teeny-tiny lobby and elevator feel industrial. Otherwise, Body Restoration scores high on all fronts. Definitely in my top three for spas in the city.

text: I didn't let my complete ignorance of Indian food stop me from trying it. Outside of a few curries here and there, I have precious little experience with this cuisine. So the only parameter I can use to rate it is, did it taste good? I ordered a tandoori shrimp lunch, which was an assortment of foods served upon a large metal plate that brought back memories of an unpleasant afternoon spent at Riker's Island a long time ago. There were a few shrimp, which appeared to have been grilled, along with a ramekin of a green sauce. The shrimp were on the dry side, but the dipping sauce (I presume) was tasty. Included in the lunch was a cup of dal - is it supposed to be all broken up like that - because the lentils were so cooked down as to be unidentifiable. Somewhat tasty, but a textural failure, IMO. There was another cup of a potato and pea mixture in a spicy broth - I liked this quite bit. The lunch was accompanied by a large pile of basmati rice - this was perfectly cooked and very good. There was also a salad of very tired greens and thinly sliced cucumbers - I left all of it. Service was disinterested - waiter spent more time in the doorway looking up and down State then he did checking tables. I enjoyed the basket of naan but have no idea as to how authentic it might be, All in all, not a great dining experience.
label: NEG

text: I stayed at an oceanfront suite at this hotel in May. My complaint with this hotel is the bar! The bar is located at the oceanside of the hotel, outside off of the parking area. And it plays loud music on the weekends, starting in the early afternoon. Very loud music. Music so loud that you can still hear it at the water's edge way down on the beach. Music so loud that the noise competes with your TV set in your room even with the door closed. Music that can be played until 2:00 am, although it usually cut off before then. I will say that the management sometimes responded to our requests to lower the volume, but not always. And we had to repeat our requests every Friday, Saturday, and Sunday that we stayed there. The necessity of making all those complaints irritated us, and it irritated them to hear them. Even with the music volume lowered or off completely, there is still the sound of people drinking and partying. Now, if I had wanted all that bar noise, I would not have paid money for an oceanfront suite - I would have rented a room above a bar. I don't go to the beach to hear loud music or the sound of inebriated people. I go for peace and quiet, and the sound of the ocean as I read on my balcony. This is not the place to do it. The hotel is a narrow one, so you cannot get an oceanfront suite far away enough from the bar to not hear the noise. They have plenty of oceanview suites where you probably would not hear the noise as long as the room was way in back of the hotel. The noise from the music at bar would still impact you while you're on the beach, though, no matter where your room was. In addition, the management misrepresented the situation when they told us that we were the only ones who complained about the noise. Conversations with other patrons in the elevator showed us that that was not true. Its too bad, because the hotel itself was actually a good one. The rooms were clean, modern and pleasant. The staff was very good and immediately responded to our needs. The kitchenette was decently stocked. The beach is terrific, with nice sand and the warmest ocean water I've ever had the pleasure of swimming in.
label: NEG

text: Let's just get three things out of the way: 1) Exposed brick doesn't make you historical. 2) Having beer on tap doesn't make you a brewhouse. 3) This is pretty much a 2 1/2 star review. text: I dined here recently with a huge party of 14 or 16 . . . as you can imagine, disaster resulted. *tear I forgot to mention in my last review, but there's a corkage fee for your BYOB, i think $3 per bottle of wine and then $.50 per bottle/can of beer - LAME! So you don't want to pay for a bar license, but you want to charge your customers money for their desire to have a simple glass of wine, they bought, at your restaurant? I know this is protocol at many places, but still! So our large group was here for a birthday. They were able to seat us, but did so in tiers (understandably) as we arrived at different times. The waiter was not very devoted to us, at all. I suppose he assumed we would be difficult or take forever to order, but he circled us several times - servicing the people around us, but never even paused to ask us if we were ready (we were ready to order at least 25 minutes until he finally came to take our orders). I understand it was Saturday night and they were busy anyway, but they couldn't get it together with regards to ensuring we all received our food in edible condition. I ordered the Garlic Tofu and by the time it reached its optimal devouring position in front of me, it was pretty cool, no steamy hotness or warmth to it. Additionally I ordered it HOT and it was completely not spicy at all. At least I received my food. Two people in our party never received their Chef Special's - some fish entree. So the poor souls ended up picking at the other people's plates. Nearly thirty to forty minutes elapsed and one of them decided to inform the waiter (as he paused by our table) that they were no longer interested in their entrees, being that we were all gearing up to go for some birthday celebratory drinks. Now this part was annoying! The waiter INSISTED, the entrees were about to be ready in five minutes and we just needed to bear with him because the kitchen was swamped and the dishes were already being prepared so could we just be patient. Uh . . . what? So one of the people who didn't receive their fish entrees, decided to actually pursue our waiter and firmly explain to him that the rest of the 14 people were ready to go AND it was nearly closing time. He finally agreed to cancel out the fish entrees, but begrudgingly. I assume he did, we never really checked the bill since we were so rushed to leave. So yeah, was not really pleased about that whole shebang, but I still like their food above all the other Thai places. Anyway, that's that!

text: Fashion Nails is a small slot located near the Macy's in Park Place Mall, nestled between a massage parlor & a cell phone store. Horrible service. A friend and I went walked in for fills (a seemingly simple procedure). We were barely greeted at the door by the two employees, only one of which was servicing a client. My friend was seated first, and while I was waiting with her, her technician just left. She just up and bounced, no explanation. I was then seated with the newly free second technician, and only after we asked her what was going on, did we get the explanation of another technician coming in for my friend. My friend is a very gracious person, but her technician was rude and did shoddy work on her nails. My friend pointed out a few nails that had been filed crooked, and her tech sighed heavily and threw her file down, before composing herself and doing her job correctly. My tech wasn't much better. Neither of them made any attempt to small talk us, they barely even asked what we wanted to have done. She was rough with my hands, and filed skin as well as nail. Service aside, there is nothing else to make this place even remotely attractive. The space is small & very very cramped. While not filthy dirty, it's not clean either. Sketchy Item #1: Sketchiest thing I have ever seen was that the sterilizer and the microwave occupied the same shelf. This is a nightmare to me. Sketchy Item #2: When asked to sign in, most people assume they are simply notifying the staff as to what service they would like, and this information can be used by the establishment for research purposes. But here, you are signing a LEGAL document, assigning yourself as the responsible party and forfeiting any rights in case of screw up on their part. Signing in allows this place to forfeit any responsibility to operate a clean & healthy establishment. The fact that such a document is printed for you upfront, tells me that some sort of slip up has already happened, and who knows what happened to that poor girl. I believe that Fashion Nails is a sister store to Creative Nails, located in the same mall but by the movie theater & food court. Creative Nails looks like a better space, but if it's operated by the same schmucks, I'm not feeling that joint either. Do not waste your money or time here. Their mark-up is higher (since it's in a mall), the service is horrible, the end result isn't all that great, the space is a mess, and it's a legal & health hazard.
label: NEG

text: If you do one tour in New Orleans, skip the mule and buggy and take this amazing walking tour!! You won't be dissapointed. We just took Le Monde Creole's "THE INSIDER' S FRENCH QUARTER" tour, which, for those that have been to Laura Plantation, revolves around the life of Laura Locoul Gore's family. An incredibly interesting history tour, it is very well researched without being stuffy. As with Laura Plantation, one of the things we appreciated most was that the tour guides did not "sugar-coat" the topic of slavery, as we've found many tours to do. An added bonus is that you have the unique opportunity to visit private or normally inaccessible French Quarter courtyards as you listen to the story of New Orleans and the Locoul line. It does get to be quite hot and sunny, and the tour is around 2 1/2 hours covering most of the Quarter, so do be prepared with your water, sunscreen, and comfy shoes! Thanks, Bill, for a great tour!!
label: POS

text: I can cook. Not like, "chef" cooking, but I can feed myself and make food that tastes alright. So a lot of the reason I eat out is because someone else can do it better, and do it in an atmosphere that fits the grub and, well, makes food into a meal. I went to Mercato recently with a group of 6, for restaurant week, and my ears are still ringing. There are other reviews that warn of the noise level, but it was deafening. The open kitchen, overpacked dining room and lack of wall treatments or whatever made it a chaotic echo chamber. At one point, half the place turned to stare evilly at a woman who was singlehandedly making eardrums burst, but it felt hypocritical...Mercato is just LOUD by design. Too loud. We were pretty happy with the food - crispy trout with cippolinis, pasta with lobster, grilled artichoke, though the gnocchi were overcooked (saved only by its sauce) and the other apps we got were ho-hum. We had some great wine to go with dinner, a 2003 Frog's Leap zinfandel I've been saving since....2003, but this package, this meal, amounted to an INTENSE, frustrating, annoying experience because of the noise level. Mercato was neither good for a group nor for a first date, unless you are (already) deaf. Should it matter that the place was packed due to restaurant week? I think not. They didn't set out to create an ambiance for a half-empty house. What we saw was the business in what should have been its optimal state, and it sucked.
label: NEG

text: The Botanical Gardens is one of a few major attractions in St. Louis that I hadn't yet reviewed on Yelp because it was a complete no brainer. This, along with the City Museum, The Zoo, and (arguably) the Arch, make up the core of the must-experience things one must do when visiting St. Louis. It's huge, diverse, and among the best botanical gardens in the entire country. And if you're a STL resident (and an early riser), it's free. Whew, where do I start with this one. Ok, you like stuff that grows out of the earth, right? Sometimes you eat it, sometimes you wear it, sometimes you smell it, sometimes you sit under it, sometimes you smoke it. Plants are everywhere, and we all take them for granted. They become part of the background, scenery. Stuff to decorate our other stuff. But it's not until you're completely surrounded by them that you appreciate how many crazy, awesome, weird, and kickass plants are on this earth. And it's not until you visit MOBOT that you realize this. Do you like roses? They got a whole garden of them, in every color imagineable. "Big deal. Everyone's got roses" you say. Well, when was the last time you visited a formal Japanese zen garden? Or an English woodland? Or the Amazon rainforest? Or the Arizona desert? MOBOT replicates all these gardens and environments, both indoor and out, with a wide variety of species that would impress even the most snooty botanist. "Alright, I'm not here to study plants and explore the amazon or whatever. I just want to relax and look around". Well you're in luck too buddy. There are fountains and ponds galore (even a waterfall or two), along with a fragrance garden and an edible garden where you can see how much better their tomatoes are than yours. There's a children's garden as well where you can let your rugrats run free (for an additional charge of course). And bring along a few quarters so you can feed the mammoth and ravenous Koi fish, which I'm convinced would eat a baby whole should one accidentally fall in. Add to this the various sculptures throughout the gardens and the super relaxed atmosphere (it almost never seems crowded no matter how many people there are), and you have a morning/afternoon of fun that is virtually unriveled in all of St. Louis. MOBOT is big enough to get lost in but small enough to feel next door. It's not an experience to be rushed. There's a reason St. Louisans keep returning, and keep recommending this place.

The wife's tacos were on corn tortillas that looked amazing. I tried her carne asada taco and the corn tortillas tasted as fresh as they looked. I can only hope that the beef entrees aren't the same consistency. Dessert was something I completely forgot was included, but since it was, I went ahead and ate it. Duck Confit & Breast with fingerling potates and green beans was cooked perfectly and a very generous portion. Rack of Lamb with black eye pea cassoulet was as good as it gets. Bananas foster beignets-rich, decadent, it was perfect ending to a amazing dinner. Menu is getting ready to change so we will be back soon for sure.

text: I had been tanning at the old Caughlin Ranch location for years (since 2000) and was SO excited to find out about the Sparks location after my move to Spanish Springs. Sunsation offers excellent customer service, a great central location, and an extremely clean facility. The staff is very friendly and knowledgeable; they make it a point to learn your name and greet you as you enter the salon. The owner takes pride in her business and it shows. She is very approachable and professional. They offer your traditional low-medium-high tanning beds and also mystic/airbrush tans. I wish I could give Sunsation more than 5 stars! They are just fantastic!! :)
label: POS

text: This place is a mixed bag. Some good things, others not, but not much is really great. Except the service. Exceptional and friendly. Based on the food alone, however, I don't have an overwhelming urge to eat here again, as I have with other BBQ places in town. There is certainly better BBQ, even in Tucson. The ribs were dry and overcooked, the pulled pork and brisket were good, and the chicken had an odd spongy texture and did not have much flavor. The Okra and beans were top drawer, green beans good and slaw was just ok. A core feature was lacking: the basic BBQ sauce was missing zing, but the Hot BBQ Sauce was much better but still missing something. It certainly helped carry the meats, which needed to be carried by something. Good Apple cobbler, but a bit on the sweet side. Texas Toast. So so. Just like our meal. For a chain, I would have expected much better food. Oh, one more comment: although BBQ may be served fast, BBQ is NEVER fast food: it it slow and low cooking only or it isn't BBQ. So it is entirely fair to compare it with other BBQ retaurants, even Famous Dave's. In my opinion, Famous Dave's (a chain), Brundog's, and Bubb's Grubb (not chains) have far better BBQ than Shane's.
label: NEG

text: One of Tucson's best local roaster/espresso joints period. I've now consumed nearly 180 shots of their espresso over the last 2 years and the quality over that period of time is astounding. First of all it is the only place in Tucson that you can get all three espresso types; Northern, Central and Southern Italian profiles! Sure their blends, but most espresso is. Michael and his baristas spend a lot of time perfecting their craft of pulling espresso and have little tolerance for anything but the best. Personally, I believe they have the best macchiato in Tucson. I recommend you order it with their Mazzo shot. Clearly a coffee giant in Tucson!

text: Charley's is more impressed with themselves than I was with them. Steak was bland... No flavor, the sides were also tasteless. If the staff/Kitchen spent as much time on the food as they do selling it you, it might be better. Skip this place and go around the corner to Roy's or Selmon's.

text: I went to this establishment because I am on a never ending quest to find the greatest burger ever made. We arrived at lindy's about fifteen minutes before closing time. The place is very small and was packed. We quickly snagged the only table available. The bartender/wait staff was very happy(high) to take our orders. The menu consists of burgers that must have been created by a mad burger scientist. I ordered the double mac n cheese burger and a miller high life on tap. The burgers arrived about fifteen minutes later. Not a word was spoken until we had all consumed our massive burgers. My buddies and I all agreed that lindys burgers were best we had ever had.
label: POS

text: I've tried Fozzie's several times, with varied experiences. It's a cute little place with a little outdoor seating area right on Big Bend - not the most scenic atmosphere, but it's nice that they offer outdoor seating. The main problem I have with this place is that you don't always get what you order. On one particular occasion, I called ahead and ordered the beet salad to go. What I got was a salad that did include beets, but nothing else that was listed in the salad's description on the menu. Instead of a light balsamic dressing, I got something that resembled mayo - gross! Also, the salad was warm and limp. I ate a few bites and threw it away. Another time, my husband ordered "The Pretzel" sandwich which was supposed to come on a pretzel roll, but he got some other kind of bread. Maybe they ran out of pretzel rolls? I don't know. On the other hand, I've gotten their "Classic Gyro" twice, and both times it's been delicious! I would highly recommend it. I've found what I like here and I'm sticking to it! Also, their shakes look really good, but I haven't ventured to try one yet.

text: I have been going to this place since it first opened in Reno. So my review of this particular restaurant is not based upon one single visit. In fact I would have to be honest and say I have actually been here probably 50 times over the years. The chips and salsa are very good and the vegetarian burrito (called the calabasa) is delicious. The environment is pretty comfortable and I have had mostly good service here. The biggest complaint my friends have is that the rice leaves something to be desired. All in all I think it's a perfectly good place to eat. So try it! *****************UPDATE****************** The other day my friend and I were sitting at work thinking about how much we felt like eating burritos.. So being less than 5 miles from Hacienda I thought we should go there! Sounds good right? Yeah.. so anyway it was Sunday and we didn't get out of work until 4pm so my friend suggested we call them and find out when they switch from the lunch menu to the dinner menu. Why pay 3 dollars more for the same thing? So I make the phone call and a man answers, I asked him specifically when they switched over the menu, he told me 5:30 or 6pm. I said, "Even on Sundays?" He said, "Yes." So 4 o clock rolls around and my friend and I drive over to Hacienda. We arrived not even 10 min after 4pm. No one greets us.. employees just walk past and try to ignore us... finally after standing there for about 5 min a hostess comes up. I ask her to make sure she is grabbing lunch menus and she said it was already the dinner menu. I proceeded to tell her about the phone call and so she grabs the owner. Now, having been to this place no less than 50 times in the past 8 or so years.. I have seen this man many times. I told him what was happening and he said, "The lunch menu changes at 4pm." It was not even 15 min after and one of his employees told me it was at least until 5:30. What a jerk!!!!!!! I will never go there again.
label: NEG

text: My husband and his friends went here for a guys' night out. They had a good time and enjoyed the atmosphere. The guys were asked for a credit card to start a tab. No Problem. My husband gave his. At the end of the night when they were ready to go, they asked for and received the bill with credit card. They paid in cash and left. My husband's next credit card statement showed the charge applied to the card. He has since contacted the establishment with no response from the owner Brian. He has contacted them and left two verbal message with an employee and four with the voice mail. The owner suddenly is never in and has never returned any calls. Now, my husband is disputing the charge with his credit card company. Yay! Cheers to the owner for looking out for his customers. If you go, make sure to pay in cash.

I know Philly can be a little ghetto, but this "hotel" epitomizes ghetto. And they overcharged my credit card even when they promised to fix error. Since this "hotel" was run by a couple of gay guys, I had expected better services and decor. But it was not inexpensive either!!!! Third-world standards at First-world prices. Won't make this mistake again!!!

text: I adore this place - not to mention it's location. It's just a short walk from my apartment! Regency has a great selection of coffee/coffee related beverages, both hot and iced, not to mention the various steamers, italian sodas and teas. My favorite: the iced medici with whipped cream (traditional mocha with hints of orange). The staff is always incredibly friendly and all the drinks/sandwiches/salads are made to order. Their food is nothing short of delicious! They are known for their homemade quiche - a new variety every day! We tried their breakfast sandwiches (they serve breakfast all day - AND you can call ahead to order) and they were FABULOUS! The bagels were perfectly toasted and they hit the spot. It's the type of breakfast that keeps you full for quite a while. They always have fresh baked muffins, cupcakes and cookies but I've yet to try them. This is a great spot to bring some paperwork, homework or a good book and just relax. You can people watch from your table inside or enjoy the weather with their outside seating. Either way, you'll love this place.

text: For almost $150 for two and the Vetri name, Amis should have been great. Too bad all we got was disappointment. Vetri is known for his exquisite attention to detail, but apparently this was forgotten in the latest expansion of his mini empire. The guinea hen lacked a crisp skin and was covered in fat. It tasted like an amateur cook roasted it at too low of a temp. The oxtail gnocchi sounded amazing until I chomped on an accidental oxtail bone that was the same size, shape, and color as the gnocchi. This was the first dish I sent back to a restaurant in years, and the waitress comes back not with "I'm sorry about that can we make you another," but "that's not a bone- its cartilage so its ok." Tell my near missing tooth that. Other dishes were ok but everything was rich and greasy. The menu lacked balance due to a scarcity of vegetables and greens. The concept, location, and space are terrific. But Amis needs some serious refinement before we go back.
label: NEG

text: I can be very judgmental. Slowly but surely I'm maturing and letting go of my quick-draw assumptions. I can tell a few employees at Moriarty's have yet to reach this point or even start the long haul towards adulthood. I've been here once before so I'm far from a regular and didn't realize that behind door #1 is a clear walkway and behind door #2 is a huge wooden bench that will stop you dead in your tracks. I was quick enough to catch myself before toppling over it, but the guy who entered a few seconds later was not. Everyone got a real kick out of it and I was the only one, staff included, to help him up. Maybe we can move the bench now? Or lock door #2? Just some thoughts. My friends, a married couple with a newborn, were home from Hawaii for one week. In that one week they had to squeeze in three sets of families, a wedding and tons of visits from friends. As smart as they are, they plotted to kill a few birds with one stone and have all the college buds meet up at Moriarty's to see them, the babe and savor the wings that even the beautiful Maui sunsets couldn't erase. The staff was more than annoyed that we rolled so deep without a reservation. They also weren't too keen on the baby. We had to split up between a booth in the back and seats at the bar and our server actually had the nerve to ask us to only order drinks from her. OK. So we'll stand by the table, order drinks, then go drink them by the bar. 20 minutes later they relinquished a large, unoccupied table held for a no-show reservation. Some of us moved to the table, some stayed in the booth that was within arm's reach. They said we had to give up the booth. This still did not solve the problem of the lacking seats. So we left. I've never felt so unwanted. If it weren't for the wings and stellar happy hour deal ($3 drafts from a hefty selection) I'd knock off a star in the ratings.
label: NEG

text: This place should be called Sunyata, as in the opposite of Nirvana. The wait staff refused to greet us when we walked in the door and made us wait 15 minutes when there was obviously a table ready. The food was mediocre at best: I ordered the chicken chatnad which was far too spicy, and I love spicy food. After the first bite I could no longer taste the coconut paste. My girlfriend ordered the chicken tikka masala which tasted like bland chicken with a can of warm campbell's tomato soup with lots of pepper mixed in. The naan was burnt. They didn't even use basmati rice which is unheard of for an Indian restaurant. The service was slow and the waiter gave me a dirty look when I asked for a new glass of water (the one they gave me had chunks left on it). This is by far the worst Indian food I've had on two continents. I love Indian food but I'll never come here again.
