text: Met friends here for dinner and drinks. I love the concept of this place. The menu has wine and beer in order of how far they are from the restaurant, clever. They also use all local ingredients and even make their ketchup from scratch. I had the grass fed burger with Huntsman's cheese. Who would have known that Huntsman's cheese is a combo of cheddar and blue cheese? Yum! The burger came with a heaping mound of fresh fries which I couldn't help but devour. We ended up staying for quite a few rounds of drinks. The waiter was helpful in making choices too given my beer knowledge is limited to bud light, miller light and amstel light. - OOOps. I found it rather comical though that all the drinks the boys ordered seem to come in these girly - should have a beach umbrella - glasses and all us chickas got pint glasses. Great times with great friends. I would return.

text: Went here after a stiff night at Vango TRYING to celebrate a birthday. We left, came here and the celebration really began. Cheap drinks, great music, mixed crowd, friendly staff, plenty of seating, room for dancing. Is there anything else you could ask from a place? Let's just say The Raven Lounge gives you the kind of morning you wake up laughing to, only remembering where you were because they gave you a business card before you left. Awesome time.

text: Fomerly the Jazz Cooker. Currently, one of those places I'd rather gnaw my arm off then go to. A couple of the frat bros. used to love this joint and went here often. Now they live in NYC and I couldn't be happier that I almost never have to go here, unless they come to visit, in which case I am more than happy to meet them at the gate to go somewhere else. If; you have not been here you can not begin to understand why its so foul. First the place stays at a balmy 125 degree year round. Windows open or closed, AC on or off, summer or winter. They have live music, which would be nice if the place was more than 20 sq. feet. OK, so it's not that small, but it's close. The bar is nearly impossible to get to, and the bartenders always act like they have something better to do. I am your income, please be nice to me, or at least pretend. They charge cover...I mean really, $5 to get in the door of this place...get out of town. Imagine one of your friends made you pay $5 bucks to cram into their living room with no drinks and loud music pounding in your head....argh, this is getting my blood pressure up...next review.

text: Guajillo Mexican Grill is yet another restaurant to add to the ever growing list of Mexican style burrito, taco and quesadilla bars. This new type of fast Tex-Mex is growing in popularity with "staples" such as Chipotle, Moe's and Qdoba. Guajillo has yet to master their fast Tex-Mex offerings. My friend ordered a bare burrito, basically a burrito minus the tortilla. It was served to him cold. Cold rice, cold chicken, cold beans. Not appealing. I had better luck. I got a chicken queasily which I would classify just as bland. The chicken had some flavor but could have used more cheese. The best part of the meal was their chips and salsa. The testates had a good flavor with a hint of lime. The salsa, although runny, still had a nice kick.

text: Hi, My name is Carrie and I am a second hand junkie! I have traveled the world in search of treasures and I can honestly say that the Santa Barbara Consignment Company is the BEST consignment store in the U.S.A.! The store is huge, clean, and packed with beautifully displayed, high quality merchandise. The inventory is ever-changing and I hate to miss a week for fear of missing a treasure. The merchandise is priced to move! The owners, Jennifer and Susan, are very helpful and FUN too!

text: I was really excited when this place opened. Finally---an independent coffee shop that was conveniently located on my side of campus. No more raging guilt when I had to stop by Dunkin' Donuts or Starbucks because there was no other place to fetch coffee on University Ave. in the early morn. Oh, but how quickly my hopes were dashed. On my first visit, I waited in line for fifteen minutes. My simple order---buttered bagel and black coffee---had to be repeated three times because the girl kept ringing it up wrong. I was forgiving---after all, they had just opened. Then I got back to campus with my bag and found a bagel slathered with cream cheese. Um, was it really that hard? But again---forgiveness. So some friends and I skipped over before class one day to grab coffee. This time we were in line for 15 minutes, and then it took 10 minutes for our orders to come out---and no one got anything more than a coffee drink and a pastry. Plus, out of the six of us, one person's drink was missing the sugar and someone got a pastry they didn't order. That's a pretty crappy error rate. That peeved me, and I vowed never to return. But, a couple of weeks later, still somewhat squicky from the night previous, I was lured in by their chalkboard offer of a coffee and bagel for some cheap price. Despite my two bad encounters, I decided to go for it because there wasn't a line. I went inside and asked for the special, which was evidently beyond this girl's vocabulary. "On the chalkboard? The bagel and coffee?" She nodded and rang things up---but it totaled more than advertised. When I pointed out the discrepancy, she rolled her eyes and huffed, "It's like, *fifty cents.* What do you want me to do?" I was feeling too hungover to argue about the principle of the matter, so I just walked out. And that was the last time I ever set foot in that place. I hope it closes and gets replaced with something that isn't staffed with incompetents.
label: NEG

text: This place is crowded at happy hour. The menu is very good for an Irish pub, with such yummy apps as the blue-cheese covered steak tips. Great atmosphere, decent beer selection (but only the crappy beers are usually on HH). Great waitstaff, mostly cute =)

text: Seamus is one of those place that once you go, you'll crave to go back every week. The staff is friendly and fun. The outside patio is amazing when the weather is nice. And don't forget about the food and drinks! I'm a veg, so I can't comment on how good the burgers are, although I've heard many a good word about them. The Seamus salad with their homemade blue cheese dressing is fantastic. Mmmmmmm crinkel fries with cheese sauce! Mmmmmmm garlic cheese bread! If Seamus would add a veggie burger to their menu, I would change my four stars to five!
label: POS

text: Order charbroiled oysters. Eat. Repeat. And that's Drago's!

text: Saigon Restaurant is the place to go if you want to try something a little bit different, but not be at all disappointed by the flavor, cleanliness, or ambience of a seemingly hole in the wall Vietnamese restaurant. On the outside, it looks like it could be just another dingy ethnic restaurant pushed into the corner of an... interesting strip mall, but stepping inside and having lunch is an entirely different experience. They have awesome, well plated appetizers, Pho (which you absolutely must try at some point in your life - don't be shy with the Hoisin sauce!), and several excellent vegetarian options. The portions are the right size, the service is great, the place is almost always at least half full of people from every walk of life, and the price is right. Also, if you want a real treat, get yourself some bubble tea (I recommend the Thai spiced tea variety)!

text: Run away as fast as you can!!!!! Never, EVER buy a used car from them. Ever. Shady dealings and they will tell you anything to put you in a car. I worked with Tim Hughey and he was not helpful or very friendly. He didn't know anything about the car and made up stuff along the way as he saw fit to justify things wrong with the car. text: As far as Broadway honky tonks go, Robert's is the best I've experienced. Tourists and locals alike come here to take in the nightly live music, which is reliably high quality, even in the middle of the week. With the country music mural above the stage, the shelves of elaborates cowboy boots along one wall, and a relatively tame crowd, Robert's seems much more family-friendly than the average lower Broad Bar. If you only had only one night to spend in Nashville, Robert's would be the one essential stop.

text: 5 stars simply because they serve breakfast (burritos, not tacos but close enough) all day. Very clean space in South Franklin. Owner runs the register and is very helpful & friendly. Shared a bacon/egg/potato burrito, crispy beef taco, 2 fish tacos, and an order of nachos for the boy. Lots of food, good quality -- not greasy spoon, everything very tidy and excellent flavor. They are opening a new location on the north side of Franklin (Mallory Ln, across from Centennial HS by Garlic Jims) in October 09 -- a little closer location for me. I will be sure to check them out again -- this former Texan gives it an informed Gringo Tex Mex connoisseur seal of approval!

text: I've been meaning to write this review for a while, so here goes. When I got my first flat tire ever, I was freaking out. What do I do? Is it just the tire, or the rim as well? How much is this going to cost? You get the idea. I first took the tire to Firestone across the street. Since the Firestone on S. text: My girlfriend (now wife) & I stopped in to Cisco's a few days after we moved into our house in Flourtown. Nice cold beer, but a couple of bland previously frozen fried hamburger patties left us really cold. Too bad we didn't know any of the locals at that point - maybe we would have ordered the cheese-steak hoagie.

text: I stopped by here to pick up a half gallon of milk one night , only to discover this was not your ordinary corner store/mini market. In addition to the super clean deli that makes scrumptious Vietnamese and American (Philly) Hoagies, the store in itself, is full of wonderful Organic, Vegetarian, Natural and Ethnic food products to prepare at home and cleaning products. Several types of tofu, Tempeh, Veggie proteins, some fresh produce, healthy snacks. Prices seem reasonable or what you would pay at Whole foods. Hoagies are a good price too. The store is clean and well-organized. I explored the store while awaiting for my Vietnamese Tofu Hoagie. It's true, you must be patient when ordering or like other reviewers call ahead. I think it's wonderful to have a mini-independent whole foods in my neighborhood, as well as a place to get a quick hoagie. This tiny "mini" store's name shouldn't fool you, as they have lots to offer this diverse neighborhood!!!!
label: POS

text: I LOVE THIS AQUARIUM! Seriously. I won't shut up about how awesome it is. I fell in love as soon as I walked in and saw their aquatic tunnel. You can walk through and view their Caribbean Reef. How cool! I really enjoyed the different sections they have. I couldn't believe they had an Amazon Rain Forest area. It was definitely interesting and had a sweet treehouse type thing that I loved playing in. I could have spent the entire day at this aquarium. At the end of our visit we sat and watched the animals in the big tank for quite a while. It was dark and peaceful in there and I totally wanted to take a nap. I can't wait to go back to New Orleans and visit this aquarium again.

text: Hehe, I love this place. Cheap and yummy and all-you-can-eat. There's a lot to choose from, so you're bound to find something you like. It's mostly Chinese food suited to American tastes, but my Chinese family still likes it. Even though the food isn't exquisite, it is better than a lot of other buffets I've tried, given the sheer variety and price. There's Chinese, seafood (I always see mussels and crab, and they do shrimp in a million different ways), simple dim sum, American food, and sushi. The dessert bar is a hit-or-miss. They'll have a good cake or two but their cheesecake sucks. It's a layer of cream cheese on top of a layer of cake. Haha, get it? Don't say I didn't warn you. They also have an ice cream machine and a cold bar with fruit, salad, and jello. I always leave here full and happy. The Good: Great price for a very tasty WIDE variety The Bad: This is quantity, not quality, people! Don't expect too much. Also, I'm not really a fan of their desserts.
label: POS

text: Usually supermarkets that have olive bars are pretty classy. This one however, not so much. Maybe its the people that shop there, or the 10,000 screaming children, perhaps the hairy guys in tank tops who don't' shower or wear deodorant that have tainted my view of this store so much. It is always way to crowded, it's like everyone has the same idea at once 7 days a week to buy rotisserie chickens and bad soup for dinner. The setup of the store does not make a lot of sense, you go up and down isles 56 times looking for a can of string beans that are for some reason next to the bread (naturally). If you hate long lines, and crowded isles don't go here. Also if your looking for a lot of organic foods their selection is rather non existent except for a few things in produce. text: On December 2nd, 2009 I saw on Man vs. Food that they did the episode in Tucson, AZ. where Mi Nidito was featured. So after shopping in Tucson, my bf and I decided to go try out this "delicious" featured plate called the "Presidential Plate" at the place. The following is a step by step review of what I saw, and experienced: As we pulled near the restaurant, we noticed that the parking lot was freaking tiny, the place didn't even have enough place to park. After making a long and uneasy parking lot "U" turn, we noticed that there was another parking place in the back of the restaurant, but it was also small and packed. At this time, I thought: "Ok, it's packed, so it HAS to be good." After waiting for 25 mins to get a parking space, we headed in. The minute I opened the door, was when I felt like I was in a swarm of mindless ants near a sugar pond. We were told that it was a 35 min wait. However, after about a 50 min wait, and having to hear people around us saying: "I didn't even know about this place until it was featured on Man vs. Food last week" for about 15 times, we finally had our names called for a seat. We were shown the menu, and I was instantly disappointed. They didn't even have carne asada!!! What Mexican Restaurant place doesn't have Carne Asada??? I saw the "Presidential Plate" that was featured on Man vs. Food, so I ordered it. It took another 25mins for our food to show up, and at first glance, it looked good. However, upon tasting...not only was I disgusted, but I realized that everything on the plate was just mediocre food covered with cheese and enchilada sauce. The "mini tostada" didn't even have more than one spoonful of beans in it! It was filled with shredded lettuce and unknown cheese that wasn't even good! There was a hard shelled taco that tasted just "ok" to me, a stuffed jalapeno pepper with string cheese and then smothered again on the outside with cheese. The last two junk was a beef tamale and chicken enchilada drowned in enchilada sauce. Final Ratings: Was it worth the 50 min wait to eat there? HELL NO. Was the food good? NO. Would I ever go back to Mi Nidito? NO. Would I ever recommend the restaurant to anyone? IN THEIR DREAMS I WILL. NO. I think the only reason it was even packed was literally BECAUSE it was featured on Man vs. Food. I'm sorry, I lived in CA, and the Allertos Mexican Food, hell, even the Alberto's Tacos here in SV taste 5 times better than the nasty junk they served today. So i don't know what all the "hype" is about that place, if canned enchilada sauce doesn't sound tasty to you, then why the heck would it be tasty at a hole in the wall restaurant? It's just not real Mexican food at all.

The food is okay, but the service is absolutely terrible, and I consider myself a very patient person. text: I was trying to find a massage place and most of the stuff I found through Philly Yelp were a little on the pricey side. Being from LA, it's really easy to find a place that will give a great massage on the cheap. Thank goodness I kept searching because I eventually stumbled on this listing, which led me to their website. I was happy to learn that not only do they offer student massages, but they also have certified professional masseuses there as well for really cheap. I booked an appointment with an apprentice and paid 40 bucks for an excellent 1 hour massage. She really paid attention to my problem areas, was really friendly and helpful, and the best part, she wasn't trying to have a conversation with me while I was being worked on. You could tell she really cared about giving me a great experience, which is great considering sometimes you can get a seasoned professional that could care less about how you feel. They take credit card, but are unable to accept the gratuity that way so make sure to bring some cash with you to tip. Also, this place is located in a big building with other businesses in there so make sure to jot down the address because you won't be able to see it from the street. Also, just because it's a clinic, doesn't mean you'll be in a cold, stale room with florescent lights. Their place is actually quite nice. It's definitely not a spa/salon, but it's pretty comfortable with scented oils, dimly lit, and quiet. Water is available in the front. And once you get inside the rooms, it's definitely relaxing and salon-like. You get the music, comfy sheets, aromatherapy, etc. I've gotten plenty of massages in my lifetime, and I can honestly say if you're simply looking to get your body worked on, this place is totally worth it. For 40 bucks for an hour, it's quite a steal.
label: POS

text: A mixed bag. Location is great, bar is good, rooftop pool is nice, etc. But the rooms are hit and miss, some are updated and comfy, some still have the old spring mattresses, all are relatively tight but not unusually so for New Orleans. So just make sure you specify when you make your reservation that you'd like to stay on one of the updated floors. We went down to the hotel restaurant for breakfast one morning, figuring we would sacrifice quality for convenience. And the breakfast buffet looked good but nothing special, however the items we ordered off the menu (in particular the eggs benedict) were outstanding and the hollandaise was made fresh. But the most memorable thing was our server. She very purposefully asked everyones names, instantly memorized them, and never spoke to someone without mentioning their name. She was a mix of downhome charm, and attentive professionalism I haven't experienced before. What blew me away was when we came back the next day and she still knew us all, remembered my sons allergy to milk, my coffee preferences, etc. That's a rare gem that the restaurant has working for them and I hope that they realize it.
label: POS

text: The room was tiny and it smelled like smoke. We asked them for reservation at Ruth Chris and they forgot to do it so we had to find another place to eat. It has a good location and that's about it.

text: Mind you, I know people that love J B Dawson's, I just don't happen to be one of them. When they first opened the food was better, it has gone downhill. For instance, I used to love their baked potato soup, now it tastes like they lost the salt shaker in it. Ribs are okay, not the best I've had, but they are good. Prices are too high, when you can get the same thing, of the same quality, elsewhere, for less. Like their filet, 9 oz. for $22.95. and it is nothing spectacular. If you are so hungry for a good steak, go to your favorite steak house because you are not going to get it here. I must say that I love their fries, when they come out hot and fresh. They are crispy shoestrings and almost like eating a meaty potato chip. They have a very large bar & lounge area, which has quite a few obvious regulars popping in. The restaurant is dimly lit and attractive..

text: Like Matthew M, I also just moved back to NOLA after a seven year hiatus, and I loved the bar. It feels relaxed and sophisticated, yet still has a certain funkiness that makes it comfortable and endearing. The selection is fantastic and the prices are very affordable. On the particular night I visited, I guess there were some issues with the service crew. The owner was behind the bar and super stressed and made us wait for nearly 10 minutes for the second half of a glass of champagne (he emptied a bottle with the 1st half). Then, he was talking to someone else while he finished the pour, but didn't tell us how much we owed him. My friend became quite pissed, as she was in town visiting friends and didn't want to be staring at this stressed out bartender--she wanted to be with her peeps. Understandable. I thought this would be a good opportunity to try out a theory. I wanted to sort of shame this guy into good service since we'd be there for a few more rounds, so we left him an $8 tip for his crappy service for our 2 glasses of wine. It totally worked. However, this is not a tip to service industry-types who may read this. He didn't get a tip at all the next round, so it came out even anyway. Also, he knew the people at my table, as it turns out, but once he got things under control, he came around to wait on our table regularly. So, I'm not sure if it was my smartass/jackass theory or him knowing people, but at least we had perfect service after that. This would be a fantastic date spot, by the way.

text: The Panang salmon was phenomenal. The flavor was absolutely perfect! The papaya salad was, for the first time with such a salad, something of which I could enjoy the complexities of the flavoring without setting my mouth ablaze in mild discomfort. Not that I mind such things: it was just nice to feel balanced with the spice, the fresh lime juice, the peanuts, the tomatoes, etc. The hot tea was a perfect compliment for a chilly night. And I met my soulmate* at the next table over. Didn't even order him: he just appeared! Appropriately random for February 29th. I went to SB from LA on a whim: my friend was doing a beer promotion at a couple bars, and had a free hotel room for the night. She invited me along, and I figured "what the hell." Little did I know (that one's for you, Stranger Than Fiction fans!), I would end up being the one to find a hot guy to make out with, which is what she had wanted to do. I figured I'd just kinda enjoy some alone time and just relax. I must admit I enjoyed my non-alone time, and though I felt a little guilty, hey, it's not like I was looking: it just happened. She was very gracious about it, though. :} So I'd spotted the other Thai place down the street when we first got to town, and that's where we headed after parking. Even though I was looking, we blew by it. But hey there was another one, so OK. They had no tables for me (she was getting hers to go) so I just hung out till she got her order, and planned to proceed to the other place. Well, I'm glad I didn't have to leave: a table opened up. I was very happy with my meal, and was given a happy excuse to exchange looks, comments, and smiles with a lovely gentleman when I had trouble getting the attention of the lady serving me (she was a good server, just a little hard of hearing) for a hot water refill. This gentleman happened to be dining alone also, at the table next to mine, facing me, wondering like I was, "What is this sexy person doing here alone?" He had been seated a good while after I had, so I was finished before he was, and offered him company. We ended up hitting it off. I mean, sparks flying everywhere, like damn I finally remember what this feeling is, and as much as I would have liked to feel it, and admittedly force it, for many years, it just happened right before my very eyes and heart. Bam! I don't know what Zen Yai puts in their food, but it tastes incredible, and seems to have some magical qualities as well! ~~~~~~ *UPDATE: definitely not my soulmate. But a fantastic story nonetheless, so I'll keep it up. Hope is good, right?
label: POS

A ton of classic floppies for a Reno shop, every comic store flops here so hopefully support will continue and these guys can expand. No trade paperbacks at all which was a bit of a downer but very helpful in redirecting to what I needed. A solid shop but needs to develop.

text: You know you've had a solid sandie when the pickle goes untouched. How do you know? Well.. you look down at the lovely gerkin and your like, "ah, snap I'm stuffed like a bum so much so I gotta wrap up the pickle to go." If a sandwich shop offers a Reuben... the Reuben is a good way to put 'em to the test: with its strict ingredients... it's up to the creator to bring it on home with their own touch. (By the way, Protzel's in STL has forever ruined me as their Reuben is the best in America and I was so lucky to once have it bestow itself upon me.) At first glance this Reuben didn't seem worthy of its $10 price tag. Much like the vast expanse of a dessert... it just kept going. The kraut had a peculiar (in a good way) tang to it, same went for the apple kraut. Maybe I'm spoiled on amazing corned beef... but I want my Reuben to be pretty beef forward. I want the corned beef to lead the Reuben march like a frontline general, rather than have so much cheese the beef takes a back seat. I decided to look up what "emmenthaler swiss" is... and it's like the double speak of "chai tea." Chai is Tea and Emmenthaler is Swiss... just so you know when you look at it on the menu and give it a "que?" It's the Swiss cheese from the cartoons. In the end, I'm definitely down for this Reuben... yet I have a hunch their other sandwiches are more in their wheelhouse & better. I really love the space here. Especially if you saw it before as a appliance shop... it's pretty damn lovely in here. High ceilings, high windows... bright white, cold gray floors.... Considering it's in a lowly old strip mall, next to a headshop... it's a haven. The salad menu looks like the true value here. And that will get me back in the door... oh, speaking of doors... I arrived 3 minutes past 3 (closing time) and they unlocked the door for me (me the scruffy, flannel, bearded guy). Then, they gave me a free cookie for being the last served of the day! What A Treat! Note: truly homemade, freshly daily cut potato chips & fries!
label: POS

text: Mike T and I tried to eat here last night. We had tickets to see Avenue Q a The Fox and wanted to grab a quite bite beforehand. Both Mike T and I have worked in the service industry and understand what it's like to be busy. Totally understandable. What's not OK is ignoring customers. All the bartender had to do was say, "Hey guys, I'm slammed right now. Give me a few minutes and I'll be right with you." And we would have gladly waited. But we didn't. And it's too bad because I was looking forward to eating here. Oh, well. Some other time perhaps.

text: I love walking into a restaurant, sitting down, and seeing 4 different tables around me eating a whole fish dish. Then you know the seafood must be quality. Well, welcome to Kim Son. I'm disappointed for not having had this place in over a year (damn, you law school in Chicago, damn you to hell.) Almost every dish I've had there was simply divine (aside from the quail - it was a little too dry). I loved the blue crab - I think it was salted pepper - and the banh xeo was also very good. I love the abundant amount of seafood available at this place. One of my companions had said that the bun he had was delicious. The appetizers (spring rolls, egg rolls, crab rangoon) aside from the banh xeo that I've had were all good, but not overwhelmingly excellent like some places (think Pho Grand's egg rolls or Banh Mi So #1's spring rolls as some high points in St. Louis vietnamese appetizers). The service totally sucked, but delicious food normally makes up for that for me. In this instance, that was certainly the case. Next time I head back to the STL, I would love to revisit this place. When I do, keep a look out for a blond girl stuffing her face full of a whole fish dish and a banh xeo, and maybe even some crab. Excessive - yes. Delicious, double yes!
label: POS

Try their warm, grilled reuben ($8.25), corned beef and Swiss on sauerkraut, with russian dressing on crunchy rye bread, plus a side of crispy chips. Hungry yet?

The sushi is some of the best I've had in this area, and their menu selection ranges from Singaporean/Malaysian to more standard Japanese fare. The desserts are delicious (I've tried them all) and the Singapore iced tea is amazing! Honestly, regardless of what I've tried, I've loved everything! The restaurant is somewhat small, but it doesn't feel cramped -- In fact, the atmosphere is pleasant and relaxing - It's easy to spend hours lost in conversation and good food. Suffice it to say, I highly recommend Singapore - It's not to be missed!

text: My husband (who was my boyfriend at the time) took me to waterworks for dinner on a whim. He said, get dressed we are going out- and that is where we landed. We sat outside, candle lit and it was so beautiful. We walked around the gazebo area at night by the water, it was a fairytale kind-of perfect. The waterworks always stuck out in my mind as probably our most romantic dinner and night ever. Food was great. I had Boursioun Chicken... He had steak. We had asian style appetizers that were also excellent. It was expensive but worth it. Fast forward: I got married here and my reception was in the restaurant. I was torn as to where to have my wedding in philly When I found out that waterworks did weddings, it was immediately decided and it was perfect. It was truely a romantic scene for such a romantic day. Our guests raved about the food as it was unlike normal catered fare. It seemed more personally prepared. The plated appetizers were excellent too and a big hit was the fried oyster. This restaurant will always be special to me and my husband.

text: I've had the tacos from the Kogi BBQ trucks down in LA and while I'll probably draw flak for saying this, I like the ones from Kogilicious just as much. The meat is marinaded and cooked perfectly and the low price let's me get a good variety of flavors even on a grad student's budget. If you're going for taste I suggest getting one of each kind of taco: bbq beef, spicy pork, chicken, or tofu. If you're attempting to induce a food coma get a burrito. Like all burritos in IV they're stupidly large but much better tasting and even slightly cheaper. Everyone behind the counter is adorable. Every time I walk in, their faces light up and I'm tempted to greet them with an "Annyeong haseyo!" but I don't since I know I'll botch the pronunciation. Maybe you should try it. I have to dock them one star mostly on principle. They charge extra for credit card purchases and while I know every store in IV does this I still don't like having to carry cash around in my wallet. I also have to raise an eyebrow at the similarity of name and logo to the original Kogi taco trucks.

text: Alright St Louis.... Whole Foods...... er, Whole Paycheck as I have had many people now refer to this place as, is absolutely spectacular. I live near the Brentwood location and love that one but this one is even bigger and better. Let's knock out the #1 criticism of any Whole Foods. Price. NO SHIT it's high cost. That's what this place is aiming at for clientele. If you want a big vat of butter for $1.99 go to Dierberg's or Costco. This fine establishment is catering (and does a banging great job of it) to people who want high quality produce, food, and other things (there isn't a whole lot you can't find like perfumes, stationary, bulk grains). The store is always immaculately clean. It's like they decide to go all Marine Corp and have little bitches clean the store every morning with toothbrushes. I like to be eco-friendly when I can and this place goes above and beyond any other place I could imagine. Seriously their garbage compactor is run on solar energy. Who does this shit? Whole Foods that's who. Now for another part of this place that is AWESOME. The pre-made foods and lunch/dinner counters are crazy good. Freshly made pizzas, soups, noodles, and almost anything else you can imagine with fresh, nutritious, healthy items are ready to be eaten and or reheated. HUGE PROPS WHOLE FOODS. This store is a winner.

Wine was cold those of us drinking white and the food was tasty. I selected a special they had that evening with crab stuffed sole. We ordered a few apps and the staff were all friendly. When we arrived we didn't have reservations but they hostess was able to squeeze us in on the patio. I would go again if your ever near the brewery and need a nice semi-casual place to eat.
label: POS

text: Have been hearing about this place forever from the folks. Finally got a chance to go to their Thanksgiving Sunday Brunch (buffet style). As I arrived I thought to myself...in Landsdown - really?? Just an odd place to have a gem like this. Walked in to this warm and inviting space and greeted promptly with a smile and "Right this way". The room was set up with a buffet on one side of the room which was displaying beautiful fall colors and decorations. We were greeted by the owner Steve and Chef Sam - the actual Chef. Very comfortable and pleasant conversations. AS we waited a few moments we were looking at the spread most noticeably the steaming hot Suckling pig ready to be carved. We must have been VIP's as we were the first table allowed to go up to the buffet - NICE! I enjoyed Suckling Pig with tasty gravy, a spinach salad with roasted almonds sliver sliced red onions and cucumbers and some sort of fabulous secret dressing which was fabulous. A pretty assortment of pastries ans cinnamon buns. After that a colorful display of fruit and then a huge plate of fresh salmon which was delectable. And if that wasn't enough a made to order omelet station served my Chef Sam himself, choices included Fontina or Gorgonzola cheese, mushrooms, ham, tomatoes, or spinach. I myself had tomatoes, ham and fontina and it was the perfect brunch size and soo tasty. We also enjoyed the mixing menu. We had the La Paloma and the Indian Ocean with our own Vodka. Fantastic idea for a BYOB to provide the mixers and let the patrons provide the booze. Yummy. Indian Ocean was very smooth and sweet. After all was done and the eating was finally finished the pig looked much worse from the day....not his best day - but yummy for us. The Spinach Salad was refilled at least three times and the bowl remained empty at last. We were filled up and boozed up and ready for a much deserved nap...eating is hard you know?! Chef Sam was a delight and I will be back every time I come back into town for their main menu. Really excited to try their main menu. This is a must go at any time. Casual to mid dressy attire, great service, excellent food, and a fantabulous experience and worth every penny - although not too many pennies are needed.
label: POS

We had THE WORST SEAT in the place . . . in the aisle (an ADDED table for 2). My husband's arm was always getting bumped. The draft from the door opening and closing was bitterly cold. The food was late (SOOOO LATE) and cold when it arrived. It took 25 minutes for the baked potato fixings to come . . . after we asked three separate people. When we complained, they gave us half our meal for free. But after all the bumping and the begging for bacon bits and the cold food, and the lack of bread, it didn't seem like enough. text: I received hair removal services at ALC in 2005-6 and have nothing to show for it, except much lingering bitterness. The hair grew back completely after the six initial sessions and several "free" sessions during the 2 year post-treatment period. I'm back at square one, except poorer. Hair growth was partially suppressed only during the treatment course. The sessions themselves were mostly painless, probably because they were totally ineffective. I have serious qualms about their business practices, namely their hard sell tactics and 'no refund' policy. They won't give you a quote over the phone. Their prices are arbitrary (the manager is thinking only of her commission when she sets it) and they hand out meaningless coupons like candy. Their corporate office is totally unresponsive to customers. You will regret doing business with them, maybe not during the treatment period when you are still somewhat hopeful you'll end up 'hair-free', but certainly when everything grows back. Until there's better science and a proven record of results, I won't be trying laser hair removal again.

text: I stopped in with a friend for an afternoon breakfast after seeing the sign from the road. The food was good and the portions were hearty, but it wasn't anything particularly unique or remarkable. It was, however, served piping hot, which is a plus in my book. Pricing was pretty typical for the area--not especially high or low. Everything from the decor to the menu names was poker-themed. It's kind of cheesy, but I'll acknowledge their effort. The one negative that has me knocking my rating down a star is that my friend found a porcelain chip in her food. She didn't want to make a big deal out of it, but she also didn't want anyone else to have the same problem. She alerted our server who took the issue to the kitchen. Our server came back with the response from the kitchen that "it must be a piece of eggshell" without anyone from the kitchen even coming out to check it out or looking for a chipped dish. I completely understand that accidents happen, but the lack of concern about the issue was disappointing to say the least. A simple apology and some visible sign that the problem was at least being looked into would have sufficed. I didn't have any problem personally at the time, but I tried eating my leftovers this morning and finally just threw them out after finding a fifth porcelain chip. :/

text: Ah, Mi Ranchito. (Or, as my friends and I call it, The Ranch.) How you tempt me with your quickly prepared meals of deliciousness. How you satiate my drunken appetite with your sweet concoctions of lovely tequila-ness. How you do all of this without breaking my bank. Mi Ranchito sits in a non-descrip strip mall just a few blocks north of the Loop. Started as a small Mexican joint, this place blew up with a few well-placed reviews in the Riverfront Times and Post-Dispatch. Now, the restaurant has expanded into its unoccupied neighbor and fills the place each weekend with hungry Mexican food lovers from all over. What makes Mi Ranchito (please, The Ranch) so good is how it is so simple. They don't do anything super fancy. It is straight-up-the-gut Mexican food that delights our Midwestern appetite for non-crazy "foreign" food. The fajitas are always hot and sizzling (did you know they just put cold water on the hot pan to make it sizzle?), the chips are crisp and warm, the entrees are plentiful and appetizing. I frequent The Ranch several times a month, and I admit going once every day for four days in a row! But, every now and then, there is a small misstep. Maybe the server wasn't right there when we were seated or maybe they messed up by giving me flour tortillas when I asked for corn tortillas. Nevermind all that. They are consistent, affordable, and comforting. Now, if you are on the hunt for authentic Mexican food, please step on by. If you don't like large crowds of Wash U students or the occassional family having dinner, move your happy butt along. But if you are part of the crowd that craves El Maguey and Casa Gallardo, doesn't mind eating a little later to avoid a crowd, or just needs a quick burrito bite that isn't from gut-bomb Taco Bell, this place is for you.

text: It has to be difficult to own a restaurant that sits in the looming shadow of the infamous Venice Cafe. Not that, at the end of the day, Venice is something so special that you can't possibly coincide with them, but imagine how difficult it would be to get people to notice your brand new taupe-colored siding if your next door neighbor had decorated their house in a glittery mosaic of jazz hands and rainbows. Now yes, Frazer's may not be the kind of place where you can pay for a sandwich with a song, but honestly I'm not really one to sing in public anyway. Their atmosphere is formal enough to match their amazing food but not too stuffy so that you feel you have to dress up or can't relax. Their servers are also friendly and knowledgeable and I have found them to be very helpful when deciding what to order. It's nice to have someone who can explain the specials in an authoritative way without talking over your head or being pushy with the up-sell. On a recent trip to Frazer's, we brought an out-of-town guest there for the first time. The goal was to kick back, have a few drinks and have a delicious but "normal" meal. We absolutely accomplished this goal at Frazer's. For starters we had the cheese plate and the chorizo stuffed dates. Both dishes were very flavorful and a great start to the meal. Among the three of us at the table our order consisted of only items from the special's board. I personally had the sweet potato enchiladas and holy crap they were good! You will not hear me say that often about a vegetarian item but I will definitely have those again. Ok, now let me go back to the chorizo stuffed dates... I order this dish every single time that I go to Frazer's and I don't see me changing this pattern anytime soon. Frazer and his crew are doing some amazing things here with, to be quite honest, a food item that I have long since avoided, the date. You get 4 of what looks like a small meatball, in a spicy tomato sauce. Not having seen how they make these, I won't even begin to act like I know how they're prepared but let me sum it up for you: they take a ball full of MAGIC and wrap it in a strip of BACON. Yes, I said it, BACON! Simultaneously you taste a little spicy, from the chorizo, sweet, from the date, salty from the bacon, and acidic from the tomato sauce, in what is an incredibly delicate balance of awesome flavors. I could honestly go on about the stuffed dates for hours but all I really need to say is get off your butt, trek out in the snow (it's worth it) and get yourself and order of your own. Now! Oh yeah, they have beers and cool stuff like that too. Be sure to get your drink on while you're at it. Bacon!

They are a ma and pa type hardware store with a huge drive in lumber yard in the back. Sometimes I go to home depot out of convenience for all hardware/home repair needs, but 3 times now, I've gone to Home Depot looking for a specific piece of hardware (screws nuts bolts), or something needed to do a basic home repair, and home depot has been out of it...or their stock was in such disorder that I gave up trying to find it after digging through the unopened boxes of stuff. I go to Channel City, am greeted by a friendly howdy at the counter and what do you know, they have exactly what I'm looking for exactly where it should be. The staff is ma and pa shop friendly. You can drive your vehicle right up to the stacks of lumber in huge yard in back...no more loading it on to a cart, dragging it up to the front counter, having them awkwardly look for the barcode on the end of each piece, then rolling out to your car in the lot. text: This is easily the best of the three bus company (other two-greyhound and new century bus) options for my fortnightly trip down to Baltimore. Before I get into the review, I want to give you some advice for riding the Apex bus to DC (Baltimore). - Buy your ticket online and print it out before arriving at the station. - Be sure to check in at the office 30 min. before your departure (FYI this is 45 min. for greyhound). - Leave at least a 2 hr. buffer between your ETA and your next scheduled event. - Avoid using the mobile bathroom on the bus. I love this company for three reasons: 1) I can bring my bike on the bus without hassle. 2) Planning ahead by buying a ticket online guarantees that you will make it to your destination at a reasonable time. 3) Some of the buses have free wireless internet. ---------------------- 1) Greyhound and AMTRAK both require that you break your bicycle down and put it into a box. They will charge you for the box if you don't have one and they lack tools to help you do this (no surprise really). The Apex and other "chinatown" bus drivers are very cool about bikes. Often they take me around to the other side or open up extra compartments under the bus to help me find space. However, the first come, first serve system puts those with large luggage items (like bikes) at a severe disadvantage (see 2). 2) Apex is especially good because they give priority to those who planned ahead and bought online tix. This means that those with e-tickets board the bus before those who purchased their tix at the station; however, e-tickets are only good for a specific bus where the purple tix sold at the station are good anytime. Bear in mind that they do not regulate the online ticket purchases, so during holiday weekends, when they get overloaded, they cope by scheduling multiple buses instead of limiting ticket sales. Not all of the buses arrive at the same time (some are up to an hour later), but they get you where you need to go. 3) Apex recently purchased some new buses that are equipped with wireless internet. I imagine the facilities are nicer as well, but come on people. Remember when your parents told you to use the bathroom before long trips. That was meant to be a life-long lesson.

text: Best grocery store ever. Yes, this location is too small, and it turns into the Thunderdome on weekends. text: This is my first Yelp review, so bare with me. I am a vegan whose favorite Philadelphia restaurants include Rangoon, Mi Lah, and Horizons. I also like Blue Sage a good deal. As you may know, or may have gathered from these reviews, Thoreau is the new restaurant from the Blue Sage owners. First, the much discussed ambiance/space. It is a bit cramped. We (I went with a friend) were lucky enough to get the table in the back, near the server station and kitchen, which was far enough away from the general seating that it was a bit private. But, if the restaurant was packed, and I had to sit super close to another party, I'd be complaining about it right now, as that's a huuuge pet peeve of mine. The decor is very sparse. Sort of greyish walls with a couple pieces of abstract art. The decor is passable, if not a bit boring. First Impressions of the Menu: Pricey. Entrees average $22. This seems to put the price point a tad above Horizons, and way above Mi Lah, Rangoon, and most delicious Asian restaurants. But, if the food is good, then it would obviously be worth it. Soup: We ordered the soup of the day, which was some sort of Indonesian Peanut soup. It was good. It was pretty tasty with wholesome chunks of sweet potatoes, fresh herbs on top, and peanuts. It was very filling. We split it, and it served to fill us up a great deal. The soup could have been a bit spicier for my taste, but it was good just the same. I'd give it a B+. For me, the soup has always been the best part about Blue Sage. Well, that and the Paninis or Pubanos or whatever they call them. Entrees: Ouch. I'll say up front, neither of us enjoyed our entrees. My friend ordered the "Blue Plate: Rosette of purple Okinawa sweet potatoes atop sweet corn gravy, grilled avocado with edamame succotash, brochette of Szechwan carrot syrup-glazed shiitakes." The potatoes were lacking flavor big-time. Their lovely swirling presentation and texture was the best part, but they had no kick, no butteriness, no garlic flavor, nothing. The seared avocado was good and creamy, and the edamame was, well, edamame. The mushrooms were good. The tangy sauce that covered them was interesting enough, but they were completely slathered in this sauce, and it was a bit overwhelming in this way. I wanted to enjoy a bit more of the natural mushroom flavor, rather than only this tangy sauce. I ordered the "Tamarind Peanut Noodles soba noodles, grilled asparagus, chopped peanuts and many herbs in sweet-spicy tamarind-kaffir lime broth. topped with tatsoi-white asparagus salad." And I'm still regretting it. This dish was odd, ill-conceived, and terribly muddled. I kept picturing Gordon Ramsay going raving mad over this sorry dish. In short, it tasted like a strange mix of spaghetti and tomato sauce with asian flavor notes. The peanut noodles lay on the very bottom of the plate, in a wet, watery mess of sauce. There were about 2 asparagus stalks total, which were good. There were a few tiny red/purple potatoes that were ok. The greens on top of it all were really out of place. While they looked nice, they just did not seem to fit the dish at all. Additionally, there were whole cooked shallots throughout, that were a bit slimy as well. I ate about 1/5th of it, and threw in the towel. This dish sounded great on paper, but again, came off as a strange mix of a sort of sweet tomato sauce with faint hints of asian flavor. I could never picture eating it again. Dessert: Was good! We got the Blue Sage staple of chocolate mousse with caramelized bananas and some sort of cookie. The mousse was delightfully rich, and I enjoyed gluttonous bites of all three elements. Service: Was excellent. Out server was sweet as can be, on the ball, and very attentive. I forgot: They offer some sort of butter (for the OK bread) that we were told was sweet pepper or something, I forget exactly what it was supposed to be, anyway it tasted like nothing but butter. Except it was orange. In closing: Based on our experience, Thoreau is a bit overpriced for mostly subpar food. I understand that it may be organic and stuff, and that's great. But, I cannot see how my dish, or my friend's, should have been $22. $14, maybe. The presentation and preparation are evident, and impressive, so there is that, but still. A handful of soba noodles, 2 stalks of asparagus, some greens, shallots and a couple potatoes in sauce = $22? Without a protein? No thanks. Here's the thing. I will still get food from this restaurant, because I think it can get better. Only, I will order the soups, which at Blue Sage, are consistently good, and can be a meal for one, as well as the Pubano(s) which are always very savory and delicious. I will not risk $22 on another subpar entrée though. I desperately wanted to love Thoreau, but didn't. Maybe in the future, with some improvements, I will love it. Until then, it's soups, pubanos, and dessert for me.

text: The Drafting Room is a staple for beer lovers in the Chester County area. Voted one of the "Top 50 Places to Have a Beer in America" (based on BeerFly Reviews - link at bottom of this review), the Drafting Room goes well above and beyond to ensure its draughts are different, desirable, and delicious. In 2007 alone, they tapped 313 different beers, most from well-regarded US microbreweries, with a focus on Mid-Atlantic brews from Sly Fox, Victory, Brooklyn, Weyerbacher, Oomegang, and others (see their site for the full 2007 list). As Erin mentioned in her review they always have Lindemans' Lambics on draught (though not always framboise), and their bottle selection is similarly exceptional. In short, The Drafting Room is probably the best taproom in the area for anyone wanting to surprise themselves with some excellent beer choices from the finest crafters in the US and beyond (although TJ's Everyday is making a run for it). The DR also occasionally hosts beer events there on Saturday and Sunday afternoons, such as "Heavyweight Down for the Count" to say goodbye to the beloved NJ brewery and other tastings. These can get crowded but are a lot of fun and the people that are attracted are lively area beer aficionados. The icing on the cake is that the DR's food is great too. The nachos aren't the hugest I've seen but are perhaps the best in the area (they use the tri-color chips and put a layer of refried beans on the plate for dipping). They have an excellent weekend brunch buffet with many delicious choices such as made-to-order omlettes, roast beef, waffles, bread pudding, salmon, maki roll, bagels, home fries, mac & cheese, pastries, salads, etc. Seating can be scarce so be sure to make a reservation. They know how to make a good Bloody Mary so if you go for the brunch, give one a try. The waitstaff is universally cheerful and pleasant. Unlike most places, we tend to get in jokey conversations with our waitstaffers whenever we visit, because they seem so open, laid back, and approachable. They have a few outdoor tables in front of the bar area that I highly recommend if the weather permits. I've had a few wonderful evenings out there sipping great beers and munching on tasty appetizers. The only thing that is lacking, in my opinion (and those that I know that frequent the DR), is the decor. The DR has been very successful but they haven't updated their decor in a long time and I've heard their bar area described as "airport bar chic" (sarcastically). I share the opinion that it's time for them to roll some money into renovating and updating the worn & dated interior to enrich the overall experience, but this is a small gripe among so many positives. If you love beer and are in the area, you should also hit Victory Brewing Company, about 15minutes drive from the Drafting Room. Links: Top 50 Places to Have a Beer in America: http://beeradvocate.com/acbw/2006/places Victory Brewing Company: http://www.yelp.com/biz/victory-brewing-company-downingtown#hrid:44jhQi6hBzd_W8VFvxWDrw Heavyweight Down for the Count: http://www.brewlounge.com/2006/08/beer-event-heavyweight-down-for-count.html TJ's Everyday (about 15 Minutes from the DR): http://www.yelp.com/biz/tjs-everyday-paoli#hrid:BtYI0g_bjgxzkjZHv0dQHA

text: Prove It! is a testing service that provides online technical tests for various disciplines. Never *ever* attempt to use this service. They are so incompetent that they can't even ask the questions correctly! There are numerous typos in the example code and questions that makes it *impossible* to answer many of them correctly. I took the Ruby 1.8 test, and in *multiple* places there is code that will not run, due to typos or incompetence, that you are expected to answer as if it were valid. If they can't spend literally two seconds to copy and paste their test code into a Ruby interpreter to see if it even compiles or runs, how in the world can they be trusted to even know the correct answers to their own questions? You end up having to guess what the questioner really was trying to ask. Imagine seeing a question like this: Q. 2 + 2 = ? A. 7 B. 3.6 C. -4 D. All of the above Now you have to guess... is the -4 a typo for 4? Is the 3.6 correct because it's the closest to 4? Should "All of the above" actually be "None of the above", but the question writer was too distracted to notice? Or was the question itself wrong, and the guy meant to write "2 + 5" instead of "2 + 2"? There's simply no possible way to answer this correctly without guessing. That is exactly analogous to many of the questions in the test I took. Stay away from these people, they are incompetent charlatans, and you simply cannot trust the results of their tests. If you are basing your hiring decisions on the results of these tests, there is a very good chance you are missing out on the really good candidates who will throw their hands up in frustration after they see so many completely impossible to answer questions. (FYI, just so you know I'm not simply writing this review due to bitterness about my own personal score. In fact, I was told I scored higher on this test than anyone else so far... I'm not upset about my score, I'm upset that these idiots have the audacity to judge people when they can't get it right themselves.)

text: Started off a 7-bar pub crawl on Saturday at "The Mack". Three ordered the steak sandwich and I went with the 1 lb "Man Burger" (I knew I'd score some of the steak from my petit bride). The burger was fantastic. If you've read my recent O'Connell's burger review you'll see I was none too fond of their offering. The Mack's burger blows O'Connell's burger away. Ironically, O'Connell's was just named the number 1 St Louis area burger according to the RFT. I challenge anyone to try them side by side and prefer O'Connell's flavorless bloodbath of ground-beef. Anyway, huge props for this massive, tasty cheeseburger, nicely priced at $7.50. That all said, I should have gone for the steak sammy, as was the original plan. From what I tasted of my lady's sandwich, it was the best cutlet of steak I've had in all of St Louis. Yes, it was better than anything I have tasted at Tucker's Place (and I've had a steak or ten there). Trimmed of fat and gristle, the 5 chunks of perfectly-seasoned steak served between two pieces of cheese garlic bread were a steak-lover's dream. At $9 for the sandwich and side, I'd challenge anyone to find a better or larger cut of steak in the land. I have had dozens of mediocre steak sandwiches in my day. You know the ones where you take a bite and the entire piece of steak comes off in your teeth as you try to bite through the sinew and gristle, then inevitably have to spit a chunk of it into a napkin because there's no way it's fitting down the gullet? None of that here. I would estimate that the total weight of the 5 chunks of steak after cooking to be around 16 oz (or more). This is a bargain by anyone's standards. Golden Tee on the widescreen. SilverStrike antiquated 2007 version. Nice side room for steel tip darts (5 boards). Friendly staff. Several flat screens. Bon appetit!

text: Not unexpected, the beer at the Iron Hill Brewery is far superior to the food. I went with family in the late afternoon and we started with beers and appetizers. We'd ordered the egg roll sampler including a Tex Mex egg roll, a cheese steak egg roll and one with salmon in it that I didn't get to try. The Tex Mex egg roll was very tasty and the cheese steak egg roll was interesting, not bad but not the way a cheese steak ought to be eaten. The rest of the table informed me that the salmon egg roll was very tasty, so I'll have to take them at their palates. We also ordered the crab quesadilla which was rather scrumptious and came in quite a large portion! The last app we'd ordered was the artichoke & cheese dip -- please avoid this. It was bland and just a waste of an app. For dinner, I ordered the Macaroni and Four Cheese made with black forest ham, sweet peas, vidalia onions and an almond crumb topping. It was pretty yummy, but the cheese/sauce was very thing and it was made with ziti, which just didn't seem right. Definitely sticking to Bethlehem Brew Works mac&cheese from now on. I did get to sample a Belgian meatball which was delightful: they came in a roasted mushroom sauce that was divine. Major thumbs up for the Raspberry Wheat beer, the Dunkelweizen, the seasonal Belgian IPA, the Vienna Red Lager, and the Le Monstre. Not disappointed by a single one. Iron Hill is trying to cater to a more affluent clientele, made apparent by their hoity-toity menu options, but really, it's a bit over the top. Definitely stick to the beer.

text: Yesterday afternoon I called my vet because my cat was obviously having some pain and symptoms of being sick. They told be that because he was going to the bathroom, it was not an emergency situation, and to make an appointment for tomorrow (today). This morning when we woke up, my boyfriend and I saw that our beloved cat was unable to move and looked like he was dying. We called this emergency service, and they let us know that it sounded like renal failure and would be 1500 to help him. 1500 dollars that they needed up front, and even if we brought him there and he was dying, without being paid up front they wouldn't be able to do anything for him. This was their words, not ours. Our vet doesn't open till 9, and at around 7:45, my cat Oliver died. Words can not express how sad I am, and how heartless this practice is. I'm angrier than I have been in a very long time. I understand that they want to limit the amount of unpaid bills they have, but to just let an animal die because we didn't have the full amount up front, makes no sense to me. Two years ago we used them because another cat of ours was rough housing and did something wonky to his leg. It was on new years eve, and they did fine work, though they never really found out what was wrong, just gave us some meds. We took him to our own vet to check up after. But now? All 5 of us ordered different stuff and not one of us enjoyed our meal. Lots of leftovers, and no one requested a doggie bag. That about says it all. I won't ever be back. Additionally, the seating was wobbly, high and uncomfortable with no where to hook your purse over the chair. All three of the women on this outing noticed this and were miffed by it. Since eating there I've moved to Texas where we have GOOD Tex-Mex, but even in Edmonton I've had better examples of this cuisine. text: After reading some the negative reviews on here, I had major doubts about this place, but since I haven't had any Chinese food for over two weeks, my craving out voted my logic, plus I was going to watch a movie at Ritz next door anyway, it's the convenience. I walked in and this place was huge, I swear I heard my echo saying "table for one...one...one" it was sort of sad to see only one other person eating by herself, I figure it maybe still early for a weekday. Instead of seating me near the other lady, the waiter/owner sat me by the window, I guess it would look good for people passing by to see an Asian eating in a Chinese restaurant, I'm onto this guy. My plan was to order a noodle soup since this is a "Noodle Café" but after browsing thru the menu, my craving out voted my logic again, and I ended up ordering the Curry Lamb with rice and a Tsingtao. Interesting on the menu was the Chef's Special "Lam with Black Bean Sauce" and "Explosive Shrimp", someone didn't proof read before printing, well maybe they did, it was charming in a way. My dish on the menu showed a picture of a chili, at the bottom it said "Mean Hot & Spicy", well it really meant it. Sweat was pouring out like I was in a sauna, but it was so tasty I couldn't stop eating, I asked for extra rice to mop up all the curry sauce, and thankfully I had extra Tsingtao to replenish my lost fluid. In a way I was cleansed, my system flushed. When I left it was around 7:30, there were no other patron in the restaurant, no one came in between, I thought of going back to give them more business after the show, but after 2 hours I was still way too full. The location may not be the best, as it's off the main street, but it's next to Ritz East with plenty of parking, the restaurant is actually a part of the parking garage, and there were even more parking in front as well. Next time when I'm in the neighborhood I'll order the noodle soup, logic will out vote craving at least once.

The past handful of times I've been, however, they have really been pushing a LOT of extras (fuel system cleaning, power steering fluid change, etc.) It's just plain annoying. I have to endure a relatively passive sales pitch from the person keying in the information up-front and then, after I have sat down for a minute or two, am called out for an aggressive sales pitch from another employee. They essentially use scare-tactics. My favorite time was when a mechanic pulled out my oil dipstick, pointed at it, and told me about how I obviously needed a fuel system cleaning. He quickly changed gears and after trying to get me to agree to a few other unnecessary services, let me sit back down. text: No review of California surf beaches would be complete without a tip of the hat and a bow to the queen herself, Rincon. Rincon, the "little corner" by the sea, possesses one of the finest waves anywhere, bar none. This is California's tame version of South Africa's famous Jeffrey's Bay and it's why it has earned the honorific of the "Queen of the Coast". And rightfully so. Catch a big, outside wave here and you'll never forget it. With the right swell, you can take a wave from the outer reef and ride it all the way to the freeway, one of the longest rides you'll ever get and your legs will feel like rubber when you finally kick-out. A quarter mile? It'll feel like it! The shape of the wave is ideal for both short or long-boarders and both species will be vying for the perfect take-off position. While never as crowded or aggressive as Malibu, it does get packed at times and you should be prepared to stand up for your right to surf. Show respect and, most of the time, it will be returned. With internet weather projections and beach cams available at the tip of your finger, everyone knows about the approaching swell and it's getting more crowded out there every time...something you just have to get used to. So while Rincon will always offer one of the best waves in the US, it's no cake-walk and you'll have to earn your place in the line-up. If you're shy, you might as well stay home. However, there's always some good news: All the homes in the area have old. leaky septic tank sewage systems. That means they leach waste sewage right into the surf zone. Can you spell "giardia"? Many people won't surf here after a storm...some people don't want to get sick. I know, I was side-lined for a week after surfing a big ground-swell a couple years ago, on the tail end of a storm. So pollution can be your friend, in a sick, twisted way. "Hey Robin, was it worth it?" you ask. "Oh, hell yeah!" (big grin) (it'll be a perfect score when they replace the septic systems)

text: Let me start by saying that I am a big fan of provel cheese. I wouldn't say that I'm a die hard fan nor would I make the claim that it's "DA BEST CHEEZ EVAR!" but I do enjoy it on occasion. Enter Imo's pizza, another iconic restaurant with a long standing tradition in Saint Louis- famed for being one of the first pizzeria's here to not only use Provel instead of Mozzarella, but also claim to be the pioneers of thin crust pizza. I can't say I'm a huge fan of their pizza. Please! Be reasonable! Before you throw the first stone, hear me out! Do as I did when I went this last time, order your favorite pizza and get half of it mozzarella and half provel. I got a deluxe. I really liked the provel side. I like that the cheese is creamy and sweet. How it somehow homogenizes the tastes of all ingredients into something rich and unique. I also have to admit that it's easier to eat since I don't have to play cat's cradle whenever I pull a slice from the pan. All in all, I can see why this unique flavor has kept Imo's in business over the years. A taste of the mozzarella side provided some further insight. Without the unique flavoring of the provel as a crutch, the pizza was, well, terrible. The veggies on my deluxe were sopping wet (not to mention the whole damn pizza!)- most likely an indicator that they used frozen vegetables. Which is a violation of Pizza 101- NEVER USE FROZEN INGREDIENTS! Running the frozen stuff through the ovens only thaw the ingredients...which means you end up with a lot of excess water on the pizza AND uncooked ingredients. Additionally, all ingredients were somewhat flavorless compared to the provel side, and, as the last straw, the mozzarella was very tacky and chewy- a noxious entity in it's own right. If I woke up in the middle of the night craving pizza, would I hold vigil until Imo's opened? No. If I were passing by an Imo's and felt a craving for pizza, would I return? Probably not. But for those who have never experienced provel on pizza, I think it's worth a shot. Just once. Why not?

text: As Downtown residents, the beautiful wife and I (well, it was really my idea) decided to finally get down to Union Station. And hopefully I'll be knocking it up another star. However, for the rest of Union Station (a.k.a. the "mall" part), yeah, it's fairly sad -- very touristy and not practical for Downtown residents. BUT, that's not the point of it -- the point is to have a place to get the tourists to buy St. Louis souvenirs. And, it also acts as a place for people to eat -- pretty much all chains, though there are places that looked interesting (Pita King and St. Louis Taco and Grill will have to get sampled at some point). There's a fair amount of empty storefronts, but despite that, it was actually pretty busy when we went -- both outside with the paddleboats and whatnot as well as inside. Extra bonus: they have a "Hurricane Simulator" that for $2.00, you get to stand in this booth where the winds go up to 75 MPH (which yes, puts you at Category One). Best fan you'll find in St. Louis.

text: I'm in love, no really, I am. I'm the snootiest person when it comes to Mexican food, but I have found my favorite. text: Mitchell Deli is the newest addition to the burgeoning little district at McGavock and Riverside in East Nashville. This place is brand new, but it's already completely won me over. Mitchell Deli was opened by local chef David Mitchell with help from Julia Helton, formerly of The Family Wash, in March of 2008. In addition to offering a huge and diverse selection of sandwiches, this deli also sells fresh produce as well as meat and cheese by the pound. They offer a salad bar as well as breakfast by the pound in the mornings, and their soups and fresh fruit are exceptional. Mitchell's sandwiches are incredible, and I personally opt for either their Ruben or Muffaletta, both of which are piled high with cold cuts and spicy fixings. The prices are completely reasonable, especially considering the quality. Seating inside is somewhat limited, but there are plenty of tables out back on the patio. Mitchell has already proven very popular amongst the locals, and something tells me that people will probably come from far and wide to sample this tasty little joint's cheeses and locally grown organic produce. This area, at the southernmost part of Inglewood, is growing rapidly, and Mitchell looks like the best spot to grab a casual lunch. The staff is friendly (but constantly swamped), and I guarantee you can't just go once.

text: I was just here on Friday with two friends and I was pretty unimpressed. While the futuristic, mod decor was kind of cool, it wasn't that different from places in New York I had already been to (It had the same chairs as Spice on University Pl.) Sadly, the food in the restaurant was not as good as these other restaurants. We all split the chicken dumpling and the sweet and sour pork dumplings (each about ~$9) which were actually pretty good (but not phenomenal.) For an entree, I ordered the wasabi crusted filet mignon with wasabi mashed potatoes ($29!) I'm not sure how it was screwed up, but the outside was very well done, but the inside was so rare that it made me fear eating it. At least the mashed potatoes were okay. My sister had a $25 sashimi plate that was "decent, but not the best." Our other friend had the crispy grilled pork tenderloin ($19) that was surprisingly 75% fried outside. Tastewise, it was reminiscent of a chicken nugget. Our drinks were okay, but nothing great once again. At the end of the meal, we felt we had just wasted a whole bunch of money on our food and cab fare to West Philly.

text: Good place for a business lunch. Went there with no expectations at all and was frankly surprised... Enough to write a review about it, even. Three reasons to visit for lunch: 1) The Tomato Basil soup. Awesome. Fresh strong basil flavor and peppery. 2) Smoked Rainbow Trout. Sublime. Smoky, creamy, and light. 3) The price. About 12 bucks. Not bad for a full tasty lunch.

text: Support your local library! They offer amazing free programs in addition to books, music, movies, and more! The music selection at this library is impressive. I enjoy looking at the exhibits, too. Update: after visiting other libraries, I was reminded at how sad this main library can be. It obviously needs the planned renovations. Had to take off a star because of the way some holdings are 'stored' (meaning, leaned up against a wall or shoved atop a cabinet). To be fair, I will make a donation to support the renovation so rare and valuable items can be handled with more care, and the librarians won't have to work in makeshift conditions.

text: Once again, another establishment that receives high acclaim on Yelp crashes and burns in a sea of disappointment. And I thought Ted Drewes was overrated. As far as ice cream stands go, the seating, service and pricing were the standard norm. No problems there. What I do take umbrage with is the actual product. I ordered a banana and Snickers 'concrete.' Of course, my concrete could only be classified as such if we are talking about concrete before it's mixed with rocks, dirt and everything else that makes concrete solid. The actual consistency of the yogurt (or custard as the case may have been) was extremely soft and turned to soupy in no time. Faster than Ted Drews, which is saying a lot in my opinion. The flavor of the ice cream was typical for vanilla and the bananas were actually pretty fresh. But just as it seemed that Mr. Wizard's had finally clawed it's way out of its stinking cesspool, it stumbled and tipped backward in again when I crunched down on a Snickers morsel. Imagine how a Snickers ought to taste- and I have a great idea since I just had one the other day (thanks Circle K!). Imagine the smooth chocolate and caramel, the crunchy little peanuts, and the soft nougat. This was hard and brittle- like peanut brittle, brittle. All aforementioned ingredients were indistinguishable from each other and instead was replaced with a rough, hard, amalgam flavor instead. It tasted remarkably as though it may have been sitting in a mothballed closet, forgotten by it's Alzheimer's afflicted owner. Was it edible. Of course! It's Ice Cream! I finished the small serving with no problem. I would like to add, however, that shoe leathers are edible if given no other alternative. I would not recommend, nor would I go back to Mr. Wizards of my own free will. However, if a friend was really psych'd about going, I would be willing to go back in case my experience had been a fluke.
label: NEG

text: Two stars because once, when I was there, I saw a gigantic roach on the floor. (I still eat there. I am lying to myself that it just came in through the open door.) I literally live across the street from Royal Pizza, which makes it very easy to justify dropping in. It is cheap, the food is decent, and they are really fast (calling for a personal pizza will have it ready in under 10 minutes, depending on how busy it is). The same personal pizza, probably enough for two meals, is under $5. In fact, I don't think I've ever spent more than $10. There is no seating so it's only good for takeout... not that you'd really want to eat in there. It's always a billion degrees and you can smell it 100 feet away! The food is nothing remarkable. I like the buffalo chicken cheesesteak although it is not great as far as those go--it just tastes like hotsauce and is light on the cheese. The pizza is more of the crispy, buttery crust that you sometimes find in this city...not bad but not always what you want for a pizza. It's very greasy, so it's satisfying late at night, but you feel a little ill afterwards. My favorite thing to order is the chicken souvlaki, however, which you wouldn't think to find at such a pizza place. But the pita is warm and lovely and salty, the meat is well seasoned, and their tzatziki offers a nice, cool counterpart. Every tim I go in there, though, I picture that bug. :(
label: NEG

In my opinion, this place is just a spruced up 60's-era motel. Granted, they've added some nice touches like a very comfy bed and some decent bath products, but it wasn't as nice as I had hoped for. The nicer inns I had checked with have a 2-night minimum on the weekends so that didn't work for us. There's really nothing wrong with this place I suppose, but it just didn't grab me. text: On my visit, food was just ok, service was terrible. Waiter's were non attentive and very condescending, my wife did not feel well on our visit and ordered a soft drink, I had a beer. We did not have a large bar tab (obviously), and we felt ignored during our meal (perhaps due to the small bar tab - but not sure) and got poor service - felt like we were being snubbed. My wife ordered a chicken dish with a mediterannean rub, and it was too highly seasoned, she took one bite and did not touch it again, wait staff did not ask if all was ok until plates were ready to be cleared. Again, this was very poor service - a fine restaurant would approach a customer if, after a few minutes, they do not appear to be touching their meal, and see what is wrong and do what they can to address the issue - this restaurant staff did none of the right things. Served 4 petit fours at the end of the meal as an offering of their apologies - wound up being a meaningless effort after a poor meal where we were ignored - again - doing the right things at the right time would have resulted in a far better experience - this restaurant either did not have the understanding, committment or attitude to do any of the right things. There are many fine restaurants in New Orleans and this was one of them (would recommend some very consistent old standards such as Commander's Palace, K-Paul's, Emeril's and others that deliver fine service and great food consistently) - will never return to this restaurant again and cannot recommend.

text: If you haven't had a Domino's pizza at least once in your life, you've probably either not been in the country long or your parents sheltered you. If that's the case I envy you. If I had never had one I wouldn't be as perplexed as to how poor the general populations' taste is. How much cornmeal can you slap onto the bottom crust of a pizza? Dominoes probably hits the limit allowed by physics, because their pizza tastes cheifly of corn. And the sauce may as well be ketchup. Why would you want pizza that tastes like corn chips? Why would you purchase more than one of these? Why has Domino's not gone out of business or made like Little Caesars and been pigeonholed to Kmarts and creepy towns in North Jersey? Oddly vivid memory for my age when it happened: In early 1993 in my old house in Mayfair I was palaying T2: Judgement Day (Arcade Edition) on Sega Genesis with a friend when we heard a loud crash outside the window. Going outside, we discovered a Domino's pizza boy had rear-ended an elderly couple in a Dodge coupe, and caused gasoline to spew everywhere. Luckily, no one was seriously injured. It's stuff like that that ended the whole 30 minutes or your pizza is free thing. So they try other campaigns like $5 pizzas when you order 3. $15 for 3 small barely-edible pizzas? DEAL! Embrace the Noid.
