text: Warning! Do not stay at this Ramada Inn! My family took a short vacation to Reno last weekend and decided to give the Ramada a chance. We stayed in a two bedroom suite, which is very spacious, but very outdated. I also don't recommend swimming in the pool if you expect it to be heated like they advertise; because clearly it is not. Our children only lasted five minutes in the pool before the temp. became unbearable. My BIGGEST complaint with this hotel occured during the night. Shortly after we put the children to bed we started to smell cigerette smoke in our room. We are not smokers so it was obvious the smell was coming from an outside source. My husband called the front desk and we were informed they were full for the night and did not have anywhere to move us. They said that the smoke was probably coming from their "old vent system." In otherwords, someone was smoking in a near by room. We were told this was a non- smoking hotel. The staff at the Ramada was not concerned at all that our daughter is allergic to smoke. The next morning our daughter wolk up and could not speak at all. Her voice was gone due to breathing in smoke all night. She did not recover from this attick for 24 hours. To make matters worse the hotel was not willing to compensate us at all. I will never stay at this hotel again.

text: Had my hubby's bday party @ Chifa last night, staff was very nice in arranging it for us, and we got into the Machu Picchu booth, which was fun and felt "exclusive," but honestly, food wasn't great. I was so so excited for it, as the website and menu are exciting, but overall, ideas were not executed well, and boy were most dishes salty! We all shared many dishes and here they are: CEVICHE: *Hiramasa: pretty good; fresh fish, like 7 pieces, but emulsion was not strong enough to pop, as it is at Alma de Cuba MIXTOS: *Shellfish: most disappointing dish of the evening; deconstructed paella with a bar of rice (tasted like rubber), cold mussels and shrimp in an emulsion (tasteless and meh), couldn't taste the one tiny paper thin chorizo circle *Duck Ceviche: cold chopped duck in uninspiring sauce DIM SUM: *Pork Belly Buns: pork was tasty, but the rice bun isn't as good as Chinatown's; overall salty *Chicken Wings: 4 TINY wings and ok (salty!) but has nothing on Pearl Akoya's *BBQ Ribs: yummy, but once again, small, salty, and nothing special NOODLES & RICE: *Chaufa: didn't try it but my friends said it was just overwhelming MSG *Red Curry del General: ok; tasted like any thai dish SPECIALTIES: *Wagyu Skirt: wayy too salty; I'm a hypertaster but my hubby is a dull taster, and said it was a little salty. Portion small for price FISH: *Hot Pot: cod was yummy and delicate (as it always is), but broth full of MSG and just any other asian dish *Chupe: solid; we all enjoyed this one *Hiramasa: the best dish we had; fish well cooked (though honestly Marigold Kitchen does it better), clams yummy, chorizo great DESSERT: *Funnel Cake: it tasted...weird...powdery and with a metallic aftertaste, and grilled basil over it?! The banana sorbet was yummy though. I seriously hope that Tinto is better. Was rooting for Garces (we think Starr is overrated and that his ambiance is better than his food), but am starting to change my mind. Amada was better.

text: Over the past 6 years, my best friend has lived in these apartments. Although they have a decent amount of space for the cost, it is not a decent place to live. Aside from the questionable tenants constantly moving in and out, the complete lack of attention to malfunctioning appliances, water heaters, plumbing issues, and air conditioning units is appalling. The routine for the past six years has gone as follows: something breaks (because it's old usually), my friend calls the front office, they may or may not send a maintenance person, they don't fix it, and it later ends up on fire because it is malfunctioning (this is an absolutely true thing that happened to both the dishwasher and hot water heater). At this point, they actually consider it a problem and fix it... or "repair" it. Recently, the air conditioning has been out for weeks. Instead of someone coming out to fix it (after repeated phone calls) someone came out and turned it off. That's all. Now, because it's been trying so hard to work at keeping the apartment below 80 degrees but simply cannot, the electricity bill is 157% higher than any time in the past. I understand maintenance people are busy when in charge of an entire apartment complex. It is not, however, ok to decide that something that is potentially a fire hazard or negatively effects basic living conditions is fine to neglect at the renter's expense. Perhaps if their lack of response was an isolated instance, I would not hold this complex in such contempt, but as it is, it's a normal occurrence to have to badger the front office to get anything done. This complex is certainly not worth the rent it's charging. I would avoid it at all costs.

text: I came here for a few NBA Finals game and I love it here! Décor: You got your bar right when you walk in and you got the rest of the restaurant with all the large flat-screen TV's. I LOVE sitting in the front part of the restaurant where this like.. 4-foot screen is in front of like 3 tables. I am literally like 4 feet away from this gigantic screen. LOVE it!!! Service: The waitresses are quick, friendly and know how to serve! I have never had a problem and you seat yourselves and they'll notice you pretty quickly. I don't know how they do it, lol. It's just like bread with whatever cheese you want smushed inside and you pull it apart when it's all gooey and melted. mmmMMmm * Baked chicken wings: I don't even need to describe these, since other Yelpers already got this covered! I got the Honey BBQ ones before and I think a spicy mild one. It's not that spicy, but either one is pretty delicious. I like that interesting crisp that isn't on normal fried chicken wings slathered with sauce. * Honey Wheat Crust BBQ Chicken Pizza: You can't really mess up a BBQ Chicken Pizza, but what I loved the most? THE CRUST. You can taste that wheat crust and they slather on honey in it and roll it up I think. It's SO GOOOD. And the nice bbq kick with the onions? Yummmmm. * Quesadilla Appetizer: decently-sized. And pretty good, nothing to rave about but nothing to complain about either! They have your sides of guac and sour cream without asking, so that's nice! * Philly Cheesesteak: BF thought it was okay, not great but not horrible. * Gyros w/fries: decently sized! A bit dry with the meat, but still okay. Beers and stuff are a better deal if you go to any of the big sporting events. Price: Pretty good! Usually around ~$10+ a person? Bottom Line: This place is GREAT if you and your friends want to catch a game while eating some decent food. Not a smokey or obnoxiously loud environment. Very chill and nice people come here, so thumbs up! J

text: The ambiance in this place is pretty awesome, it almost seems like you walk back in time to the olden days of taverns and beer wenches. That being said...the con's outweigh the pro's.... text: "More Like a Poly-Cotton Blend" Tweed, you're new, so I'm going to give you some tough love in the hopes that you improve. Because you have the potential to shine. I was squealing with joy at the prospect of trying Tweed. Perhaps I expected too much so soon after launch. The big sell is local ingredients. I like this, so I'll sprinkle some stars. The space itself is quite handsome and the location can't be beat. More stars. My appetizer, yellowtail sashimi with various sauces, was just OK. The fish was tasty. The fish-to-sauce ratio however was perplexing. Four pieces of fish, five sauces. That leaves one sauce in the lonely. Cutting the sashimi pieces into even smaller pieces was not an intuitive solve. The sauces, ranging from squid ink to cayenne, wasabi and creme fraiche, were too heavy and at times, a bit nauseating. The squid ink sauce in particular: it has the consistency and interest of tar. My lamb entree with a smidge of kale was fine, but not notable in any way. It was attractively sliced. It was nicely plated. It was a bit undercooked. It was neither delicious nor undelicious. It simply lacked oomph. The kale provided no contrast or texture and seemed besides the point. One nice touch: I was served cucumber water. But then, it was topped off with un-cucumbered water. In other words, diluted cucumber water. Something to fix. My dining companion had the soup of the day (a gazpacho, I think) and the chicken. Both were pretty but not necessarily tasty. And now, some star-smashers: - The service - Rule #1: Know your menu. If your menu says the yellowtail sashimi appetizer is plated with "a painter's palate of colors and flavors," be prepared to tell me what that means. (It was blots of different-colored/flavored sauces.) And if I ask you what panna cotta is, please don't try to bluster through and fake it. It breaks the illusion of feeling like you're somewhere special. Rule #2: Pace yourselves. Allow people to be fully seated before you start asking what they want to drink. My lap had barely formed. And give me literally more than one second from the time my fork hits the plate before you pounce the table and clear it. Rule #3: If you don't like the gays, maybe don't wait tables in the Gayborhood. From the moment we were seated, I got the feeling that the waiter was uncomfortable serving two men. (Other servers were great.) It's not something he said, it's not something he did. My friend put it this way: "He didn't say one more word to us than he had to." Now, I don't need to be draped in a rainbow flag or fed a dildo lolly to feel I'm welcome. But do try to manage your bro tone. It might hurt a little. That's OK. - The dessert - The carrot cake roulade was blah. It's two Hostess Ho Ho-type roll-ups dressed fancy. The cake component was faint on flavor. The filling, goat and cream cheese, lent none of the freshness that goat cheese should. The butter pecan ice cream was frozen, rough, inadequately emulsified, and in a nose-thumbing to science, curiously dry. The dish was finished with praline-type crumbles, which did not provide the hoped-for save. Rather they had the panache of gravel. Good coffee helped balance things out. - A note on design - Should you wish to use the bathroom, you will need to pass behind the grand center staircase. Good luck. Clearance is tight and the lighting is low; consequently I nearly clonked my head on the back of the stairs. Overall Tweed has the right idea. Outstanding menu, if not outstandingly executed and served. I'll give it some more time as it merits a second glance.
label: NEG

text: I agree that the service is sweet. I agree that the decor is charming and cheerifying (i.e. makes you cheery). I agree that the prices are very reasonable. Yep, I'd gotten a Medium cone, which translates in Bobbie's Dairy Dip-speak into a small cone piled high with a towering mound of soft-serve ice cream. I'd ordered the cone dipped (on the advice of several other Yelpers), but the chocolate dip must be somewhat warm because there was melting ice cream oozing out from under the dipped shell from the moment the cone was handed to me. But I wanted the full dipped-cone-experience. So anyway, by the time I had demolished the top half of the cone, there was like a river of ice cream running down my hand and onto a pile of napkins that the girl at the counter had generously handed to me. It's kind of horrifying to know that the ice cream on your cone is melting, but you can't do anything about it because it's hidden behind a hard shell. Oh the angst. Anyway, eventually I gave up and dumped about half the cone in the trash. I'll go back, but any future cones are going to be naked (un-dipped) and I may just have to go totally stress-free with a shake or sundae. Oh I'm definitely going to order a Small, which I assume will translate into a Large, but hopefully not ridonkulously Large. ps - Bring clean wipes. Even after using all the napkins, I was glad I had something else to wipe my hands and save the interior of my car from becoming irredeemably sticky.

text: In Portland we have a Goodwill store called The Bins where giant bins are filled with random goodies and you can stock up your cart with whatever looks good and then pay by the pound. Yogurtland is The Bins of soft-serve frozen yogurt. But better. And Portland needs one. BADLY. Being new to the concept, we wandered in off State Street for some frozen goodness and did a quick recon of the situation. We got in line, grabbed a cup and waited patiently before we could actually get to the wall of yogurt spigots . Deciding was the hardest part. Each self-serve unit offered two flavors each, one on the left, one on the right, and a sexy little flavor twist of both in the middle. I didn't count, but I'd say there must have been about 16-20 flavors in all. I chose the newest flavors - Nutter Butter and S'mores, as well as the classic toasted coconut and Oreo cookie. That's right people - 4 flavors!! In one cup!! And I could have gone for more because it's SELF SERVE which means YOU have the control! A little bit of this, a lot of that, whatever your little heart desires. And THEN there is the toppings bar. OMG. Everything you can imagine from fresh fruits to nuts to cookies to candy. I put some crumbled Oreos on the Oreo cookie yogurt, some coconut on the toasted coconut yogurt, crumbled peanut butter cups on the Nutter Butter yogurt, and then threw in a couple Nilla wafers for good measure. As if all this yummy goodness wasn't enough, I reached the end of the line, and set my cup on the scale by the register. At $.30 an ounce it's hard to go wrong. I got a huge cup of delicious for $3.00, made to order by the only person who knows exactly how I like it - ME. In a way I am glad we don't have one because I might be there all the time. But after reading some other reviews of the "must" flavors I didn't try, I am ready to fly back for more. Unless someone wants to help me buy a franchise for Portland? Anyone??

I will say that they had an excellent selection of seasonal beers (magic hat, yards, dogfish - but not your everyday brews, they were all varieties that I rarely see around) The bread/crackers/oil/butter were great...but the rest was a little blah. The 'Chorizo & Wild Mushroom Fundido' was nothing as advertised...we couldn't taste chorizo and we certainly didn't find any chorizo in the dish. And the 'wild mushrooms' were comprised mainly of sliced white mushrooms (and they looked/tasted like they went to shoprite and picked them up pre-sliced). The corn tortillas were decent, but they didn't seem like they were homemade. The 'South American Shrimp' were a disappointment well...they only deveined about a third of the shrimp (which also looked like they went to shoprite and picked them up precooked)- not really what I was expecting. I was pretty excited about the 'Yellow Fin Tuna and Ginger Braised Short Ribs' but again, the dish disappointed. They wrapped the yellow fin in sliced potatoes and then sear it so the potato should be cripsy and the tuna fairly rare...instead the potato was soggy/oily (the tuna was cooked pretty well though). The short rib looked awesome...it was removed from the bone and they cut a cube (it was square-ish to go along with the theme, but more rectangular all in all) from the meat and put it in the korean bbq sauce. The meat was way too salty and the bbq sauce was as well (again, the sauce tasted like they went to shoprite and bought a bottle of the far east brand stuff). The menu sounded extremely good, but it just didn't come together for some reason. I will not be going back for a full meal anytime soon.

The first thing that strikes you about BF is the smell. It's one of the most aromatic restaurants I've ever been in. A mixture of wine, garlic, tomato, and chorizo permeate the room. We were seated in a rather uncomfortably small booth--my dad and I had a hard time getting our legs in past the table leg. We all had the brunch specials. My dad and I had the Numero Dos, an egg+peppers+potatoes thing which came with applewood smoked bacon--DELICIOUS--a slice of toast with a tomato spread--DELICIOUS--and a fried cheese/apple "foam" thing, which wasn't really for me. The tapas style works well. The portions seem small but I'm still full, two hours later! My mom and I loved it. My dad enjoyed it, but, according to him, "It wasn't really up my alley." It's hip, it's trendy, it's probably better at night (their alcohol menu was rather extensive and local.) Definitely recommend it, but not with picky eaters. Taco Mamacita has moved in, Edgehill Cafe has new owners and a new vibe, Whats In Store, Tweed Baby Outfitters, Steadfast + True Yoga Studio, Sleeveless, Ivey, and more have reclaimed this area. Hopefully others consider Edgehill Village when they are holiday shopping because this is a really great destination to shop local and support independent businesses! Lots of gorgeous mosaics and statues of saints all around the cemeteries, too. text: This place does Bosnian right. When I say that, I don't just mean the food. EVERYTHING in this place is done well. The restaurant is beautiful and spacious. I had the cauliflower schnitzel...it was nothing short of melt in your mouth delicious, my friend tried the cevapi, a spicey Bosnian sausage and after practically licking his plate, said it was so good he wanted to order more to bring home with him. I have to say, the goulash that the woman next to me ordered made me long for my days of beef eating and steamed and smelled like it came right out of Budapest... I had no idea we had restaurants like this in St. Louis. I had no idea we had restaurants like this west of the Danube for that matter. If you are looking for a totally different type of dinner experience and looking to be filled up with what can only be described as some of the most comforting foods in creation, you have to check out Grbic.

text: Hmm... Overpriced drinks? Check. Cramped space? Check. Too few lanes, forcing a constant wait to bowl? Check. Oppressivly smoky atmosphere? Check. Charging twice as much as you'd expect for bowling? Check. Hipper-than-thou clientele? Check. Mediocre to crummy food selection? Check. Decor that tries way too hard to look cool? Check. Ok, by now you should realize this isn't a bowling alley with a bar. This is a bar that happens to have a couple of lanes for bowling. A bar that tries oh-so-hard to be upscale. The look of the Pin-Up is alright, but it has that feel of going way out of it's way to try to be unique, when in fact it's copying its style from the many "boutique bowling alleys" that have popped up in the last 5-10 years. It has the look and feel of a chain, and not in a good way. Not to belabor the point, but this place is small and crackerjack-like. Seems like I'm always bumping into someone or waiting for someone to move in order to get somewhere. I suppose this is to be expected at an expensive bar, but not at a bowling alley. Which I guess brings me to my other point. Don't go here to bowl. It's just not a place built for bowling. The lanes are too cramped together, and at this point there are regular bowling alleys that have the features that the Pin-Up does (flat screen tvs over the pins, crazy weird automatic scoring machines). Not to mention you can walk in and start playing at other alleys instead of having to wait and drown in a cloud of cigarette smoke and overpriced drinks. I don't think this place really works as a bar or a bowling alley. Because it's small, it's hard to get away to have a conversation with someone. The atmosphere seems manufacturered, like it's trying to put forth a cooler persona that it should. This place might be popular for the right crowd, but if I'm going bowling I'm going to a real bowling alley, and if I'm going to a bar, I'm going to a larger and less crowded one (and one that doesn't periodically charge a cover...wtf is up with that).

This is Tucson in the Desert!!! Dont people want to play in the water? There has to be a solution and some way to do better business. I am just disappointed in this park. text: My lovely college friend came to town visiting from Boston and I had a major decision to make. Do I show her the greasy food Philly is known for or do I show her what all Phialdelphians know, that we are indeed a city overflowing with delicious upscale restaurants that put NY and Boston to shame. I chose the latter. I was told you have to have reservations at Amada, but we had no problems getting a table on a Sunday night at 7pm. The atmosphere is lovely. Great lighting, great textures, very intimate....perfect for sharing some food together. We of course had to get a pitcher of Sangria. Amada had three choices, but we went with the refreshing white. It was great! My friend, though she hated that it had rosemary in it, raved about it and the girl was born in Mexico. The staff was wonderful, explaining things on the menu for a tapas virgin like myself. We chose some bold choices and some safe choices. The bold choices proved to be the better. We started with goat cheese on toasts with a beautiful array of roasted vegetables. Delish and a perfect start. We then moved on to garlic roasted shrimp-one of our safer choices, but done perfectly. Next was Flat Bread with Duck Confit, Jamon Serrano, Cabrales & Date Glaze. This was an even tie for my favorite dish. It was amazing! Also worth mentioning, are the lamb meatballs with manchego cheese. Beautifully plated were the spicy potatoes. As if I couldn't eat anymore, my friend wanted dessert and since the decision was too hard, we went with two choices. Banana Torrijas, which was a crispy sweet bread with caramelized Bananas, Maple Syrup Ice Cream, Banana Anglaise. This dessert punched you in the kisser with all its flavor, but surprisingly, our favorite was the Manchego Mousse. This consisted of Sheep Cheese Mousse, Pistachio Shortdough, Apple Crumb, and Apple Cider Sorbet. The flavors in the Mousse dish were so slight, layered and complex. Honestly, I thought the bill would have been so much more considering the two desserts, and the never ending pitcher of sangria, but it was about 60 dollars a person with tip. I was happy to show my Bostonian friend that Philly has so much more to offer than cheese steaks and soft pretzels- though they may be the heart of the city. I can't wait to go back!

text: I got some take-out here tonight. The location is great, and the place looked nice. I ordered an avocado salad, tofu teriyaki and a side of vegetable tempura. Romaine lettuce and grape tomatoes with sliced avocado fanned on top. I've had ginger dressing countless times, so I decided to skip that. There is so much they could've done with this sald to make it better while keeping it simple. Use darker greens. Add some herbs. Some chopped peanuts. Mango. Whatever. The tofu teriyaki. This was 6 pieces of heavily battered tofu with caramelized onions and steamed broccoli, bathed in teriyaki sauce. Now, I've had tofu and other teriyaki dishes at lots of Japanese restaurants. This tofu was weird. The batter was too thick, and since it was dressed in the teriyaki sauce, was soggy. There were too few vegetables. They could've added carrots, asparagus, so many other things that they could've used that woul'dve made this good. This came with a side of rice. It was fine. They were stingy. I haven't had the soup but it smelled good. All that said, I wouldn't not get this again. I tried the teriyaki sauce on its own. That was some really good teriyaki sauce. It wasn't cloyingly sweet like some can be and it wasn't thick and goopy. You couldn't appreciate the teriyaki sauce they way the tofu was prepared. Fix the tofu (steam it, or figure out how to improve the crust, whatever), add some vegetables, and they could have a real winner. Now on to the vegetable tempura. Simply put: this was the worst tempura I have ever had. The batter was way too heavy and puffy. The vegetables included sweet potato, broccoli, onion and mushroom. The broccoli was tasteless, it had a sort of par-steamed texture, and then since it was wrapped in this terrible batter, was all around bad. The sweet potato was ok. The onion was weird. It was a thick ring of batter with some slime in the middle. The mushroom was the worst. It was this weird, slimy, thing and I couldn't eat it. If I were them, I wouldn't serve the tempura to dogs, much less human beings. There's some promise here, and I'd go back to try other things, but they need some real work.

text: Camping in Santa Barbara for a week, and the starter motor on my 1955 Buick stopped functioning. More than a hundred miles from home, and on vacation, I had no resources on this area, but found positive Yelp reviews for a different repair shop. They were honest and told me that I should go directly to AGS. I called Matt, the owner of AGS, early the next morning and had my car towed in a couple of hours later. In Los Angeles, companies that rebuild components like these usually require that you bring in the motor itself -- they rarely let you bring the entire car, and offer removal and installation. After Matt told me he could do this, I was sold. When the tow truck guy arrived, and asked me where I was going his exact words were "That's the best shop. Quality work." It reinforced everything I had heard. I learned that AGS stands for Alternator, Generator, Starter, and Matt himself was very personable, knowledgeable and his rapid diagnosis matched mine: starter motor. A couple of hours later, before the close of day, I received a phone call from him. He had pulled everything apart, diagnosed the problem and estimated project completion by about noon the next day. I was even more impressed. This was a semi-major component (not as major as an engine or transmission, but close) and to have complete service and repair in fewer than 24 hours, on a car that is 55 years old, is pretty impressive. As I drove away, I began to experience a carburetor problem, which I incorrectly thought might be related to the starter. Matt went through the system, and examined and tested things. We found out that it wasn't anything related to the starter motor -- the problem was in a completely different part of the engine -- but he still fixed it in. And he did it in about 10 minutes. Wow. Thank God I broke down in Santa Barbara. Any other town and I would have been royally out of luck. Possible scenarios would have been leaving the car somewhere in town, having it towed hundreds of miles or waiting a week for a mechanic only familiar with modern cars to figure out older technology.

text: I spend the weekend in Philly with my boyfriend and some of our good friends. Josh H and I decided to go off by ourselves for a romantic dinner. I hit up the trusty ole Yelp app on his I-Phone for a recommendation. We were both craving Italian, and Modo Mio showed up as the first 4.5 star rec. Conveniently, it was also in the same hood that my friend was having her bday party. Finally, as an added bonus, I found out this place was BYOB, which means that Josh and I could splurge a little more on food instead of spending 50 bucks on a bottle of booze that really cost 15 dollars at the distributor. We arrive at like 7:30, sans reservation. All the tables inside were booked, but we were able to sit outside right away. It was a touch too hot to eat outside, but by that point, we were starving. The waitress explained that a lot of people try the 'tourista' menu. For 32 dollars, one can get: an app, pasta, an entree, and dessert. For Josh, who can eat a lot, this seemed like a good value. Knowing myself, I stuck to an entree. I could have ordered pasta if I wanted, however, because they have GLUTEN FREE OPTIONS! Yay!!!! They can do any spaghetti and gnocchi dish gluten free, which ROCKS. However, the lamb shank and wilted dandelion greens combo looked pretty outstanding, so I chose that. Josh went with: snails and capers over toasted bread, shrimp and arribata gnocchi, breaded pork loin with gorgonzola over corn, and vanilla panna cotta with biscotti for dessert. We were both super pumped. What we loved: Josh loved his snails and the cheesey bread that accompanied it. He also liked the gnocchi. He said that it had a small spicy kick, but that even someone as spice sensitive as me could have handled it. He loved the pork, especially because it was covered in gorgonzola. I was kinda meh about my lamb. The lamb itself was cooked perfectly, but the accompanying tomato and plumb puree was a bit cloying. Josh's pork dish looked way better. If only the breading were gluten free. Otherwise I would have gone halfsies with him. All in all, this place was super cute. You could tell that they care a lot about food. If my lamb were not covered in that saccharine sauce, I would have easily given Modo Mio 5 stars.
label: POS

text: Can someone please explain to me why Nashville can't make garlic bread?!! I fell down an incline trying to leave my apartment to go pick up the pizza. Instead my boyfriend had to go. All I wanted while soaking up the blood and performing minor surgery on my foot was some good garlic bread. You failed me Pizza Perfect, got that FAILED! I was told, you will not find good pizza outside of NY pizza. It's true, but this place is decent, actually might be better. Their thin crust is actually thin crust. text: Food Road Trip: New Orleans, LA Day 10 Exploring the French Quarter, looking for places to eat since we did not prepare in advance which places we should try. We actually didn't think we would be going to New Orleans because of the hurricane so I was texting my gf to ask her friend who use to live near New Orleans for some recommendations. One of the ones he recommended was Cafe Du Monde, so we remember seeing that and headed over there. Being the newbies that we were, we did not know that all they serve were beingnets and drinks. By this time, we are starving, so we head towards Market Cafe and was solicited by one of the employees to try them out. She hands all of us a menu and we sit down since we really needed to eat. What drew us initially to this place, other than being hungry was the live band playing. That was a nice touch. The waitress was very friendly and the food came out pretty fast, which was a big plus at the time. I had an oyster poor boy and I was not disappointed. The sandwich is pretty simple, some crusty toasted french bread lettuce, tomatoes, pickles, mayo and the fried oysters but it was oh so good. Side note: I finally realized while I was eating this that the South has perfected the art of deep frying. Everything fried thing we ordered from Richmond to New Orleans so far has been really good. Since we like to share, I also got to taste Market Cafe's jambalaya, gumbo, red beans & rice and crawfish etouffee. The jambalaya was better than Mothers and the etouffee was on the same level but it was cheaper. Those 4 items cost about $16 and the portion was the same. I had a good time eating there since the band was playing throughout our lunch. Friendly service, jazz music, good food, and decent prices: I'm not a greedy guy so I couldn't think of a better place to spend for lunch.
label: POS

text: I can't say enough good things about Lithe. I hate that it took me so long to discover it! Lithe is much more than pilates. It's barre work, pilates, strength training, cardio--it is truly a workout that offers it all! More importantly, it will kick your a$$ and you will love every moment of it. You will probably feel soreness in places you didn't know existed, but its a good kind of sore. I've been going here since October 2009 and it has been hands down the best workout experience I've ever had. I've tried it all--Bikram, running, spin, Turbo Jam, personal training--you name it, I've done it at least once but Lithe is the first workout I've stuck with consistently. There are always new classes being added to the schedule, which helps challenge your body in different ways and prevents the boredom that can come when you get used to a routine. They frequently introduce new techniques and tools to keep the workouts fresh and at the forefront of innovation. Aside from the workout, I don't think you could be tought by a more talented group of instructors. The instructors care about their craft and want to see you get the most out of your workout. However, what I've truly come to appreciate is how warm and friendly everyone is. Despite its popularity, Lithe still feels very personal and close knit--a very impressive accomplishment. I would absolutely recommend Lithe no matter what your level of fitness is, your age or your goals. You can truly shape your own experience here and have absolutely no doubt that it will be rewarding.

I tried a piece of the french toast and it was above average and that says a lot because I really don't care much for that particular dish but you could taste the cinnamon and the bread simply melted in my mouth. A quick word about the establishment, when looking for this location, we found the new one and walked in but only to ask for directions to the older one and it was very clean but small and I have to say that you would be better off going to the older one because it is also clean but much more interesting. The staff was nice but not as friendly as I had hoped. I tried a brownie and a piece of a large rice crispy treat and while the brownie was decent, the rice crispy treat was dry and all that I could taste was the cereal. It looked yummy but they didn't use enough marshmallow. My husband really enjoyed the cafe Mocha but I can't say much else because I did not try it. text: During my two months in Philadelphia, I found the Brasserie Perrier to be one of the biggest disappointments in terms of restaurants. So why did I find myself there at least two or three times a week? Well...there was nowhere better to go. But lucky for you, my frequent presence can only make my rating all the more valid. The first time I came, I was a little impressed. The bar was modern, the wait staff looked good, and the whole place was rather open. Even my first meal there was good. But by the end of my second trip, featuring a five-course meal, I realized that the Brasserie really isn't that good a restaurant. So from then on, I stuck to the bar/lounge portion of the restaurant, settling for drinks with light fare and desserts. But gosh, these people don't even know their drinks. Ordering a Scotch or Armagnac by name invariably resulted in a confused look from the server and me having to point out my drink on the menu. text: In all fairness I can't comment on the quality of ATG's repair work nor venture a prognosis on the life expectancy of a vehicle based on my band's return road trip... because I didn't get beyond the estimation stage with these guys. What I can say, is that if cost as well as quality is important to you in establishing a business relationship with an auto shop (my car will need a considerable amount of work over the next six months) then I strongly suggest you look elsewhere. Find someone who will work with your repair needs AND your budget. When I was quoted $990 for a front brake rotor replacement and replacement pads for the rear brakes, I was floored... "That sounds exorbitant. I'm not in a position to pay over $900 for a brake job." "Well, we can just put the tires back on and you can pick up the vehicle." "How much just for the front brakes?" "Oh, about $600. You know that includes the grease... and we only use the absolute best parts." (He actually played up the cost of grease.) "Can you send me an itemized estimate over email?" "No, my computer doesn't do that." (Hmm, time warp back to 1997.) I attempted to negotiate less expensive parts, etc. but ATG wouldn't work with me... AT ALL. They wouldn't knock off $100, or use a differently priced rotor or brake pads. Nada. Zero. Not... one... penny. So I finally said that I didn't think that a brake job should cost that much. The shop manager then asked me, "Well, then how much should it cost?" Excellent question. I got off the phone, called two additional shops and explained that the front rotors and pads needed replacing. The first one, off the top of his head, for my make, model and engine size quoted me a price of $450. The second shop actually took the time to price out the parts and quoted me a cost of $302, including labor. That's $298 less than ATG quoted me for the exact same front brake job. Both shops were located between .5 - 1 mile away from ATG. ATG, I actually considered giving you an extra mercy star for maintaining a polite demeanor while trying to fleece me, because I'm nice like that. But I think I'd rather just be honest about my experience, because I'm accurate like that. Oh and one more tip for those of you who read through this entire review... check out Napa Auto Parts online to get a quick ballpark on the price range of low to mid to high end auto parts. Peace.

text: This was such a bad experience that I am writing about it years after the actual event! The summer of 2003, I was working in Washington, D.C. and my mother's health was failing on the west coast. Of course, a nice dinner out in the French Quarter was a big part of the trip to New Orleans. I chose this restaurant because my mother thought she knew the family name from Lake Charles and my father remembered that they had dined at this location shortly after they first met. When I waited tables, rule number one was always to take special care of the timing with tables with the elderly and small children. Not only had this staff apparently never thought of such a rule, they seemed intent on ignoring us BECAUSE we had someone elderly with us. After 45 minutes I had to go find a manager to please, please have someone come take our order. I explained that it was getting difficult to keep the party there, my mother's condition and that it actually seemed we were being ignored. I was very nice about it and was begging them to help me since this dinner was an event more than a meal. When the server arrived, he was apparently bent out of shape at having been sent to the table. Another 25 minutes later, when our food arrived, I sincerely believe a salt shaker had been dumped in my dish. Since we'd already had the wrong food come to the table and were, at this point, famished, I tried to choke some of it down. I was trying to keep spirits up at the table and did not, against all urges, complain. On top of all this, it was not a cheap evening for me. I sincerely wish this place were no longer open. I see others commenting on the service and am at least happy to learn that it was not just us!

text: This review is based on the Ethiopian food only and not the alcohol. A friend and I decided to go to Era, which is somewhat close to the museum district where he lives. Well, it was definitely closer than the West Philly establishments anyways. We walked into the "restaurant" and it was definitely a bar in a rectangular shape that takes up the entire room. We asked if there were additional tables (there was only one tiny, pathetic table for 2 near the door), and were pointed to a room in the rear. One has to walk through a hallway/additional room that looked into the kitchen. A lot of hot air was coming from the kitchen, too bad this was already a very hot day. I took a look into the kitchen, because of course it is a good idea to scope out where one's food is coming from. There was one lady standing there, and it looked very old and cramped. However, it wasn't visibly dirty in the dim lighting. The back room was cozy with only about 6 tables in it. Although, all Ethiopian restaurants are really pretty cozy "hole in the walls." There was a back door that opened into an alley. There were paintings on the wall for sale by an artist that wasn't of an Ethiopian flavor. However, the tablecloths were of an Ethiopian design and looked pretty new. They are almost identical to the ones at Abyssinia. We received water fairly quickly, but ordering and getting our food took a bit of time. Typical Ethiopian timing despite for the fact that we were the only people in the restaurant. Overall, there were really only about 2 more people in the bar area. A man, who I assumed to be the owner sat at the corner of the bar when we came in and was still there when we left. I ordered my usual yebeg (lamb) tibs, which came with 2 sides. I chose the salad and the potato/carrot/cabbage dishes. My friend chose the yebeg wot dish with the collard greens and the potato/carrot/cabbage dish. There were only 4 choices, and the last was a lentil dish that neither of us chose. My food was somewhat spicy, but not really spicy. My lamb was good, but not extraordinary as was my friend's. His yebeg wot was much spicier than my lamb. The salad was nothing to write home about, and there did not seem to be much, if at all, a dressing on it. The potato/carrot/cabbage combo was good, but the potato and carrot chunks were too big, and so not as flavorful as one would have hoped for. However, all the ingredients seemed to be very fresh, which is a good thing. The injera was mediocre. It wasn't as thick as some of the other places, and definitely not as sour. It was adequate and not bad, but definitely not the best injera I have had. The portions were on the small side but the price was on the low side as well, although well within the range of typical Ethiopian places. The food was adequate, service typical, portions and prices comparable and no other customers came into the restaurant part of the establishment the entire time we were there. The overall experience was very uneventful, except for one small occurrence. At one point a marmalade cat walked into the hallway outside the kitchen and started to approach us before being shooed into a room with a closed door by our cook. Made me wonder if they have mouse problems? Conclusion is that this is a good place to scratch your Ethiopian itch, if you can't get into West Philly, but there are definitely better tasting Ethiopian elsewhere.

text: NO STARS, REALLY THE WORST MEXICAN FOOD ANYWHERE I can say that because I am a native of Tucson and KNOW good Sonoran Mexican food, but the crap they let out of their kitchen is an abomination. We were in Tucson this past weekend for a visit with family and I wanted, no, needed, a carne seca chimichanga enchilada style. We should have just taken the drive to south 4th Ave and Mi Nidito or just gone a little further down Speedway to Midway Molina and my night would not have been ruined nor my blood pressure elevated. Anyway, we get in there and are seated at first, in a booth, right next to a table of about 12 people, where the chair from the head of the table, nearly touched the end of our table. I looked at the hostess with "are you joking?" look, since there was hardly anyone in the place (now I know why) and she moved us to the end of the room...fine, okay. Our waiter bounces up next and his cologne is so overwhelming that I come close to gagging. We then order 2 original Margaritas which was the only reasonably priced drink on the menu ($7 each) and a cheese crisp with green chilies, and one carne seca chimichanga enchilada style to share (thank god, my husband convinced me to split it). I was first concerned when the waiter asked us which enchilada sauce we wanted on our chimi....what? Since when is there any other enchilada sauce but red? Oh, we could order a green, tomatillo sauce (not recommended for beef, imho), or sour cream (also not good for beef), but there you are: a choice. We went with the red sauce. He brings us our drinks riding the cloud of cheap after shave and asks us if they brought us the chips and salsa....do you see any chips and salsa on the table? NO! so here they come a bit later. Little did I know how much better off we were with a bare, chip and salsa-less table. We get the stuff and dip away....THE SALSA IS NOTHING MORE THAN TOMATO SAUCE!!! I kid you not! The waiter comes over again to check on how we're doing and I ask him if this is the hottest salsa they have...yes is the answer. I am stunned! I ask: "Do you have any kind of heat for this?" to which he tells me all the salsas come cold. I said I knew this, but don't you have any chili's or anything like that and he says: "the pico de gallo comes with chili rellenos". I knew then, it was a lost cause. He told us the regular shipment didn't come in, but they still made the same recipe. What????? Apparently that recipe didn't have ANY spices or salt and pepper in the ingredients. I pretty much downed my 'rita by then...then.....out comes the cheese crisp....BURNT!!, YES BURNT! how anyone could let that come out of a kitchen is beyond me, but the bloody thing was dark, dark brown on the edges and the chilies on top? teaspoons of glop from a can and the thing looked like it had been sitting under a heat lamp for awhile before incinerating it under a broiler. But the Chimi....yeah, well it was burnt, too and had been sitting under the same heat lamp. I had to hold myself back from throwing the plates at the kitchen. I honestly wanted to go back there and make food for the people....REAL SONORAN MEXICAN FOOD! I know Monica Flin is spinning in her grave. This is what they've done to your food and recipes: made it Gringo Central and lost their souls to expansion and greed. If you want good, authentic Mexican food: STAY AWAY FROM EL CHARRO PS. I have to finish and tell you that at the end of the meal, when the stinky waiter asked if we enjoyed our meal (I was speechless and knew I'd make a scene if I opened my mouth) my husband said we'd had better and the kid said we sounded like we'd eaten there before and we told him we ACTUALLY LIVED OUT OF TOWN, but used to live here, he then begins to sell us a frequent eater pass or some-such bullshit and we just asked for our check and ran out of there.
label: NEG

text: I made my family to go there after reading reviews on Yelp. They were not very hungry in the first place and not impressed by the way the restaurant looked. We had one 5-year old picky eater, one whining a pre-teen, and one-year-old who had her snack right before so that (we were hoping-this trick usually works well in other places)she doesn't bother us much. Should have known better, because she kept eating everything she could reach! So much to say about the food that kids cannot stop eating! I was the only one excited about the place at the beginning, but by the end of the meal EVERYONE was in great mood. Even pre-teen got nice and happy, and picky eater ate every single bit we put on her plate - 3 times. We ordered Salt and Pepper Tofu, Green and Black Beans Chicken, 2 kinds of soups ( Seaweed one was the best), XO Grouper, Wine Chicken and Orange chicken. They don't bring each plate to the person who ordered it, they rather put all of them in the middle of the table and provide empty plates in front of everyone, so that, using the large spoons provided, each can put any amount of anything on his or her own plate. So, pretty much everything is served the way appetizers are normally served in American restaurants. Note, that portions are very large. Make sure you check the specials board located by the register - those offers are not even on the menu. We ordered our Green and Black Beans Chicken from it and my husband said that this is something he is going to order every time he comes here from now on. The service was great, I don't know why so many people commented about how poor it is. I prepared for the worst in that department, but was surprised to realize that it;s quite the contrary. Everyone was very attentive, quick and friendly. They didn't even mind the baby who was loud and messy, not even the gloomy pre-teen, they smiled to both of them and tried to entertain them (successfully). The waitress didn't even hesitate when the 5-year old was placing an order and told her that the only things she wanted were macaroni n' cheese or chicken nuggets. She replied with an offer of orange chicken nuggets and was granted a consent. Orange chicken turned out to be beautiful and delicious and our daughter said this is the only kind of chicken nuggets she wants to eat from now on. No dessert on the menu, but if you ask, the will provide one. We, however, chose the boba tea in the tea room right next to this restaurant. Our bill turned out to be little more then $50 and we felt like leaving a good tip. Will definitely be back
label: POS

text: First off, the pictures uploaded by the business on Yelp are not accurate at all. What we got were way mininature-rized versions of the rolls (see pic). I ordered and waited over an hour for them to come, even though they are only 7 blocks away (yea, I know I'm lazy). We even had to call them again. We got four rolls for about $40 dollars so I just basically spent $20 bucks on a bad dinner. What we ordered: 1) Apple Roll ($13.25, WTH?!) : OK I don't know what I was thinking when I ordered this. I guess the sound of apple in a sushi roll sounded interesting. What we got however, was a different story. A small sushi roll with a very thin piece of salmon and tuna on the outside, and a tiny piece of yellow tail in the inside. What made up the core of the roll? LOTS of apples. I couldn't even taste the fish. SO hmm I guess I paid 13 bucks for mostly apple slivers. 2) Love for Tuna ($10): There is no love here. I am in disbelief how tiny this roll is for being $10. It was the same size as the non-specialty rolls and at twice the price. To make matters worse, I decided to just eat a piece of the Tuna separate from the roll. Talk about not fresh. It was dry and grainy... SAY WHAT? Dry and grainy tuna?? YEA.... 3) Tex-Mex ($8.50): Again, sounded very appealing and fun with having jalapeno. Again, teeny tiny, and the chicken inside.... text: My boyfriend and I just took the Bolt Bus from Philly to NYC this weekend. It was our first and last time. The whole experience was horrible. For the ride to NYC, we got to the bus 10 minutes early. It wasn't early enough. The bus was mostly full and some obnoxious girls had put their stuff all over a big block of seats to save it for some friends that hadn't arrived yet. So we were stuck sitting in the back by the bathrooms. The smell of urine was nauseatingly strong. I sat with my hand over my nose for most of the ride. I thought I was going to vomit. We figured that for the ride back we'd arrive early and then would not have this problem again. We were wrong. For the ride back home, we arrived about 45 minutes early. There was a huge mass of confused people waiting for both the Philly & Boston busses. No one knew which bus was which and all the busses were running late. I asked one of the drivers a question and he said he was a Boston driver. He pointed to a Philly driver and told me to ask her. So I went up to her and politely said 'excuse me'. No answer. She completely ignored me. So thinking that she hadn't heard me, I said again 'excuse me'. She turned and screamed to me 'CAN I DEAL WITH MY LIFE FIRST?!?!' Her response was so absurd, so rude and uncalled for that I was completely shocked by it. I just walked away from the miserable hag, I wasn't about to have it out with a bus driver. When it was time to board, the passangers swarmed around the bus. We then realized that it was boarding by sections (A, B and C). We were in group C. Wonderful. We again were stuck in the back of the bus and this time couldn't even sit together. Oh, and lucky us, the bathroom was covered in puke. The driver was nice enough to warn us that the bathroom was 'nasty'. Pros: cheap, convenient pickup/drop off locations Cons: horrible customer service/rude drivers, dirty bathrooms that stink up the back of the bus, unreliable electric (our outlet didn't work), no guarantee of a good seat no matter how early you show up to board. Needless to say, I will never ride the Bolt Bus again. If I wanted to ride a smelly bus where people yell at me I'd ride the Chinatown bus.

text: Into the very same orifice that I use for pie I have been known to insert a libation or few as well. I find that a small tipple of the aqua vitae can be, (and usually is) quite refreshing. I also am very fond of the pictures of dead presidents I collect in my wallet. Although I like to engage in quaffing adult beverages, I really hate trading exorbitant numbers of my pictures of these past patriots for the aforementioned elixirs. And I REALLY hate trading my little paper images for single servings or said hooch, especially in high-priced entrapment locales like the Gaylord Opryland Hotel. Please bear in mind this is not a knock on the Gaylord. They are a business and are not holding a gun at anyone's head. If you don't like the price, don't give them the booze business or better yet, do what I did and buy your liquor off-site ala BYOB. Enter Donelson Liquors. Or to be more precise, enter me into Donelson Liquor. Now, I need you to understand something. This is one of the reviews where I am torn between giving them a one star and a five star, with precious little middle ground. I gave them a four, and I'll explain why. Liquor laws in Tennessee suck. You can buy beer (and I assume wine) just about anywhere, but an establishment selling "hard" liquor is much harder to find, especially in the environs of the racket that is the Opryland, Gaylord and Opry Mills Mall. But again, that's a different post. Suffice it to say you cannot buy a bottle of liquor at anything like a "reasonable" rate anywhere near Oprybiz inc. I don't know what the liquor taxes are in Tennessee. I do not understand the logic that thinks that limiting the places that sell alcohol will limit the number of people with drinking problems. If that were true no one in America would have a cocaine problem. In other states you can get liquor in grocery stores, pharmacies, why heck, I've known a few country hardware stores that carried it as well. This is not the case in Tennessee. It may be that Donelson Liquors knows they have you "over a barrel", (pardon the pun). What I paid for a Tennessee product made in Lynchburg at Donelson Liquors was double what you would pay for it in a grocery store in California. DOUBLE. In Pie-Hole Boy's world, thatsa' lotta' dead presidents. Is that Donelson's problem? Nope. Did I shell out the DPs? You bet. It was still cheaper than drinking at the Gaylord. So here goes: One star, you bastards, for fixing the game against an innocent libertine like myself in my pursuit of "Knowing Jack". Five stars for having a cool neon sign in the window with foot tall letters spelling out B-O-U-R-B-O-N. Sweet. Five stars for having the product to back up the sign in the window. (Folks, these people do have a serious selection of bur-ho-bon.) Same five stars for just simply being there and selling the stuff. Upshot? Four stars. If you go, allow yourself some time to peruse what appears to be a fine selection of whiskeys, in particular the bourbons.

text: If your love for overpriced yet delicious smelling products is as fanatical as mine, get to Blue Mercury.....stat! Smack in the middle of Center City lies this beautiful small boutique, where you'll find upscale skincare, makeup, fragrances, hair care products, candles and general grooming goodness. They've got the usual suspects (Bliss, Frederic Fekkai) cult following favorites ( N.V. Perricone M.D.,Terax, Shu Uemura- think eyelash curler) Classics ( think grandma's bathroom - Darphin, Molton Brown, Acqua Di Parma) ....and they're equal opportunity groomers, so the boys will like it too - even the non metro guys! (though he'll stand in the corner rolling his eyes for street cred. No doubt he's secretly eyeing the Anthony Logistics Razor Burn Repair behind you, trust me.) Sure, if you want the entire Kiehl's line you'll have to walk down the block, but Blue Mercury carries the 'best seller' products of each brand...and for the smaller or independent manufacturers, they cover the full line. If the cool packaging doesn't draw you in, the chic, shiny staff will. Beware! They are quite knowledgeable and sure, learning about the latest green vegan chicken friendly product line is fun, (did I mention they have some awesome up and coming brands as well?) but before you know it, 2 hours have passed and you're in credit card debt. Save the mascara purchase for Rite Aid, but get the face wash here! There's a small spa/salon which is part of the store as well...I've never tried it myself (other than a one time eyebrow wax which was, well, an eyebrow wax) but I've heard mixed opinions....if we're talking haircuts, I suppose I'll have to review House Productions next...

text: It's kind of funny I waited until now to review First Wok. Had I done it a month ago, it would have received a 4 out of 5 from me. However, after some changes made in the last month, it has now dropped to 2 out of 5. I have been going to First Wok for a couple fo years. Co-workers and I used to go once a week until we moved into a new sight that was too far away from First Wok. As a result, I usually go twice a week or so between my two jobs and get the buffet to go. This had worked great until the above mention changes, which I will get into now. The three main buffet items I get were the General Tso's chicken, the orange chicken, and the First Wok chicken (chicken in a sauce that tasted like a combination of Soy and BBQ). First, for some odd reason, First Wok only offers General Tso's chicken on certain nights. It used to be an every other night pattern, but about a month ago it has turned into more of a "when we feel like it" schedule. This was a drag as it is really good, but as long as they had the orange chicken and the First Wok chicken, it wasn't a big deal. Second, about three weeks ago, the First Wok chicken disappeared and was replaced by Burbon Chicken. I've eaten burbon chicken before, and this does not taste anything like that. It isn't bad, but the fact that I have no idea what the sauce is made from is a bit disappointing. Again, not a big deal as long as the orange chicken is there and the General Tso's is there once in a while. Third, and this one isn't related to the buffet selection, about two weeks ago, the carryout containers got significantly smaller. This was total crap considering that they are still charging the same price as before. The old containers were enough for a full meal. The new ones, pardon the pun, are so small I'm hungry again in an hour. Look, I have perfected the art of filling these containers to the point where they just barely close, but this is crazy that I have to do this to get a full meal. It is also sad that for the same price I can go to any number of places nearby (non-buffet) and get a full meal, but I like variety, so the buffet is more of an appealing choice. The final straw was going by three nights ago. Big shock, no General Tso's chicken. Big shock, still no First Wok chicken, just the "burbon" chicken. Big shock...no orange chicken. It had been replaced by some kind of chicken I have never heard of before. I ended up leaving with a container of rice and noodles because there was nothing else available that I would eat. I really hope someone that works there reads this. If you don't want to go back to the old containters, fine. At least bring back the food that people like. Believe me, I'm not the only one that feels this way. You get one more chance, then I'm taking my business to one of the five other chineese places that are within three miles of your place.

text: New to the Collingswood BYOB scene is NOT another Italian bistro, but a much needed American comfort food. I couldn't wait to try this one out so when there wasn't any grub in my fridge, my boyfriend and I were ready to check out West Side Gravy. The atmosphere is creative with kitchen counter top tables, funky artwork and a clean look that could fit any type of casual lunch or dinner. Our server was in training but she did a pretty good job of naming off the specials. I ordered the mushroom sandwich (Grilled portobello, boursin cheese, lettuce, tomato, red onion on a toasted baguette) and my boyfriend went for a meatloaf sandwich (bacon wrapped pork and beef meatloaf, sharp provolone, pinot noir sauce on crusty bread). While waiting, I noticed little things that I liked: the thick disposable napkins (I hate thin crappy ones), clean windows and plenty of seating for large parties. Our food was just as the menu said it would be. One problem: no toothpick for little mouths. Everything else was how I liked it, fantastic combo and all fresh. The cheese wasn't overpowering and I was able to taste all the ingredients. I did take off one or two onions, that was a bit much. The boyfriend said his sandwich was a 4 stars. For me, it's a 4.4 stars but since this is the 1st review for WSG, I'm going for 5. This place is definately my new local feeding frenzy.

They have awesome beers on tap, make bangin bloody marys, margaritas and manhattans, and even soak the cherries in brandy! text: Egads. Where to begin? I'll start with the line outside, which stretched halfway down the block towards 16th, and moved at a glacial pace. text: Our first visit to Vin de Set, with another couple, proved to be a very nice outing. I puzzled over the name, trying to translate "vin" as "wine". It turns out it is a somewhat inaccurate attempt at a phonetic spelling of vingt dix-sept or 2017, which is their address on Chouteau. With that explained, we enjoyed rooftop seating in some very nice weather. It is a great atmosphere. Everyone enjoyed the appetizers. Ms T and I both had crab bisque, which was excellent, but should have been served hotter. The complimentary bread is rather ordinary, but don't worry, you don't need it. For her main meal, Ms T had one of the specials of the evening. It was chicken breast, grilled with mushrooms, tomato, spinach and basil and a balsamic reduction, served with rice. She thought it was wonderful and since there were two pieces of chicken, she had one to take home. I agonized between the sea bass and the grilled pork tenderloin special, then settled on the sea bass. Great choice! It was served on an interesting bed of thinly sliced Brussels sprouts that were billed as creamed. I expected steamed sprouts in a heavy cream sauce, but these were lightly sautéed with a very light sauce and some balsamic reduction around the edges. It complimented the sea bass perfectly and not a scrap went to waste. I ordered haricot vertes so I would have plenty of vegetables. They were fresh, crisp and tender, just right. Portions were excellent. Our dining partners ordered salmon and something called airline chicken and were clearly pleased, in both cases. Again, nothing went begging. For dessert which we certainly did not need, but could not resist, we had beignets and cheese cake. The beignets were served with three dipping sauces and the cheese cake was very creamy and smooth and well garnished. The urge to lick the plate was barely stifled. Vin de Set is another $100 per couple place that I keep saying we don't do often. If I am selecting one for a nicer occasion, this would be high on my list. Rooftop dining is really nice, but there is a really interesting looking room just off the bar.
label: POS

text: OK. So, I went here last night with 7 other people for a late dinner/drink extravaganza. Only two of us ate dinner, others just had drinks and snacks. The Good: The "Sexy" Shrimp and Grits. It was fantastic. Really. The spicy sauce was absolutely fantastic, the grits were perfectly cooked and creamy, and the portion of shrimp on top was generous. I inhaled it. There was no way I was sharing that! It was so good. The remoulade-like sauce that accompanied the fried calamari was really delicious. The Decent: The bread brought out before the meal was really tasty, hot and fresh. The drinks were priced well and the fact that the kitchen stays open till 11 is great for the area. The space is also nice and welcoming. The Relatively Passable: The spanikopita with roasted tomato-whatever sauce. The spanikopita itself was delicious, but the sauce was overwhelming and pungent and the spanikopita was swimming in it. Too bad the calamari that accompanied that delicious remoulade sauce was incredibly greasy.... it had a nice flavor, but I couldn't deal with the grease factor. The Inexplicably Bad: OUR SERVER. He started off with gusto and a little awkward charm, but honestly the best thing he did the whole night was recommend the Shrimp and Grits, which really saved the whole night. He proceeded to ridicule my friend based on the fact that she asked questions about ingredients since she doesn't eat anything with added sugar. At first I thought he was just awkward and trying to make a lighthearted joke, but he kept DOING it. Not cool. But THEN he proceeded to completely forget about us during the second half of our meal. Who I assumed to be the manager served us our food and the bartender brought us the check. The "server" was present the entire time, screwing around and giving us dirty looks. Unprofessional. We were one of two tables in the whole joint, he wasn't ignoring us because he was busy. It was clear that he was just avoiding us. It's a server's job to answer any questions a patron may have, not to get pissy when someone asks questions, and then ignore the table for the rest of the night. It's a shame, because the food had potential and was priced well, but I do not plan on returning.

My highlight here was the whimsical and oddly inspiring Dia de los Muertos exhibit which I enjoyed tremendously, especially the "ofrenda" that memorializes the loss of notable American actors, musicians and politicians this year. text: Every once in a while, as a former big-city dweller, I get a craving for cheap, greasy Chinese take-out. You know -- big battered nuggets of chicken in unidentifiable pink syrup, pan-fried dumplings, and mysteriously salty egg rolls. Maybe I'm alone in this, I don't know. Anyhow, though, my one experience with New Golden Buffet has convinced me that this is not the place to satisfy those cravings. For about thirty bucks, I got a take-out meal consisting of Moo Shu Vegetables, a slightly spicy dish called Ma Pu Tofu, General Tso's Chicken, along with dumplings, pork fried rice, and an egg roll. The dumplings were fine, and the Moo Shu vegetables weren't too bad, but everything else was, frankly, terrible, and as you can see from my other reviews, my standards aren't exactly high. The chicken was almost too hard to chew; the egg roll tasted like it hadn't been completely defrosted before they heated it up, and the tofu dish consisted only of chunks of mushy, flavorless tofu floating in copious amounts of gloppy "sauce" (which appeared to be soy sauce thickened with cornstarch, plus sweetener and hot sauce). The dumplings tasted identical to the dumplings I've eaten in hole-in-the-wall Chinese take-outs around the United States, so they were fine. The Moo Shu vegetables were reasonably good; they tasted fresh, and the flavorings weren't too salty or sweet. Now, most folks go there for the buffet, and there was a bit of a crowd there, so maybe the buffet offerings are better. But for thirty bucks I expected something a little better than this. To top it off, the service was incredibly slow. I'm still looking for that cheap Chinese fix. Website (which features a take-out menu, as well as -- oddly enough -- a list of current quotes from financial markets): http://newgoldenbuffet.com
label: NEG

This is a bit unfair, $5.50 would still be a great deal assuming the quality is anything like what it was (unless it takes an hour to get it -- what do they do when the place isn't completely empty?), but it's amusing nonetheless. We have to give them a second star because the quality of the food was actually pretty good, although most of the menu items don't seem like much of a price value -- the biscuits & gravy were good and cheap, and a few of the specially-prices items are good value, but normal menu items aren't. text: This spa is a must! It is simply amazing and totally worth every single cent. It is also the perfect gift idea, I have purchased several gift certificates. I have been to this spa about 4 or 5 times now, for different treatments over the past year and a half or so. I have had a pedicure, several massages, and several facial treatments. My only wish is that the deep tissue massage has a little more pressure. I'm sure she would have pressed harder if I had asked, but of course I didn't ask :) The overall feel and look is very nice and everything is clean. Yes it is pricey, but you HAVE to show up several hours before your scheduled appointment and take advantage of all the spa amenities. Last time on my day off I showed up like three or four hours ahead of time and tried a little bit of everything they had to offer and I had the best time! I was there on a weekday so it seemed like at any given moment I had the whole facility to myself, and only occasionally I would see other guests walking by. I have also gone on a very busy weekend - street vibrations- and it was much more busy, but still enjoyable. I do prefer going on a weekday though, its just quieter and more relaxing). Each guest has their own slippers, robe, and locker..... towels are available throughout the facility, and an elevator is used to get from floor to floor. The woman's private area is my favorite I think.... hot and cool pools, cascading showers, sauna, steam rooms, vanity area, healthy snacks and drinks..... perfect! I thought it was nice how even though I was laying and relaxing right next to the hot tub there was not an ounce of chlorine smell in the air.... just a nice eucalyptus scent. It is a totally relaxing ambiance with Tuscan inspired art and relaxing music. They offer iced towels throughout the facility. Then they have the men's and women's pool area with the secret garden (comfy music vibrating chairs with ipods and headphones). The pool is neat and has a large water fountain in the middle spouting water into the pool..... and on the side are more hot and cool tub dips.... and the cascading showers. This area also offers snacks/drinks. You can also order room service in this area and they will bring it up (as I was told.... I have not tried it myself). Weather permitting there is an outdoor sun area too. And then there is the relaxation area, on the same floor that some of the services are performed as well. They have a name for the area, but I forget what it is.... but it is a really relaxing lounge room with dim lighting and a large glass water fall and ipods with headphones. Again, the snacks and drinks are offered here as well. The beds used for the massages and the facials are the vibrating music beds and the rooms are very nice. The chair used for the pedicures is not like the one pictured on their website, it is much nicer. It also vibrates with the music and is very comfortable. All of their staff is very nice and helpful.... they will point you in the right direction if you feel like you have gotten lost in the large facility. But at the same time they keep their distance and don't bug you, which I really like.... because you are there to relax! So like I said, it is so worth treating yourself to at least one day at this spa! Even if you are on a budget you get your money's worth if you show up early and stay after your treatment.

text: If you're 20-something, live in Levittown or Langhorne or thereabouts, and you're too lazy to drive to Philly, then the Hulmeville is the place to be on a weekend night. In my case, I date a guy from Levittown, and he and his friends love this place. So I tagged along when he and I started dating, and the place really has grown on me over the past year. This place is historic, as well as fun. Located on Trenton Road in historic Hulmeville, PA, the Hulmeville Inn has been in business for over two hundred years. Originally, it was a hotel and stage coach stop for those traveling between Trenton and Philadelphia. There is still a hitching post and a stone step that was used to board the carriages located on the property. During Prohibition, the Inn operated as an ice cream parlor. Now it's a great place to grab a beer and watch some sports. I like this place because it's spacious (yet tough to get a table if you get there late on a weekend night), has pool tables, and has a pretty good beer selection for a place in the 'burbs. In fact, I can always count on them offering Dirty Hoes because they always have Hoegaarden and Framboise on tap (and I like Dirty Hoes... no, not that kind, the drink, silly!). They change their beer selection to keep things fresh every once in a while, so check out what they have on tap on their website before you go. They've also got bar food - fries and such. Their wings are pretty good. Usually, this place is pretty much a townie bar during the week, but it becomes 20-something central on the weekends, with a fun crowd and good juke box music. You can always find the random sketchy old dudes at the bar on the weekend, though, which reminds you that you're still near Levittown. They just add local flavor to the place and keep it from becoming too much of a hipster hang-out. The Hulmeville bartenders are always really nice, and the ID-checker guys at the front door get to know the regulars after a while. I like having people know me at businesses that I frequent. I just don't like getting hit on by the sketchy old dudes at the bar (some have said some really GROSS things to me while I tried to order a drink...). If you're a cute girl, be sure to order your beer at the other end of the bar from them. The prices are pretty reasonable, and you can also catch the Phillies game or whatever sports game on their really nice tv's. I also noticed that the owners constantly upgrade the place to keep it fresh. The decor has changed little by little since I started going there a year ago. Oh, and the pitchers have a compartment in the middle where the bartender puts some ice, so your beer stays cold until you finish the pitcher. That's always appreciated. They are open seven days a week from 11 a.m. until 2 a.m. My only complaint is that the Hulmeville is outside the Philly city limits, so the smoking ban is not in effect there. Thus, I've had difficulty breathing and leave smelling like an ash tray. Since the place isn't huge and it gets really crowded on the weekends, and since I don't think they have a state-of-the-art ventilation system, it gets WAY more smoky in there than your average bar that still allows smoking. In fact, it's so bad that I've been avoiding going there very often since the Philly bars went smoke-free. If the entire state ever institutes a ban, though, I'll be back in the Hulmeville at least once a week, like when I first started hanging there. In the meantime, I'll still go, just not as often as I'd like because I value my asthmatic lungs. If you can take the smoke, though, check it out. This place rocks.

text: So it's only been open a week, so I'm really hoping to be able to give the White Dog Cafe Wayne an updated, improved review in the future. As an active Penn alum, the University City location is a regular favorite, and my wife and I were so excited about the opening in our neighborhood. Unfortunately, our first visit (Friday 11/19) was, in summary, mostly disappointing. The "dog-and-country" decor is fun and novel, and one of our two dishes (the Spicy Lamb Bolognese) was very good - spot on! However, those two positives were strongly outweighed by a very chilly table, inattentive/slow and awkward service from several staffers (each of hostess, bar, and server), and a second entree (Prosciutto Wrapped Brook Trout) that was mediocre. The prosciutto was overcooked to a barely recognizable and somewhat tasteless point, around very flavorful and well-cooked fish, but then sitting atop rock-hard charred toast (near impossible to cut). Our appetizer - the Beef Tartare - was also less than satisfying: dense, dark beef, and the quail egg would not easily mix (it was like a rubber ball). Drinks took long to order, longer to arrive (10-15 mins), beer came with literally 2"+ of head, and all drinks (including water) ran empty at one point during the meal. The crowd is lively (even boisterous) in the bar, but the various dining rooms seem to have vastly different crowd/feel/vibe, which means that the "atmosphere" for your experience is very unpredictable. text: Oh, man.. This place is awesome. I am a fan of Oriental food and this place shows off some amazingly good Thai cuisine. The outside of the business does not reflect how nice it is inside. It's one part of a strip of small businesses that all seem to be "hole in the wall" kind of places. Once you step in, though, you're immediately greeted by a very kind wait staff that ask you to sit anywhere you'd like. You'll notice how small the place is, but the style and decor makes this an authentic Thai experience; it's a very quaint and comfy place to be. *My review of the food is based solely on the lunch specials* Being a 19 year old student, working at a dead end job, taking my mother out to Thai Orchid for a nice lunch doesn't have me feeling like I just burned a hole through my wallet, once the bill comes. Seriously, the lunch specials are offered at a very reasonable low price! The kind waiter brings us water in nice stemmed glasses and comes back a bit later to take our order. My mother orders shrimp Pad Thai and I order the Pa-Nang curry and a Thai iced tea. The waiter leaves and comes back momentarily with a nice cup of chicken and rice soup and a rangoon of some sort, that is served with lunch orders, for each of us. It's a nice small serving of each that is not at all filling, but keeps you content as you wait for the main course. The Thai iced tea here is really awesome. Thai iced tea isn't anything like a regular iced tea so I'd definitely recommend giving it a try, unless you're not into sweeter things. It is some kind of tea that has a layer of sweetened condensed milk on top. After I stir that baby up, I'll empty the glass in record time. Once our food is served I stare at it, just a bit, to marvel at how much of a generous portion is given. The Pa-Nang curry doesn't disappoint. It has the right amount of spice and goes so well with the chicken, vegetables, and side of rice. My mom and I always swap plates halfway through to sample the other person's stuff. The Pad Thai rocks. Can't say much else; it just rocks. Period. By the end of our meal I'm feeling good and full. The waiter drops off our checks and thanks us for choosing their place to eat at. I take a look at the cost of this wondrous meal; $19.75. This brings a smile to my face and to my wallet. In all, this place is great to meet up with or take someone for a nice cheap lunch. What you get here is amazingly authentic Thai food with a nice comfy atmosphere and kind wait staff. Give this place a shot. *To get a look at the food we ate, take a look at the photos for this place. Looks good, eh?*
