text: I have to agree with another reviewer who requested negative or zero stars. US Airways sucks. Conversely, I have to agree with another 'nother reviewer who compliments them on First Class -- it's the only way I'll ever fly US Air again. I'm switching to Southwest for FF points, where the people actually like their jobs. In a 10 day period in February, I boarded US Air flights 4 times, carrying the same suitcase everytime (when you fly in and out of PHL, you learn to carry on -- baggage handling is a clusterfuck.) The fourth flight, from MCO to PHL, was delayed two hours on the runway (this is when they were still charging $2 for softdrinks), while they searched MCO for a circuit breaker - I am not making this up. You might think a circuit breaker is a basic maintenance item, but no, turned out they had to fly one in from Charlotte! When they started pulling passengers with connecting flights off the plane, I called customer service from my seat and booked a flight for the following morning. I have no idea if that plane ever left MCO that day. Next morning, I arrive for my rescheduled flight to PHL and the surly gate attendant tells me my bag is too big. "Gosh, Mr. Poopy-Pants-underpaid- unhappy-with-life gate attendant," I say, "it fits in the overhead and I've carried it on 4 flights in the past 10 days." "I don't care, it's too big and you're going to have to check it." Mind you, I am extremely sensitive to people carrying oversized bags onto planes -- my BF has a skinny bag that's too tall to fit "wheels in," and takes up 1.5 times the space of my bag in the overhead, but they let him on because it's not more than 9" deep. And what the hell is up with 9"? The overhead opening is at least 14" high. So why the new rule? Duh, so they can charge you for checked bags, of course! But, I digress. I say, "Okay, can I gate-check it down the gangway?" (Remember, I'm flying to the baggage black hole of America, PHL.) "NO," the asshole yells at me, "you'll have to pick it up in the baggage terminal." Yeah, no. So he straps a claim check on it and sends me on my way. Just before boarding, I rip off the claim check, carry my bag onboard and stow it, wheels in, no squishing necessary, tidily in the overhead bin directly above my seat, and we took off 45 minutes late. SO THEN, when we land in PHL (late, BTW) our gate isn't available. Huh? Didn't the pilot tell you we were coming? Weren't we in flight for the past two hours and in radio communication the whole time? Oh, geez, sorry, this other plane is still at the gate, you'll have to find somewhere else to offload your passengers. That added another 40 minutes to the travel time. I wrote a letter to US Air's ombudsman (aka teflonman) who defended both the lack of basic maintenance items and the 9" luggage limitation (he said it's an FAA rule, which, hello, it's not.) And the gate thing, well, he basically gave me the customer service version of "shit happens." So last Thursday, I flew to PHX on business (BTW, packed an even smaller bag than before to avoid any more unpleasantness), a flight I had booked with Amex points on February 6. I couldn't select seats when I booked, but figured I'd do it when I checked-in online. On Wednesday, I checked in and selected a seat. Sunday morning, when I went online to check-in for the return trip, seat selection was not available, so I'd have to do it at the airport. I honestly didn't think anything of it. When I got to the airport and went to the gate, I told the pseudo-cheery (but, I suspect, equally unhappy-with-life) gate attendant that I needed a seat assignment on the flight. Guess what she said? "This flight is oversold, you don't have a seat." WTF? Yeah, apparently, even though your ticket is issued and you have a confirmation number and a ticket number, YOU ARE NOT GUARANTEED A SEAT ON THE FLIGHT! Chirpy-psycho-killer gate attendant helpfully informed me that hardly anybody reads the fine print but it's in there! I did my level best to remain calm until she opened the flight on her Fred Flintstone computer and allowed as how she could give me a middle seat, and I should feel damn lucky with it. That flight took off 30 minutes late, landed on time and, wait for it, the gate wasn't available AGAIN! How do they get away with it? How do they charge your credit card (or in my case, Amex Points account) and not guarantee you a seat? Isn't there a Customer Bill of Rights these assholes have to honor? And you know the ultimate irony? US Airways has the best ontime rating of any airline in PHL or some such nonsense. I can only assume that they're self-reporting, because I haven't left on time on a US Airways flight in 3 years. They build so much fat into their schedule that you sometimes arrive on time, but I've still missed meetings, appointments and social events thanks to their incompetence. And no, it's rarely weather related. I hate US Air.
label: NEG

text: Le Pavillon has its charm, but then again, charm can only take you so far. The reviews on Trip Advisor that talk about the place being old and dingy are not entirely off the mark. Conversely, if you aren't looking for the clinically minimalist design of the W, but rather some old school charm, you probably won't be disappointed. Upon arrival, we were greeted with a million facets of light radiating off the crystal chandeliers, juxtaposed with the smell of grandmas. Talk about a statement. The place oozes old-school Southern opulence, but also has tinges of just plain old. Not going to lie, the paintings on the walls and the creaky sounds all make this a great place for ghost hunters - it all feels like the inspiration for the Disney Haunted Mansion. Not to mention that our running toilet seems to flush sporadically in the night - I think a ghost is haunting our bathroom, if you ask me. Our room was oddly upgraded to a 2 queen room (what did my husband and I need an extra bed for?) which apparently had extra space. Fine. Come to find out that the hotel pool is being painted (which no one told us) so we think that the upgrade was meant to cover that up. They offered us the pool at the Homewood Suites next door, but that was a severe downgrade given that it was A) indoors and B) across the street. PB and J bar is kitschy - I actually hate PBJ, so not my thing, but a cute touch. The hot chocolate was all over the table and table cloth when I got down to the bar, and the mess (coupled with the heat) turned me off. Room service was actually tasty, despite the price, but then again, when is room service not expensive. Gumbo was flavorful, and the oysters in my po-boy were crispy and delicious. If you are stuck in the hotel, you could do a lot worse for a comforting meal. If you are a stickler for cleanliness, you may want to skip this place. There was still small trash on the floor of our room, and hair on the bathroom tiles. The entire room looks like a holdover from the early 90s pretending to be the early 1820's. Maybe that was the last time the place was properly cleaned. All in all, I can't say that we are having a horrible time here, but we certainly won't come back. I was at the Intercontinental last time, and despite the much higher price tag for the room, it was a huge value over this place.

text: Walked in last Friday night around 8 pm, no reservations, wearing shorts and a t-shirt. Hostess said she was booked inside, but we could sit at the bar or wait for a table outside to open up. We decided to eat at the bar, and boy, I'm very, very glad we did. We split the peach salad, which was served with house made ricotta, greens, and a raspberry vinaigrette reduction. It was spectacular. The ricotta and peaches were such a great combination that I went to the farmer's market on Saturday and picked up some myself. She had the bacon wrapped meatloaf, which was great! Perfectly cooked, well priced ($11!), and came with spectacular mashed potatoes. My wife was extremely pleased with this dish. I had the pompano. I couldn't resist ordering fish after hearing the raves about the chef's work with fish, and the raves were spot on. It was served blackened perfectly, atop some house made creamed corn, some kind of bread/biscuit, and with some tomato confit. Perfect all the way around. I loved this dish, and found the portion to be absolutely perfect. This is fine dining at its best, and very reasonably priced. Yays: - Great service, even at the bar - The food was outstanding. Some of the best I've had in St. Louis, and served quite nicely. - The pricing is kind of ridiculous. Our total meal, including a beer for my wife, was under $45. That's insane for fine dining. I've paid well more than $25 for a fish entree like I got here. - The portions are just right. Some might complain they're small, but I left pleasantly full from my meal, and we didn't even have dessert. - It's great to see some fine dining in this area that isn't overpriced italian. Nays: - It's a small venue. I think they should take over the rest of the block. - My pompano did take forever to come out from the kitchen. My wife had already finished her meatloaf by the time it showed up. I'm not sure if this was planned or just poor execution on a busy Friday night. I excuse it since the chef came out to let us know it would be a bit, then delivered the food himself, and THEN came back to see if it was OK.

text: This was a very disappointing meal for a special occasion. I had family visiting me for my birthday and chose not to make a reservation at any restaurant to keep things flexible. At 6:20 I called Hoof + Fin to see there availability. The person who answered told me they could seat our party of 4 at 8 p.m. outside only. Though this was a ways away and we were hungry we accepted. When we arrived there were about 6 four-tops open inside and the waitress told us there was no seating outside. I complained that we were told that there were not any reservations until 8 p.m. (when there were clearly tables open) and that we would be seated outside. She argued that they don't take reservations based on location. When I asked to see the manager she told me that I couldn't because he was cooking. This put an immediate sour taste in our mouths. After some complaining we were seated outside at a small table with mis-matched chairs. The waiter was quite verbose, we received appetizers within about 20 minutes but it did take an hour and half to receive our entrees. The waiter apologized several times that the kitchen was backed up. We ordered a paella type dish, 2 scallop plates and a fluke. All were mediocre at best and each member of our party had expressed that individually. The scallops were not much better than I could have cooked them myself and the fries and grilled vegetable were luke warm and not exciting at all. My paella type dish was very bland and lacked complexity. I had acid burn on my tongue when I left the restaurant because of the amount of lemon I had to squeeze on it to give it some flavor. The fluke was incredibly sweet and lacked any acid or heat to mellow it out. Parties that were seated after us were told right away that there would be a long wait for their food. We all felt disappointed in the food and that we had paid $25 for parking on South Street to avoid missing our reservation. We were not at all eager to try dessert even though it was my birthday. In the end I could think of at least 10 restaurants within walking distance that serve better food. Next time I'm in the neighborhood I will be much more excited to try Hosteria Da Elio or Adsum before considering eating here again.

text: When I saw the name of this Mexican BYO my first thought was "Chinicuiles". Hildalgo is one of the States of Mexico and Chinicuiles is their favorite food item. My companion ordered one of the specials, red snapper with avocado, lightly breaded and covered in a cilantro sauce. Some other items on the menu were Queso Fundio (a cheese melt with chorizo and chips), Cohnita Pibil (prok cubes with axiote baked in banana leaves) and many other pork, chicken and beef dishes. The restaurant is owed by a Mexican couple. She waits the tables and he is the chef. The service was friendly and attentive. The dinning room was clean and neat but not posh. text: Maybe I am just not artistic, or maybe I am old school...even further, maybe I just don't get It. Whatever IT is, I am apparently out of the loop. Why, Why, Why do people find this at all interesting? I love mosaics, I think the process and the design that goes into them is phenomenal. But when I think of a mosaic I think of the cone mosaics of early Mesopotamia, or Byzantine Icons....not old plates, mugs and mirrors smashed up to make formless nothings, goofy faces, and nonsensical phrases. I get the modern draw to make art from trash. taking discarded items and making them anew. But what happened to the idea of beauty, or functionality? Places like this lack sustainability because they have neither. the first time you see it you are in awe of everything, the next few times you see it you may nod your head at it's wonder, after that it progressively becomes more and more of an eye sore. This modern trend to shock us, and make us gasp has become boring and tedious. Because it will always take more to shock us, they will continue to have to up the ante, and find new and even more disgusting things to catch our attention and shock us for those fleeting moments. And yet, something like the Sistine Chapel continues to put us in awe. Not because it shocks, not because it is ever changing, but because of it's beauty and workmanship. Places like the Magic Gardens are a flash in the pan. True art and true beauty is timeless and eternal.

No matter, I don't like to punish a good product too severely when that itself is fantastic. Onto the important stuff! I got the peanut butter cup cupcake and the red velvet. I was tempted to just stuff them into my mouth because I was so ready to eat them after my search for the shop, but I didn't think that would be the right thing to do. I knew these had to be savored. They aren't huge, but they aren't regular size cupcakes either, so I did cave and use a fork. The peanut butter cup was to die for!! I'm definitely not an icing person. I'm that guy who scrapes it off of every birthday/wedding cake or cupcake I've ever gotten and leave the pile on the edge of my plate like an unsatisfying-looking pile of sugar. HOWEVER, I'm sure I could have spread this peanut-butter icing on pizza and it STILL would have been delicious! It was like a whipped peanut butter, buttercream heaven. Not to mention, they sprinkle generous bits of reese's on top. I mean, cake is cake, but when you can top it with something like that, you get a masterpiece! I'm not sure I can be as enthusiastic about the red velvet, though still a wonderful cupcake! Very moist german chocolate cake with a smooth, whipped cream cheese icing. I didn't eat this one until later and split it with my husband. Maybe the reason I don't think of it like I do the peanut butter cup is because this cupcake was just a delightful dessert, not an escape from a horrible day. In any case, it was still wonderful. I still think I'm partial to the peanut butter. Overall, very tasty treats that I would love to go back for, but I think when I go back, I'd rather not drive myself.

text: New Orleans Birthday Trip = Music in the French Quarter So this here, this back in an ally, is the House of Blues. It's dark and it's ominous and it really feels like it should and would be an great place to grab a drink and listen to some music. It may not be the first, but it's the best because it's basically awesome. Venue: HoB is a real music venue, that's what it's built for. It's a stage, with a lighting truss and music set up, two floors and a balcony, and every spot is within spitting distance of the stage. Both floors have their own bars, and while the space may get crowded, just remember there are 799 other people here just attempting to enjoy the music, so don't be an ass and share the space. It's dark inside the hall, with various mood lighting in blues and purples, and be careful where you put your foot down, because there might just be a step or two there. Largely, the entire venue is deceiving. There are upstairs, downstairs, private rooms, music halls, parishes and patios. You could throw whatever the hell kinda party you wanted down in NOLA at the House of Blues and probably never run out of space. Downside of HoB nowadays it it's national chaindom. Back when NOLA's HoB was the second in charge and still a novelty, there was nothing better. But now they seem to be everywhere, even at Disney, and they're owned by Live Nation--the authenticity has been lost a bit. Still, in certain glimmers of chords and powerful vocals, you can find it: that true music hall feel, so go for the history too, but always for the music. Music: The entertainment at HoB run the gamut. They'll have everything from The Naked Brothers Band a la Nickelodeon to David Cook to burlesque shows and real soul music. Take a pick, but always go, even if just for the opening act like we did. That's right, we went to House of Blues for an opening act: acoustic Vertical Horizon, or the frontman at least. It was awesome, and spontaneous and well worth it, because the venue is welcoming and acoustically primed. There's food too, but we skipped out after VH was done (and yes I knew every song). I here the brunch is pretty good though, so if you're in town for a while, try both.

They had us down for 6:30, not 7:00 like we confirmed when we first called, so had we shown up for the initial reservation, we probably would have lost our table. On my second visit (to celebrate a promotion for a friend who chose this restaurant based on the online menu), the entree I had was good, and everyone was happy enough with their food. We got the bacon brownie this time, and despite seeing bits of bacon, we could not taste it. Plus, the brownie itself looked and tasted like something you'd get at a school cafeteria, flat and just ok. I could buy two store mixes for the cost of that brownie, and they would have tasted better. And we did get the bread pudding again, which was just as crusty and dry as the first time. Finally, the cocktails on the second visit were just as bad. I ordered a drink with two sweet types of liquor, but could only taste bourbon. The other guests' drinks were also way too strong. When my boyfriend asked the bartender what kind of beer the Abita Andygator was, he very emphatically said it was "like, a really, REALLY strong Abita." Boyfriend tried another approach, asking what style it was. "Uhhh, like... like a regular Abita? But stronger." Turns out (as we just found out at the Abita tasting room) it's a barleywine. There's no such style as an "Abita." Abita's a brand, jackass. He did admit that he'd only been bartending for a few days, but you would think that at a place claiming to be the best beer joint on Bourbon, they'd at least give their newbies a crash course in beer styles. All this could have been forgiven (as we were on Bourbon Street and it's been established that beer, especially craft beer, is not exactly its claim to fame) if it hadn't been for the fact that the 22-oz Chimay my boyfriend eventually ordered was $18 MOTHER-LOVIN' BUCKS. Also, the completely uninformed bartender was something of a douche, talking way too much and bragging on himself, and bummed like four cigarettes from us before we bailed for greener, cheaper pastures. So! Do not go here if you (A) know your beer or (B) like your money. However, if you aren't particularly attached to your bra, hand it over for a free cup of Stella to go and then get yourself over to the Frenchman Street area as fast as possible.

text: I'm in shock as well kim d. I just don't get it. Have these reviewers never eaten quality BBQ before!?? This joint is Mediocre, AT BEST. We ordered 2 quarts of beans, and 2 quarts of potato salad. Guess what we got? FOUR QUARTS OF SLAW! Not even CLOSE to correct. Our fault for not checking before leaving; their fault for simply not including what we ordered. Well, what we did get was shockingly bad for a place as overly Hyped as this. Brisket was dried out and bland. Totally tasteless. Worst meat of the order. I have cooked and carved hundreds of pounds of brisket at the NYC BBQ festival a few years back and it's a shame to call what we were served brisket. The chicken was marginally better. Not at all great, but simply passable. But still, far FAR short of what one would expect based on all the raving mad Hype this place has. Pulled pork was the the 'best', and I use that adjective loosely. Wasn't great by any means. It simply was the least offensive of the three meats we ordered, and I'll leave it at that. I love, eat and RESPECT great 'cue. I've eaten it all over America. I've eaten at most of the BBQ joints here in nYc (Daisy May's, Virgil's, RUB, Hill Country, et al.) and any one of them will DESTROY Pappy's Smokehouse. It's a shame...I was really hoping this place would be great, since I was venturing into what I thought was the BBQ heart of the country, if you will. text: I've lurked Yelp for awhile, but my experience tonight at Black Thorn has prompted me to finally write a review. I figured restaurant-goers would want to know about my abysmal encounter with one of the employees (possibly a shift manager, I'm not sure). I took my dad from out of town to the Black Thorn tonight. I just moved into the TGS neighborhood, the place is only a couple blocks from me, and had heard great things about their pizza. As everyone else said, the place is a gritty dive, and I enjoyed that aspect of it. The pizza itself, after waiting an hour and a half for it (which I didn't mind, we had a good time in the interim), tasted great. The problem was that it wasn't, after all that waiting, what we ordered. My dad had ordered a supreme; was very clear - "I want everything on it - no, not tomatoes, anchovies and artichokes, but everything else." When it came out, they called up "Mike F" (we even had our initial behind it, so it was very clearly meant for us) and it looked like sausage. I was wary, but having never had deep dish before, we thought maybe the rest of the ingredients were inside. Poked at it, took a few bites. Nope, definitely just sausage. Someone must have put the wrong order in. We weren't going to wait ANOTHER hour and a half for them to remake it, so we went ahead and ate it. It *was* delicious. But not what we ordered, or paid for. I took a piece up to the man behind the bar that took my order to make sure it was sausage and calmly explain what happened, and see if we could just get the extra $4 difference back. Our exchange went a little something like this: Him: "You ate it?! You ate someone else's pie!" Me: "It's under Mike F, you gave this to us. I didn't know if it was supreme in the deep dish." Him: "God damn it! What were you thinking?!" then screaming at the bar, pissed off: "Is there a Mike F at the bar? Because if so, this girl ate your pizza." The people at the bar looked shocked and embarassed for me; some nervously giggled, some gave me dirty looks. I was MORTIFIED. I said, "No, Mike F is us! And this is what you gave us!" He's pacing, mumbling things, yelling at the other employees about this awful travesty I committed, flailing his arms about and making a big scene, and told me: "You should have brought it back!" Me, raising my voice now: "I didn't want to wait another hour for you to cook another one!" Him, yelling back: "You wouldn't have had to...god damn it! Shit. YOU DON'T JUST EAT SOMEONE ELSE'S PIZZA!" I said, "You know what, forget it" and stormed off to my table while he's yelling at me to "come back and deal with this." I'm so shocked and appalled I'm in tears. I'm at my table shaking in anger. I've lost my appetite. Another employee who witnessed the exchange comes over and apologizes on his behalf, saying, "He gets like that" offered to buy us a beer or something, and then said she'd talk to him and see what she could do. Turned out that he wrote "sausage" on the order....but still charged us the extra $4 for a supreme. So HE made the exact mistake I suspected. It wasn't someone else's pizza, it was ours. HE fucked up, and I WOULD have had to wait another hour for the right one. Yet he assumed I was a selfish fuck-up and instigated a screaming match at the bar as he accused me of stealing someone else's pizza. He comes over a few minutes later (obviously because the girl went back and told him he's got damage control to do) and his "apology" was "Sorry for getting like that, but I'm really busy." Nice excuse (and they weren't even all that busy. The place was only half full on a Saturday night. Even then....there's no excuse!). He said he'd give us the $4 back. He also asked my dad how he paid for the pizza. "Oh, you paid cash? SWEET. Because if you paid by card it would have been this big pain in the ass to refund you the money on the card." Wow, how many excuses does this guy have? If we paid by card, would he have caused yet another dramatic shit storm over it? The girl comes back over to see what he did, and she says, "Uhhh he really should comp you the whole pizza. But I'm not the boss, he is." (My dad asked if he was the owner and she said no, so that's my thinking in that he's a shift manager) He comes back over a few minutes later and comps us the whole thing (again, I think he was nudged to do so). And apologized again. I told him, "Being busy is a SHITTY excuse. I've worked fast food, I've waited tables, and I'm a nurse on a busy floor in a city hospital - I know busy. You DON'T talk to people like that. You need a lesson in customer service." At this point, he did seem sincerely sorry. I said I appreciate him trying to rectify the situation. But I'm so infuriated I'm never going back. And telling all my friends to avoid this place like the fucking plague. I would give this place ZERO stars if I could. The 1 star is for the poor girl who was obviously mortified and tried to make the situation better.
label: NEG

The meat was plentiful and the different components of the meal just harmonized perfectly. The 8 ounce prime rib was on special, so that is what was also ordered. He said it melted in his mouth. text: Went here upon recommendation of some fabulous Philly Yelpers. My mom was in town this weekend for my birthday and wanted to take the boyfriend and I out to dinner. The decor is really fun and interesting to look at; definitely a conversation piece. We were seated in a booth upstairs and ordered drinks first. I got the Champagne-O-Rama ("champagne & shot of raspberry vodka in a grenadine & sugar rimmed glass"), which was $9 -- one of the cheapest drinks on the menu. It came in a champagne glass, which made it a very small drink, in my opinion, for $9 (that was a little annoying). But it was definitely yummy and it gave me a really nice buzz, even with all of the food. It took us a while to figure out the menu and that everything was kind of share-style. Boyfriend thought that was kind of gimmicky, but I rather liked it. There were so many things on the menu that sounded good to try, so it made it easier that everyone could share. I got the BBQ chicken quesadillas w/ avocado sour cream and I was SO pleased with them. They were a little bit adventurous for me, as I'm very picky about food, but I'm glad I tried them. Mom got the chickpea crusted shrimp and those were fantastic as well (but you only get 4 in one order). Boyfriend got the Rad Na Thai Chicken, and was kind of disappointed -- it sounded like it was going to be something Chinese food-like, and ended up being a gigantic salad. We also got an order of the Schechuan shoestring fries with Chinese mustard sauce to share between the 3 of us. Those were really good, but I was surprised at how tiny and thin the fries were -- they almost weren't big enough to consider fries. Still tasty, though. The servers are all super friendly, and ours wished me a happy pre-birthday at the beginning of the meal when she checked my ID for my drink AND before we left, so that was nice. The bus boy was nice, too. We got there around 5 on a Friday, so we just beat the ensuing crowd. That may have a little bit to do with how fast our food came, but I was still really surprised at that -- I was really hungry when we got there and the food came before I even had time to think about it. So that was another huge plus. The only reason this place lost a star is because, as I said, boyfriend didn't seem to like it so much. text: Ate here on a Monday night, and I am still in awe of the food. I nibbled my leftovers all day despite the fact that they were so spicy... Han Dynasty is the best sichuan food I have ever had in a restaurant --and this includes all of the Philly Chinatown Sichuan spots as well as the big ones in midtown Manhattan. I own both of the fuschia dunlop cookbooks and this place is serving very authentic food. we had dan dan noodles, wontons in chili oil, and cold pork belly slices in chili oil for appetizers and the dry hot pot with chicken, the chicken in the chili oil with peppers and celery/cabbage, and the triple fried beef with peppers. I liked the fact that they offered a choice of light or dark meat for the chicken, since the dark meat has way more flavor. All of the food was very flavorful and you could tell that everything was fresh. And, this place doesn't mess around with the spice. you like it hot? you order it hot and you get it hot! Despite the large amounts of "Ma La" flavor, you could still taste the ingredients and you couldn't stop eating despite the sweat on your lips and brow. It's a byo, but the owner was kind enough to provide us with a lindemans peche lambic to try with the food. the sweet fruit taste of the beer paired really well with the hot food. Han also set us up with an order of fried chinese sausages and garlic slices. These paired really well with the Kenzinger and Newbold IPAs we brought to drink. I am sure I will eat at this place many times in the future, I am always on a quest for real sichuan food that truly provides the heat, and this place has that in spades. Probably the only bummer is the fact that with the prime olde city location parking may be a bit of a hassle on weekends-- but it is very close to the market st el stop so no biggie. The word is already spreading on this place so, if you have been on a quest for really authentic, top quality sichuan-style food in philly, you need to go here ASAP.

text: No es bueno. Phew! And i thought taking 6 years of spanish was all for nothing! Having worked in Deleware for the past year, 2 places pop up quite frequently, Grotto and La Tolteca. You cant travel more than a mole anywhere in The First State, without running into one, the other, or both. I had already tried Grotto, but La Tolteca had long been on my list. After years of eating faux mexican cuisine such as Taco Bell, Chillis and On The Border, I was anxious to try "authentic" mexican food. So keep the fact that Ive never had real mexican food in mind, as you read my review. Even though I love being an asshole, I hate giving bad reviews, but I really was disappointed by La Tolteca. First the good... The decor is awesome, from the colored tilework to the outrageous paintings ( one was a Napoleon Dynamite inspired shot, of an eagle eating a snake). I also like that the entire staff seemed like real mexicans. Call me racist, but I like my ethnic restraunts to be run by people of that ethnicity. Forgive me if I dont want my fajitas served to me by Amber or Troy. Sadly, the good things I can say about La Tolteca, ends there. Good atmosphere and service can only get you so far. If the food is terrible, theres no point. Id eat food from Sycamore, while sitting in a dumpster, served by neo nazis than eat a bad meal in a great place. The food at Tolteca wasnt THAT bad, but it wasnt good. Again, I know not from authentic Mexican food, but the chips and salsa were average, drinks were weak (even the ginger ale), and the food failed to impress me and my family. 3 of us got the beef fajitas, one of them being my daughter, who was trying them for the first time. Fajitas were my wife and I's favorite meal, earlier in our relationship and weve tried them at a few places ( Chilis being the best, believe it or not) These happened to be the worst. I feel like the guac was frozen. When even Ruby Tuesday is making fresh to order guac, this is unforgivable (I may be wrong, but it seemed cold). The Fajitas were burried under veggies that I really dont even associate with Fajitas. The onion and peppers were OK, but mushrooms and tomatoes were too much. It would have been Ok if the meat was good, but it was bland and tough. I got a good taste of the beef because... ...They only gave 2 tortillas! And to order more would have cost extra $$$!! Not only was it just 2 tortillas, but they served them in a crumpled piece of aluminum, where the tortilla on the outside was burned and the one on the inside was cold. Also...No cheese!!!! It wasnt a mistake..none of us , who ordered fajitas got any. Now, im waiting for someone to tell me that this is how its done in Mexico, and if thats the case, La Tolteca is doing it right. However, Montezumas Revenge is also something authentically mexican, it doesnt mean I want it. My sister and her BF got sampler platters and they liked it, but werent really impressed. They both said theyve had better. The only one who was really satisfied with his meal was my son...who had the chicken nuggets and fries. He thought they were great, and said that he, " likes mexican food!" I forgot that we all liked the Churros, for dessert. So in summation, go there for desert and atmosphere. Id also say it was a little pricey, for mexican food, especially when it was crummy. Honestly, if the chain mexican food is wrong, I dont want to be right. As far as im concerned, La Tolteca is mexi-cant.

text: Panda King is actually two restaurants in one: a buffet place open every day and a push cart dim sum place in the adjacent building that's only open Saturday and Sunday between 10:30am-3pm. Dim sum is basically like Spanish tapas, except dim sum came first and it's better and cheaper. This review is for the dim sum experience ONLY. If you're curious about the buffet, I can sum (haha, I made a funny) it up in a couple sentences: there's boring, and then there's the Panda King buffet. It's bland even by Chinese buffet standards, and the selection is pretty weak. THE GOOD Push Cart Service: What do I mean by push cart? Traditional Chinese dim sum is served on carts that are wheeled around the restaurant, allowing patrons to select what they want as the carts pass by. I really like this style as opposed to the a la cart style that you may have tried at Royal China in Metairie. It just adds so much to the dining experience. The Food: There are so many choices that it can be intimidating for newcomers to the experience. Trust me, it's all pretty good at Panda King. Here is a partial list of what we have eaten: *Ha Gow - steamed shrimp dumpling. Standard fare, but always good when done right. They do it right. *Shu Mai - steamed pork dumpling. Also pretty standard, but larger than expected which is good. *Cheng Fun - rice paper rolls with meat inside. This is probably my favorite dish. It's basically the same noodle as in beef chow-fun, wrapped around either sweet BBQ pork, shrimp, or beef. The kicker is the sweet soy sauce that they pour on top. Absolutely divine. However, you need to practice your chopstick skills before ordering, because the combo of noodle and sauce make this dish kind of hard to pick up. *Pork Spare Ribs - usually comes with black bean sauce. Their version also has red bell pepper with it, which I found kind of odd. *Chicken Feet - yes! If you don't mind spitting out tiny bones onto your plate, this is the dish for you. Theirs is spicy, which can be good or bad depending on your preference. *Fried Taro - fried shell (Panda King gets a gold star for making it perfectly light and crisp) with steamed taro inside. You're not gonna find texture like this in any other cuisine, so it should definitely be on your try-it-just-once list. *Carrot Cake - not at all like the dessert, it's a mixture of carrot, taro, and meat (maybe some flour too) pan-fried and cut into squares. Same advice as with the fried taro. Success again as they didn't over-dry it, which can happen more often than it should at other places. *Steamed BBQ Pork Buns - sweet BBQ pork wrapped in a fluffy white bun. A favorite for everyone. They are generous with the pork which is always a plus. *Congee with "thousand-year" egg - Rice porridge with preserved egg. The egg looks old and gross but don't let appearances fool you, it tastes delicious. *Gai Lan - The famous Chinese veggie. Dark green leaves still attached to crunchy stem. It is topped with oyster sauce, which helps counterbalance the slight inherent bitterness of the vegetable. *Egg Tart - OK so maybe THIS is my favorite dish. Flaky pastry shell filled with a flan-like center. I once ate twenty of these by myself. If you like flan at all, then you'll love this. Perhaps my favorite dessert, ever. Price Point: This place is super-affordable as long as you stay away from the big dishes like Peking Duck or the large plates of Fried Rice/Chow Fun. Those are the trap dishes. At prices ranging from $1.99-$4.99 for every item, just stick to the dim sum and you can be completely satisfied at $10-20 a person depending on how big your appetite is. As for the Peking Duck, just walk to the other side of the shopping complex to Hong Kong Food Market and get a whole one. More cost-efficient, plus you get to watch the butcher chop it up for you. THE BAD None. PURGATORY Speed and Quantity: This is the one dining experience that I want things to go quickly. PUSH THAT CART OUT ASAP! Unfortunately at busy times if you happen to be sitting at the tail end of the restaurant you may have to wait for the cart with your favorite items to be reloaded once or maybe even twice before it gets to you. I think I counted about six carts in total, but they need more. Man, dim sum diners can be straight vultures... OVERALL Is this the best dim sum place I've ever had? Nope. Have I been spoiled by the awesomeness of places in Vancouver, Canada? Most certainly. That's why this place gets 5 stars: In no way would I have expected to get push cart dim sum in this city, and not only does Panda King deliver and then sum (I did it again!), but the quality at the price they charge is more than suitable to satiate my dim sum cravings. Good job Panda King. Now get more carts. Go if you: like dim sum, are adventurous with food, want to try new things, like eating for value. Don't go if you: like sticking to the basics, don't like going to the West Bank

text: El Camino Real, known as The King's Highway, was a 600 Mile stretch of road in California connecting 21 Spanish held missions from 1683 to 1834 connecting San Diego to San Francisco. Northern Liberties is now home to it's very own El Camino Real offering two menus of either Mexican or Barbeque fare. In the resting place of the former Deuce in Liberties Walk, owner Owen Kamihira (also of Bar Ferdinand next door) has taken a swing at the ever growing mexican genre in the eastern most section between Spring Garden and Girard. With SO many places in 10 square blocks to get nachos and burritos, can the king's highway possibly bring anything worthy to the table? Can I at least get a decent margarita?! Please? Upon entering El Camino, I notice that the kitchen has been opened up and the bar swings all around - similar to Johnny Brenda's. The chairs have a mission-made look to them, the lights aren't too dark and the decor is far from overdone. It's like, a restaurant! The three flat screen tvs behind the bar are welcoming for those who want to keep up on the game. For those trying to get away from the game, there's a large seating section in the back away from the bar and potential rowdiness of the inevitable Philly Phan. With so many mexican't offerings in the neighborhood, I focused completely on the barbeque. You have your apps, ala carte, entrees and sandwiches and some sides to boot. It turned out that because the place has been so busy in it's opening week they were out of a few items that I would have loved to give a try. The menu includes pork ribs, beef ribs, short ribs, brisket, burger, shaved pork, links, and one seitan offering. I went with brisket and shaved pork and a side of potato salad. To accompany my barbeque, I ordered an El Camino Margarita. Folks, BEST margarita I've had in a long time! It's five bucks and I really can't urge you enough to try one for yourself. The food arrives and I take a bite of my shaved pork. I think it might be a pork loin, it's nothing like ham. Much firmer and barbeque-y. Very tasty and even better with the side of BBQ sauce. The potato salad was splendid. Some of the best I've had. Rustic and creamy with red skin and chives and onions. I've saved the best for last though. I'm not sure if The King's Highway has a signature dish but I'm going to write a petition to have Great Northern Liberties Brisket Day. My guess is a little more than a half pound of the slowest cooked beef ever to set foot this side of the Schuylkill. Want to get your vegetarian friends to eat beef? This is the deal my friend! The only thing that could have made this MOUTH-GASM any better would be if there was six more pounds of it. One of my dinning partners exclaimed that this beats ANY philly cheese steak ANY day. Mr. Chef, I bow in your greatness. Obviously, no dessert would have been any better than the meal we just had but we had a shot at some banana pudding anyway, just to see if this place is still taking us seriously. Sure enough, they've even managed to make the best pudding ever! I just need to go back here as often as possible and try everything on the menu. Next time will be the mexican for sure. I doubt anything is going to beat the oral-brisket-gasm but... what if I'm wrong?!?! The drinks alone are going to be a good reason that you're going to find me there at least once a week. Plus, I live around the corner so that helps too! See you there! I'll close with noting that El Camino has not been open very long. They're still working out the kinks here and there so if you can be patient, I guarantee you'll be well rewarded.

Mall is supposed to be convenient, not "Ugh, where is this store that I'm looking for?" Despite its size, I feel like they lack variety when it comes to the stores. Some of the stores are repeated throughout the mall - for instance, there are two Coach stores in the mall, which in my opinion is totally unnecessary. For a mall of this size, you would think there would be Barney's New York or Saks Fifth Avenue, but no. Even Atlanta has them, but not King of Prussia. Overall, I think KOP is like the gifts you get from your frenemy (Friend-enemy). It has really grand and pretty wrapping, but once you open it, the item is simply useless and awkward.

text: I really wanted to like this place. I'd had a poor fitting at Nordstrom a few weeks ago and decided that I should use it as an opportunity to visit a few speciality shops that specialized in bras of all sizes and fittings. A quick flip on the internet brought me to Hope Chest, which had wonderful reviews. So I drove the 90 minutes into the Philly surburbs to take a visit. I had no clue that this place was so small. Two employees plus two customers equals a crowd. I browsed for a few minutes before one of the two employees decided to ask me if they could help. I explained my fitting at Nordstrom, she had a "tsk tsk" face, and then proceeded to measure me over my shirt. And just a band measurement. She then determined my size, and handed me two bras - one lined, one padded. They might have had two other bras in my exact size, so there was definitely not a lot of selection. The lined one wasn't quite right, and the padded one was a style that I currently own but threw out because it didn't hold up. I asked about other options, and the lady looked at me like I was crazy. She swore that they only carried one style of one brand in a push up bras. This is a bra store?!?! How in the world does that work?!?! Then she decided that perhaps I really was a different size, and handed me the same band size in a smaller cup, and a smaller band size with the same cup. I really liked the second one but it was a bit snug. I took it out and mentioned "hey, this is the right amount of padding - I thought you said you didn't carry anything in between" and she just kind of shrugged. Asked about a 34A in it - shrug. Didn't offer to order me the correct size - just told me that they would probably restock over the next few weeks and I could come back in. That was a pretty disappointing response when I told her that I had driven 1.5 hours to visit. I'm not going to drive back down in hopes that you have something. Their site says that they offer 32AA-40DDD and will order items as well - beware that they had very limited stock on smaller sizes when I was there. When I was browsing, they literally had one 32AA and one 34AA. I'd call before you go and verify how much inventory they have. I maybe wouldn't have left so aggravated if they would have offered to order me what I was looking for. They did have a quite beautiful selection of lingerie but I was pretty miffed about the poor bra fitting experience and their lack of customer service and just skipped it. Voting with dollars, I suppose. Maybe if you are a more average size, or don't need any help, this would be a good option? But I thought the whole point of a bra fitting lingerie shop was that they were good at these things...
label: NEG

text: I've driven by this restaurant about a million times before I decided to give it a try. To be fair, it really isn't a "restaurant" but a take-out/delivery place, but they do have some seating and tables so you can eat there. After looking at the posted menu, I decided to try a regular donair and a poutine. It wasn't that busy, so I sat down and watched some hockey on the big screen they have there. 5 minutes......10 minutes.......15 minutes........I watched almost a full period of hockey before my food was served, and like I said they weren't that busy. The young tard behind the counter then grabbed a plastic fork by the pronged end and handed it to me! Not very sanitary, methinks. And then I had to ask him for napkins(good luck eating a donair without them.) I put my tray down and commenced eating. Remember when you were a little kid eating at McDs or Dairy Queen? The table they had their was so high and the stool I sat on was so short that the table edge was at my upper chest! And I'm 6 feet tall. Try eating something in that way sometime.....it's very uncomfortable. I dug into the donair first. The filler was about standard, but the pita shell was stale and doughy, which took a lot of chewing. After the arduous task of finishing off the donair, I took on the poutine(after wiping down my contaminated fork). It was made of frozen crinkle cut fries you see in the supermarket. The fat girl cook in the back didn't burn them, but they were way overcooked and hard. In fact, the plastic prongs on my fork bent when trying to grab them! I had to eat my poutine as a soup. So to sum up here's what your money will get you at Richard's on 50th: -long wait times for food -horrible service by incompetent employees -very uncomfortable dining -garbage quality food Need any other reasons to avoid doing business with this so-called restaurant?

text: This hotel was a disaster. The worst feature for me was the large window in the front door to each room. The towels were stained with yellow spots. There were no spa facilities of any kind. Their idea of spa facilities is a list of masseuses who make incalls. text: How could I forget to review this museum? I went here over Thanksgiving break & on a rainy, boring Sunday afternoon I popped into the Dali museum. What a treat! Since I still have my student id & look about 12 years old, I got in for $10.00-score! I wandered around the museum with my brother & mom trying to be sophisticated, artsy and deep. Unfortunately, we're a bunch of immature clowns & couldn't help but talk about the random genitalia or body parts that frequented many of his paintings. It actually made the trip a bit more enjoyable & put me in a much better mood since the sun was not shining on my last day in warm, beautiful St. Petersburg. The museum is fantastic, new, and chalk-full of Dali paintings. Pieces that I've seen in books or posters, but also pieces that I've never seen before. I love that! The gift shop is awesome as well. I bought two prints of my favie Dali paintings to hang in the condo & postcards for friends. I could have bought the whole store, which ranged from Dali movies to Dali calendars. From Dali inspired jewelery to Dali inspired martini glasses. If you're ever in the St. Pete's area, I would definitely check this place out. It seems to be pretty unknown, so it's never busy & you can take your time enjoying all the beheaded women, melting clocks, and random penises.

text: The World Cafe has gone through several different owners in the past few years. I suspect this is because the location isn't quite ideal for a business. Although it's only a block or two from busy streets like Kingshighway and Chippewa, it's actually at the intersection of two relatively quiet residential streets. The main customer base is the surrounding neighborhood residents, myself included. This is one of the things I love about the World Cafe. It's the local independent neighborhood coffee house with a great atmosphere and friendly staff. While it might not be the most promising business investment, I prefer it undiscovered by the public at large, if only for my own selfish enjoyment. The drinks are prepared well, the environment is relaxing and I often find myself in an interesting conversation with another neighborhood resident. This particular version of the World Cafe is relatively new. It re-opened the first week of February, and it's still in its infancy. The menu is still evolving, particularly the food. At the moment, only a few prepackaged items are available, but I understand that plans are in the works to expand the menu by the middle of March. I look forward to its continued development and wish it all the best.

text: This is a large pet store with Training services, Adoptions (I always see them outside on Saturday), grooming, and Banfield veterinary care. There is lots of parking out front and is accessible by Septa. Within the store and outside on the islands in the parking lot are cleanup stations with hand soap, towels, cleaning spray, and disposal bucket to clean up pet mess. It is highly recommended that you make an appointment to get your pet groomed. They are usually booked for two weeks every time we try to make an appointment. You can book as early as around 7:30-8 in the morning. You need to ring the bell to get in. The grooming depends on the groomer that does your pet, but so far I've only had one time I wasn't happy and that was because they wouldn't groom my sisters' dog. It was a special circumstance and misunderstanding but it left a bad mark. I still highly recommend this service as there is usually rarely any problems. The Banfield Vet service I highly recommend. The only thing I DON'T like about them is that they don't do needles in front of you. They tend to take your pet to the back to administer shots. I haven't requested they stay in the room and do it in front of you so I don't know what their policy is regarding that. The vet techs are friendly and nice and I love the vet that takes care of Molly (my sisters' dog). They also have a high concern for your pet and their care is top notch, they are second only to the best (Matthew Ryan Penn Vet). The visit fee is around $30. They sell flea and heartworm meds, too. The fish look well taken care of. The betta fish are isolated in little cubes that share the water that is filtered for the other community fish in larger tanks beneath them. This care is better than what I've seen at Petco. The only thing I found strange is that when you buy them, the floor person went in their and grabbed them with her hands. I guess it's because a net wouldn't fit into the little cube but I can imagine how that was stressful for the betta. There is one row of other pets like rats, guinea pigs, hamsters as well as some birds. The cats are on display near the cat products. Dogs are available through outside adoption agencies that station outside of the store on the weekends. They also have lizards and turtles but those are limited. There is plenty of variety in food, snacks, furniture, accessories. I would recommend smaller boutiques if you are looking for clothing (see Doggie Style, Bonejour). During the holidays like Easter and Christmas, you can have your pet take pictures with the Easter Bunny or Santa Claus.
label: POS

text: Budget my ass. I needed a car rental this week at the last minute. My usual car rental places were sold out. I had no idea who else to turn to, but Budget ended up being the cheapest. And by "cheapest" I mean for a measly 28 hours I paid over $200 for a compact car. W to the T to the F. Price aside, I wasn't impressed. I'm so used to Alamo's painless renting (you can prepay online, then go straight to the car class, pick your own car, and drive off), that I guess I'm spoiled. The shuttle picked myself and a couple other passengers up at the airport quickly. Except the driver drove like a maniac. Another renter and I sat in the back of the shuttle, in the 5 seats that go across the back. Our driver flew over a pothole so fast we both flew up in the air and slammed back down. Normally this would just suck, but considering I had taken a bad spill that landed me in the ER 48 hours prior to this, my entire body was already sore. The pothole slam dance did not help matters at all. I was not pleased. We arrived to the car lot, and though I had already prepaid, I still had to go inside. AND WAIT IN LINE. They had 3 employees working the counter for both Budget and Avis. One woman was working two computers at once in what seemed like an effort to make things go more quickly, but I actually think she just slowed things down. As I waited I looked around for computer screens like they have at other rental places (*cough* Alamo *cough*) that allow you to check yourself in. Budget/Avis has no such thing. Lame. I finally made it up the counter thirty minutes later. That's right - half an hour. I was already in a foul mood because of the reason I was in St. Louis, their crazy shuttle driver, and if you know me at all, you know my feelings on standing in line. The woman was nice and I smiled politely and handed her my credit card and license. Then the sales pitch began. Oh, THIS is why you force your customers to stand in line - to hear a sales pitch! I politely declined all of the things she tried to tack on to my already ridiculously priced car rental. Then she asked me a second time. No. No no no no no. I said no the first time. Asking again isn't going to change my answer. While I wasn't a bitch to her (god, I should win an award for that restraint), she should have read the look on my face that I wasn't in the mood. It's called "reading your customer" and can be found on page one in your Sales 101 manual, folks. While she processed my paperwork, a man came in saying he needed to switch cars because he was too tall for the one they assigned him. You would have thought you asked them to find a cure for cancer. Surely this situation has happened before, but that situation required 3 employees and an act of congress. Seriously, oh my god. Bad customer service. Luckily I am vertically challenged and I fit into my assigned car just fine. I finally drove off and had no problems with the car while I had it. When I returned the car the next day it was late afternoon, which seemed to be a busy time for returns. And yet, they only had ONE employee checking people back in. I saw other employees milling about, and even asked one if I was in the right place to check in. He assured me I was and motioned to the guy 5 or 6 cars ahead of me. Sigh. I finally checked it back in, he printed my receipt, and I reluctantly got on the shuttle again. Luckily this driver drove a little less psycho. Overall, I don't think I'll be using Budget again, especially at this location. I'm so used to the way Alamo makes everything a breeze to get you in and out, and Budget is the complete opposite of that. While I do think the fact that they are severely understaffed was part of the issue, the fact that they make no effort to make things speedy for the customer isn't helping - oh sure, they have the 'preferred' club or whatever they call it, but I watched those people in line and their service wasn't any quicker than mine. There is zero efficiency in the way they run their business, and I don't like doing business with places that aren't efficient. Never again, Budget.

text: Sorry but I have to give this place 2 stars because they can't even do the 2 most basic dishes a Vietnamese restaurant should be able to produce. Some background: In an authentic viet restaurant there will always be a huge pot of beef broth boiling day after day with new water and charred beef bones, ginger, onions, other spices added to keep the original broth going. That is how you get the super deep rich flavors in a good bowl of pho. We had the combination pho with all the parts - the broth that came with the soup tasted too new/clean. It was like they started their broth that morning. The color was also all wrong too light and a little murky, and of course as expected the deep rich beef flavor was no where to be found. The rest of the ingredients were as expected, but the broth killed it. We also had the other classic viet dish - combination pork chop plate. Classically to be paired with a char-grilled pork chop, the special egg cake made of meat and other great things, and shredded pork. What we got was soooooo different. The pork chop was dry from overcooking, artificially colored pink (gross) and also did not have any grill flavors to it at all. The egg cake was replaced with a fried egg.

text: "Hot damn these are the best wings in town!" ... "Ohhhh these wings are dry and over-fried. Where's the sauce!?" ... "Man alive these wings are good!" ... "Oh, well, yeah, buffalo sauce would be cool with buffalo wings. I'm never ordering these again." Yeah, The Union Jack Pub is as streaky as your Old Man's briefs. Which, streakiness is really more annoying than just plain awful, because I feel a serious indecision every time friends think about going. There is one thing I know that I'm going to get here though...a damn good bloody mary. It's the celery salt on the glass rim that gets me every time (and it's a meal with its shrimp addition). That ain't pizza...I've seen it...I don't care what you say that is not pizza. I mean...it's not even traditional Chicago-Style Pizza it's something called "Deep Dish Pub Pizza." Huh? Is this what Britons think pizza is? Is this what pseudo-Brit Hoosiers think pizza is? And, yeah, in theory putting a menu on a wooden pizza paddle is a good...in practice, it's over-whelming considering the tables aren't large enough to comfortably put a pizza on. Oh, and I'm not sure if they're trying to make us think it's a "family" restaurant if a 14 year old is the hostess (on 3 separate occasions we were taken to a table -- through the bar -- by someone in braces and a white-shelled necklace. It's terribly awkward communicating with someone who frets over being able to ride roller coasters, or someone who wants to ride roller coasters for that matter. Freakish, really, to have a teenager as a Host. What kind of message is that sending? The service is sloppy. You know the discomfort you feel when your belly is too big and you kind of pull your shirt away from it...hoping to give it some room to breath? Our servers are those uncomfortable bellies. Awkward. Chuckling sniffles like they just toked a bowl. The best is when a server dropped croutons off the salad served then began to pick them up and place them back on my date's plate. That was entertaining...considering...she's into cleanliness. I don't want to hate on the place entirely. The early morning bloody mary and English soccer games are really appealing. Note: weird harsh lighting at times. Especially on the family-seating side. Note: it's more of an "Eatery" than a "Pub" really. Price: Drinks...decent. Large Portion beer specials. Food...you're going to drop 20 on two people here...so...consider what you get for it...and think about what 20 would get you say at...Bruges? Their menu makes "white bean chili," seem exotic. Thrilling. IF I were to go here...I'd take the time to go to the original location on the Westside, and I'd go during May...where you get Race-fans in town. Plus, they have a fireplace, it's cozier, and more authentic in regards to Indy history. They use to have Karaoke! At least 2 years ago, on a weeknight, you could've seen my red-bearded, by the fireplace, stirring and extraordinary rendition of "Me & Mrs. Jones. Mrs Jones! Mrs. Jones!" If that karaoke still happens...no doubt go to the Westside location. My own syntactical grievance: Is it "Union Jack" or is it "Union Jack's?" I want to know. The signage says "Union Jack," which makes no sense: "I'm going to Union Jack...wanna join?" Huh? Is that a verb? If anything...the signage should say, "The Union Jack Pub." But, with everyone's inclination to add the possessive...they should acquiesce and posit that it is indeed Union Jack's Pub. I see this blunder as their waffling ("ahhhh geeeee you don't have waffle fries?") between being really an English Pub or really just a Hoosier Eatery.
label: NEG

text: Preface: I LOVE the local philly music scene. Ever since the GSP went the way of the purple buffalo, I've felt a little displaced. Orphaned by the music scene and desperately in search of a new venue to catch my favorite local bands. How is it that Doc's wound up with the honor? I've been to this bar plenty of times, but to go from such a great set up at the Grape to this makes me so sad. The sound quality is decent and the staff upstairs is always cool, but as a venue, Doc's is pretty lacking. It's tough to actually SEE whoever is playing, unless you're right up front and center. The atmosphere is also really strange. I've been to so many local shows and even though there's a decent amount of crowd changeout on a 3+ band lineup, plenty of people tend to stick around to catch the other bands elsewhere. That's always been one of my favorite parts about the scene: your chances of catching an amazing band you've never even heard of is so greatly increased just by going out to see a band you've already been following. Unfortunately, at Doc's, that's just not the case. It can get so claustrophobic upstairs that people seem to be chomping at the bit to get the eff out of there after the band they came to see is done. And it doesn't help that the other bands themselves don't even stick around. How can anyone expect a local music scene to thrive in such an environment where there's very little support? I feel like the set up of Doc's has lended itself to that air. I mean, maybe they're like the unwanting godparents who suddenly found themselves with this task of taking care of all of the fans and bands that have been left by the wayside after the death of GSP, but I just wish there was something better! I know they do what they can, but I'd rather catch a show somewhere else. Sorry Doc's, nothing personal!

text: who doesn't like an all you can eat buffet?! i am sooo for them. i still have a lone tear from oasis (the all you can eat sushi place on walnut) closing and now being replaced by alfa/walnut room. all you can eat sounds a like a good concept...in theory. this place is near riverview theater and like many buffets, there are no frills. it is a big place and there are set prices. lunch is cheaper. duh. about 7-8 bucks, but dinner is steeper about 9 or so, sunday there is no lunch price, it is all dinner prices. the buffet has a plethora of different types of foods. it is like a hodge podge of left overs. you have your usual fare of fried chicken, fries, the american cuisine. they have a good selection of seafood and since it is all you can eat, go to town! they have jumbo shrimp, crabs, crawl fish, and there is also a sushi bar! the sushi is ok. but it is fresh and made in front of you. they offer fried rice, lo mein and a variety of dumplings and shell fish, oysters and clams and i have even had mussels. the desserts include soft serve with rainbow jimmies, fresh fruit, if you are lucky they put out a big bowl of lychees and ice.mmmmmm. mangos and watermelon and pineapples. they have a plate of cookies, but i was bit scared since i didn't recognize what kind of cookies they were! so i stayed with stuff i knew and that was lychees and soft serve. the service is insanely quick about picking up your plates, cleaning and are attentive. they run a pretty tight ship. they put a bowl on your table for the bones, shells, fruit rinds, etc. and empty it even before you can ask. they seem to keep an eye out on all the tables to make sure your dirty plates don't pile up. the crowd is not center city or old city. you have families there, people stopping before going to the movies, the hung over crowd sitting there eating all fried noodles, etc. memo to yo'self, since it is an all you can eat buffet, i would suggest going with a hearty appetite to truly take advantage of it..and wear elastic waisted pants....ok, perhaps not. but you get the jist. the food is average. i mean the sushi was fine, nothing to write home about, but the variety of stuff there was good, not a lot of vegan/vegetarian stuff, but carnivores should be ok! for the price and the choices, this place is ok. it is a place where it is ok to have plate of sushi, a chinese donut, and red jello. i support all you can eat buffets since it makes eating an adventure!

text: I went here for the 5 course tasting menu on Sunday, 28-Dec-08. From start to finish, Pumpkin delivered a fantastic meal. I would definitely return without an iota of hesitation. Make sure you call about a week ahead for a reservation. I really enjoyed everything about this place. It was a small, cozy place that was well decorated. The service was top tier. The servers were passionate about what they did and always had a smile. Service is one of the most controllable and influential aspects of dining out so its nice to go to a place that really cares about satisfaction. The meal was good sized portions for a tasting menu which is nice considering the potency, complexity and balance in each bite was worth revisiting. I really enjoyed the walu appetizer and flank steak entree. The only part of the meal that was just OK was the salad. This meal was really good because for the week before hand, all I ate was Polish holiday food in my hometown so the freshness and flavors were a great break to that monotony. The only potential downside of this place is that it can be loud. When I was at Pumpkin, there was a table of six people who apparently could only communicate by shouting to each other despite being 3 feet away. Also, I cannot understand how a restaurant like this doesn't take credit cards. I can see the point of not taking cards from a logistic and managerial standpoint but I hope they start taking cards in the future. They also should have a real website. If your a fan of an ever evolving menu and fresh, wholesome ingredients, then you should definitely visit Pumpkin. Great place that I hope is around for a long time.

text: Curses to anyone who has ever posted a bad thing about this place. Vin de Set is an absolute St. Louis gem! From the ambiance, to the food, to the service - everything was impeccable. Let me break it down for you: The Ambiance: I took my mom here for her birthday. Being a weeknight, we had no problems nabbing a spot on the roof - but I can see how that could be a challenge on a weekend. The roof was much larger than expected and, actually, contained its own bar. The true beauty of it came when it started to get dark. First, the views are fabulous. Second, they have cute little white lights dangled that contribute to the cool! The inside is impressive as well. Exposed brick, dark - whoever designed this place has mad mood-setting skills. The Food: Oh Muh Gawd...the deliciousness started immediately with, of all things, the bread plate. The bread comes with three toppings to savor: 1) olive oil, 2) olive tapenade and 3) herbed butter...that I'm pretty sure I could eat straight. Don't judge me! From there we tried the baked brie appetizer - my least favorite item of the evening, but not horrible. I had the Steak au Poivre (grilled beef tenderloin medallions w/ brandy-pink peppercorn sauce) and every bite melted in my mouth. Steak was cooked exactly to my liking. My mom tried the Seared Duck Breast w/ cherry balsamic glaze and loved it. I'm not much of a dessert person, but had to try something here b/c the offerings are ridiculous (in a good way). We split the Maple Mascarpone Cheesecake. This was eyes-rolling-in-the-back-of-my-head delicious! I venture to say...the best dessert I've EVER had. Bonus points that you can order your coffee in a French Press to go with it! The Service: Service was excellent from the minute we stepped off the elevator and were greeted. Our server was very good at explaining everything, being around but not overbearing and, generally, adding to our good experience. My only complaint is that their wine list doesn't provide any short descriptions to distinguish between the offerings. We told our server what type we were after and she didn't fail with her recommendation. My Jerry Springer Final Thought: This place costs much less that it could or should, considering the entire experience. Great value. It has the whole package and I'll certainly be back.

text: The short review: I'd heard such good things about this place before I went there - it's a shame my experience was so awful, mostly due to service. The experience might've been salvaged if the food was amazing, but it wasn't ... it was normal diner food. Overpriced diner food. If you're looking for an enjoyable, relaxing breakfast where you don't get yelled at for asking for anything, DON'T go here. It might be different on a Wednesday at 10:30 am, but us poor work-a-day folks on a weekend brunch schedule deserve a decent breakfast experience too. The amazingly bad details: 1) You'd think that a veteran breakfast joint would know to have a lot of food available on a Sunday morning. We tried to order FOUR different items off the specials list, and the server crossed off each one as we ordered it. He then checked, told me there was one order of X available, and ten minutes later, came back to tell me he was wrong, and that was sold out as well. How does a diner run out of food?? C'mon. It's ALL YOU DO, people. If you're a diner, you might want to, I don't know, have more food available. So we ended up with overpriced, normal eggs, pancakes, bacon. Fine if we're going to the Melrose. NOT fine when we pay $30 for breakfast for two. 2) My companion asked if they could add bacon to the frittata - the server snapped "No special orders today!" Um, okay. Fine. No need to be snippy. 3) Any server worth their salt will be able to deal with a busy Sunday brunch with minimal problems. This particularly cranky server forgot to bring the hot chocolate (after I reminded him twice), forgot ketchup, forgot the pancake syrup (twice), and totally forgot our order of grits. Then gave me a dirty look when I asked for these things again. I'd normally give some slack because it's busy, but when a server makes ME feel bad for asking for something a few times... well, that's pretty inexcusable. Again, it's what you do. Don't be bad at it and expect a good review. Or tip. 5) When we got the not-small check and noticed grits were still on the bill, we asked about it POLITELY. The belligerent server then snapped that he already took it off, and then said to the host (still within earshot to us) "I hate that f***ing table." Seriously? For politely asking one question after you've overcharged us, don't have anything on the menu, and forgotten everything we DID order? Bullocks to that. You couldn't pay me to go back to the Morning Glory, and if a friend asked me for a choice between this place and another, I'm pretty sure I'd always choose the other. Shame.

text: The Bleeding Deacon is a dark, smoky, S. City neighborhood bar with music related decor and lots of bald headed, facial haired, pierced individuals running around (think Royale, CBGB's, etc.). The service is friendly. They have a jukebox with an eclectic selection of tunes, or you might hear everything from Red Hot Chili Peppers to Cheap Trix via iPod. They also have Wi-fi, multi player LAN games and a small patio out back. The menu is definitely a step up for pub grub. Lots of comfort food with a modern twist. Very reasonably priced. The entrees average $10 and most every thing else is less than that. The value is very good. And while bacon is a menu staple (even on the dessert menu), they also cater to vegetarians. Sweet potatoes are a staple too (mashed and salsa - yum!). A couple of negatives... the place is smoky, the chicken with mac & cheese entree is sounds great but fails to deliver any taste and the 20% gratuity for parties of 6 or more is a joke. Mandatory gratuity for small groups (less than 10) is quickly becoming a St. Louis standard and is ridiculous. I understand with large groups but let's get this straight people. GRATUITY IS OPTIONAL and not enforceable under law (unless it is agreed upon and in a contract, such as a restaurant discount program or a catering contract). In addition, PAY YOUR PEOPLE. It's not our job! Amount of tip is for me to decide based on the service provided. There is nothing wrong with suggesting a tip, but adding it is another thing. Overall, I think the Bleeding Deacon is a great find because of the affordable, bar food that is homemade and tasty. I've had better comfort food in a bar for less, but it's a great value, which gets them almost 4 stars. If it was smoke free, it would be four stars without a doubt.

text: On this cold and rainy day here in Philadelphia, what better thing to do than walk around the West side and see what there is to see? The Last Word Bookshop was one of the two places of salvation I stumbled across haphazardly--the other being the Green Line cafe a handful of blocks further out. I did my normal run through the poetry section, and then checked out a few of my "hero-novelists" (D. H. Lawrence, Henry Miller) and had some pretty damn good results. Lawrence's "section" (an entire row!) proved to be the most fruitful I've stumbled across. I picked up a rare book of his essays for five bucks. Oh yeah--the poetry section was huge, featuring a lot of small/no-namers, which I consider a bonus, and a lot of classic/canonical tomes that one could expect any book store to have. I wish there had been a modern/contemporary section, though maybe there is, and I just missed it (some book stores like to section off their "popular/hip poetry" from the ol' dusty lyrics. The atmosphere is definitely nice--books piled up on the floor, but all the shelves maintained with quirky precision--genres both specific and broad, for every type of browser. I met the owner upon checking out (at least I think he's the owner)--Frank, who said business was good and welcomed my recent move to Philly. Go him. Most book store owners are cranky zealous socialites.

text: short answer: very disappointing! I stopped by this restaurant with a bunch of friends when we were passing through St. Louis. I was really excited when I saw their menu - there was so much awesome-sounding vegetarian food that I wanted to try! I remember saying I wished I could eat three meals in a row. Thank god I didn't. I ordered the special baked cheese fries and vegan chili which our server highly recommended. The service was friendly but mostly inattentive. (Come on! There were only two tables!) The food seemed to take around 40 minutes to prepare, which seemed a bit much for a diner - but I was so psyched to try this place I didn't really mind. When it eventually arrived I was disappointed to find that the "specialty" baked fries were indubitably Ore-Ida frozen crinkle cut fries, right out of the bag. But much worse was that they were obviously burned to a crisp. Literally blackened. It was the same for everyone at the table. Burned in the sense that I would probably not feed them to my dog if I had one. I'm by no means a restaurant snob or even a very picky guy, but I was still incredulous. But I was equally starving, and made an attempt to eat the less blackened fries. Amazingly, they somehow managed to char the outsides while leaving the insides lukewarm. I turned my attention to the veggie chili which was also less that hot and less than tasty. Out of the 6 of people at our table, only one had a positive experience (he had the seitan reuben). One of my friends suggested that his tuna tasted like cat food. The server did not check on us until it was time to settle the check. She acted surprised to see burned fries left on the plates and offered me a $2 discount. What a joke. The cooks knew they were inedible and so did the server. Not inedible by restaurant snob standards, inedible by regular people standards. I understand that sure, things are gonna get burned once in a while, but for f**k's sake either make it again or apologize and offer something else to the customer. Honestly, I had such a uniquely awful experience at this restaurant that I created a Yelp account just to let people know.

text: I really want this place to be great, so we keep going back - but every time it's simply not. It could be a fantastic neighborhood restaurant - it's cozy and they have a great outdoor area when the weather is nice - perfect to walk to! We went last night (a Tuesday night)after getting the Hot Sauce deal that morning and I thought they would have ramped up the service because of that extra publicity - not the case. There were only a few tables occupied when we arrived, but at least 3 of them hadn't been bussed yet. Our server was really very pleasant and ultimately extremely helpful but even that couldn't overcome the shortcomings of the meal. We started with the chorizo stuffed dates, by far the BEST thing we ate - they were super tasty. The mushroom soup had no seasoning, the veal meatball capellini was a bowl of mushy noodles with no seasoning in the tomato sauce, and the mushroom ravioli needed salt, too. The grilled cheese was the second best thing we ordered - and I always LOVE the sweet potato fries. We had a few minor mistakes with our dishes which our server remedied to our satisfaction. I hope they work the kinks out (even though they've had a few years to do it by now) now that the Hot Sauce deal is out there...
