text: I have lived down the block from Era for the last 3 years and of course have ventured there for some quick cheap drinks both before and after a night out on the town, but had never eaten in the restaurant they have in the back before. My roomie and I decided before moving out of the neighborhood next week that we should check out Era's Authentic Ethiopian food since we have only heard good things about it. To my surprise, the food was EXCELLENT! The service was great. I ordered the beef with exotic spices, while my roommate ordered the lamb with mild spices. We both ordered the lentils on the side as well as the veggie side dish (note: the side salad has a very spicy dressing if you like spice). I was impressed with all the flavors and spice the dish had. The sides complemented the main dishes well. The injera (bread) was essential to the meal (the earthy flavor helped cut the heat of the spices in the beef) and served the dual purpose of your utensil. Since they didn't provide utensils, you used the bread to scoop up the food. I really enjoyed this aspect of the dining experience. Overall the food was great and reasonably priced ($10/entree...another huge plus). We ordered some beers along with our dinner, but wine and liquor were also available. If you have never had Ethiopian food, I would highly recommend it, especially if you are a fan of Indian food as the spices were reminiscent of Indian cuisine.

I really liked the fact that he was nearby (5 Points) and that his business was fairly new on the East side. He has another location in Pleasant View, TN. When I called to make my appointment, I discovered that the East location is currently only open on Tuesdays and Thursday until they build up more business. We were able to book my appointment within the same month. When I arrived yesterday for my consultation, I was very impressed by the gorgeous new building that was tweaked out with top of the line equipment and design. The office is very modern but still offers up warmth and charm. The dental assistant did all of my x-rays of my teeth and took pictures which she transferred to a disc for my records. I just had to lay back in the chair and watch the television that was plastered on the ceiling. Stress free! When Dr. Hadley zipped in, they did a comprehensive exam of my teeth and explained everything thoroughly including suggestions for future cleanings and work. He was thoughtful and did not try to "over-sell" me on any unnecessary services. I was disappointed to find out that I have my first cavity at 30 years old but hey...it could be worse? My office visit was an efficient 45 minutes long with no wait time! I will update my review after my teeth-cleaning and other procedures are completed but we are off to a great start!! TIP: Very laid back office...Dr. Hadley wore a bright orange lab coat to get the point across that he's a TN fan. I wouldn't talk trash to him while he is performing any procedures! text: I had a perfect new year's eve here. After seeing that sign, as well as reading the reviews beforehand that their portions were huge, we decided to go with one pasta dish and have a appetizer sampler instead. Their stuffed mushrooms, caprese were good, but I couldn't help noticing that I was totally indulging in their spinich and artichoke dip. Oh... and their rolls, infused with olive oil and all the good Italian herbs, were excellent. Then came the half portion of meatball spaghetti. Half portion was so huge that two of us never got to finish. Their wine list isn't that huge but they had a nice mix of Italian wines and California wines. We had a Pinot Noir from Meridian that was highly recommended, and it paired really well with the food. What was even more awesome was that we actually had an opportunity to pass this winery at Paso Robles, on the way back home from Monterey. The place had lots of people dressed up for New Year's Eve parties, but the atmosphere isn't all that dressy. The interior struck me kind of odd, and seating wasn't all that comfy, and their service was kind of slow, but hey, it was New Year's Eve when everyone should be happy. So it's all good. text: Syberg's is in the same genre' as Bennegins, Applebees, etc. with a fishy little twist that I like. Attached to the Hampton Inn on Market, it is a casual and popular eating place for the local lunch crowd, happy hour crew and hotel guests. It has a sporty atmosphere, a bar/smoking area and the decor has local flavor. If you are looking for a sandwich, burger, salad or plate of pasta, you are in a good spot. The appetizer menu is also decent and features the usual suspects: chicken wings, potato skins, etc. What I'd like to suggest to you are the two things that really sets them apart. Number one, the shark bites (available as an appetizer or as a lunch/salad combo). They are tender, lemony, seasoned and served with drawn butter for dipping. If you get the appetizer you get a fruit salad (mine was mixed melons, pineapple and a single grape. :( I really like grapes, sadly). If you get the lunch combo it comes with a tossed salad. I grew up near the ocean and let me assure you that most shark leans towards the dense and dry. But not here. Next time I go I'm going to actually try the shark steak dinner. I can't wait! We also had a turkey club croissant. The bread was flaky and buttery, just perfect. The fries were ...eh... crinkly and could be bought at Schnucks for $1.99 frozen in the bag... but the sandwich itself was great, no complaints at all. My Number two reason for trying Syberg's... the beer. The BIG beer. They call it the Macho. I have no idea how big it is, but it can't be less than 40 oz and served in an ice cold glass mug. The beer stays cold, even if you are a nurser. I've tried a few of the other things as well - pastas, salads, bread. All good, not outstanding, but certainly solid and reliable with regards to quantity and taste. Now, here is the thing Syberg's gets HUGE points from me on. I had to be somewhere very nearby by 1 p.m. We were seated at Syberg's at about 12:21 p.m. I told our waitress that I was in a super hurry. She said 'no problem'. We ordered, ate, paid (using a credit card), had cheesecake wrapped up and taken to go and I made it in the door of my destination by 12:57 p.m. I was beyond impressed and for that reason alone they are forgiven for the fries. :) P.S. The cheesecake was yummy. Vanilla bean and the Raspberry. P.S.S. They don't normally deliver, but I know that they DO make an exception for the poor guests over at the Courtyard Marriott, since they have no attached restaurant of thier own.

text: I wanted to love Onesto. It's very cute inside - like a local pizza place with style. Painted tin ceiling, lots of staff, free (delicious) garlic knots, and a real wine and beer menu. The menu looks fantastic, as does the pizza. We saw lots of pizzas on their way to tables, and each one looked better than the last. Despite all appearances, this was not a good experience. Let's look at each course that we ordered. Garlic Knots: Fantastic. Really. They keep them in a little oven by the door so they are piping hot when they give them to you. Fried Mozzarella: Delicious. Great sauce, great breading. Spaghetti with Meatballs: Two of us planned to share this and a small pizza. The pasta and sauce was good, but the meatballs were RAW in the middle. When we pointed this out to the waitress, she apologized and said they've been having that problem with the meatballs lately. She offered to make us another one but we decided to pass. Pizza: It took about 45 minutes for the first pizza to come out. I'm pretty sure they must have forgotten or burnt it, because we saw quite a few other pizzas come out while we were waiting for ours. I say "first" because the toppings were not as we ordered them. She said she'd put in an order for a plain pizza as well. By the time the second pizza came out (around 10:30 PM), they had turned up the lights and had started cleaning up for the night. I had a slice of the second pizza (cheese only) and it was OK. Not amazing. Definitely not as good as Raccinnelli's, or even Domino's. Then the bill comes and, to my surprise, they charged us for the spaghetti and meatballs! I asked her to take it off the bill, which she was happy to do for us. She also sent a free tiramisu dessert home with us as an apology. I know the timing of the food and the undercooked meatballs are just small glitches that you can expect from any new restaurant. If the pizza was amazing we'd probably go back... but it wasn't, and we probably won't. I should mention that the service was great... very attentive and friendly. Our server apologized several times for the problems they had that night.

Literally designed with this stuff in mind, I was able to find exactly what I needed. When it came time to organize the kitchen, I liked the idea of the jars but needed airtight ones. Not a problem. What size? Did I prefer round, or square, or bell shaped? They had it all. I even bought an oversized one to keep cat food in. Yes. I'm. That. Organized. Of course there are thousands of other items to feed that obsessive compulsive disorder, closet organizers, shoe trees, kitchen widgets, office supplies that you didn't know existed but certainly can't live without. text: Yeah yeah let's all make fun of Whole Foods by calling it "Whole Paycheck . . .". Okay, finished? Now yes you can't expect Walmart supermarket prices from here, but let's face it - Walmart sucks for a variety of reasons (i.e. exploitation of their employees), but Walmart in New Orleans is downright SCARY. The employees don't get paid enough to care about their jobs and the other customers are sometimes very scary (I won't delve too deeply into personal accounts, but I was semi-stalked there once by a random fellow customer and I truly RAN into the restroom). Sure John Mackey, CEO of Walmart, is a verifiable nutjob, but there really isn't too much else in terms of vegan-friendly, organic, environmentallly conscious grocers in New Orleans (grrr!), so Whole Foods is my heavenly haven. The employees are mostly super duper helpful and friendly. Sometimes too friendly . . . but very well informed about their products and if not, they can always direct you to someone who is. As far as Whole Foods as a whole (hah, I made funny!) goes, this one has a little less selection in terms of vegan products (but more than the larger Veteran's location), but there's plenty more regional-themed products to satisfy the locals. They have excellent quality control for their produce, meats (I am told) and they even take great care to not stock the damaged boxes and cans (for the most part). Some of my favorite ares are the bulk section (buy in bulk and it will be comparable to Wamart prices!), the salad bar (love that tofu), and the wine area is pretty darn decent. Also it's kind of not-so-nice that the products at this Whole Foods are noticeably pricier here than they are in Austin or Houston but okay, I'm over it. Also a minor point, but in case anyone is curious - I only buy my cat's food here. I don't like feeding her Purina and all that other awful stuff, but I can't afford Pet Promise, so she's stuck with the 365 brand of dry and cat food. She's not a finicky eater, but she was a bit snotty about the dry food at first - now she loves it. And it is completely cheap and a billion times better than Iams and all that mess. Just a FYI! Oh and Whole Foods publishes a "The Whole Deal" coupon, recipe, etc. booklet every month or two and the coupons sometime coincide nicely with the weekly deals. Check it out!

text: Friday evening, 7:00pm reservation. We got right in, were seated a super small 2 table. Ordered drinks, waited at least 15-20 min. for them to be brought to the table. Ordered appetizer (carpaccio), salads (caesar and pear gorganzola) entrees (veal Marsala and lobster pappardelle). I wanted the truffle fetuchini but was told they were out of duck. After another wait the appetizer was delivered, but it was wrong. Instead of Carpaccio we were brought Capresed (tomato salad) I guess they both start with C. The server who was not the waiter apologized and returned it for the right order. We ordered a 2nd round of drinks, which took even longer to get than the first time. We were told the bar tender was busy. The carpaccio came out, the presentation was pretty but I have never seen beef sliced so thin! We couldn't even lift it off the plate without it becoming a mushy mess plus there was way more arugula than beef. It was OK as far as flavor but nothing special. As we were waiting our entrees were brought... I told the server that we hadn't had our salad yet. He looked confused but said there must be some kind of mix up in the kitchen apologized again and left. Finally the salads were served, my husband thought the Caesar was good but hard to eat since it was presented in a bowl made of parmesean cheese which tended to want to tip over . My pear salad was good but the pear was not very pleasing to look at. I don't know if it was because it had been slightly grilled or if it was turning brown from being left out too long, plus it was hard. Finally the entrees were brought back, I actually asked if these were the same plates they brought out in the first place I was told no, they threw that out and these are fresh plates. But.. there was no pappardelle.. they ran out and didn't tell me this. They substituted with a rigatoni like pasta. Charlie liked his veal, he thought it was very good. Mine tasted good, but it wasn't the pasta I wanted and the pasta was under cooked. Plus the lobster was out of those thin little legs and I think they only used one or 2 legs.. no lobster in there what so ever and for 25.00 I would expect more lobster. Desert was Tiramisu which was just OK, coffee was luke warm. They charged us for the Caprese so we had to sent the bill back and then we found that they didn't charge for the lobster pasta.. which was nice but the waiter never came to tell us that they were going to comp the dish or apologize for all the mix up. It took us over 2 hours to get through dinner. We will definately not be going back there again.

text: I probably am being harsher than it actually is. Perhaps, i could have given 3 stars. However, this place was no more than "hip" restaurant that serves average asian food that's far worse than a lot of authentic places in chinatown and vietnamese establishments in washington ave, purely in the name of "fusion". I personally hate this type of place. By this type of place, here's what i mean: 1. menu is not coherent (they serve an array of things that are *asian* from thai, japanese, chinese, etc., without any real thoughts behind it...they are just...well, asian...) Why do I hate this thought? IMHO, it gives away the thought that asian is something you can categorize as Italian or French. Why not call a restaurant a European fusion and see what kind of menu we can come up with? 2. Asian BBQ Pork. Seriously? Don't just call BBQ pork Asian...each country (each region of each country) has very distinct taste... So you call something "asian bbq" because it resembles something in a regional Chinese cuisine? Come on... Just say what it is...five-spice, Korean chili paste infused, etc. It just seems ignorant. 3. The sashimi, dumplings, and whole fried fish...they were all average if not below average, compared to thai restaurants that serve whole fried fish, experienced sushi chef, or places in chinatown that serve dumplings. So putting them all in the same place justifies the food being average because the place has a bit of everthing...i don't think so. 4. The place is just too "hip". It probably has to make up in the ambiance for what it lacks in the food department. 5. Their "famous" lobster dish is no more than lobster with mashed potato, Morimoto's curry-spice infused lobster dish is a fusion I can be comfortable with; otherwise, just eat at the ethnic places. The only saving grace for this place, IMHO, is the dessert. Everyone in my party enjoyed the deserts: the dessert "bento", the tart, and the chocolate cake...they were all pretty good (the reason why they are getting 2 stars).

text: A trip to Elizabeth's Restaurant is like returning home. This beautiful old house in New Orleans' Bywater area has braved its neighboring levees and survived around 100 years of intense weather conditions. The quaint two-story dining destination offers a casual downstairs space, as well as an upstairs bar and cozy eating room. Though Elizabeth's has received substantial praise, especially for their Sunday brunch, the crowd appears to be more locals than tourists. One of our native friends recommended that we visitors cancel our reservation at the "stuffy" Rib Room in the French Quarter and opt for this local favorite. She drove us out to the remote cottage, which was oddly surrounded by factories, lumber yards, and other appetite-suppressing views. This down-to-earth spot even lacks a traditional parking lot, causing patrons to brake their vehicles on the steep grass hill across the street. As we approached the cafe, we noticed several people waiting outside and knew that our hunger was not going to be satisfied any time soon. We were politely told that we could wait for our table at the upstairs bar, where we were surrounded by the post-church crowd and other groups of locals. The unfriendly bartender brushed off our drink request, but finally returned with our spicy bloody mary's about twenty minutes later. Though I usually do not like this earthy beverage, the Elizabethan blend was sweeter and tangier than most. A crisp string bean was dipped into the glass as a complimentary garnish. We were later seated at one of the country-style wooden tables in the small neighboring dining room. We enjoyed their famous pralined bacon appetizer; the sweet glaze was a delicious balance against the greasy meat. I also ordered the "Basic Breakfast", which included two scrambled eggs and my choice of hash browns or grits. I opted for the clumpy corn grits, trying to get in touch with my Southern side, but was not impressed. The dish was not very interesting, but I guess I received what I ordered - a "basic" meal. My friends seemed to enjoy their various versions of Eggs Benedict, but also just picked at their grits. A meal at Elizabeth's provides the opportunity to escape the glitz of the French Quarter and relax among a real N'awlins crowd. The food is above average, but I would suggest ordering one of their unique meals and cocktails rather than the safe, "basic" option I went with.

text: Every Tuesday night, Square One has a "Build A Burger" night. The basic burger starts at $2, and you're handed a list of toppings -- I think there are about 30 in all -- which range from .25 (for a leaf of lettuce) to around 1.50 (bacon). The burger itself is far from special, but the price is right and the process is fun. You can construct a pretty amazing, specialized burger for less than $6, which won't even get you off the ground at a place like New American Burger in Central West End or Burger Bar downtown. My goat cheese, lettuce, tomato, carmelized onions, bacon, and chipotle mayo burger was pretty fantastic -- and the fries are great as well. Square One is more than just a burger restaurant, though. They've got a nice, big menu and, of course, the beer. Last night I tried the Wheat Wine, which was unique and delicious. The cocktail list is also impressive. Square One is also just a cool place to hang out; the staff is nice, the bar (even on a Tuesday night) was comfortably packed, and the restaurant had its own section so you were away from the smoke and noise. One note, though, to late diners: the kitchen is supposed to close at 10, but they start to pack up early so if you come past 9:30, be prepared to be rushed through your order. Enjoy!

text: Yuck. HIGHLY disappointed. used to hit up Scotty's in Bloomington all the time when I was in school. Somehow I don't remember it being as overpriced and underwhelming as it recently was. It was actually so poor it is why I'm on here right now bc it inspired me to finally get on Yelp and stop being a lurcker and just post something myself already. We went on a Thursday, around happy hour time. good crowd, competent and attentive server. liked the personal tvs at each table. Boyfriend's draft beer had too many bubbles in it. but whatever, he ordered cheap beer and maybe should have gone with a microbrew instead. So if I had to give stars based on only those elements, maybe 4. But definitely sticking to "1" for the food. I know a good burger and I will pay good money and travel a good distance for a good one. this was most decidedly NOT that, not comparable to Capital Grill or Harry&Izzys or 14 West or McCormicks where their prime burgers are even less expensive to begin with! and it truly paled against any of the local (and cheaper!) awesomeness like Barringer's or Bub's, or heck, 96th street burgers right down the street, where they all always deliver the whole package--beverage-burger-fries/rings--deal spot on right. Everytime. Scotty's really likes to push the build-your-own-burger where even the condiments are an extra 75 cents. Our server's every other sentence promoted that. I had the bison burger cooked medium well on a ciabatta bun. Onion rings on the side. Ciabatta bread was so dry and stale it was unsalvagable-- even with bandaids mayo, ketchup, nothing worked. it wasn't even toasted and it literally just crumbled in your hands... i ended up having to eat a carb-free burger with fork and knife. Also, my patty was not medium well, it was well-well. I asked for pickles and got 2, which they brought to us ever so ceremoniously in a small container sitting on it's own little plate. for TWO pickle slices?! I mean, you had to laugh. what, do i have to cough up another $0.75 for 2 more? is it that too much to ask? I got 5 small soggy cold onion rings for my $2.50 upgrade. My friends, Hardees has better onion rings. steak n shake has better onion rings. you get my drift. AGAIN, i don't mind the cash, just could you please just make it so i'm paying for something reasonably half-decent! Boyfriend ordered the Indiana Prime burger, cooked well, w/ cheddar cheese and bacon. w/ potato soup as the side. His bun was okay, burger was medium--- NOT well, as he'd requested his. Cheese was a ghost of a slice, as if it had melted completely away before it got to the table. Bacon slices were limp and chewy. Meat did not taste any better than any other ol ground chuck patty. Soup was goupy and flavorless-- he said even crappy foodservice Outback's is better. So the check came and our two sandwiches came out to about $15 each. For all that you have just read above. and that's that folks. FAR TOO MANY other great burger joints around town than to give this one a second chance.

text: **want to clarify it wasn't the food that made him sick, he had the flu** I've been here many times and always had a pleasant experience. However, I went here over the weekend with my boyfriend. while we were there he started feeling very bad (he ended up having the flu). He tried using the bathroom but it was locked. He had to basically run from the back to the front of the restaurant to make it out the front door. He got sick right outside. He was extremely embarrassed but did not have any other options. A woman who worked there proceeded to walk out and yell at him as if he did it on purpose. He was so mortified that he just left. After a text from him, I asked for the check and headed to checkout. This is where I headed to the register to find the entire staff laughing at his expense. when I let them know that I was with him the woman ringing me up said- "well why didn't he try to go into the bathroom?" I was then asked by my server "well I hope last night was fun, was it worth it?" - I let the entire staff know that he was not in fact, hungover, but actually quite sick. Although it was embarrassing for the both of us, and inconvenient for the restaurant, they are in the hospitality industry and probably shouldn't have yelled at one of their customers for being sick. They also shouldn't have assumed that he was drunk/hungover. And speaking about him infront of everyone, not knowing that I was with him was extremely rude. I have always raved about this place. But i am so put off by their behavior over the weekend that I wont be returning and don't intend on ever telling anyone else to go here. while I do apologize to them for the unfortunate incident that happened at the restaurant, I do believe that their behavior was absolutely unacceptable.

text: Felipe's does the cheap taqueria thing well. Fresh ingredients, tasty food, light on the wallet...nothing fancy...and it doesn't need to be. The food speaks for itself. I'm not giving it five stars because when I went there it was a slammin' Thursday night, and someone thought it was a brilliant idea to be training someone on the line while the place was packed and the line was quite literally out the door. No. I'm sorry...but you just don't do that. Not unless you want for it to take 5 minutes per customer to go through, and for people to leave after already waiting for 15 to 20 minutes with the line not moving an inch, which is what was happening. Save the training for the day shift. But after waiting the half an hour to get to the counter, I have to say, that was one of the better quesadillas I've ever had (carnitas with monterey jack, pico de gallo & guacamole, if you're interested in knowing...though I went back two days later and got a steak quesadilla which was equally as good). Their salsa bar was really good too. I especially enjoyed the pickled carrots. I've been home from N.O. less than 24 hours, and I'm already missing Felipe's.

text: This market is an absolute miracle for downtown Nashville! Even though residents of downtown had food selections available at Walgreen, Dollar General & several small bodega-type stores prior to the arrival of H G Hill Urban Market, we haven't had anything comparable to this in decades. H G Hill Urban Market has a full line of groceries, frozen food, beer, produce, meats, snacks, household items, etc. A very important feature within the market is the deli, stocked full of prepared food and desserts. I have no doubt that a person could purchase all their groceries here and never really feel the need to venture elsewhere ... certainly not more than once a month or so for favorite items not found within these walls. The market is appropriate for quick items & meals for office workers and tourists and as a complete market for downtown dwellers. To make matters even better, the hours are fantastic, open every day (including most holidays) from morning until 9 PM. I am giving the full five stars. Considering the entire picture, I don't feel that it is appropriate to deduct points just because there is not space enough to carry every brand of every cereal, etc. There is certainly enough of everything to provide all of us with what we need. Regarding the prices, I don't find them especially different. Certainly some items may cost a few cents more than at a large suburban market; but some items are also on sale at any given time. Some of the items may seem high priced because they truly are upscale and/or organic items; but there's plenty standard selections for those on a budget. THANK YOU H G Hills for coming to our rescue!

text: I went to this place around 6 PM on a Saturday. It's small and dimly lit, there are several tables and a couple of bar stools. There's a flat screen TV hanging in the corner. The restaurant was fully packed, nobody was waiting to be seated but a couple of people just sat at the bar and ordered so they wouldn't have to wait for a table. Service was very slow and awkward the entire night. I'm thinking the waiter must have been new because he kept asking us what drinks we had so he could get us refills, but then he'd forget to actually refill the drinks. This happened more than once. We also had to go to the bar to ask for silverware because our server fogot to bring us any and he was nowhere to be found. I also think he forgot to put in our order. I can understand fried chicken which is cooked to order taking about 20-30 minutes, but our waiter came to our table to "confirm our order" 40 minutes after it was placed, and then our food arrived 20 minutes after that. Bogus. The food itself wasn't bad. I had the fried chicken, white meat, with red beans and rice, and my friend had chicken wings with mashed potatoes. The chicken came out hot and juicy, the skin was battered nicely (although I'd rank it below Willie Maes). The three piece white meat was just under $9, and if you order chicken wings they charge something like 75 cents per wing. The most striking thing about the entire dinner was that we saw TWO ROACHES climbing the wall while waiting for our check. I'm a little suspicious that the waiter saw the roaches and pretended not to see them. Nobody made any attempt to remove them from the eating area, and they scurried to hide underneath some wall decorations. Yes people, when you eat here there may be roaches hiding along the walls next to your table. I couldn't pay my check and get out of there quick enough. If I was rating this place strictly on food then I'd probably give it 3 and a half stars, but when you consider the service and hygeine of the place I can't justify anything above one star. If you're that much into their chicken just order delivery and try not to think too much about the cleanliness of where it came from.

text: I love Ron's! The service is great, and the beer selection will knock your socks off. We've been several times in the last few weeks, and absolutely everything we've ordered, whether the wings or a salad or a sandwich or their signature "ovals" (basically pizza sans sauce) has been terrific. It's worth pointing out that the bar area and restaurant are two completely different worlds. The bar is beautifully decorated, warm and welcoming, and the service is exceptional -- even when busy. The restaurant feels like a separate establishment. Still good, but tons and tons of kids and families. Which is fine, of course, but the bar feels much more sophisticated (but still casual) than the restaurant, which is a little more generic and Olive Garden-ish. If it's just you and your significant other, or you and a couple of good friends: head to the bar. If it's you and the kiddies and grandma: the restaurant is the place to go. Not in the mood to dine in? Head next door for their take-out, which features an amazing selection of beers, both obscure and well-known. Either way, Ron's is a must-stop for any and all beer fans in the area.

text: If overpriced, inferior quality ingredients, poorly prepared, served with a doze of snobbism, in a pretentious atmosphere, is what you are looking for, Georges' is for you. The bread basket was visually stunning, and if all we desired was to bask in it's beauty, it would have been great, unfortunately we were hungry. The bread was hard and dry. The "epis", (wheat stalk shaped loaves), were so hard, you could have broken a tooth, if you foolishly attempted to bite into one. The bread was served with only an oil dispenser, that did not dispense. No herbs, no seasonings, no salt or pepper. The dinner itself was also unpalatable. There were three of us, all the dishes were loaded with salt. We actually love salty foods, but these courses were way too salty, even for us. My soft-shell crab, that I normally love, was smothered in blue cheese. Not only all you could taste was the blue cheese, no taste of crab left, but it had soaked, and moistened the soft-shell, making it tough and un-chewable. The steak and frittes, was a small, inexpensive, half gristle, cut of meat, served with greasy fries. The New York strip, was small, salty, like everything else, and cooked well, opposed to medium rare as requested. Dessert, was unremarkable at $9.00 each. The service was snobbish and un-warm. Even though two thirds of our meals were left unconsumed, we were never asked if the meals met with our satisfaction. I don't understand the good reviews! High prices do not guarantee a good repast! Are the high prices, snobby waiters and pompous surroundings, deluding the clientele into thinking they had a good meal? I am in my middle fifties, and have been lucky enough to enjoy meals all over the world, some fabulously wonderful, some not so great. I've had top quality, and humble ingredients, both expertly prepared. I have learned long ago, not to equate price with quality. Georges' will go down in my culinary experience, as one of the worst value, incompetently prepared meals, I have ever had the displeasure of partake of. We left unsatisfied, unhappy, puzzled by the good reviews attributed to this restaurant. Maybe they were having a bad day? Maybe the chef was on vacation? Maybe the salt shaker just slipped of his fingers, it will remain an unsolved mystery. We, will never know, go back to Georges', or recommend it to any of our friends and family. Our enemies, if we had any, now that, is a different story.

text: Summary: If you are passing through Tucson and need a place to stay for the evening at an affordable price with an added adventure, this is definitely your place! Now the reason I ended up in this interesting establishment is because my family's home was pretty packed so I decided to make other sleeping arrangements. It was only going to be for a night, so I said why not. I took this as a great opportunity to explore new places and play secret shopper! Experience: Let's just say this is no Hyatt Regency! I've stayed there and I wasn't impressed with them either, but that's another story. The customer service offered at Motel Super 8 is non-existent. I had a friend mention to me that when he researches hotels, his criteria is for the service to match the price, which can be somewhat debatable. But in this case, he's right on. Before I checked in, I asked the clerk if the rooms had wi-fi. He said yea. Then he continued by saying, " Are you trying to get a hold of some Johns or what?" I looked at him and said excuse me, you're joking right!! Then I asked the clerk how the area was and he responded, " Well I think the cops are looking for someone so it should be safe since they will be posted near." I looked at him with my eyes wide open and asked him to clarify what he meant. He repeated the same thing as he gave me my keycard. At that point I should have grabbed my bags and left. But I didn't! I was tired and wanted to sleep. Moving forward the key card didn't work, so I walked back to the office. I was already paranoid, so walking was more of a fast walk to the office and back to the room. Finally, a working keycard! I opened the door and panned over the room and thought I must be in a horror movie. The top lock was halfway unscrewed as if someone was trying to push the door open from the other side. So I used my key card to screw it back in. It worked! But that's not the worst part; I was on my laptop surfing when I heard a noise. I couldn't distinguish what it was, so I turned down the T.V. From a distance I heard not a scream, nor a yell, but someone crying from the pit of their stomach, " Noooooooo"....Noooooooo". I was like WTF is going on here! I turned off the lights (I'm not sure why I turned off the lights). The cry was getting closer. Then literally it was right outside my door!!! I looked through the peephole and I didn't see anything! I was thinking to myself -Oh my god it's the Llorona (Mexican Folklore). A few minutes later it was gone. I will have to say this motel would be a great place to visit on Halloween. Forget haunted houses, just visit Super 8! Location: 715 W. Starpass, Tucson, AZ Uniqueness: Very, but come equipped with a bat or a tool belt. Affordability: Less than $40 Cleanliness: Somewhat Services: * Easy Access to I-10 & I-19 * Free HBO, ESPN, ESPN2 * Free wireless High Speed Internet

text: I desperately wish I could give this place more stars. I *love* Ethiopian food, and as far as I know, this is the only Ethiopian place in the St Louis area, so I had really high hopes. I went with some friends for my birthday, so I was hoping for great food and maybe a cool atmosphere. Well, the restaurant is shockingly run down. It's right smack in the middle of a really vibrant area, I would have expected more than white walls and plastic tablecloths. Oddly enough, the plant next to our table was wearing an Arby's name tag. That really didn't help with the ambiance. On to the food... It wasn't bad. I know people joke about how Ethiopian food is a grain of rice on a plate, but really, Ethiopian cuisine is really vibrant and tasty. (It reminds me a little of Indian food, what with the heavy reliance on stews and lentils, but the seasonings and flavors are completely different) The entrees came out in those oval-shaped dishes, just like in cheap Indian restaurants. The injera was pretty good. Not really noteworthy, but since it effectively a combination side dish and utensil, it doesn't really need to be. The real stand-out parts of the meal though were the couple of lentil-based side dishes. Holy crap, they were delicious. I don't remember much about our entrees, but I remember those. The red lentil one especially. Unrelated to the restaurant itself, I also want to mention that our waitress had a beautiful accent, and was drop-dead gorgeous. Models would kill for her cheekbones. I will probably go again, since I regularly get cravings for Ethiopian food, but I so wish that the restaurant itself were nicer. If it could really be a cultural experience as well as food, I would drive into the city for it all the time!

text: Before my second visit to The Resort at Little Harbor I was committed to trying The Fish House. Partly because I had passed it many times during my first visit and it didn't attract my group enough to pull in. It doesn't have a glamourous facade and it's not always open. So we just found ourselves passing by. Since my first time in Ruskin, I had found scattered reviews and brief comments on multiple sites- all good. This trip was with The Boys and we were more inclined to be attracted to the comfort food aspect of those reviews. This wasn't a high maintenance group. The Fish House was perfect for us. In fact, this was the only meal that we ate outside of our rented condo with full kitchen. The Fish House rated that highly with me before and it remains highly rated enough to earn 5 stars in the category of casual, home-style and affordable roadside seafood. Ok, I just created the category. It's owned and run by a Mom and she only opens on Thursday, Friday and Saturday so that she can be a Mom more than an entrepreneur and slave to her business. I love that. She works enough to provide at a comfortable level and focuses on her family. Great concept. The food is a predictable mix of Florida casual seafood and is incredible. You know, the grouper, shrimp, fries and slaw thing. But this is different. The welcoming greeting, conversation, care in coaching you to the right choice, preparation, presentation and ongoing chatter enhances the incredible meal that you always hope for at a roadside stand. I was hungry. I left full for about $8. I was guided to choose the fried "House" fish sandwich. I never heard of the fish, but we were given a little wikipedia with our meal. It's called Pangasius and is a "shark catfish". It's not a bottom feeder which probably contributes to it's completely non-fishy, clean flavor. And the rest is up to The Fish House. There is care in this meal. It's not a processed, thaw it and slap it deal. The fries were a perfect side balance with the slaw that was fresh, light and crisp. You also have multiple choices of main dishes such as grouper, mullet, catfish, clam strips and shrimp as well as preparation- fried, blackened, etc. You place your order, get a number and before you can arrange a place at one of the picnic tables out front (the only seating available) you're being called to come-n-get-it. Then, the best of the experience begins. Even though I love a meal that is built around fish, I believe that texture is the attraction, not flavor. I'm not alone in a dislike for "fishy tasting" entrees. At The Fish House, texture dominates. It's pure freshness. It's not likely that you would find yourself in Ruskin and especially near The Fish House when it is open. But if the opportunity presents itself, seize it.

text: Hmm, what can I say about West Ed that no one else has said yet? Not much, so I'll just take a bunch of quotes from everybody else's reviews. Just kidding! As a local, I too have a love/hate relationship with this mall, but lately it's been bordering more on the love side of the coin. You gotta go in an easy-going mood. Do not, I repeat DO NOT go when you're stressed, cause you'll probably end up hating this place forever. It's packed, there are lots of people, and most tend to walk slow because they're window-shopping at the same time. So try to clear a little time for yourself when you visit. I used to be one of those people who would bulldoze through the crowds to get where I needed to be, and it took me awhile to figure out it just doesn't work that way. Go with the crowd, don't fight it. You'll be less stressed, and make people less irritated that way. The shops at WEM have been getting better over the years, with the introduction of names like H&M, Hollister, Abercrombie & Fitch, and Coach. There is a good mix of affordable and expensive high-end shops, something for everybody. WEM has several food courts, and the one by Galaxyland is the best because it offers more variety, including Korean and South Asian cuisine. If you've got more time and want more than fast food, Bourbon Street is the place to be. This is one of my favorite places in the mall. Even though they've replaced some of the older restaurants that had more character with typical chain eateries, this corner of WEM has so much going on. Choose from the Old Spaghetti Factory, Moxie's, Tony Roma's, Hudson's, or even Hooters in this special part of West Ed. There's so much to do in this mall, even I haven't tried everything yet. There's the waterpark, Galaxyland fun & rides, mini-golf, sea lion shows, shooting range, movie theatres, bowling, and Fantasyland Hotel, to name a few. They used to have more animals in cages and behind glass throughout the mall, but they've stopped doing that since some of the animals became sick. I'm glad for that, because it was so depressing to see them cooped up in a shopping mall. I mean, a zoo is usually bad enough, but a shopping mall? I wonder how long the poor sea lion is going to last. If you're a first-time visitor to West Ed, I suggest approaching it with an open mind. Don't go expecting the time of your life, but still be open for a fun afternoon. As for me, this is still my favorite mall in the city, because it's got everything in one place.

text: Ah Preservation Hall...the one place where I will always tell people they must go to when they're in New Orleans. Many of us have this inner yearning to fully experience New Orleans at it's height. We want to see how good New Orleans can get. I completely underestimated what that height is. This music is as good as it gets. We waited a considerable amount of time in line outside to see this show and it was well worth it. It isn't dirt cheap, but $10 was also well worth hearing the greatest music I've ever heard in my life. Get there early. Be in the front of the line. Only the first few rows are seated rows and the rest have to stand. I was lucky enough to plunder my way to the front side where you can sit on pillows and against a wall. The music takes place in a venerable wooden room that actually provides the perfect acoustics. It's small and when the band plays, everyone shuts up so we can hear the full impact of the music. In walks a band called the Tornado Brass, who has the most soul and casual talent that I've ever seen. I say casual talent because it looks like they're barely struggling or thinking at all while playing the serenades of the Gods. When I remember my time in New Orleans, I will remember most the people, the food, building homes for victims, and the sounds that are bouncing off my memories that I collected at Preservation Hall.

text: Just when I had given up on Ethiopian in St. Louis... My wife and I had a friend in town and were looking for someplace interesting to go. I went online and came across a listing for Meskerem. I was surprised--I had no idea this place existed and I've been jonesing for some good Ethio for months. We decided to check it out, and we're very glad we did. The place is awesome. We had a big, mostly vegetarian, party so ordered a couple of salads and a bunch of the vegetarian combinations. Any review of ethiopian needs to start with the injera. The injera at Meskerem with thin and soft, just the way I like it. It wasn't served warm, which is my preference, but it wasn't cold either. Both the salads we ordered--the timatim and the avocado--came wrapped in injera. The avocado was my favorite--it was tasty and very fresh. The vegetarian combo at Meskerem is billed as a meal for one, but could easily feed two if you get an appetizer. Not only was it very good, but of the seven items that came on the platter, three were totally new to me. Having eaten many times at what I consider some of the country's best Ethiopian restaurants in Oakland, CA, Los Angeles, New York and Chicago, I was pretty damned impressed. The service was attentive, the injera was plentiful and the owner stopped by several times to check on us. I had a chance to chat with him after the meal and learned that the restaurant had just had its one year anniversary. He and his brother opened it together and work there in the evenings while working their day jobs too. I'm glad they did! Meskerem is the best Ethiopian place in St. Louis and I highly recommend it.

Momma also taught me (damned if I don't sound like Forrest Gump) that ladies love opening turquoise boxes like they love Cool J. While it's a tenth of the size of the New York location, this is a great place to look around and marvel. One day... one day...

text: What a surprise! My boyfriend and I stopped in while weary from walking during our vacation. Figuring it would be a decent enough meal from this restaurant chain we recognized from our hometown of Los Angeles, I was pleasantly surprised at the quality of our choice of dishes. We share everything and the waiter was friendly and accommodated us by serving us separate plates of the chopped salad and Tuscan chicken pasta. The quality of the chicken was great. I definitely recommend this place.
label: POS

text: This place is really good. Try the smoked salmon with that cheese that they pair it with (I don't remember right now). It's great.
label: POS

text: This place is my favorite mid-afternoon lunch spot. High ceilings, and warm, exposed brick walls make the decor rustic and charming. Their menu consists of mostly locally crafted foods: regionally cured salamis and meats for their sandwiches, small-farm raised pork for their pulled pork sammie, and a few vegetarian sandwich items comprised of locally grown veggies. They have daily and nightly specials. They host farm-to-table dinners, where you can come and meet the people who grew/raised what you're eating. Pretty forward thinking people-- it's great! I'm taking off one star because I'd really love to see them expand on what they've got. They've been open long enough now to start working it out a little, and change the menu up. This place could easily be five stars if they push themselves outside what's "comfortable". P.S. I tried borscht here for the first time. INCREDIBLE. When would you think to yourself, "damn, some cold beet soup sounds awesome right now"? I was suspicious too. Then I took my first bite, and was sent to the heavens in one swallow. Summer is coming to a close, so they might not have it on the menu again for a while, but if you EVER see the borscht, order it fast.
label: POS

text: This place is going for a very sleek, contemporary feel. Everything from the dining room decor to the food presentation is kind of post modern. I wish they would focus more on the quality of the food and cocktails and less on looking cool, though, because I just was not won over by the taste of anything and the prices left a bad taste in my mouth. They serve sushi and I suppose they are kind of known for that, but the sushi was not good, and certainly is not better than other, less expensive places in Tucson. I don't think we will be going back here.
label: NEG

text: We went to Mirna's last week on the advice of friends. The food was outstanding, especially for the price. I had a the Meditteranean appetizer plate, which was huge, fresh and flavorful. The best dolmades I've had in this region! My greek salad was generous and tasty. Hubby had the grouper, which was out of this world delicious, with a complex, rich sauce. The only drawback was their pita bread, which I find dry and flatter than the average. Also, don't expect a private tete-a-tete with your date, since the tables are close together. But even though small, the decor is simple yet elegant. Mirna's is a definite keeper!
label: POS

text: 3.5 stars really. Day by Day has been a reliable lunch spot and catering go-to place for me and many people at my firm. The fried chicke toss salad is delicious and they serve a "safe" selection of sandwiches. In the summer- the gazpacho is a refreshing and tasty choice. The specials of the sday - often fish and omelettes are also really, really great. They often sell out of the fish special - so come early for your lunch. They don't do dinners - although last summer they briefly toyed with a "dessert cafe" concept which I wish had fared better. Anyhow - it's a great place to grab a safe, reliable lunch.
label: POS

text: We have been patrons of Billy Bryant's since 2003, so I thought it was time to write a review This is not your ordinary barbeque restaurant where all the meat is drenched in sauce. This is excellent smoked meat, in true Kansas City fashion. When a restaurant can smoke meat this well, I am hard press to add sauce the the meat. Our typical order is the beef ribs and pulled pork. However, their pork ribs and smoked sausage are also crowd pleasers. My favorite is the smoked prime rib, which they added to their menu for a Friday night special. If you have never had smoked prime rib, this is the place to try it! The prices are very resonable. With a few exceptions such as ordering a full slab of ribs or the prime rib dinner (on Friday nights only), you're dinner is usually less than $10. Billy Bryant's also offer catering services. While it appears that another reviewer may have had issues with his "to go" order, ours has always been accurate. Colleagues that I have referred to this establishment have raved about their experience and the excellent quality of food. This is a family run business. Since we started going here years ago, we have had the pleasure of getting to know the family. It is always a treat to see them and catch up of the current happenings of their lives. While we live over 30 miles from Billy Bryant's, we are always happy to make the trek to eat some of their excellent food.
label: POS

text: You know how sometimes you find a little hole in the wall restaurant that is really great? Well, Leo's isn't one of those by a long shot. The menu is generic Mexican and the only two seasonings they seem to have in the kitchen are salt and grease. Food was way too salty and most of our group ate about one third of their lunch before deciding it wasn't worth it. There are too many other good Mexican restaurants in Tucson to spend any time here.
label: NEG

text: Dooky Chase Restaurant. What can you say about a staple of NOLA's history. Established in 1941, Dooky Chase's survived not only hurricanes Katrina and Rita, but they survived Camile as well. Whatever hardships have been thrown at Dooky's, they have always come back. The tour books and some of the reviews here say the neighborhood is "iffy" or 'has been slow to come back after Katrina". Well I was there 4 days ago (as of this posting) and I can tell you that there are a dozen new houses being constructed across the street and down the block, a rebuild on the street is currently on going and the restaurant itself looks great. Maybe the neighborhood is 'sketch' at night if you aren't a local but in the immediate area there is vibrancy, but you'll have to judge for yourself. Our part consisted of five, one of which was a professional chef. We order several main stays of the menu such as fried chicken, stewed chicken, baked mac and cheese, greens, etc. Everything was fabulous, except for the fact that the item ordered by the chef, stuffed crab cakes was sold out. The chef in our party sent word back to their chef to "send me whatever he'd like to make me that's off menu". The chef did not disappoint. He sent out a deep friend, herb encrusted crab dish that was fantastic.. The fried chicken was well received, the stewed chicken practically fell apart in your mouth it was so tender. The food was the classic 'home cooking' style you would expect from the south. The dessert menu is limited but according to our party, when the peach cobbler is that good, you don't need a larger menu. the cobbler was fresh, sweet and most certainly home made. We also had a rare occasion to meet Ms. Leah Chase, owner and operator of the restaurant. She is 87 years old and is the quintessential southern black lady with sass. She is pleasant, interesting and very engaging. Has stories to spare and has basically seen, heard and done it all. If she is there when you go, let her bend your ear for 20 minutes, you won't be sorry. Portion sizes are good, bordering on huge for both lunch and dessert. Currently they do not have enough staff for dinner but if you eat there for lunch, you won't need dinner. If you want a great food experience in NOLA, you can't go wrong with Dooky Chase's.
label: POS

text: I definitely thought this place was a hibachi joint, imagine my wife and I's surprise when we found out it wasn't. Oh well, we didn't have a back up plan, so we figured we'd give this place a try. AMBIENCE- I must say this place looks pretty nice. It's definitely got a trendy, hip feel to it. That being said, I figured this was more of a place to be seen, rather than a place to eat, but more on that later. A lot of young professionals and hipsters seem to come here, and in the middle of all that, my pregnant wife and I. SERVICE- there seemed to be a lot of servers working, though the place wasn't all that packed. Our server was friendly, though she would go missing for spots at a time. We didn't ask her too many questions about the menu, but she was able to answer the questions we did ask. Not bad, but certainly not great. MENU- the menu is not all that big. sushi rolls, appetizers, and a couple of entrees (and when i say a couple, I mean like 6-8 or something). There seemed to be a decent variety in the sushi rolls, but since my wife was pregnant, we just looked at the entrees. FOOD- I ended up ordering a scallop dish, and my wife got steak. What we ended up getting was not at all expected. The food came out in a very modern, aesthetically pleasing manner. I quite enjoyed my dish, but my wife had to send her steak back, as it was medium rare, and not medium well as she ordered. I understand it costs a lot to just give her a whole other steak, but by throwing the same steak back on the grill, it really lost it's juiciness, and wasn't all that great. OVERALL- this place was voted best new restaurant by Indy Magazine? I don't think so. I'll pass on coming back to this place. Celebrity Rating- Jeff Foster of the Indianapolis Pacers
label: NEG

text: We dined at Station Grille over the weekend before the Blues game. Needless to say, it was dead. Only us and another table. This is fine dining? Don't think so. Decent? Yes. Overpriced? Oh yeah. Since we had a friend from out of town with us, we had to introduce her to STL's famous "fried ravioli." Instead of the usual meat filling, it was a quite nice spinach/feta cheese mix. Only problem was they wanted us to eat it with ranch dressing..my arteries were already to be clogged with the feta. Nice thing they offer a marinara with the bread (which was interesting.) Entrees included: rib eye ($35) with mushrooms, and a chicken tortellini with a spicy, puttanesca-like tomato sauce ($25). Sides are additional (@$8). Again, why do I have a problem with "medium" in St. Louis? I queried the waitress about the definition of "medium" - "Oh, it's red in the center.." Boy have I heard that before! I didn't trust her and ordered medium rare. It came as she described medium. $50 says "medium" would have been the usual STL "lack of any color whatsoever." The rib eye (didn't feel the need to spend almost $40 for a NY strip) was fatty and stringy. Flavorful and juicy, but not a great cut of meat for the price. The chicken tortellini was good, but a bit overboard on the peppers. Tended to overpower the rest of the dish. Wait staff was pleasant and quick (had to be. Tumbleweeds were going down the aisles...) Nice ambiance. Biggest complaint? Way,way,way overpriced for the quality of the food.
label: NEG

text: We went here for a bachelorette party. we called a month ahead to pick out a family style meal and reserve a table for 20. my friends sister in law knew the owner so they were gonna hook us up with apps and dessert. It was such a busy night in new hope that the resturant had to ask friends/fam to help out. i tried to keep that in mind. but the person we spoke to the whole time we planned the event wasnt there that night and we didnt get the exact food we had planned. some was the same, not all. the service was pretty bad. they served us food before bringing us plates. then they brought us little plates for the main meal and we made them switch for bigger ones. then we waited for 30 min 4 the check. and we didnt get the dessert we were told we would. the food was good - nothing special. they did reserve us two parking spots which was nice. but i wont be going back.

text: A very small Chinese restaurant located in a shopping strip mall anchored by a supermarket. A real mom & pop operation complete with crying baby in the kitchen. That's OK. What's not OK. is the food. Inedible fat laden pork slices, and really, really deep fried dishes. Fried rice tasted like it came from a box. Food had no taste. Sauces were as thin as water. Too bad. The server was friendly though. This upper middle class neighborhood would gladly embrace a good Chinese sit down restaurant instead of this marginal attempt at Chinese cuisine. Unfortunately the message in the cookie at the end of the meal should say : "Next time best go to chain fast food Chinese restaurant down near the Walmart". This small shopping center will probably have better food choices once the new freeway overpass is completed.
label: NEG

text: As first timers to SB, we wanted explore and have dinner at a random place on the pier, the Dick was pretty depressing and empty, the other forgettable restaurants didn't seem convincing; low and behold at the end of the pier was an establishment with not only a vast amount of spectators, there was also a wait for a table; not to mention a to go window on the other side ( how awesome is that?). So I picked the Shellfish Company. Apparently winners chose other winners. This place was pretty damn awesome. Service was prompt and friendly, Lauren I think her name was, really sweet; she offered to turn on the heater above us so I could enjoy the meal without cowering under my companion's jacket... Clam Chowder: Yuuum...it didn't even need any pepper, it was seasoned to perfection, just the right consistency. Lobster Bisque: Delicious as well, not overly salted like most. Soju Bloody Mary: My new favorite drink, I scoured SB the rest of the evening for this, and the "soju" mary we had with breakfast the next day tasted like watered down horseradish sauce/cocktail sauce. This, however, was perfection in a pint. Salted/peppered rim with limes and a celery stalk. Main Lobster: I finally fulfilled my fantasy of Daryl Hannah in "Splash" when she went to town on an entire lobster. It was however, split in half when it arrived, but I just wanted to say that I've had an entire lobster, not just the tails like most restaurants serve it. I've never used claw crackers before, but there's a first time for everything, and it was worth the non-work. I not only drenched all the edible meat in the melted butter tin they gave me, I also took the remaining precious liquid as an after dinner shot. Alaskan King Crab Legs: Fabulous, the meat by itself was buttery, but wouldn't you know that it came with it's own companion of melted butter heaven. Not to mention, kinda loved the coleslaw and onion rings....so wrong but so good. All in all, we were seated on the outside deck, facing the sunset, stuffing out faces with alcohol and butter sea goodness. It was an awesome ending to what might possibly be an incredible beginning.
label: POS

text: This restaurant used to be the top of the food chain. It's now hit the bottom. They had great fried chicken and stakes but now it is very bland and burnt. It's prices are out of control and the food is awful. Save yourself the time and money and go to McDonalds for better eats.

If you have horses you can bring them too, as there is lots of areas to ride and when the wash is dry its great on their hoofs. $6 per car

I finished my meal both nights and still had room for more food. I got lobster ravioli the first night and the calamari and linguini the second night. There just wasn't enough flavor in the sauces. As for the ravioli, I have had much better filling in a ravioli. I thought there was too much cheese and not enough lobster in there. Also, the place is extremely cramped. It is a very small restaurant and you feel like you are walking over other people to get to your table and exit the restaurant. I guess it could be considered cozy if you were on your date. But then again, if you were on a date, be prepared to have the people at the next table hear all of your mushy gushy sweet nothings

text: I went to Maureens today because I had read about it in the Delaware Today Magazein's Best of Delaware list. However, I would not consider it a Best of Delaware, more likely a worst of Delaware. I went to get a massage, a spa pedicure, and a spa manicure to celebrate my birthday. The massage I received was mediocre, but the pedicure and manicure were the worst I've ever had. I have had many manicures and pedicures at many different salons, and I have never had this bad of an experience, especially considering the cost! For a $50 pedicure, I left with toenails that were unevenly filed. (It looked like a 3rd grader did them.) And, the red nail polish was smudged on several of my toes! During my manicure, again my nails were filed unevenly and I bled as a result of my cuticles being trimmed too much! I recommend you try somewhere cheaper because at least then you won't feel so bad if you have a bad experience like this one!

text: Every time I go to Seafood Unlimited, I'm reminded what a terrific little restaurant it is. Everything I've ever eaten there has been well prepared, tasty and reasonably priced. My cousin, who is notoriously difficult to please, never has trouble finding something on the menu to make her happy. They are flexible and are typically really happy to accept substitutions and special orders.
label: POS

text: I finally dined at the Tampa landmark, Bern's, just before moving out to San Francisco. I must say, it made me feel carnivorous again. And I liked it. The steaks are delicately aged, they have this down to a science. It was suggested that my companion and I split a large steak vs. having it cooked in two smaller pieces for added flavor & perfection in preparation. Suggestion noted & it was worth it. Imbibed a delicious amarone with dinner, can't remember the specific name but look for it on the menu. After dinner we did the tour of the wine cellar and kitchen, I like seeing where the food is prepared & marveled at the large saltwater fish tank where our delicious friends from under the sea lived until their demise on someone's plate. We also found out they have their own organic farm where they harvested the veggies we ate, they are self-sustaining, in a manner of speak. Neat, IMO. We finally came to rest in the dessert room. I'm not big on sweets but had banana creme pie and it didn't disappoint. A glass of port and I was finito! The dessert room is an ideal place to play hide n' seek. I'd like to rent it out for an evening to indulge this fantasy.
label: POS

text: Great neighborhood bar! Good things on tap, and the menu offers up delicious items not seen everyday - Ostrich, Bison, Rabbit, Boar, Duck. Staff was friendly, jukebox eccletic, and the crowd nice & mellow - actually allowed me to enjoy my date and our discussion. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!! Good to know - they have a 2nd floor that offers additional seating, pool table and more TV's for your viewing pleasure.

text: Ate there and enjoyed the food, but the service was very poor. Our waiter pretty much hung out at another table that he seemed to know. We waited for water we asked for for near 10 minutes until he was finished with his conversation. One complaint we had about the food at the time was that it was very greasy, especially for a chicken dish. Well, what seemed fishy at the time became a huge problem a few hours after dinner. The evening was ruined so horrifically (that and the abysmal service) that we have vowed never to eat there again. We have since been going to Chinnar (across US-202 from Barwarchi) and it has treated us well.

text: went there on valantines day and was not impressed. the salsa taste just like it came out of a jar and not homemade. the tacos are good and priced right. however, the drinks were horrible. they boasted of premium tequilas and liquors, but the margaritas are so syrupy sweet it will give you an instant headache and ruin the fine tequila. i am so tired of $6-12 corn syrup margaritas. if i lived in the downtown area and just wanted tacos only, i would return.
label: NEG

text: At least they don't waste good whiskey... We didn't have dinner, but whiskey and appetizers. We found this place on Yelp because we were looking for a place to sit down and sip some scotches. We walked in, I took one look at the menu and my wallet started to bleed. And I don't mean the food prices. Yeah, they have a lot of whiskeys. A LOT. But every single whiskey that I've had elsewhere, they were charging about double what I would expect to pay. I can get excited about trying new scotch, but not when I'm paying double what every other bar I know charges. OK, so they have a 2oz pour, slight larger than average. Still, I'm not quite sold. Anyway, the girl liked the place, so I agreed to give it a try. We decided to do a flight of tastes, which we built to our own interests. Oban, The Macallan, and Lagavulin. Of course the scotches were good. BUT, the bartender mis-poured and accidentally poured out a measure of Laphroaig, which was another we had considered. Now that one was $30 for a taste, so I was thinking that's an expensive mistake. But, no, I couldn't believe my eyes, he poured it back into the bottle. Wow. That's class right there. In addition, they use a common measuring cup to measure all of your drinks, so each one is actually contaminated with a little of the scotch before it. Wait... I ordered a single-malt, not a blend. The only food we got were the cheese balls. They were tasty ...and tiny. I'm sure the food is good and all, but I'll pass, thanks.
label: NEG

text: Super cute place! It's like staying in a little villa with sweet-fragranced hanging vines everywhere, and it's really close to the beach. Modern decor inside, with mostly linoleum floors (I guess because of the sand) and some carpet tiles in strategic areas. We had a king courtyard room right next to the spa, which was convenient for getting in the spa, and less convenient when some kids decided to play Marco Polo in the spa the next morning at 9:15 AM (yes, in the spa; no, I don't get it either). The room was long with a nice seating area in front of the bed and the closet, fridge, microwave, and bathroom in a sort of parallel hallway off to the side. We paid $225 a night on the weekend but that seems like the going rate in town, maybe a little cheaper, even. No online reservations that we could find, which was maybe why we were able to get a room so close!

text: We stopped in here for lunch with the kids while visiting St. Charles. Delicious ribs with perfect smokiness that was not overwhelmed by too much BBQ sauce. I had the fish & chips with a salad instead of the chips. They were very accommodating, and the fish was great--crunchy but not greasy batter, and solid fish! I'm not much of a drinker, so I appreciated the 5 oz glasses. They have a kid's menue too.
label: POS

text: Sugar Mom's is only a so-so establishment, especially compared to the other bars in the Olde City area. The first time I went, I searched desperately for this place, which is quite difficult to find. It's tucked away at the back of a parking lot off of the North side of Market Street. You basically have to go with someone who's already been there if you hope to find it quickly. Upon arriving, my friends and I descended into a sweaty, smelly basement of a bar, which, at the time, was full of cigarette smoke (thank goodness the smoking ban went into effect pretty soon thereafter). Despite the fact that the bar is basically in a factory cellar, it is charming, with places to sit, low-hanging brick ceilings and brick columns, juke boxes, and games like pinball and pool. After fighting our way to the bar, my friends and I did manage to get some pretty cheap (although not the best quality) beer and mixed drinks, and we had a good time enjoying the juke box music and meeting new people. I do admit, this place is packed with 20-somethings on weekend nights, so it's a good place to go with your friends. However, it was a bit of a meat market, so be forewarned if you don't like skeezy guys trying to cop a feel as you work your way through the crowd on your way to the bathroom. Also, at 25, I felt like I was a bit too old for the rest of the crowd. In all, however, I had fun and returned with my friends on a Thursday night, and my experience was much less positive. It took us less time to find the place this time around, but we still had to search a bit. Then, the smoking ban had been in place in Philly for some time, but some scary looking older lady (who looked like the sun-baked old lady from "Something About Mary" - only worse!) was parked at the bar and puffing away at her Marlboro Reds. Despite complaints from the other patrons, the lady continued to smoke inside, and the bartenders did nothing to get her to stop. As someone with asthma, I didn't appreciate the flagrant disregard for the smoking ban or the fact that I left smelling like an ash tray. Despite ye olde chimney up at the bar, my friends and I got some seats in the back, as far away as possible from the smoke, and ordered $1 cans of Pabst Blue Ribbon (a good deal if you like cheap beer) and some way overcooked cheeseburgers and fries. It wasn't all that fun, and we left as soon as we finished eating to go somewhere better in Olde City. Overall, I'd recommend this place for people who want to go on the weekend and who don't mind a meatmarket and/or illegal smoking. This place, however, is really not for me.
label: NEG

text: I have been eaten here only once (and once I ran off after learning the wait is at least one hour.) So this review is based on my one dinner there. The restaurant/bar is all too crowded and loud for my taste at dinner time, I hear they're better at lunch but haven't tried them at that time. Going at a more quite time may also improve the service, the wait staff had too much on their hands and not too attentive. The food: we ordered 4 of their items, 1. Baked goat cheese: by far the nicest dish we had. But nothing special. Solid tomato sauce, goat cheese baked until the cheese melted (and a bit browned) in the oven. As a side note: the garlic bread didn't even have a hint of garlic. 2. Cured Spanish ham and cheese plate: Cheese was meh, ham was alright and the decoration terrible. 3. Chicken and chorizo skewer: chorizo was nice, chicken was tender and not dry but bland. There it was served next to some onion and grilled bell peppers that had not turned out so good (soggy and unappetizing) 4. Grilled beef tenderloin with a Rioja reduction sauce: such a great opportunity that was missed entirely. Beef was nice and grilled to perfection, BUT the Rioja reduction was more of a sweet syrup avoid the sauce if you get this dish (not recommended) All in all, I come away unsatisfied by the quality of the food and it's presentation. and I do no recommend BARcelona.
label: NEG

text: Went here for dinner last night - we were looking for Spartaco - as it turns out it's now the Osteria but it's still owned by the same guy. First off, his Italian mom was sitting in the corner of the restaurant when we got there - the owner greeted us and brought us to our table right away. Our server came over with the wine list, bread with a fabulous olive and olive oil dipping sauce was brought over. The menu is small, with nice homemade pasta and seafood choices. Kind of what you might expect in a town next to the ocean. We started with two appetizers - bay scallops in a light tomato-basil sauce and a mixed seafood in red sauce over parmesan polenta. Both were terrific - the sauce with the bay scallops was fresh tasting and had a little bite to it. The risotto was topped with calamari, littlenecks, scallops and shrimp - delicious. Caesar salads next - excellent dressing and very fresh and crispy romaine. Then for the main attraction I had homemade canneloni with meat sauce - amazing. My friend had a delicious white fish with a caper, tomato and olive sauce and I had a taste and it just melted in my mouth. We finished that off with espresso and cannolli - what a great dinner. The service was fabulous and the owner came over at the end of the meal to see how everything was. It was great!
label: POS

text: We've been to Asiagos many times including the old Cole location. Back then I always left feeling like their was something missing in the food. Flavor, pizazz, what have you. Well since they opened the dowtown location it has filled in what was missing flavorwise. It seems every time I come back it gets better and better. The service from Erin was top notch and attentive. The atmosphere is lovely. We started with minestronie for the hubby. And I had the Tuscan hummus. Hubby says soup is some of the best he's had. I would agree as I've had a small taste but it's beef broth and I don't do beef. My hummus was homemade with grilled pita bread served with two sides. One a tomato relish and the other a caper tomato relish. It was yummy. Both of us ordered the Meditarranio. I had mine with chicken and hubby had his with spicy sausage. Boy was that delicious. Just the right amount of heat with red chiles and artichoke hearts. The tomatoes, basil and the homemade fettucine was so good and fresh. Truely delicious. We topped it off with the tirimisou. Good but not the best I've had. That honor goes to Tonys Teattro .I must say their chocolate desserts looked delicious, so will try those on a return visit. All in all a very pleasant experience.
label: POS

text: For $5 an entrance fee you are getting a lot of bang for your buck! This place is seriously cool and if you take your time you will have an awesome self guided tour. Gaze into the eyes of previous voodoo queens and doctors on the walls; photographs and paintings are plentiful. Marie Laveau (I & II)'s lives seems incredible.. I had not heard of them before visiting this place! Lots of altars and cool history to read about. We loved the voodoo dolls and various items throughout the two incredible rooms. Left an old Dodger's ticket on the altar for good luck- the table was filled with all sorts of crazy things people dropped there- old licenses, pictures of children, wishes on paper, a bottle of nail polish, condoms, etc. They encourage you to take as many pictures as you like and that's exactly what I did. In the front of the shop (before you get into the tiny museum) there are voodoo dolls, gris gris bags (for love, luck, fertility, etc.), potions, and all sorts of charms for sale. Really fun and an enjoyable way to spend some time while in the French Quarter.
label: POS

text: Melted Mexican queso with bacon chunks and fresh tortillas. Do I really need to say more? I've been going to Super-Rica for as long as I can remember, and it is ranked as a top Taqueria by Julia Child, the LA Times, and The NY Times for a reason. text: I am sorry to write such a negative review, but this place is abysmal. I went for a massage. The therapist I was supposed to have was unable to make it (that's fine, these things happen) and the receptionist said she left a message on my phone, which she didn't. There was no changing area or place to secure your items, you just took your clothes off in the room. I don't care about "bells and whistles" such as a separate changing room, or even being given courtesy calls if your therapist changes, as long as the treatment is good. It was atrocious. The therapist applied hardly any pressure, it was as if she was fondling me. I'm not even sure she is a qualified therapist (she may just be a skincare specialist), she had no idea what she was doing. I asked for firmer pressure, but still felt close to nothing. After the treatment, they said they were charging me extra since I asked for firmer pressure and it now counted as a "deep tissue massage". I'm sorry, but light touching does not count as a "deep tissue massage"; moreover, most respectable places let you choose what pressure you want without charging. After charging me $100 for basically being fondled, the owner had the audacity to demand a tip. Unfortunately I had bought a package of 2. I went back the second time with an open mind, thinking that perhaps I just unluckily drew a below-par therapist, but the second time was just as bad as the first. The place is cramped and dingy, the staff are rude and unprofessional, and most of all the services are abysmal. Avoid at all costs.
