text: First of all, this place is pretty awesome. The owner is so friendly and helpful, and it's great to hear that they're opening up two new locations in March. (Apparently, one is going to be at 37th and Lancaster. Chaat, in MY neighborhood? I'm going to get fat. So fat.) Anyway, the wonders that Desi Chaat House has worked with this former headshop space are also impressive. The store is impeccably clean, and although they don't have any kitchen or oven space, they've still managed to stock a decently sized menu menu, from a slightly overwhelming variety of chaat to chicken and vegetable biryani, which I'm itching to try one of these days. The menu featured some recognizable names, including pani puri, bhel puri, etc., and also some more vague items like Kashmiri chaat. Also in the fridges were mango lassi and a few other drinks, one of which a friend informed me is some kind of salted pomegranate juice with herbs (intriguing!) The owner is very friendly, and I'm sure if you had questions, you'd have them answered easily. My boyfriend and I decided to split two orders, one of bhel puri and one of samosa chaat, and also bought two samosas... thinking we would split them. This ended up being WAY too much food, so he's got another lunch out of it. The portions are very generous, to be sure. Also, another thing that I really liked was that we ordered the food spicy, and it was ACTUALLY spicy, without being overwhelming. There was a nice layer of spice with a variety of complex flavors. The samosa chaat was good, but the other dish was my favorite. I was impressed at how crispy everything managed to stay, even though we waited a little bit to eat it. The sauces were piquant, the crispy bits were a welcome contrast of textures, and the chickpeas were delicious. The cilantro, other herbs, and onions were all fresh, and mixed in throughout the dish were pomegranate seeds, which added a nice citrus brightness and more texture variety. The samosas were also tasty. In short, the food was quite good! While my friends and I were ordering, a crowd of Indian college students were also there waiting for us to finish (good sign #1), and when I asked my boyfriend (who is generally very picky about Indian food that his mother hasn't cooked) whether he liked it, he also gave it an enthusiastic endorsement (good sign #2). So while 42nd and Baltimore is a bit of a hike for me right now, I would not hesitate to get food from here again when visiting friends, and I will definitely be headed to the new location as soon as they open.

text: I hate to sound like a vengeful bitch, but I just realized that this restaurant has way more stars than it deserves. Due to our vantage point, I was able to see our plates come up under the heat lamps and sit there for the next 20 minutes. (We timed it.) I was about to get up myself and grab them when Husband flagged down a busboy to bring us our order. Of course, the dinners were, by that point, inedible, and that is when I went to find the manager. Normally in a situation like this, the manager is apologetic and ready to do whatever it takes to make things right. Not here, though. The manager was rude and treated me as though I make a habit out of trying to get free meals, despite the fact that neither myself or Husband had touched our food. He grudgingly comped our bill and sent us on our way without so much as an apology. I know a lot of people really like this restaurant, but I am unwilling to gamble my time and money on a place that was willing to treat even one customer so incredibly poorly.

text: Whatever you do, be careful to hang onto your paperwork if you take anything into this Best Buy store for repair. I dropped off an Ipod (the 80 GB) and they said they'd get it back to me in the mail within three weeks. It never came. I called, they said they'd look into it. Finally, two months later, I received a phone call from a woman who said I should come and pick it up. When I asked why it wasn't being mailed, as promised, she said it was because they couldn't fix it. I told her it would be a few weeks before I could make it out there. She said no problem. I asked whether I needed any paperwork (this was probably a big mistake). She said, "No." She then called me a month later and reminded me to pick it up. I said I'd try to get out there, but that I was having some difficulties arranging for that. To make a long story short when I went, a few weeks later, to pick up the Ipod they told me they had no record of my ever having dropped it off. They refused to believe me, even though I have bought thousands of dollars from that place, which they could see when they pulled up my record. I then showed them my cell phone log, which showed that I'd received several calls from the service department of that very store, and I described the voice of the woman who called me not once but three times, and what she said. They said, "Well, that doesn't prove anything." I couldn't believe my ears. I asked to speak to the manager, who told me that Best Buy was a big store and my view of them didn't matter. I said, fine, perhaps I'll start writing some reviews about what seemed to me criminal behavior. The next day I received a call that they had "found my paperwork" and that I could come up and get a new Ipod. I never received an apology for the way they embarrassed me and tried to con me out of an Ipod, not to mention squandered three hours of my time as they pored over records and paperwork that "proved" I'd never been there. It was not just the fact that everything about the service was subpar, that they didn't keep good records, or that people are stealing stuff, but also the amazingly ugly attitude that I encountered from everyone related to the service department and the store manager. That said, the salespeople and checkout clerks have always been nice. Apparently the manager didn't train them. I'll never buy another thing from them, however. This was the first time I ever needed something repaired, rather than just replaced, and it was a total nightmare. I wouldn't want to be in that position with, say, a computer or plasma screen.

text: I didn't climb on top of the food chain to be a vegetarian and to celebrate, we stopped by the rib festival in Sparks, NV. It starts from 11 am to 5 pm daily during Labor Day weekend. A few fellow YELPers and friends make an annual pilgrimage to Rib Fest. But this year, there was only two of us that was left in the race by Monday, so we paced ourselves with a sampler from each booth, averaging about 3-4 ribs at each stop. Willingham's: Their ribs weren't falling off the bone, but each one was as consistent as the first. Their cajun sauce wasn't spicy at all, but we preferred it over their Sweet & Sissy sauce. Kinder's: They had 4 sauces in which I tasted, but the ribs were dry. I felt a bit cheated since the ribs I had from their sampler were very dry while my friend's was falling off the bones. It definitely wasn't as consistent or I just had a bad batch. (Update: I guess the took first place. I really can't see how they did. I guess Ireally did get a bad batch then.) Pork n Beans: Their taster's sampler was smothered in BBQ sauce before we could even put more sauce on it. Their ribs were definitely tastier than their pulled pork. Their sauce was lacking a kick, but my friend wanted to try this place again since it was pretty good last year. Checkered Pork: Last but not least, this place had sauce on it already, but they didn't smother the meat in it. They had enough so that you could eat it as is or dip it in more sauce. The meat was tender and falling off the bone. When we asked about hush puppies (thinking they were jalapeño poppers of some sort), they let us try one each and it was basically corn meal/bread that was fried. We were glad they let us try some before committing to a half dozen. This place gets my vote. *thumbs up* Notes for next year: Bring a small cooler, a pack of baby wipes, hats

text: There never seems to be a shortage of restaurants that rely on quantity over quality. Acme is no exception. Just three weeks ago, my wife and I drove to Boston to eat at the Neptune Oyster Bar. We savored the delicate flavors of the kumamotoes, the kushi's, maine and cap cod oysters. Some reminded us of the sea, the kushi of cucumbers. Heading to NOLA, we were excited to sample LA oysters for the first time. Oh, what a disappointment. We asked to be seated at the bar so we could see the oysters shucked. We immediately noticed that the oysters, and the bin the oysters are held, are covered with Lousiana mud. The shucker's hand, and shucking tool, also were completely covered in mud. After opening each oyster, he'd use the muddy tool to separate the oyster from its shell. Lousiana oysters are big compared to oysters from the pacific northwest and the northeast, as other yelpers have pointed out, and not terribly expensive. But as we were disappointed to discover, LA oysters are also rather tasteless. Quite frankly, the only 'flavor' I could taste was the gravelly mud that was smeared on the oyster, from forementioned muddy tool. They just weren't good. Expecially in contrast with our experience in Boston where the oysters actually had subtle flavors of sweetness, saltiness, and so on. Sadly, another case of quantity over quality. Not surprising for an establishment that hangs a sign with names of patrons that can dozens of oysters over a short period of time. I suppose I'm not the right target customer. The Acme customer is the guy who recently yelped that he could "throw down oysters" and had "36 oysters in like 5 minutes". We also tried the fried oysters and the char-grilled oysters. Fried oysters weren't bad, but it wasn't because of the oysters. It was the fried dough that was good. The char-grilled oysters were alright, but again, nothing special. Acme was strike #2 for our NOLA dining experience. See my comments on Commander's Palace for strike #1.
label: NEG

Ironically, the rock originated from Oklahoma, but, being that it was, in fact, in Indiana at the time and was older than any other rock there, it was technically correct, though deceiving. Next was a room with a life-sized wooly mammoth falling into a lake of ice. Not sure if Indiana was known for its mammoths, but it was pretty cool. This wing also had a bunch of Native American-themed stuff, including some crafts you could do. Into the modern era we go. There was a giant glass case containing, presumably, treasures from Indiana. Key riches included a little girl's pink dress, a picture of the USS Indiana, a Japanese-made machine gun known for jamming and killing its operator, a not-all-that-old green rock, and some wheat made out of wax. Maybe it's because I'm not a native to Indiana, but I just didn't get it. Contrastingly, the exhibit of all of the famous people who came out of Indiana was quiet interesting. James Dean actually got his own hallway. Finally, there is an Indiana of the Future exhibit. According to their predictions, in the future, Indiana will abandon science and technology and return to its home-owned, organic, agricultural roots. They have close-ups of futuristic dirt here. At the very least, I was amused the entire trip.

If you're ready to drop about 15 buckaroos for a ho-hum lunch (that includes a beverage), I guess you can. Jake and Max and The Mexican Post are the most affordable of the bunch - but their offerings aren't very appetizing. The DiBruno's, is just a replica of the one on 18th with a smaller selection. Tokyo and Under the C are pretty pricey and they too, offer pretty average stuff. La Scala seems to be the better of the bunch, but only if you're prepared to spend a little more for their gourmet pizza entrées and salads. Sook Hee's produce is fresh and the juice bar is pretty good. They've got a nice orange juicer and I like to treat myself every once in a while to a small one at $2.99. I'd still prefer to get my produce at Sue's (definitely cheaper) on 18th, though - even with the walk. If the weather is shite and you're stranded in Suburban with nowhere to go, the Market is a good option - it gets pretty crowded during mid-day lunch rush (go before noon or after 1:30), but there are always tables available. text: "A peculiar flavor" is how my wife described the taste of her bacon and eggs. 10pm on a Saturday night and in need of a snack after a movie at Clearview before heading home to the kids, we decided to make a pit stop at the City Diner after reading the reviews on Yelp. Big mistake. First of all, it's in a sketchy location - the parking lot of a Metairie La Quinta Motel. Unless you have a concealed weapon, this isn't a place to take your wife (and I would never bring my kids here). Once seated in a comfy booth, I ordered a philly cheesesteak po-boy because it sounded interesting and I love po-boys AND cheesesteaks. How could they go wrong? I asked for "no bell peppers" but it turns out it's a pre-mixed formula and they can't do it without bell peppers. So, I ordered a buffalo chicken sandwich instead. All breading and sauce way too spicy for even my seasoned New Orleans palate. French fries were awesome and that's all I ended up eating. My wife's greasy bacon and dry eggs were another story. She couldn't even get through two bites. I give this place two stars instead of one because at least it's open late and the service was good and food was served quickly. The restaurant seemed clean and bright. The menu had some cool options on it including Crawfish Monica, but this is not the place that I would order that kind of thing. The waitress asked if we liked our food and I told her "yes" just because I felt bad for her. I don't think we'll be going back any time soon, but since it got so many good reviews, perhaps we just caught them on an off-night.

text: I like the gimmick, I do really. Their drinks weren't horrible, but they were astounding either. With that said, service was quite horrible. We were a table of 5. text: The dining experience here is absolutely fantastic! We started w/ their turtle soup. We had to, it was so highly recommended! They kept serving us fresh, hot bread and they even gave us fresh garlic bread, too...mmmm. We had to ask for seconds for the garlic bread, though. We also had the crawfish linguine with bacon & edamame. Super delicious! The artichoke salad was really great, too. We really liked the dressing they used. For our entrees, my husband ordered the filet mignon, which was cooked to perfection and I had the special Gulf fish, which was a Black Rim? Whatever it was, it was light, flaky, and yummy! We really gave it a valiantly effort to save room for dessert, but we just couldn't do it. text: NOLA 4-EVER!!! So we decided to go to an Emeril restaurant during our N.O. stay and we were not disappointed. Here is our menu from start to finish Japaleno corn bread - this was quite good Sweet potato bacon biscuit - this, my friends, is heaven Oysters brochette Caesar salad Shrimp & grits Garlic crusted drum We liked the oysters; I usually prefer a thicker sauce but this was light and tasty. Marcel really enjoyed the Caesar salad very much. I too, liked this nicely tasting plate of romaine in a lighter dressing The Garlic Crusted Drum was like heaven on a plate. Every bite I took, I made a yum noise. How embarrasing! Do yourself a favor and order this when you go. The Shrimp & Grits were delicious. It is an order of 6 grilled shrimp served on a bed of grits. It may seem like a small order but those grits are so damn rich, any more would pit you into immediate food coma!! Wow! We had no need for dessert since our food was primo!! Our bill came to $120 with minimal drinks. I will definitely go here again!!!

text: I'm new to Tucson and was looking for a Chinese cuisine "not Panda Express'. This place was recommended by a couple of locals. We ordered, hot and spicy chicken wigs. The wigs were salty and dry, there were plenty of green peppers and garlic. if you like salty wigs, This is a perfect disk. KungPao Chicken has too much of water chestnut, and not enough chicken, I think they might have replace water chestnut for chicken. This dish has more sweet flavor. Their "Crispy Chow Mei" is unusual. Instead of using egg noodles (yellow), they use fried flour chips. It's weird. But it was tasty. Mongolian beef was pretty tasty. We all enjoyed it. If you are in the mood for soup, their Sizzling Rice soup was delicious. Overall, I wouldn't recommend for out of town friends.

text: My friends, this is the cool place to be! Euclid Records has been rocking Webster Groves since 1981, and there's no end in sight! More than just a record store, Euclid Records has an active blog and also has fun events every now and then. In fact, it was at one of these such events that my fiance and I really clicked. A few years ago Euclid featured Punk Rock Night, playing punk music and punk films. We watched Rock'N"Roll High School together, and the rest is history! We've been patrons of the place ever since. Check out an image of the projector screen they use to show movies in the photos! Euclid Records is broken in two. In the front half you'll find the register, new cds, used cds, and dvds. Most of their cds are rock, but you'll find every genre available. Remember, they can order anything your little heart desires! The walls are covered in awesome music art posters and the musty smell of old records makes you feel so darn cool just for being there that you'll want to keep on coming back. In the back you'll find records, records, and more records! I cannot tell you how cool this place is! JUST GO!!!! You will find every type of music here, and don't forget to check out the dollar bins! Be sure to look along the walls and in the corners in the back half for framed artwork that will rock your world! The environment of this store is really sweet. Want to browse anonymously? That's fine, they'll leave you be. Want to chat away the hours? Boy, did you pick the right place to wander into! The staff is cool yet nice, and there is no air of superiority among them. I've seen every type of person in Euclid Records, and I can guarantee you that you'll feel right at home. So go ahead, support a local St. Louis shop and stop on by!

text: Staying at the Monteleone had been a dream of mine even since I became interested in the city of New Orleans. On my 2nd annual trip with my best girlfriend, we chose to stay here. Let me sum it up for you- This hotel is like a bleach-blond bimbo, pretty to look at and that's about it! First, the rooms are tiny. I mean, itty-bitty. There was hardly enough room for all 4 of our suitcases. Forget the idea of room service, it had to be wedged in between our 2 beds leaving us a huge obstacle to work around while trying to get ready. The hotel is so noisy! All of the street noise seemed to flood in and disturb our sleep every night! Not to mention loud singing idiots returning to their rooms at 3 o'clock. The first night we were there our water went out for about 45 minutes. It turned out to be a city problem, but the operator on our telephone was rude, short, and refused to give us any answers. We had to change our plans that night becuase it got so late while we were waiting to shower. The next day, we returned to our room after a full day at 4pm to find our room was never cleaned. After questioning the maid staff we were told someone could come back at 5:30. What? While we are in the middle of dressing and showering for dinner? We already missed one nights plans. Another negative of the hotel was that they only serve room service till 10pm. So when I come in at midnight, craving pizza and junk food I cant order squat. I hope they come to realize how much drunk money they are missing out on. The whole weekends stay was disappointing, did not meet up to southern hospitality standards, and lacked that special spark I felt last year at the Ritz. text: [this review is for the restaurant side of the S. Grand location, as I have not tried any items from the bakery... YET] This place, frankly, makes me want to get my Tina Turner on and yowl "You're simply the best!" every time I get started on my food. This is the best Chinese food in St. Louis and rivals any I've had elsewhere. The most fantastic thing on their menu is the scallion and ginger lo mein -- surprisingly light and flavorful, and fantastic as a cold leftover too (I always deliberately order extra so I can either eat it cold the next day or heat it up in some broth and hot sauce to make delicious soup). Apart from that, the entrees are all very flavorful and good (although you may want to ask them to go light on the sauce) and everything is quite reasonably priced. I also think they put cinnamon or something similarly magical in their crab rangoon, which, while hardly a hallmark of authentic Chinese cuisine, are a damn good movie night nosh. Bump this place to the top of your list... you'll never want to go anywhere else for Chinese food. Seriously.

text: Wow, I feel honored with this "First to Review." Jazz Daiquiri... how I loved you! This is not really a "lounge;" more like a hole in the wall that sells daiquiris, which we always took to go. text: I am always pretty weary about the restaurants inside of casinos (but that usually doesn't stop me from trying them.) Dolce was a complete surprise - it was one of the most delicious dinners I have ever had. We ordered a couple of appetizers - the calamari, the tuna tartar, and the oven roasted eggplant. Even the vegetables in the fried calamari were delicious. I have never had tuna tartar before but it might be my new favorite food. And I HATE eggplant, there is something about the texture that makes me gag. However, I decided I would try some of the oven roasted eggplant, and boy am I glad that I did - it was extremely good! I order the truffle fettuccini for my main dish (duck, peas, prosciutto, and mushrooms). I have never had duck before, but this dinner was very good. The only problem that I had with it was that it was very fatty, but I'm guessing that has to do with the duck (not sure though). The service was very good - we were one of the last people to leave the restaurant and our waiter had no problem with it. We were able to pay our compliments to the chef after dinner, who was very appreciative of our comments. This is a rather expensive dinner, but well worth it.

text: This is another fabulous small mom and pop type restaurant located on the Loop. It's cheap, fast, delicious. Nowadays, it's gotten so much attention that it's not as particular, but still great. It is a great, hidden diner that gets really busy on the weekends for brunch and breakfast. I am not much for sweets in the morning, but the pumpkin pancakes are SO good and unique to the place. I usually get the scrambled eggs w/ onions, green peppers + pepper jack cheese on ciabatta bread. AND unlimited coffee :)

text: I was pretty jazzed when I signed up on the Peppermill website and received a 2 night stay for free. I have been to Reno plenty of times but have never stayed here and was looking forward to it. Unfortunately once I arrived it was underwhelming to say the least. The Italian theme of the outside decor was pretty spectacular, although I quickly got over that once I was inside. The inside of the property looks like something Willy Wonka threw up all over. Neon and mirrors everywhere, 70's looking carpet, and even though the property was huge (which can sometimes be a plus) in this instance it really just made my visit confusing and a big pain in the ass trying to find things. On the positive side - the room was very nice. Big flat screen with HD programming and extra ports to hook up other media devices. Bed was comfortable, although as with most other hotels I hated the pillows..way to soft. Front desk personnel and check in/out process was quick and easy. They also had a few computers set up at the front desk where you can print up a boarding pass...nice touch. The sports book was spectacular. Tv screens everywhere, and plenty of individual seats with your own monitor which you can change to whatever sporting event you want to watch. That's where the positives ended though. On the down side - No security guards checking guests for room keys when entering elevators so anyone or their mom can wander up to the rooms. Food in general was ridiculously expensive (I think in part this was because the Peppermill is all the way at the end of the strip so you are kind of trapped and stuck in the property and they know they have you by the short hairs). Food at the buffet was sub par and expensive - $20 for dinner. Coffee shop had a good deal going from midnight to 6am everything on the menu was $6.99, I had the steak and eggs which was pretty good. Mini bar and room service were incredibly overpriced so I never tried them ($8 for a water from the mini bar..WTF!?!?). They have slot machines everywhere, but none of the newer ones that you see in other casinos (not having the Wheel of Fortune slots is basically a deal breaker for me). Very limited table games as well. They essentially have one big pit of table games and even though I was there on a Sunday-Monday they were always completely packed. Weird that this place was completely packed for the majority of my visit. I'm thinking it's more of a local hangout so they don't have to deal with all the tourists downtown. Also their comp program sucks, I spent a lot of money (seriously, I gambled basically the whole time I was there) and got nothing in return. Would I go back...maybe if it was free. I would probably spend the $2 to take public transit downtown though where me and my money would be more appreciated.
label: NEG

text: I LOVE GARCES TRADING COMPANY. Both trips were really great experiences and we had the pleasure of meeting Chef Garces on the second night! Along with other Garces restaurants, this place ranks among my top favorites in Philly.

text: It's a buffet on the main floor of a casino in Reno. How great can it be? As long as you ignore the fact that it'll cost you almost $30 for all you can eat, the answer is surprisingly good. While it lacks ambiance, the selection is wide and well chosen, and the quality is better than you would expect. In fact, it sometimes even approaches awesome. Take the bacon wrapped fillets. Bacon wrapped anything is going to be good, but these were nice, thick, tender fillets. I could cut it with my fork. All you can eat. Salad bar had much more than lettuce, with good pasta, cucumber, southwestern (corn and chickpeas), and seafood salads available. The crab salad was especially good. In fact, the amount of crab and lobster they had in various dishes was surprising. Lots of seafood choices. They had some good herb encrusted sole, as well as heaps of fried shrimp. All you can eat. Prime rib. Build your own stir fry. Taco bar with decent chile verde carnitas. Frickin pile of BBQ ribs. All you can eat. Dessert. Ice cream. Fruit tarts. Pie. All you can eat. Man, after spending a week in the desert, this was like heaven to see all this just piled up for the taking. Nothing like ending a week of debauchery with a night of good ol' fashioned gluttony. What the hell, it's only once a year, right?

text: Best raw oysters in NOLA! If you've seen any of my other NOLA reviews, I've been all over the city looking for the best oysters, and Luke's definitely tops all the others. I've been there 3 times in 16 days. They have the fantastic happy hour special, during which they have .50 cent oysters and half off beer. Can't get a better deal. And their oysters are the fattest, juiciest oysters in the city! They actually have a minneret sauce and the sharpest horseradish sauce that just goes straight to your senses and cleans your airways. Love it! I also had the shrimp & grits once, and I had never had them before, but the dish was wonderfully balanced and delicious, unlike some of the other New Orleans restaurants that only heap on the salt and butter. Their bread pdding is a wonderful dessert as well. Again, very balanced with an even texture, with handmade ice cream piled on top. The only reason why this place has 4 stars instead of 5, though, is that the service is not great here. Wonderful, wonderful food, but they have some of the slowest service I have had here. I do hope that things pick up for them, as it's a place that I'd like to see flourish.

text: I've been to LC several times, and I am impressed. The interior is homely and country, and the portions are BIG. Yes, HUGE. I recall getting a taco salad that was so huge, probably almost twice the size of regular taco salads. The fries are o' plenty, and depending on the day I suppose, they're a little salty. And most of the food isn't healthy, so don't expect a dainty salad as a meal coming your way. However, unless weight loss or maintainence is a life or death thing, just GO! Eating healthy isn't about what you eat, but how much you eat. I suggest 1) Going here on a empty stomach-- not empty as in you have 1/4 tank left in your car, but when you're running on EMPTY, hungry. Unless we're talking about pizza, foods generally are best fresh, so why not waste your money and eat as much as fresh food as you can instead of having it microwaved and soggy! 2) Stop eating when you're full and take the rest home. You can always have leftover food the next day or so. As I've been eating healthier, I come to appreciate those dainty places that don't serve greasy food. However, if you're ever hankering for some great southern delicious greasy food, this is your place.

Starting off were the free chips and salsa, the chips were excellent the salsa a first seemed a little mild for my taste. As I continued eating I felt a nice little burn. Salsa gets a 3. For my dinner I had the Carnita's De Puerco, the pork was very tender and not loaded with chunks of fat that you often find in pork dishes. The rice and beans were excellent. The Margarita's were a cut above the standard 'Rita found most anywhere else. The outdoor seating was small and decorated well, though be advised it sits only about 6 feet form the street, so it can get noisy. The bottom line, if in Tampa, and you want Mexican with an upscale feel try Miguel's Mexican Cafe.

text: I LOVE Tzin!! My favourite wine bar in the world thus far (ok, so I haven't gone to all that many), Tzin is a tiny and intimate spot that's just bursting with good food, good wine, good staff, good decor and good atmosphere. Tzin is going for excellent quality in small doses, from their 10 item (but delicious) tapas menu to their 1 bathroom that looks like something out of a home decor magazine for the rich. Expect to be crammed in and not have much elbow room, but expect it not to really matter as you enjoy the company of good friends and the knowledgeable and friendly advice of the servers and owners. The wine menu changes frequently, so be ready to try something new - the servers have a wealth of information and are great at helping wine newcomers like myself find something new they'll enjoy every time. If you're hungry, go for the steak or mushroom crostini - both are heavenly. The one concern is that Tzin isn't cheap - while it's easily affordable if you want just one (half) glass of wine, if you're planning to make a night of it there or to eat enough tapas to constitute dinner, things may get expensive fast. That said, it's definitely worth the expenditure, as the quality found at Tzin is difficult to find even at places that cost far more. Just one word of advice: show up early if you actually want to get seats - Tzin is relatively full of the after-work crowd until about 7pm, but then fills up for the evening by 9:30 (but they do take reservations).

Soup: Gumbo - this was okay but they got the gumbo's mixed up and gave me the chicken one instead of the seafood one Main: bf had "A Taste of Soul" Platter - Filé Gumbo, Red Beans & Rice, Jambalaya, Greens, Fried Chicken, Catfish Strips, and Bread Pudding, collard greens, while I had: Stuffed Bell Pepper - A green bell pepper stuffed with ground beef, shrimp, spices, and seasonings, baked and topped with our light home-style brown gravy, with red beans/rice, and mac/cheese shared the bread pudding for dessert BF really enjoyed his entree, while I found everything about mine to be lacking. BF's was good because all the fried seafood was low in fattiness, had a nice cornmeal crust and was light on oil. Mine sucked because the stuffing in the bell pepper was just whatever, and the mac and cheese was embarrassing - it had the texture of being reheated leftovers (overly mushy noodles and hard cheese) and tasted like almost nothing, box kraft is better. And it was not hot like the bell pepper. The cornbread was not warm either so I didn't get to enjoy any nice crust on top. Bread pudding dessert was hot and delicious, though it had nuts so it automatically became all mine. This was the best part of the meal. Beyond the food being less than impressive, at least my dish, the service was pretty lacking. It took a looong time for a server to get to us, while a neighboring party sat down later, ordered and received their food before us. Another neighboring party had super crappy service too, and even asked for a comment card, and of course did not get one. The melon cakes shrank quite a bit recently, so they lose a star for that. I was pretty sad since they're my favorite pastry here. text: Hands down, my new favorite restaurant in West Philly. I know, I know, I just called Marrakesh Express my favorite West Philly restaurant a little over a week ago, but then I went to Demetri's... Self-image problem or not, Demetri's really is a pearl in the rough. They are smart enough to realize that to survive at 45th and Chestnut, they'd better deliver junk food to the college students. But their also smart enough to realize that this area has been waiting for something more... a nice BYOB with good service and ambiance that WON'T break the bank. And in this regard, they truly do deliver. I've been to Demetri's for dinner twice, and both times I left full and happy. Everything that I've tried has been a winner. The first time, I ordered the San Marco salad; a salad with grilled chicken, dried cranberries, goat cheese, and glazed pecans (which were actually walnuts) and raspberry viniagrette. I can usually finish the salads that I ordered, but this one was HUGE and had a ton of chicken on top. I had to give up prematurely... The second time I ordered the gnocchi pesto with shrimp, which was amazing. The gnocchi was amazing, the perfectly light and fluffy, and the sauce was delish. It came with a side salad (yes, drenched in dressing- if you're not a dressing hog, ask for it light) or soup, plus garlic bread, made with fresh sharp garlic. Yummy! We also ordered the fancy cheese and the spanikopita as appetizers. The cheese was super yummy and on fire (extra points for that) and the spanikopita was really big and really good. All in all, an amazing new restaurant on the West Philly scene. My fingers are crossed that everyone loves it as much as I do...

text: I walked in about five minutes before my appointment time and walked up to the desk. A woman saw me walk in and walked over the the desk and smiled and said hello. "Can I help you?" she said. "I have a one o'clock appointment for a pedicure." I said. She asked me name and my address. Then she told me to pick out a polish color as she pointed to the polish rack. I went over to pick from what seemed a limited collection of colors. I wanted a bright pink but the closest they had was coral or magenta. The salon was well decorated with muted earth tones. Nothing very eye catching but not at all dull. There was good quality furniture all throughout the salon and the occasional retro touch with an old book on hairstyling or an circa 1920's wall art piece. The salon looked very clean but I was very hard to tell if the technician had cleaned her implements before or after using them on me. The implements and products were places on a bamboo place mat that is impossible to sanitize. The pedicure chair had light on it to indicate if it had been sanitized but the light was not on. The chair had internal jetting, which always makes me nervous. And the chair next to me that was not being used had water spots and streaks on it. Could have been cleaner or could have been from the previous pedicure water. There was a bottle of bleach cleaner in the pedicure room. Sandy was the manicurist doing the service. She was very nice and well dressed with a cute zebra print skirt. I followed her to the pedicure room and the pedicure tub was already filled and jets running. She had me start by putting my feet into the water. After a very short soak, she took one foot out removed old polish, shortened filed toes nails. She then pushed back my cuticles and smoothed out the nails with a buffer then applied a "sugar scrub". After that she applied a lotion and did a foot massage. Her movements were fast and although I did enjoy the massage it was mediocre at best. Next was polish...I had chosen a shimmery coral color. She applied base coat, two coats of color and then top coat. Then without missing a beat applied cuticle oil. Now, as a manicurist myself I know that polish drys through evaporation. Polish cannot dry when covered with oil. There was so much oil my flip flops were all oily when I got home. Plus when she was applying the oil she put her finger into the polish on my big toe and then reapplied more polish after the oil was on the nail. That nail is now very thick with polish. But the worst was the lotion. I think it was Hempz and I just hate the smell of that stuff. I gives me a headache. But most people love it. The one thing that defines a pedicure is a good polish job. This was not. My feet were slipping around in my flip flops from all the lotion. I had to walk very gingerly. I would recommend bringing your own polish with you since their selection is not the best. I paid $46 for a 30 minute pedicure. This is a little on the high side. For the money, go somewhere else.

text: I found out about this place by googling "best mapo tofu, philadelphia" and some Yelp reviews and other reviews popped up. By the time they showed up, I had decided our menu: dumplings in spicy sauce, golden eggplant coins, mapo tofu, 3 pepper chicken and two other dishes they could choose to include the spice-intolerant. They chose Triple Delight with Spicy sauce and a chicken noodle dish. The spice-intolerant who chose the noodles said they were bland. Well, duh. The Triple Delight was chosen because the friend enjoys that dish and uses it as a comparison. He said it does not compare to his favorite place, but it was well-made and he enjoyed it. Those two dishes, along with the eggplants, served as our non-spicy complements. The eggplant coins were delicious! Probably our second favorite, after the dumplings in spicy sauce. However, the sauce with the golden coins was uninteresting, and we used the remaining dumpling sauce with it. That spicy dumpling sauce is amazing. I would drink it like a milkshake. The mapotofu was tongue-tingling numb, like a good szechuan peppercorn dish! I enjoyed it, but my friends who had never had the peppercorn before had mixed reviews about the sensation. And one friend who had peppercorn before said he felt it was too strong of a sensation compared to his previous experience. Nevertheless, I enjoyed it, including the silky texture of the tofu and the fine mince of the meat. It seems to me that most folks get take-out (both from reviews and my experience seeing a lot of delivery orders prepared). I would go back for when I want that peppercorn experience, especially for the dumplings. Though, I think Dim Sum Garden will remain our go-to Chinatown joint. Oh P.S. It is BYO, so bring either a white wine or cold beer to counter the spice!

I gave the bartender a knowing look when he mentioned there was no menu...I rested my hand on the bar and said, "I'll take a screwdriver." He gave me a puzzled, unimpressed glance and when I realized I'd just asked for a orange juice and vodka cocktail, I quickly retracted my request and said, "bartender, what a clumsy mistake I have made. I will take a Sidecar, not a screwdriver." He released a subtle sigh of relief and assured me I'd "come to the right place." And so I had. My mom and I split the Porterhouse "for two." This 28-day aged cut had me pulling a Meg Ryan all throughout dinner. People stared, I didn't care. If you want the best steak of your life, this is it. At least it's the best steak I've ever eaten...and I've eaten lots and lots of steaks. The hash brown side was phenomenal and came out looking like a crispy potato pie. Golden on the outside with tiny potatoes on the inside. The green beans were also fantastic. We kept our order simple, but simple is right when the steak is this dang good. If you like bananas or meringue, order this yesterday. Here's the foolproof way to go: Sidecars Porterhouse for two Stuffed Hash Browns Green Beans Amandine Baked Alaska I'll be thinking about this meal for a long time.

Even if you're a guy. There were police cars lined up on the street across from Neveria, but that didn't stop us from gettin some grub! We walked right in. This place is TINY! It's the epitome of 'hole in the wall'. Customers speaking in spanish, a hot grill sizzling and steaming, chipped paint on the ground, colorful walls. It was great. I felt like I was in a movie or something. My coworker is a vegetarian, and neither one of us were super hungry, so we ordered the vegetarian burrito to share. I was a vegetarian for 7 years in the past, but now I'm a full-fledged meat eater, so the idea of eating a veggie filled burrito didn't excite me. However, this was the BEST veggie burito I've had. Ever. I don't know what secret spice they put in there, but it was AMAZING. The burrito came with 2 different sauces, radishes, pickled spicy carrots and jalapenos, chips, and guac. I think the total came to like, 5 dollars? And this fed two people (I guess it could feed one super hungry person). Amazing deal. I can't wait to come back to try something more exotic. Like tongue. Until then, it gets a solid 4 stars from me.

text: I am a small business owner, so I always make it a priority to spend my money at local businesses. As other reviewers have indicated, things started well with the Tile Source. The floor staff were friendly and they had the tile I was looking for at a fair price. I bought my first $250 round of tile with no issues. Having had a good experience, I returned to buy my second round of $415 of tile. The first red flag was that the $65 floor sealer was in a tiny bottle - a bottle so small that anyone might start to wonder, "Is this tiny bottle really worth $65?". As I soon found out, the answer is NO. Home Depot carries the same exact product for ~$30. I understand that small businesses have a hard time matching the price of an international corporation, but a $35 difference on a $65 product is unreasonable. When I went to return the sealer I was told that it is one of many many many items that they do not let you return. You might be hard pressed to find any items that they would actually allow you to return. They do publish their return policy; however, it is on the back of the receipt, so the first time you will see it is after it is too late and you have made your purchase. It is hard for me to imagine that this doesn't break standard business practices. The very clear outcome of their inflexible return policy is that the remaining tile I have yet to purchase (~$1200 worth) will be purchased elsewhere. Please read the other reviews. You'll see that I am not the only customer that has been driven away by their unwillingness to be reasonable with their returns.

text: Luke is pretty good. Went here for lunch with my husband and his parents who were visiting for the weekend. I wasn't surprised to see that it was rather busy during lunchtime on a Friday since it's in the middle of the CBD. Despite the crowd there was hardly a wait before we were seated. Luke was definitely perfect for the in-laws. Right up front they've got well-known newspapers for anyone to grab at their convenience in case you want to catch up on the news while enjoying your meal. The newspapers were right up my father-in-law's alley. I really liked the decor as well but then it's just my taste in dark wood and I was impressed with the vintage pulley fan system. I think if it was just my husband and I, I would have preferred to sit up at the massive bar. The service was swift and friendly. My father-in-law thought his gumbo was too cold so they immediately brought him a new one at the correct temperature. Personally, I got the express menu for the day which includes a cup of soup and an entree. I ordered the crawfish bisque and the redfish "court-bouillon" with crab, shrimp, oysters, and rice. Good deal, I'd say! The bisque was perfectly smooth and creamy. It was a relatively cool day outside and it warmed me right up. I might be biased though since I'm a fan of bisques in general. I wasn't sure if I would like the redfish court-bouillon but it was excellent! It came out in a small cast-iron dish and it was just a great mixture of seafood and rice. The sauce had a kick to it without being too spicy. I would definitely come back here again as I was rather envious seeing the Luke Burger being carried to other tables. It just LOOKS good sitting on a wood plank alongside some fresh fries and you get these cute, teeny, personal condiments. So yeah, next time!

text: If I were to judge Dahlak on its potato salad alone, it would be five stars, all the way, forever. And I feel like forever should be in all caps, there. However, I have to judge it also on its service and prices and this is where things go South. And not in a fun Dukes-of-Hazzard way. Okay. I'm not supposed to say this, but it has to be said, so I'm just gonna put it out there. It seems like anyone who expresses dissatisfaction with Dahlak gets rebuffed with the dead community leader card. I'm not disputing that Solomon Amare was a wonderful man or that a family business needs leeway to regain its footing after its owner passes. However, it's been three years. You can't play this card forever to cover what has devolved into, at best, mediocrity. Most of the food I've tried is good. Great? Every now and again. In the past, I mostly have depended on Dahlak for takeout. I want to believe that they are cooking everything (and I mean everything- is anything prepped?) from scratch, because I have waited at least thirty minutes before I walk to the restaurant and inevitably end up waiting another 20-30 minutes while sitting in the restaurant as they continue to prepare the food I've ordered. The restaurant itself is charming, in a dingy sort of way. I've never decided whether the dim lighting was romantic or creepy. But there are the fun little woven tables and the "ethnic" art. There are also "normal" tables for the more conventional. The last few times I've gone in during the evening, the dining room has been empty, save maybe one other table. Why is it taking so long to make my food? But for good food, I will wait. Unfortunately, it has become hit and miss. The portions seem to be shrinking. The prices seem to be rising. I fail to understand, even with rising global food prices, how a scoop of lentils can have such a mark-up. And I could probably even let all of this go- the smaller portions, the overpricing, the wait, the wait, my god, the wait. But the last few times, I get home to unpack my food and lo and behold- parts of my *&%$# order are missing. I pay for two portions of potato salad. I get one. I order two sambussas. Nowhere to be found. Apparently, Dahlak is dealing in magic, because the food I pay them for is repeatedly involved in a disappearing act. Of course, it's late, I'm tired, I've waited an hour to get my food and now I'm home. I decide to "eat" the wasted dollars of my already (what I feel is, due to the portions and the wait) overpriced meal and never return. And it's sad. Because I like Dahlak. The people are nice enough (if distant). The food can be good. It fills out the block nicely. I don't want to walk to 45th Street... But playing with my money is like playing with my emotions, so no more Dahlak for me. If nothing else good came out of this, I taught myself how to make Ethiopian potato salad. . .

text: I used to really like Blue Parrot Grille. Their muffaletta was full of tasty deli meat and olive spread, the po'boys were all good, the crab soup was on point, and the entree portions were decent. Live music helped my boyfriend and I overlook the small appetizers, the bad frying (burnt chips and fries!), and the flavor profiles that weren't always spot on. No longer, however. Over the summer, we had an awful experience here that will guarantee we will never return, and neither will our dining companions on this particular occasion. After an art loop this summer, our party of six ended up at Union City Grille, but didn't feel like dining there. We chose instead to go across the street to the Blue Parrot. We were promptly seated outside, and soon put in our orders... everyone got a cocktail or a beer, and about half of our party ordered an entree. One person in our group ordered a hurricane. When the drinks came, our friend tasted his hurricane and discovered that he didn't like the taste. He thought it tasted like powdered fruit punch instead of a mixed drink. When the waitrees returned, he asked if he could replace the drink with something else. (During this exchange, she revealed that powdered drink mix WAS, in fact, among the ingredients of the beverage.) She told us that the management didn't allow patrons to return drinks, and that she could get him another drink, but he'd have to pay for both. We were all surprised by that policy, so our friend said that since he was being forced to pay for a drink he didn't like, he didn't want to order another and would furthermore like to cancel his food order, which was soup and an entree. This was only about 7 or 8 minutes after we had placed our orders, and nothing had arrived yet, so we all felt he was justified in cancelling his food. The other two people who'd ordered food were content to keep their orders in. The waitress left and a few minutes later we were approached by the owner/manager. He said, rather rudely, "If I put more alcohol in your drink, will you keep your food order?" Our friend, bewildered, said he didn't know... it wasn't about the alcohol content, it was the taste. The owner ranted that they'd been making their hurricanes the same way for 10 years, and it was premixed in pitchers at the beginning of the evening and no one had ever complained before. After his rant, the owner asked again if our friend would keep his food order, and when he received no as an answer, he said that our friend was no longer welcome to dine there. We asked if he was serious (we were that baffled), and he said yes, that the friend would have to leave if choosing to cancel his food. He then turned and went back into the main dining area. Our party decided, of course, not to stay... and all paid for our one drink (sans tip), before leaving together. My boyfriend asked the owner's name, which he was reluctant to give. He also told my boyfriend, "The customer is not always right." Who says that?!? Soup arrived for another friend as we were finishing paying our bills, but there was no way any of us were sticking around. I've never heard an owner or manager talk so disrespectfully to a customer before. I think it's worth mentioning that while I am white, everyone else in my party that night was a person of color. There was no one else of color in the restaurant, and now I think I know why. I can't believe someone would sacrifice $30 in other food orders and who knows how much in drink orders (we were planning on staying for a while), because one person didn't like their drink, received bad customer service, and decided not to get food after all. I advise folks to consider this experience before planning a trip to the Blue Parrot.
label: NEG

text: The restaurant has only been open a week, and I'm sure we'll try it again at a later date to see if it has improved, but our experience tonight was very disappointing. We arrived today (Sunday) at 4:45. It was relatively empty, maybe 4-5 tables seated. Our server was friendly and prompt, and we ordered an appetizer and a small pizza to share. The appetizer--Eggplant Marino--was delicious, though a tad soggy. It arrived about 5 minutes after we placed our order, and we finished it at maybe 5:10. At 5:15, our server told us that our pizza should be out shortly. She scored points for dropping off a plate with two of their (absolutely delicious) chicken wings as well, to try for next time. i would love to provide a fair review of the pizza, but by the time we got to eat it it was cold, so I have no idea what one tastes like right out of the oven. While we sat there from 5:15 to 5:50, the place slowly filled up and we watched numerous people get seated and get their food. Our server stopped by 2 or 3 times and told us the pizza should be there shortly, but it never arrived. To show how delayed it was, the family that arrived the same time as we did finished their food, paid, and the next family seated at that table got their pizza before we did. Finally at 5:40 we told the server that we needed the pizza to go (since a friend was coming to our house at 6), and we finally got our boxed pizza and a check at 5:50. I was shocked that no one came to apologize for the delay, though the manager walked by and looked at us and our empty table several times. We ate the pizza when we got home (late to meet our friend) and it was tasty but cold. It would have been better hot (I'm sure) but the cheese was no longer melted and the toppings had gotten cold. We paid the full price for our meal and left with a "come again soon!" from the very friendly hostess. Will we come again soon? Not likely. But we might give it another chance again in a few months after they work out all the kinks. Again, very disappointing service, but decent food.

text: Yah, I finally went into an Aldi. I've always been curious, but also a bit intimidated. Ahhh, it's so scary! I don't want to look like a moron. In reality, it's a great idea. No carts strewn in the lot bumping into brand new Subaru Impreza's (thank you very much). None of that "front wheels of the cart over the curb so it doesn't roll away" placements. And, of course, Aldi (which is owned by the same German company that owns Trader Joe's (boo, but that's another story)) doesn't have to hire alot of employees. In fact, this store has TWO people working there. The cashier and someone behind a one-way glass who no doubt is looking for cretins stealing the FIBER NOW bars. See, very few of the products there are brand name. Most are their own private label and they are cheap and, believe it or not, really good. I go for their coffee, dog food (yes, things are getting that bad), and some snacks. I guess I'm just a sucker for weird off-brand products. I buy Crispy Hexagons, not Crispix--but that's my little fetish. The place is quiet too. No ubiquitous remakes of Korn tunes by muzak. Just sweet silence. I feel like I'm buying groceries in Yerevan, or something. Now, I'm not suggesting people to buy all their food there, although you would save a lot, but even buying certain items will save you money. And in these tough times, that's nothing to laugh at. Now, back to my Aldi knockoff Yodels called Fudgy Delights! I think they're manufactured in Latvia. yum.

text: Bucca. I love me some Bucca... For those of us who aren't familiar with Bucca, it's a family style chain Italian restaurant. The portions are HUGE, serving 2-4 people, on average. The decor is eclectic and there are photos on all of the walls. Some of the prints are really amusing, and looking at them is kind of fun. (My favorite one at this location is a SUPER large print from the late 50s or early 60s... It shows three women and they are eating spaghetti with no utensils, just their faces... Like a spaghetti eating contest!) I digress. One kinda weird thing they enjoy doing is walking your party through the kitchen as they take you to your table. I suppose they want you to see where your food is coming from, and all that, but I think it's bizarre and unsanitary. I don't want whooping cough because they want to be gimmicky. (Though honestly, I don't want to get whopping cough for any reason.) And now! The food. My favorite dishes at Bucca include the Chicken Saltimbocca and the Apple Gorgonzola salad. Their meatballs are also delicious and moist. (I'm certain that I could eat the lemon butter/caper sauce that comes on the chicken ALLLLL the time and never get tired of it!) The staff is generally pretty nice, though they do that douche-y stuff that some waiters/waitresses at certain chain restaurants do... Like coming to the table and asking, "Is everything delicious?" That phrase makes me want to stab people, incidentally. I digress AGAIN. My husband and I also love to get take out from this place... and then I eat the leftovers for lunch the next day. They are always really nice, and the food is packaged well. We often get the aforementioned salad, and they package the dressing separately, rather than tossing it beforehand and letting it wilt before we get home. They also have the curbside-to-go thing and so they bring it out to the car and such... making pajama runs to Bucca totally doable. This place is great... especially for a small group of friends (though they can definitely accommodate larger groups)! I definitely recommend giving it a shot. **I should note, however, that my husband feels this place is a bit expensive for what it is (i.e. chain Italian food). I tend to agree with him, honestly... You do get a lot of food, and some of their items are pretty reasonable, but the Chicken Saltimbocca (which I LOVE) is pretty expensive.

text: I'm sooo happy to finally say I have medical health care thanks to my time served in the U.S. Navy. It's a big relief and Bay Pines is 10 minutes away from my house. In 1933, they opened the doors there with a hospital, domiciliary, VA regional office and cemetery. Since that time, it has grown into a huge complex that processes over 120,000 vets a year. At my orientation the woman said there are 70 NEW vets a day being processed because of the economic crisis. I'm impressed with the complex which now sits on 357 acres. They have everything here except a bowling alley! I loved the food court with heart-healthy food choices as well as the cantina. text: So, you're sitting in your hotel room on a visit to Indianapolis. Not really in the mood to dress up and go out on the town but not wanting to eat McDonald's again. You want something new, something original, and DEFINITELY something tasty. Well, congratulations for using Yelp and finding this Indy gem! I was a skeptic but Yelp has never led me astray! I hopped in the car, parked in their tiny alley lot, and headed in solo. I was immediately greeted and seated in a comfy booth. It's a small restaurant but I got there around 7:30 on a Friday night and had no problem being seated. I was greeted by the waitress immediately and my drink order was taken. After looking over the menu I decided that my fellow Yelp-ers knew what they were talking about and trusted them... so, I ordered the famous fried chicken and waffle. I went with the sweet potato waffle of course! I was delivered my drink with 2 cornbread biscuits with the peach butter. SO GREAT! I could just eat the butter, but that's a little strange so I refrained. Then the main course came (took around 5 minutes) - see photos - and I dug right in. The chicken wings were delicious - tender, juicy, flavorful! Then I moved to the waffle, added more peach butter, and dug in. I can only say that if I had the recipe, those waffles may be all I ever eat! Do not let your unadventurous self take over to order bland blueberry/strawberry or the like... go for the gusto with this sweet waffle! I polished off my plate although I probably could have stopped halfway through. There were several cakes, pies, and other desserts which tempted but I was able to walk out only mildly stuffed. So, put some shoes on, grab your keys, and point your GPS to this hole-in-the-gas station place and fill up on some delicious grub! ENJOY!

text: This is not my favorite mall. In fact, except for the Roosevelt Mall, Franklin Mills is my least favorite mall in the Philly area. I live about 5 minutes away, and I only go into the actual mall about once a year, usually when a friend drags me there. It's a dark, maze-like building, and I find the layout unappealing. I do, however, like that it's 1 mile long, so at least you can get a workout while you're there, since nothing else is worth the trip. Most of the stores are weird stores that you've never heard of, which have cheap-looking clothing that I personally wouldn't waste my money on. The only worthwhile stores are the Banana Republic, Gap, Old Navy, and Ann Taylor outlets (and Ann Taylor is still expensive) and Steve & Barry's (but only for Sarah Jessica Parker's Bitten line). Otherwise, this mall sucks. I also don't like the theater. I used to go to the movies at Franklin Mills all the time back when they were in a separate building, not attached to the mall proper. But, once they attached the theaters to the mall, I noticed that the moviegoing crowd was a different demographic. Suddenly, my fellow moviegoers were the kind of people who answer their very loudly ringing cell phones in the middle of the film and then proceed to have very loud conversations for 10 minutes, or they bring infants, or they're annoying teenage boys who do obnoxious things during the movie. All of these things have caused me to stop going there (I prefer Woodhaven, which is clean, quiet, closer to my house, and which still has student discounts, and Neshaminy). As for the mall area itself, I sometimes go to Sam's Club, and I avoid Wal-mart at all costs (evil, evil conglomerate). But the beer distributor in the Wal-mart shopping center is awesome - they have a great selection. And the wine & spirits superstore has the best wine selection in Pennsylvania (at least that I've found). They're way bigger than the usual state store, and they have a lot of wines to choose from (not as many as stores in NY state or NJ or Total Wines in Delaware, but I'll take it). In all, I'd say save your money and go to a mall that has real stores. Even the good stores at Franklin Mills are only outlets, so they have last year's styles or items that were not made correctly, so basically, the stores here are reject stores. No fun.

text: We just had our reception at the Rockwood Women's Club this weekend, and we couldn't have chosen a better place. The price was mid-range for Santa Barbara - not cheap, but not outrageous. The grounds are naturally beautiful (gorgeous walkways, trees, and flowers everywhere) and don't need any decoration. The building is Mission-style architecture, and because it was so beautiful inside, it didn't need much decoration. In fact, we got so many compliments on how beautiful Rockwood was. By comparison, several other venues I looked at required that we paid for valet parking (hell no), hired security staff (hell no), and provide a playlist for approval prior to the reception (hell no). I don't know if this is the norm, or if this is all just a Santa Barbara thing, but at least Rockwood included parking in our fee and allowed us to play pretty much whatever we wanted. text: As a native Texas, I was raised to LOVE both interior Mexican food and Tex-Mex. Growing up in a state bordering Mexico, I've been taught to trust Mexican fare less the more north I go. Against all the odds, La Fiesta, right here in Nashville, passed the first test. I walked to La Fiesta for lunch and ordered the chicken tacos and and a la carte pork tamale (I wanted the shredded pork tacos but they only serve those during dinner hours). The tamale was HUGE and pretty darn good. I will say, they top the tamales with red sauce, cheese and ground beef. I'm a firm believer that tamales shouldn't be smothered in anything (I question what their hiding if I can't see the tamale). Nonetheless, this tamale was YUMMY. Next time, I'll ask them to leave off the extra tamale toppings and just spoon some of their fresh salsa on it instead. The tacos: I was pleasantly surprised. The tacos were filled with shredded chicken that had been cooked with tomato, bell pepper and onion. There was a nice flavor that, topped with their fresh made salsa, was a nice treat. I'll definitely go back to give La Fiesta another try. They do have a liquor license and serve a variety of liquors in addition to wine and beer. On tap, they have Dos Equis Lager, Dos Equis Amber, Bud Light and Yazoo Dos Perros. Happy hour is everyday from 3-7pm. The regular drink prices are pretty good ($2-3 for a pint and $4 for a 32 ounce domestic beer) so I'm curious about their happy hour rates. Give them a try, it worth it.

text: I'm sorry, how can people eat this? Quick tip - any person, place, or thing that labels itself "gourmet" (with the sole exception of the now-defunct Gourmet Magazine, RIP) is guaranteed to let you down in matters of culinary taste. I don't like to generalize, but this is one generalization you can take to the bank, along with the one that "luxury condos" are never luxurious. The "gourmet" pizzas at Peace a Pizza are of a type - the type that thinks you need to pile endless tons of "inventive" crap on top of overly thick crust for a satisfying and "gourmet" bite. When will these types of pizzerie learn that the best pizzas are the ones that take care to produce a chewy crust - not thick, but well-stretched, flavorful, and chewy - and feature a few carefully chosen toppings, rather than an avalanche of entrees? Novelty is overrated. Macaroni and cheese on pizza is wrong. Ranch dressing on pizza is wrong. Alfredo sauce on pizza is disgusting. If you want to eat a cheesesteak, eat a cheesesteak, not a cheesesteak pizza. There's something to be said for learning to do it right, rather than trying to be "original" and provide "variety." I'd rather have a plain cheese slice from any pizza by the slice place in Philly any day, or every day for the rest of my life, than another slice from Peace A Pizza.

I love frozen yogurt because it is ice cream's lighter and healthier stepsister, but I like my frozen yogurt to taste more like ice cream and less like somebody dumped a container of Dannon in the freezer for five hours and then put it in a soft serve machine. I actually have a visual of some evil supervillain, complete with curly, villainous mustache, doing this and twisting his mustache with his fingertips while saying "They'll be none the wiser!" and laughing maniacally. We looked at the menu a bit, and decided to go with the crispy crab empanadas, as well as a Schlafly pumpkin ale for me (woo!) and a whiskey and coke for the boy. The empanadas were not good. The breading tasted a lot like a pot pie, and the filling tasted like tuna, not crab. Hmm. The mango salsa that accompanied the appetizer was flavorless. I was hoping to have better luck with the entree. I went with the jerk chicken sandwich with french fries. The sandwich was just okay. Very cheesy, but not very...jerk-y? Isn't jerk seasoning supposed to be a bit spicy? This wasn't. It wasn't too flavorful either, to be honest. The kaiser roll that the meat came on was just sad. The whole thing was just bland. The seasoned fries were terrific, though! I saw that they had bread pudding on the dessert menu, so OF COURSE I had to try that! It came out piping hot and covered in a bourbon sauce. This was probably the best part of the meal. It was soft, gooey, and tasted just like french toast. A+! The service was friendly, but slow. It seemed like that was ONE waitress taking care of the entire restaurant. Are they always this slow, or was it just an unusually busy night? I don't know. She was friendly, so I'm not going to complain too much. I'm glad we had a Groupon so we could try this place. Sadly, I seriously doubt we'll be back. Maybe for drinks (my pumpkin ale was delish, as was Andy's Whiskey and coke!), but definitely not for food. Save your money. Go elsewhere.

They don't try to be anything but a good simple diner, and frankly I find that refreshing as hell in a world where every place seems to be trying to be more than what they are and usually failing at it. text: After reading all of the shining reviews for Lupita's, I was excited to try it out. For me and my friends, it was just adequate. My shrimp a la diabla was fine. The sauce was reminiscent of BBQ sauce almost and it tasted like it was made with condensed OJ. It was a nice flavor, just threw me off a bit. The carne asada was overcooked and far too gristley. I realize that it isnt supposed to be a fine piece of meat, but Ive had better versions almost everywhere else. The service was also adequate but all in all a very forgettable experience and not one worth driving across town for, for sure.

text: I come in for a second visit because the food was good for the price and I had a coupon. The coupon is for one side item. I see that wings are cheaper than what the coupon would allow and I ask if I may get the 5 wings as my side and the lady said I could only get 8. I thought that was weird but went ahead and ordered. note; the lady was I think the owner and did not take my owner, she was just walking around or something. SO i gave my order to the gentleman and it came out okay, 1 bulgogi wrap and 8 wings, the wings being covered by the coupon. I go sit down and the lady comes over to where I'm seated rather hurried. She asks if I paid for the wings I reply no I did not I had a coupon. She tells me to come to the front and says that I cannot have the wings. I then say okay well then can I have my money back because I was really only in the mood for wings. She says no we've already started cooking. Now at this point I get upset because for one no restaurant has ever not given the money back for an order not served and then tries to give me another coupon. They were handing these things out in droves, I had about 5 back at my dorm. She's freaking out and then just says fine you can have your wings after what I presume was an argument in the back. I get my food, the wings are very good by the way, and am about done when she came by to deliver food or something I'm not sure what but she says in a very rude voice, "how are the FREE [she emphasized free] wings." Before I could even respond she just walked away leaving me speechless. I was never rude to any of them I simply wanted my wings or my money back. I cannot believe the kind of service I got as I have never received this horrid service anywhere else. I've been to a plethora of wing places and worked as a supervisor in an eating establishment so i feel confident in say they lost little or no money by their mix-up. Well they did lose one loyal customer for I certainly planned on going back but now I think I'll just settle for one of the food trucks. too long didn't read: Good food, kinda pricey, awful service, pricey as in most entrees are above 8 dollars.

text: We were looking for a good place to eat in Tampa on a Saturday night, and Columbia was the unianimous recommendation from the concierge, our cab driver, and a few locals. Arriving in front of the restaurant, the architecture alone makes you catch your breath. The aroma as you enter does the same. Even though it was a Saturday night and we had no reservations, we were seated immediately. Service was impeccable, and the food...oh my god, the food. The only thing we weren't too fond of was the Queso Fundido, which tasted vaguely Italian and didn't quite go with the rest of our tapas choices. However, the Croquetas de Pollo were delicious, as was the Caldo Gallego. The standout for us was the Mejiliones y Chorizo "Andres"--definitely recommended! Can't comment on the dessert list as we were too full afterwards, but the white sangria was just right--refreshing and light, but with a little kick provided by the fresh lemon and lime. The best part? Drinks, appetizers, and dinner for two came to a grand total of $40. In NYC, this same dinner would have been well over $100...

text: I first visited this location during my lunch break, but after seeing their phenomenal beer and wine specials, returned after work. Great outdoor seating to bring pets. Also, check out their coupons to print on their website before going!!! Other things that were great: friendly and fast service and the restaurant is SUPER CLEAN which is always a huge plus!

text: This place is DERICIOUS! That means it is way better than delicious. Restaurant, deli and butcher. WOW! Anyway, back to breakfast. The owner greeted us. The BF grew up in the area and he got the special hello. That always makes you feel special. Everything comes dry and you can choose your own butter or whipped butter. I loved this. Why don't all places do this? I wish I could have eaten every bite since everything was so good, but I was simply stuffed. The home fries were also unbelievable although I would call them more of a hash. text: For my parent's 50th Wedding anniversary, we were looking for a place that would be a great 'multi-generational' vacation destination, since we were planning a 3-generation gathering. After extensive research, we ended up going to the FVC (as it's affectionately called) 5 years ago. Well, Grandparents, parents and grand kids had SO much fun, we've made it an annual tradition! Everyone looks forward to our week at the FVC. The grandkids have 'camp' each day so get lots of playtime together and truly love the fun activities they get to do. The parents get to go biking, hiking, surfing, play tennis or just hang out, while the grandparents go on nature walks, museum tours, and outings. We all get together for meals (great food and no one has to cook - can't beat that) and other activities during the day. It really is an ideal vacation for a family of any size. Oh, did I mention it's located right on the beach, just north of Santa Barbara? The accomodations are like condos -- one big sitting area, and either 2 to 4 bedrooms around it. It's a great blend of privacy and camaraderie. We're all looking forward to Year 5 this summer!

text: I hate to start off my Yelp reviews on a negative, but realizing how bad bad service can be prompted me to go from long time reader to first time reviewer. This FedEx location is right across from the Convention Center, so it should have been a quick in and out visit. It was a 50 page powerpoint on a USB drive, which I took to the self-service copier. I followed the directions, and after waiting 5 minutes, the employees behind the counter (including the manager) told me to wait another 3. Then another 3, all without even looking at the copier. They then had me re-save the file as a PDF to no avail, and then try printing from the self-service computers at twice the cost per page ($0.99 vs. $0.53). At this point (50 minutes elapsed), I was willing to pay the difference, but the printer crapped out after 15 pages. The most amazing thing is that they actually used the computer behind the desk to convert the PDF to yet another format to try, but they couldn't just print the document to end the misery. Yes they were busy, but when I finally gave up and walked the 1/2 mile to the St. Charles location, it took longer to process my credit card than to get me the print out. Long story short - if you can avoid the FedEx Convention Center location, you really should. If you're staying near the French Quarter, there's one on Canal Street, and another on your way on St. Charles that just seemed to be run with a lot more competence.
label: NEG

text: I cannot for the life of me understand why people rave about this place. (The somosas and mac & cheese are great, but that is about it.) Sunday at brunch, however, reached a new low. Upon entering, we were seated at a hightop with a bucket on the floor in the middle of the aisle passing our table.. The purpose of the bucket was to catch water dropping from the ceiling. Anyone walking past us had to step over the bucket. We could not be seated anywhere else because we were told we were too large of a party. One of our guests had to be careful not to lean too far back or she would get wet. As we were waiting for our "server" (although that phrase is too kind to describe her), a man came in, caught some of the drops of leaking water on his finger, smelled it, informed us it was not sewage and promptly left. After the reast of our party arrived, a new leak developed and two of the guests had to position themselves so the leak would drop between them. When the server noticed, she looked, shrugged her shoulders, and walked away. I decided to simply rearrange our seating. No employee made any attempt to help us. They simply watched us. I'm sure the arrangement I made violated the fire code, but then I think the bucket in the middle of the aisle violated both the fire and health codes. As for the service, non-existent is the phrase that comes to mind. Our waitress could only handle one task at a time (not one table at a time, but one task -- e.g., she couldn't remember all the drink orders and kept having to go back again and again for things she forget). I have never seen anyone so incompetent. As for the food, well mediocre is the word here. My scrambled eggs were good but cold. The toast was as hard and cold as a stone. Someone's mac & cheese was good, but others hated their meals (the fresh blueberry scone, however, was excellent). Bottom line -- why would anyone ever want to go here.
label: NEG

text: The fact that this is the ONLY record store anywhere near town makes me want to move away. Seriously. Want a new record? You won't find it. Want to score a decent used record? Good luck. Care to talk shop with the employees? Neither do they. Want to pay too much for whatever they have in stock? You're in luck. Shame on this store for making me shop for records online. text: I used to work on the same block as Buffalo Exchange and stopped in at least once a week to see what was new. text: Why pay jacked up retail when you can wait 2 weeks, and get the same new release books from an Amazon seller, backed by Amazon for 1/10 to 1/2 of the price Borders will charge?
