text: The last time we had a good meal at the Brick Hotel was four years ago. Since then, it's been nothing but disappointment. Every time there is a change in management or head chef, we get our hopes up and try again, but I think we are done. We just went for Valentine's day- mediocre food at fine dining prices, with mediocre, indifferent service. The appetizer of bacon-wrapped scallops was decent. However, the Caesar salad tasted like it had french dressing on it. We had lobster tail as our enree, which was bland and uninspired. Dessert was some kind of chocolate mousse, which wasn't awful, but not great. When we received the bill, we noticed that they had already included a 20% gratuity. This would be fine if we had fine dining quality service, but our waitress may as well have worked at a chain restaurant for all the effort she put in- a 15% tip would have been generous for her. Overall, this place was not worth the money- it's a shame, because it has potential to be a really nice restaurant.

text: I went to the Bishop's Collar this past weekend while on a day trip to Philly. The food there was excellent, everyone in my party was very impressed. (We had the hummus appetizer, the turkey burger with brie and red peppers, the burger wrap, the chipolte chicken sandwich and the chipolte chicken fingers). The service was great and very friendly and it was a beautiful day to sit at their outside tables and enjoy the early evening. I'll definitely go back next time I'm in Philly.

text: Muriel's always delivers an excellent meal. I never visit New Orleans without going here for a meal. The Goat Cheese Crepes are one of my favorite appetizers - such a wonderful savory dish especially with the goat cheese. The Turtle Soup is another one of my favorites and Muriel's has one of the best versions in town. No trip to NO is complete without this tasty soup. My husband and I always order seafood dishes and the taste / freshness / quality of the seafood at Muriel's is always excellent. No matter how full you get you MUST save room for dessert. Some of my past favorites include bread pudding, creme brulee, peanut butter bombe - just to name a few. If possible ask to go upstairs to the balcony for a drink (several times it was booked for private parties during our visits). Its the only public balcony that offers a great view of Jackson Square.

text: Chick-Fil-A is a fast food chain, and service is as good as you can expect, and there's always someone in the front trying to pawn off a sample, which is really creepy, but I still have my moments when I fall for their disgustingly greasy, mass produced chicken-esque blobs of meat. For those who haven't heard of Chick-Fil-A (what, they haven't yet reached their chicken tendrils where you live/work?), try their chicken nuggets - or whatever the heck they call them - and get a side of cole slaw. You might want to get a chocolate milkshake too - it's half-decent, and it'll clear your gullet - you'll either upchuck or thank me. Either way, there's ample seating in the food court for you to suffer in. Honestly, no matter what I write, or what star rating I give, you're going here if you like them or blowing that pop stand if you don't.

text: I give this place a few more months unless they get a rent subsidy from the Science Center. The place is across the street from work so I gave it a try, even though co workers warned me against it. I always wondered why a place so close to all the science center buildings would be so empty. I figured out why. I got a Martini and it was terrible. You know that flavor that ice has when it's left in the freezer to long? Yeah, that's what my drink tasted like. IT was a rough week, so I finished it and asked for another just in case it was a bad batch. Second one was just as bad. At that point though, alcohol was alcohol and I needed a drink. the food was just as bad. I got the burger. The burger came on a bun that was a bit dry and fell apart when I picked it up. I ate the rest of the burger with a knife and fork. the burger came with a dressing that had the same, left in refrigerator uncovered too long flavor. This place just couldn't do it right. I was disappointed, especially because it's so close to work. Maybe this place will get better but with so many other bars in University City, this place needs to really shape up fast.
label: NEG

text: Okay, it's pretty sad when the thing to do in your town is to go to the casino. That being said, this place has it all (for a small town). There are about 5 or 6 restaurants you can choose from, and the two we ate at were quite tasty. The first one sat 6 of us quickly, and the waitress was really tolerant of our changes to our orders. The food servings were ginormous, and the drinks were huge too. I think all in all, we spent $180 for three hours of drinking and eating, and shooting the sh!t in a really comfortable setting. So, I was in MO for a high school reunion, and going to Vegas for a full week after. I wanted to play some of the table games, but they were so crowded -- AND EXPENSIVE -- that I settled on the slots and played my friend's money when she ran to the bathroom. Walked away with about $200, so it wasn't bad. Ameristar is a good warm up to Vegas, but I'm glad I don't have to use it as my only source of recreation.

text: This was our escape from our extended stay hotel on the side of the highway in Malvern! Help: boredom alarm. We wanted to spice things up, so that we did. As I read here on Yelp the appetizers being the best part we reeled in some blackened gator in a mustard sauce which was the highlight of the evening. The voodoo crawfish (allegedly the spiciest thing on the menu) was also great but the sauce was a bit too thick, somewhat near motor oil in viscosity. The selection of beers was interesting and we tried a few and one brave soul (read: me) tried the jalapeno infused vodka based Vudu martini. Oh, it was spicy. I take it they received a license and it's no longer BYOB as mentioned in the other review. The service was slow and the crowd was weird, but it is West Chester and we experienced that at each establishment. The portions were fine but not huge like the other review implies. I went for the mustard fried catfish which was excellent, other got crab cakes, touffee, etc., but nothing could quite beat the appetizers.

text: I had the worst customer experience of my life here. They had old signs for sales and promotions that were no longer valid or honored. I waited for over five minutes at the counter while employees milled around back. Credit card machines were no working but the employees didn't even know. I left after 15 or 20 minutes empty handed because I was just getting frustrated. I honestly have no idea how they are staying in business with these kind of operations.

text: As I write this, my bike is definitely covered in snow and locked to a street sign somewhere in the Gayborhood, as it has been for the last two weeks. That is a testament to how much I care about my bike. Not really that much. It's a 44 pound monster Schwinn ten speed that likes to change gears by itself. I kind of hate my bike. But the people at Via always treat it nicely. They fix up the tires, replace broken pedals, realign my wheels and the like. I don't mind stopping by on a nice summer day and leaving my bike for a few hours, but sometimes they fix stuff on the spot for free. That makes me feel pretty special. Curtis the owner is really nice. I don't think he knows me as a "regular" (because I'm not really regular there) but if you watch him interact with other customers, he knows the ones he sees a lot. I like that too, it touches my heart a little bit. Via is a nice local business where I happily spend money to repair my bike when necessary.

text: The Great Escape has an edgy misfit/punk/nerd vibe that's hard for me to resist. In my opinion, it's not really fair to compare the Escape to Grimey's or Phonoluxe, because it's filling a distinctly different niche. The merchandise fits the store's name perfectly - all kinds of media that allow people to escape from every day life. Whether you prefer movies, music, or comic books, you'll find it at the Great Escape. As far as I could tell, everything in the store is used except for a small section of new vinyl, which means that the prices are reasonable ($9 for most CDs, $2-$25 for most records, depending on their rarity.) I was disappointed not to find a single Bob Dylan album in the entire store, but maybe that just means that the Great Escape's customers have good taste. The selection of vinyl and CDs is somewhat limited, but there's still more than enough good music for a casual collector to choose from. The walls are lined with the biggest collection of used DVDs I've ever seen, and of course the amount of used comic books here is insane. They also offer big old movie posters mounted on cardboard for $7-$10.
label: POS

text: Nothing Mexican about it. I went there late at night just because I did not want to walk too far from where I was staying and I was in the mood for some mexican food. The place looks like a very good place from the outside but inside is ordinary sitting arrangement. The sofa on near the wall is not appropriate height for the table. I ordered Jablano peppers and my girlfriend ordered cheese enchilada, none of them were good. Enchilada were served with some sort of mole sauce which is okay but they actually did not have Enchilada sauce at all. My peppers were not stuffed properly and overall tasteless food. I enjoyed the chips and salsa very much. Overall very bad experience. I will never go there again.

text: This place was just downright weird. It seems to be an old house converted to dance club with a maze of hallways, stairwells, and strange, dark rooms. The main room downstairs had a nice ambiance, but that's about where my enjoyment ended. The cover is relatively steep ($10 advance or $20 at the door). $20....really? The bathrooms were horrendous....especially for women since we have to sit on the nasty toilets. There was water everywhere, no dry toilet paper, and the seat was completely busted in one stall. The drink prices are a little steep, and the male bartender who served me was rude in a homophobic/misogynistic sort of way. Overall, the place has potential but the owners seem extremely greedy and negligent.

text: I came here based on Alexandra J's review below. I have no idea where Alex ate, but I don't think it was here. I got the chicken shawarma as my entree, and I couldn't eat it. It was a huge greasy pile of fatty grey chunks - I'm not even sure it was actually chicken. I guess to hide its nature, they chopped the "meat" into tiny little bits, almost like it was ground. The restaurant was deserted at noon, and I can see why. It would have been nice to have some music playing to fill the silence, but it was just strange and awkward. Mystery cigarette smoke kept drifting through the restaurant. No one was inside smoking, so I could only guess that it was coming from the kitchen. I can't believe I paid over $10 at lunch for something I wouldn't even eat. On the plus side, the lebna and microwaved (store-bought) pita bread was fine, and the house salad dressing was good. text: I had wanted to try the Cup for years but my friends in Tucson live on the other end of town and construction on the 10 was a deterrent. Recently, I met a friend there for dinner and while the meal was acceptable, it was nothing notable. But, breakfast. You always hear about breakfast at the Cup so this past weekend when we enjoyed a girls' overnight at Star Pass, I insisted on breakfast at the Cup since we were so close. We would have fared better at IHOP. We called around 9 a.m. to make a 10 a.m. reservation (if possible) and were told it would be closer to 11. Perhaps if their servers moved a little more quickly they could turn tables faster. The ambiance is so cute. Both times I was on the patio which is a narrow strip facing a parking lot but for some reason has character. After trying to let our server know we were on a bit of a schedule by suggesting we would want to order even before our sixth guest arrived, we were barely given the opportunity to order drinks. I desperately mouthed "can we please order?" to our server and still a few minutes passed before she actually came by for our selections. I had to ask for coffee refills and my water glass remained empty - I wound up drinking my friend's glass. It took nearly an hour to order and get our meals and no one even checked to see if we had what we needed once our food was delivered. I had an omelet and it was fine but the service was so dismal it sucked any enjoyment out of the meal. There are other restaurants where there are long waits (Matt's, Pizzaria Bianco) and I will gladly wait for memorable meals. There are places with sucky service (Orange Table) but, the food makes it impossible to vow never to return. Sadly, if I never go back to the Cup, I will not miss anything. And, I am so disappointed because I really wanted to like this place.
label: NEG

text: I have been to four locations. To sum up the experience in all four locations in a word, INDEFERENCE. This applies to the service and to the food. We were not going to go again, but a friend said that the service in the Oracle location was excellent. We arrived, the hostess did not greet until after she had seen us a couple of times. Then she took us to a table and walked off before we were even in our chairs. Chips came to the table but no wait staff. We left and no one noticed. We had stopped going because the food was mediocre at best and the servers didn't really seem to care if we got food or not. That's the last time we go to any location.

text: The dive bar of my dreams! This was the bar my fella and I kept coming back to during our week on Frenchmen Street, and usually where the tipping point from buzzed to drunk occurred. Great jukebox. Best of all: the barber chair is actually in use one night a week, when haircuts by Olivia cost $10 and come with a free shot. It would be hard for me to love it more.
label: POS

text: Out of all the burrito places in the area, this one is my favorite. The burritos are big and packed with deliciousness. They also have various other standard mexican food items, such as tacos and quesadillas, but I never really get any of those because the burritos are too good to pass up. They have a wide variety of burritos, and you can fill them with steak, chicken, or pork. There are two that are tied for my favorite: the queso burrito and the ancho chile barbecue burrito. The queso burrito is just what it sounds like, a burrito with delicious cheesy queso inside. I'm a big cheese fan and this burrito definitely satisfies. The barbecue burrito contains some sort of spicy mexican barbecue sauce that is packed with flavor. I was somewhat skeptical the first time I tried it, but it tastes great, especially when combined with the shredded pork. They have five different kinds of salsa. My favorites are roja (which is hot) and verde (which is medium). I haven't yet gotten up the guts to try the extra hot salsa, but now I think I'll have to try it the next time I stop in. I'll often stop by to quickly grab a burrito to take home for dinner after work, and the generally fast service makes it easy to do this. They assemble your burrito from the various ingredients while you watch, and they're pretty snappy about it. However, I occasionally happen to stop by during a busy time and have to wait in line, but it's never been a very long wait. My only real complaint is that occasionally the person who is making my burrito will be a bit stingy with the cheese. They'll usually give you more cheese if you ask (like I said, I love cheese) but sometimes they try to make you pay more for it. Come on, just give me a little more cheese. It costs them next to nothing and keeps me a happy and loyal burrito-buying customer. A minor complaint, but somewhat irksome at times. Overall, a great place to grab a tasty burrito, with a convenient location and generally quick service.

text: I like coffee shops. I study at them. I work in them. I hang out at them...way too much. I spend tons of my hard earned cash on coffee shops despite being able to brew a perfectly good cup at home. I consider myself a conniseur of the coffee shop. Bean Gallery disappoints me. Bean Gallery has terrible coffee. It's watery and lukewarm. The espresso is likewise not tasty and is expensive. The workers seem lost as to how to make a good espresso. The tea is good albeit expensive. The barista charges seem to be completely arbitrary. I don't think I ever pay the same price twice here. The cafe has many tables for studying and people turn it into a makeshift office during the day. In the morning there is a large crowd of regulars. They basically yell at each other when conversing. I've never heard people speak this loudly! One of the worst offenders has a dog that either smells terrible when he brings it inside or barks outside. The regulars usually yell to each other about local politics and news stories in the daily paper. I think it's really inappropriate. I think the regulars believe it's kitschy and cute. At night there are several tutors who meet with students on the big table. This can be a bit uncomfortable to be around and the tutors are loud. The shop features an array of used books that range from "Basics of Mechanical Engineering" to "A Guide on Planetary Leadership." The internet is so-so. It's not a bad place for study but it tends to get really loud. The morning and night regulars are pretty obnoxious about their decibel level. One of the biggest complaints I have about BG is that it's so dirty. Flthy!! It walks the line between yuppie shop and hippie shop, taking the worst of both worlds. Obnoxiousness and uncleanliness. The bathrooms scare me. I've seen worse, but these are just not acceptable for the caliber of shop this should be. The sanwhiches and food are pretty bad. They are delivered fresh daily but the quality is low. Ordering a sandwhich here made me regret not eating at one of the many other options nearby. Parking is all along the street. It's actually a little bit dangerous to avoid cars flying down Canal Street or turning down the road alongside the shop. The road by the shop is very narrow with cars parked on both sides. Cars turning from Canal are forced to speed across onto this street and go far too fast by the parked cars. Thus patrons exiting their cars in this area are in real danger of being hit. There is not a good solution to this problem other than avoiding parking on that street. I do like the mugs that are used in the coffee shop. But they are a bit dirty and do not make up for the many deficiencies. To-go cups are, as another reviewer pointed out, styrofoam. Whatever. This place has many other things it needs to address before the cups! Overall this is a usable coffeeshop but I live nearby and will drive elsewhere if I can spare the time. This shop has the bones of being a GREAT place, but it disappoints as is.

text: I've been a fan of the King Buffet for years. If not for the food, for the fact that it's just fun to eat, there. They've got an awesome selection of dishes to choose from, a complete salad bar, and even a children's food bar for those who aren't quite into their parents' ideas of good eating and apt to go batshit the entire time Mom and Dad are trying to enjoy their meal. The food's alright. But, being a buffet, you know it's not going to be as one might expect a restaurant serving fresher entrees would be. It's no worry, though, as the staff is seen regularly ferrying hotpans full of goodies to replace the depleted and, as there's always a decent amount of people around, what's under those heatlamps doesn't stay there long. Usually. There's always that one item, that day, that's not as popular as its brethren and you're left kind of wondering. But I've never had a complaint to offer toward their quality. It's just a fact that buffets of any sort anywhere share, that they're simply not going to be serving food as fresh as a traditional eatery. Some people are more sensitive to that than others. I could eat an egg sandwich left on my kitchen counter at home for nine weeks and barely suffer a burp while somebody else might go into convulsions after eating a lukewarm fry that's been out of the oil for slightly better than fifteen minutes. As it is an all-you-can-eat buffet, feel free to sample what you feel may be of dubious quality before lumping an effing ton if it onto your plate, find something you like, take it to your table, enjoy, and get on with your life. Don't be a pussy - take a chance. And have a good time. text: OOOoo I remember the first time going here and savoring every last piece of that scrumptious warm bread pudding! Back in the day, this place used to amaze me with its character, and this time it amazed my taste buds. Ordered: Popcorn Crawfish, Soft-shell crab, and the Bread Pudding! -Popcorn Crawfish- Tasty to snack on, but who can say no to fried and battered crawfish! And they don't joke around with crawfish, none of that "oh its actually shrimp," this looks straight from the Bayou. Douse it in a little Tabasco and pop it in! -Soft-shell crab- This was my first time with soft shell crab, and DAMN does it feel weird eating the whole crab but god does it taste good. The sides are a little generic and lack much flavor, as I felt the rice could have been seasoned better considering its Cajun food. -Bread Pudding with Whiskey Cream- You have to order at the beginning of your meal, but its sooo worth the wait. I was full from all the other food, but I ALWAYS have space for bread pudding from here! The cream adds that warmth that only whiskey provides into a soft bread pudding that you can finish so fast you'll forget that it was a MASSIVE dessert! Trust me, I'm not one to eat a lot, but this bread pudding is something your body will WANT to stuff inside! Additionally, the muffins are a tasty side, and I'm glad they don't charge you for eating each one like they used to! So try them all! The service is adequate, nothing spectacular, though expect delays on busy days! Overall, this is probably one of my favorite places to eat when coming home to Santa Barbara. So try something outside the typical mexican or italian of SB, go Cajun!

I felt it was well worth it for $25. They also have a $5 a glass wine deal on selected wines. text: I certainly adore this eatery. Allow me to employ my extensive research in the field to make a few recommendations for optimizing your Mama's experience: -Eat falafel. It's soft on the inside and crispy on the outside and rather delicately seasoned. -Most whole wheat pita is flat and tough and bitter, but not here. Go ahead and order it if you'd like to feel a little healthier by adding whole grains to your plateful of fried. -Don't skip the pickles at the salad bar. The olives are good too, but the pickles! -If you're the kind of person who never has enough tahini in your life, you can get an extra cup of it at the salad bar. -Add some fries if you're eating in; if you're picking up or getting delivery, skip 'em. If you happen to like your fries cold and extra soggy, strike that and reverse it. -Bring cash. Your ATM card will also suffice. -Don't even think about eating here on the Sabbath (even Friday afternoon is a roll of the dice) or on Jewish holidays. -If you want someone to bring your falafel to you, you'll want to call during an off-peak time. They don't have time for that stuff during the lunch rush. This last one is important. -Order hot sauce to liven things up, but unless you love the sensation of five-alarm fire in your mouth, ask them to take it easy. Otherwise, you're liable to end up with a few hot sauce-soaked bites at the end of your pita, and they will burn your face right off. I've warned you, now.

Some of my favorites are the short rib huarache, the ceviches, skirt steak nachos, and of course guacamole. Let me preface this by saying I am a guac-snob! I pride myself in my guacamole-which i insist on keeping basic and fresh. Not oversmashed, not over seasoned. And Distrito's guacamole impressed me. Super-fresh tasting and somehow creamy and chunky at the same time. This, I deducted was possibly because half of it is made into a creamy puree, and then chunks are added in (a method I've began to practice myself). Its also topped with cotija cheese-which i wish i could find in my local supermarket. Now-the margaritas are a bit pricey here. For about $40 a pitcher you're getting probably half as much as you'd get at a more casual mexican spot for $25. However, these are quality margs! Not super sugary or reminiscent of Hi-C with a kick of bottom-shelf tequila. This is worth the money. I highly recommend checking this place out during University City's Dining Days, where for $35 a person, you're definitely getting a lot of bang for your buck-and will feel less guilty about the $40 pitcher. Also, since they changed the whole first level to the "cantina" menu, its even more worth the trip to West Philly. Drinks and food for almost half the price of the main menu-and still all of the quality and a decent variety of selections! Wish I was there now!

text: I stopped in here with a friend because I read about their gluten free pizza menu online. My doctor recently recommended I go gluten free so I'm working on giving it a go. While the gluten free pizza menu was significantly more expensive than the regular pizza menu, that was quickly cleared up: they don't make the gluten free dough in house. Why? They make their gluten laden dough in house and can't guarantee against cross-contamination, so they buy the dough from a wholesaler. Obviously more expensive. The pizza was nicely thin crusted, as opposed to the other pizzas I saw leaving the establishment. It also had a crunch I rarely find in any pizza, but was delicious. We shared the Old time (old school, old way, something) pizza with pepperoni and it was so delicious. Also, it was the first time in a while that I had a meal at a restaurant that didn't make me want to throw up. I didn't feel sick at all eating this, sorta like my ramen/pho experiences, and completely opposed to my beyond bread meals that often made me ill immediately afterward. So, for the gluten free/celiac crowd out there: this is your joint. For someone like me, it was an eye-opening experience. Thankfully, a tasty one. The prices are a bit higher than at other places, but they use only recyclable materials (which are, frankly, more expensive) and high quality ingredients: generally organic veg, free-range (and hormone/antibiotic free) chicken, etc. All of that leads to higher base cost levels for a product. Because I appreciate their effort to both save the environment and my body, I'm willing to pay the price. But be forewarned: a 10" gluten free pizza can run you $19. If that's out of your budget, go to Sunflower and buy the gluten free pizza mix for $8.

text: I like my Sprint phone. I really do, and I'm not picking on this specific location here, but on Sprint in general. I got my Sprint phone about a year ago and get very good reception at reasonable rate on the family plan with my girlfriend. I NEVER talk on my cell, but I do send out a ton of texts, so we opted to go with the unlimited texting plan. Easy as that, no real problems for the next six months. So, about four months ago the girlfriend and I decide to upgrade our phones. Hers is getting really old (she had it for two years before we got on our plan) and mine was just always a total piece of crap. She gets a Katana and I get a Rumor. She bought her Katana at Radio Shack, so they called Sprint and switched the service over for her, whereas I ordered my phone online and waited a few days for it. When I call to activate my phone I talk to the ONLY nice person who's ever been employed by Sprint and she tells me that we're racking up a lot of text message overages that are costing us a lot of money. I explain to her that we have unlimited texting, we've always had unlimited texting, and no one's ever changed that. She takes a look at the account, reverses the charges, and re-adds the unlimited plan. I figure everything's okay. The next month when our phone bill is autopayed we get overcharged by $80. This is shortly before xmas, and right around rent time, so we really can't afford the extra money and we call to see what's up. Now, I work in a call center and I'm extremely polite to fellow phone jockeys, but these people had me nearly to the point of screaming profanities. The first guy I talk to sounds like he's high on weed and cough syrup. He tells me that, yes he sees the problem, yes it's clearly their fault, but no, he can't do anything to help me. I ask him to transfer me to someone who can, so he puts me on hold for a little over five minutes. Finally a woman answers the phone who's that special kind of irritable that implies to me that she just quit smoking, is on the rag, and just found out her baby daddy is cheating with her cousin. She tells me she can apply the credit to next months bill, but there's no way she can credit it back to my card. She implies that to do so would require some sort of wacky technology that a humble multi-billion dollar company like Sprint wouldn't possibly have access to. I ask for a supervisor. Yay! Another ten minutes on hold! A supervisor picks up and tells me I have to talk to a different department. I wait on hold about five minutes for that department, and then they tell me I have to talk to customer service. I tell them that's who I was just talking to, but they don't care and transfer me anyway. At this point I just want to get off the phone before I hurt somebody, so I just agree to the credit and triple check that my phone does indeed have unlimited text messaging. I'm told it's all taken care of. Guess what happens when I get my next bill? Guess!!!! Yep, fifty dollars in text message overages. WTF? I call before the bill goes through this time and get it reversed, have them re-add the service for the third time, and take my bill the hell off of auto-pay so I can look at it before they take my money. Oh, and somehow they've charged me for six ringtones I've never downloaded over the course of the past year as well. If you're looking for a new cell phone carrier, look somewhere else!

text: When I was looking for someone to help me out with a local move in the peninsula/south bay, I had no idea where to start. Just relocated to the bay area from Chicago last fall for a new job, had some stuff in storage in San Jose, and was staying with a family member while I looked for my own place. When the time came this spring to make the move, I went right to Yelp and was impressed with what I read about Go Pro. Suffice it to say, they did not disappoint. Spoke with Sean on a Friday afternoon, had a very pleasant conversation, and had an estimate via email within an hour or so. This was followed up by an email confirmation the following Monday. The day of the move, Friday, I got a call to say that they were running a little late for our 12-1p start time. However, when I finally met the 2 guys at my storage space near SJ Airport around 2:15p they were already at my 10'x10' unit, supplies out and ready to go. They provided wardrobes, wrapped furniture in plastic, and had padding/blankets as well. Despite an initial estimate of 3 hours, the total move time was 1.5 hours and the move came in almost $100 under the original estimate. While the move began later than expected, it also finished earlier due to the efficiency of the crew. They even set up my king size bed without my asking - which I had not expected them to do - and were tipped well as a result. I highly recommend Go Pro and would definitely use them again should I require moving services in the future. A very pleasant experience all around.

text: This annual June event celebrating Indian jewelry, art and food turns out large crowds. First, the good: Lots of jewelry vendors offer tons of variety, from Santa Fe and New Mexico flavored pieces to bright, chunky tribal ones. Necklaces, door chains, bracelets, earrings, even beaded purses and more can be found here. One unusual piece that was just out of my price range (at $500!) was a gorgeous eagle carved out of bone or ivory on a circular metal necklace. Now the bad: The Eiteljorg's parking lot is not open to festivalgoers, despite the fact that they're the ones hosting the event and it's a $10 charge to enter. Further, the food offerings are more Hoosier than Hopi--the closest thing to Native American cuisine here was the beef jerky sold in the gift shop. I'm joking--a little. Indian Fry Tacos were sold, but they make use of flour and lard, ingredients introduced to Native Americans via the U.S. government following a forced expulsion during the Trail of Tears. One Mexican vendor sold some delicious tamales, which have their roots in Indian cuisine. All the other ice cream and regular fried foods on a stick were regular state fair food. Hope next year's food offerings will be more authentic.

text: I've been to the Habit a few times, twice at this location, and it's a solid place to grab a burger. The burger is bigger and pricier than In-N-Out's, but smaller and cheaper than a restaurant burger. The quality is pretty decent, and it tastes great. If you want fries and a drink, the combination meals are the way to go. You can get a Single or Double Charburger with fries and a drink for $5.95 or $6.95. Cheese costs an extra $.50, bacon $.75, and avocado $1. I've had the Single Charburger with cheese and avocado, and it was delicious. The Charburger consisted of a chargrilled patty with mayo, pickle, lettuce, tomato, and carmelized onions on a toasted bun. The patty was thin but surprisingly loaded with deep meaty flavor. All the additions added a nice vegetable freshness and crunch, and the avocado was easily worth the extra buck. It integrated perfectly into the burger with its pleasant creamy texture and healthy fat. The Habit's fries were addictive, with a good level of crispiness, and the Single Charburger meal was very satisfying. I also enjoyed the Teriyaki Charburger, which in addition to the mayo and vegetable spread of the regular Charburger came with grilled pineapple and a dripping teriyaki sauce. This burger might not be for those who prefer a straight-up cheeseburger, but I thought it was fantastic. The sweetness of both the pineapple and the sauce was well-rounded and went well with the hefty dose of vegetables and meat. The burger was messy, but so was the regular Charburger, and I did not mind. There's a Habit near my house that I've been to once, but I think it may be time to make a return visit. I like this downtown Santa Barbara location, though, with its pleasant outdoor seating and easy take-out window. It's a great casual spot for a tasty meal.

text: This place has a restaurant and a bar section - and you can't cross between them without going outside, which is a little weird. I've eaten in the restaurant a couple times, and it's good, but nothing special. I remember enjoying it, but nothing sticks out in my mind. More often I'd be in the sports bar area, which is fun and laid back. There are a decent number of tables available to sit at, eat, and enjoy the place with your friends without actually having to sit up by the bar. But the main highlight - Table Shuffleboard. Ok, I don't know the real name for it, but that seems to fit. And everything I know about it, I learned from a stallion handler named Jim. If you're there, and you see a guy with white hair over by the table, hanging out with some younger folk who seem like they might be veterinarians and veterinarians-to-be, you should go say hi. Jim's the best! Table Shuffleboard is like shuffleboard, but on a table. Stop me if I'm going too fast for you. That would be hard, since this was written in full before you're reading it, but I'm sure you could make the effort. So there's 'sand' (actually perfectly round silicon beads - thanks, Jim!) on the table which help the discs glide across the table. The goal is to get your discs as close to the other edge without falling off, and keep your opponent from having any discs that reach beyond yours. If you're into the Olympics, think curling without the brooms. And a rectangular playing field. And an edge instead of a bullseye. Ok, don't think curling. It's really quite simple to understand. To blatantly rip off the slogan for the great game of 'Othello' - 'A minute to learn, a lifetime to master.' Pizza! Root beer! Real beer! Shuffleboard! Stallion handlers! There's always something fun to do in Kennett Square.
label: POS

text: NOOOODLES!!!!!!!!! IN SOOOUUUUP!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! My favorite thing in the world! First lunch in Philly and first official food stop on Philly food crawl brought us through an especially animated Chinatown (4th of July apparently makes us Chinese break out the....Dragon dance? Chinese operas? Cooking demos????). Ten minutes of politely wending through the crowds and we finally made it in here. The boyfriend and I are avid noodle soup fans and he was just plain delighted by the opportunity to watch real noodle-makers making noodles...by hand! I love this place for being so Taiwanese. The staff speak Taiwanese Mandarin, they serve pickled vegetables on top as garnish the way only Taiwanese people do and the menu has a big emphasis on beef noodle soups. Ahhh! I'm in Taiwan heaven! I got the beef brisket and the boy got the sliced beef. Now, you have to understand that beef noodle soup is the comfort food, the slice of pizza, the pint of Ben & Jerry's, the mac 'n' cheese of Taiwanese cuisine. And just like those wonderful items, beef noodle soup can come in many forms. At its most unhealthy, it is thick and hearty, spicy and slightly greasy with fatty chunks of tender beef. That's my favorite version of it. But I am not averse to its more healthful cousin. The light, almost clear, flavorful broth, the low-fat cuts of beef, the healthy spinach, the utter lack of grease or spice of any kind. This is what Nan Zhou serves. And it's so delicious. It's like chicken soup for the soul. The Taiwanese soul. And I can't believe it's under $6 for a piping hot bowl of this. Oh God, I wish I could bring this restaurant back to Boston!

text: We always have a good time at City House, though we never go on any night but Sunday. Sunday is the chef's night to do what he likes, and the restaurant takes the opportunity to regale its patrons with all manner of "pork snacks." As a lover of all things pork and a celebrator of the noble swine, Sunday at City House is my favorite. And since most other notable restaurants in town don't stay open for dinner on Sunday nights, City House has carved itself a niche not only for interesting uses of offal, but as one of the only places where one can get a decent meal on Sunday evenings. So last night, we went in and had a lovely time. For starters, I was especially intrigued by the Mortadella "corndogs," which, in point of fact, were actually more like lollipops than corndogs. Either way, they were spectacular: battered and fried crispy, the mortadella (made with peanuts in lieu of the usual pistachios) was tasty and stood in for the hot dog easily, and the housemade mustard was heavenly. Each bite was a blend of crunchy, fatty, tangy deliciousness. The low point of the meal (though not that low) was the pork belly, which was served with garlicky broccoli rabe. The belly was roasted, but was very fatty, rendering it more of a textural accompaniment to the rabe than anything else. Tasty, but a little off the mark. I would have preferred it less gelatinous, but if it's what the chef intended, it's what he intended. For mains, Husband went with the Kitchen Pie. He always goes with the Kitchen Pie. Surprisingly simple, it's basically a cheese pizza, but done up with chili oil in addition to the sauce and Grana Padano cheese, a cousin of Parmigiano Reggiano. It's very flavorful and the chili gives it an unexpected bite. I went with one of the nightly specials, the pork meatballs, served with a rich, yet thin, tomato ragu, and a large piece of cheese and garlic toasted bread in lieu of pasta. The meatballs were gigantic and cooked perfectly, herbs throughout. As I've stated in my reviews before, I can't eat much wheat in my diet, but I did try some of the bread as it was so tempting: crunchy and wonderful, and when sopping up the ragu, perfect. For dessert, I always get the "Lemon Thing." It never seems to fail, everytime we go in, there's a lemon-related dessert on the menu. I don't know who their pastry chef is, but he or she is a genius with lemon. Last night was a lemon and almond pound cake with a side of lemon sorbet. Sweet and crunchy, the cake was delicious: I almost forgot to share a bite with husband. Husband's dessert was a chocolate torta with peanut butter sauce. It was good, but not as good as the "Lemon-Thing." All in all, the meal was great.

text: I really, really wanted to like this place. In fact, it pains me to give it only 2 stars. The guy is not only a local legend and a national celebrity, but he lives in my spice cupboard, or at least his face does under the guise of "seafood magic" (wonderful seasoning btw). No one in the city has anything bad to say about him, and why would they? He pretty much single-handedly introduced a culture and cuisine to the rest of the world that had gone unappreciated much too long. And I am sure that at one time, when K-Paul's was still the no-reservation divey hole-in-the-wall with a line out the door, it was THE place to go in NOLA. But now . . . well, you see my stars. Here's why: the renovations with the white-tablecloth decor and high prices do not match with the food (in both quality and presentation) or with the service (felt like I was in a diner).There's a certain expectation when you pay $20-$35 an entree with your white wine and tablecloth and that expectation wasn't met. If, on the other hand, I was sitting at a formica table chugging a beer, being served by a gum-snapping waitress and paid half as much, I would've been very, very satisfied. Here's what we had: - Gumbo: I had gumbo probably 5 times while I was there, and K-Paul's was the worst. It was dark and oversalted. - Fried green tomatoes w/ shrimp remoulade: I actually liked this a lot. - Alligator sausage: Kinda like K-Paul's itself -- it was okay but at least now I can say I've tried it. - Blackened catfish: This was very, very good. I would recommend it. - Etouffee: It was pretty good. - Fried drum: It was okay. - Fried soft shell grab: It was okay. At this point, all the breading started tasting the same. - Bread pudding: Very good. - Sweet potato pecan pie: Good but not great. So overall, the food was just okay or even slightly below average. The presentation was terrible, but again, I wouldn't have cared if it weren't for the nicer setting and fine-dining level prices. Same with the service -- not very good given the enivronment. Am I glad I went? Sort of, because now I can say I've been, and sometimes as a tourist, that's all you really want. But as a tourist who during her visit was most looking forward to the food, I was severely disappointed.

That's about all that's really excellent with this place. I've always been disappointed in this place...and I only go when my co-workers and friends drag me here. The salads are always drenched with a Greek dressing that is actually too tangy for my palate. The gyros, while inexpensive, are smaller than one would expect. I love gyros...and the Turkish and Greek ones you get in Europe are huge...I always feel like they are as big as my head, and it's always a feat to finish them. Not so here. In addition, occasionally the meat itself is cold and unappetizing and the onions are too raw for my taste. They are really nothing like the authentic ones you can get in Europe. The chili, which I got to taste at the Chili Cook-Off, is pretty decent though...but I wouldn't have given it the placement that the judges did...there were better chilis out there. Finally , service, while well-intentioned, is also pretty slow.
label: NEG

text: This might have been the worst purchase I made in 2009. I ordered an arrangement of gerberas for the ladyfriend. In fact, it was a day late. And they didn't follow my instructions. Deliver to the door, not at the front desk of the apartment complex. So they arrive, and behold! They were not the flowers I picked. Also, they were placed in a standard clear glass vase, the exact opposite of what I had chosen. A note was supposed to come with them. Negative on that ordeal. And then, before the next day, the gerberas were withering! Next time, I'll just make a trip to Reading Terminal or something to buy flowers. And you know, it doesn't help when a business is run by people who barely speak English. I'm all for immigration and whatnot, and I'm not one of those jerks who yell to Mexicans to speaka engalish, but since I didn't have my book of Mandarin with me (I don't have one, that's the joke), it was difficult to get my point across when I ordered the flowers at first. The purchase was bound to failure at that moment, when communication was just...difficult. I'm sorry, but in a place of business, you should be able to communicate with your customers...

text: For starters, I've actually never liked Gyro's before this experience. My mind has completely changed! I also tried a little bit of the donor kabab which had everyone raving on Yelp. They weren't lying! Everything was absolutely delicious. We had some fries on the side and those were tasty as well, though it was the gyro that I was excited about. Everything on the menu was pretty cheap, but I'm glad people mentioned the fact that they don't take credit cards so I could grab some cash before heading over there. It's a small restaurant, so I wouldn't bring a big group unless you planned on taking it to go. What a wonderful find!!! I'm excited to go back sometime to try more of their dishes and desserts!!

text: My trips to St. Louis have not been overly positive, and I don't honestly get too excited about the prospect of spending time here. The Inn itself is British style- all heavy dark wood, deep red patterned carpeting, fireplaces and rustic old world charm. Bits and pieces feel 1970s about it, but that's true of rural England as well, isn't it? Particularly 1970s are the fantasy suites! Rooms with mirrored ceilings and hot tubs- decorated King Arthur style, how do you beat that!?! My standard room was clean and vintage and cheap- with easy access to the highway and a lively seen at the hotel bar, this place was the perfect quick stop in St. Louis- after a long drive on the road, this crazy place was just perfect!

text: I love all pizza. Thick, thin, regular, gourmet, you name it. They all have their virtues. For regular thin crust pizza (not a cracker, just regular) you can find better in St. Louis than that at Pi. It's good, but Racanelli's is still king in that area. However, when it comes to deep dish I'm officially in love. In general, it's fair to say this is very good "Chicago Style" pizza. That said, for those of you who have ever had Zachary's Pizza out of Berkeley you'll immediately recognize it as a very close cousin. And since Zachary's is the best pie in the entire bay area (in my opinion, and those of most publications) that's saying a lot. The cornmeal crust, and the rustic sauce set just the right tone. Personally, I think ordering the specialty pizzas a waste of time and tastebuds (too much crap to take away from the actual pizza) so I tend to only get 1 or 2 toppings max. Therefore I can't really comment on their signature pizzas. I noticed the whole 'green' thing on the servers shirts, but to be honest never felt like I was being beat over the head with the sustainability message like some of the other reviewers. (unlike the motor home across the street emblazoned with its humorous vegetarian messages) As for the "garlic bread". I could sit down to that every day of my life. Before it was the Roadhouse, Ella Forcellis used to provide whole roasted garlic cloves in a similar way, but otherwise it's a difficult thing to find around here. Which is a shame because it's cheap, easy, and oh so delicioso. And at $4? Uno mas, por favor. The salad was also very good ($6) but was left unfinished for the fear that I would use up some of the stomach room that the garlic bread might need. A large deep dish will feed roughly 4 people (at 2 slices each) and if I recall correctly was $18. So with non-alcoholic drinks, a large pie, and an appetizer for the table you can easily feed 4 in the $30-$40 range. Which considering it's a slightly upscale joint, has tableside service, real napkins, sustainable ingredients, and oh yeah...is awesome, etc, etc. that's pretty good (not much different than a trip to Racanelli's or Dewey's). Parking was a bitch, but not unusual for the area.

text: Zinburger is a great wine and burger place- a Fox restaurant concept. I don't eat beef, so I was a bit weary when a bunch of co-workers suggested Zinburger- the logo includes a cow! I thought the combination sounded odd, but it actually worked out well. I also added jalapenos which gave it a good kick. I noshed on the truffle fries as an appetizer and despite being described as super flavorful- I wouldn't completely agree. They are solid as fries go, but not mind blowing. The menu organizes their wine by how much it cost per glass. They also do this at True Food (in PHX) and I think it makes ordering wine for people who aren't total pro's a lot less stressful. I ordered the $5 Malbec and ended up having two glasses. The first night, I would have totally given Zinburger a five star, but it was demoted to a four star upon my second visit. Our service the first night was pretty much perfect, however, the second evening, I had to ask for my water to be refilled several times (a personal pet peeve, I will admit). I'll make it a point to return to Zinburger for that delicious turkey burger every time I'm in Tucson! Supposedly the veggie burger is also amazing, although i couldn't pull myself away from the turkey on these two visits. So, non beef eaters, check it out regardless of the cow logo!

text: I don't know how else you would be able to fly out of New Orleans' Louis Armstrong Airport without Park 'N Fly. Seriously, do you pay the $40 cab ride each way? Do you make your friends schlep you over and then pick you up? Do you take a hovercraft? Even if you did, where would you park that thang? See, you do need Park 'N Fly! I know, me too. Since the airport is not actually in nola, but over in Kenner, it is necessary to drive to be able to fly out of good ol Louis Armstrong (MSY). Park 'N Fly makes all that very simple. You go online and book your reservation, pay online by card, and then drive over. It is right on the way to the airport, off the highway, on the left. You park your own car and then a shuttle picks you up and takes you right over to the airport- just down the street. The drive takes less than two minutes and you know your car is safely waiting for you when you get back. You keep your keys so you know no one's messing with your vehicle. Upon arrival back at MSY just grab the shuttle, get in your car, and pass them your reservation info (which you printed out) while driving away. There's even a frequent parkers pass that just means when you park eight days you get one free day. So simple! Parking prices are not outrageous either. Would definitely get more stars if the parking spots were not so close together- every time i'm terrified my car will get bashed by the person parking next to me (it's never happened). The ladies there always show me some southern charm, calling me baby and whatnot, which is nice because i'm usually a ball of tears when leaving my family and flying back to Louisiana. I don't know what I'd do without Park 'N Fly.

text: Event: Green Day 8/3/10 The concert itself was excellent - Green Day always is. But I'm here to review the venue for those who can't find info elsewhere . . . We came over from PA, and arrived at 4 to tailgate for a 7pm show. There were many others who had already arrived, so the lots must have opened at 3 or earlier. We parked in Lot 1, by the Will Call window to the stadium. The $25 parking fee is a ridiculous rip off, and I would consider taking the ferry next time. I had 4 straight teens with me (16 & 17 y.o.) who had never tailgated. It was a great experience. We hauled an EZ Up tent with us, but you are not permitted to use them there. We grilled dinner and played games in the lot. The Camden police cruised through several times while we were there, and it felt quite safe. There was a lot of drinking going on, but none near us (I picked a quiet spot) and no one was out of control. Getting out of the lots is insane. There was one gate each for the two lots, and they combine to dump onto one little exit road. You would think they purposely do this to slow things down - - and slow it is. Allow at least an hour to get out of there for a big event. The venue itself was fine, but the will-call lines were miles long. We had lawn seats and, once in, found that the entire bottom center of the hill was all dirt! The dirt was completely covered with grass seed - ewwww. Thank goodness we had a blanket to sit on, because it was gross. Had it been raining . . . it would have been a huge mess. Note to the facilities guys: ZOYSIA GRASS PLUGS this fall and lots of 'em - hello??!! We were allowed to bring in 1 water bottle each, but had to remove the lids (potential projectiles). We did so to avoid the outrageously expensive food and drink prices at the Center. Worked out fine, we had our desert and snacks in the parking lot after the show, giving it time to calm down a bit before we left. Still had to wait in lines to get out, but not as bad. Footnote - We had killed my car battery prior to the show by listening to music a bit too long. When I came out, I waited less than 2 mins. before a police cruiser came along. I flagged them down and asked for help - they were as nice as can be. They sent another officer to find me in the parking lot, and he brought me a hot box so I could jump myself. Elapsed time from exiting the stadium to receiving help -- 6 minutes! Thank so much Camden Police - you were awesome. All in all, the venue has work to do on the inside, LOTS of work to do about their parking vendor(s) and traffic situation, and doesn't come close to competing with the Philly venues.

The waitress happened to be wandering by with coffee pots in her hand when we sat down, so we had a full cup quickly. This was not the case, however, to receive menus. We placed our order, and I finished my coffee. Then I waited...and waited...and finally flagged down the waitress for another cup. Maybe she was busy...she did have two other tables to take care of...(yes, that WAS sarcasm). My water finally was refilled as I was finishing my meal. Anyway, on to the food. It was pretty good - I had a salmon omelet, and the hubby had a caribou sausage omelet. Both did not scrimp on the fillings - they were tasty. The hash browns were a little underdone, but since we had gotten there after 1pm, I'm sure any kind of rush they experienced was long over. Last impressions mean a lot, too - hubby had to go to the server station to pay the bill...again, our server seemed super busy gabbing with her co-workers. Needless to say, her tip reflected our appreciation. Not sure if we'll be back - but it's nice to have an option so close to home.

text: First, I am kind of shocked I am the first to review this establishment. Second, I am REALLY shocked I haven't reviewed it yet, since I practically lived here the first 6 months of my son's life. I am OVERALL not a fan, but for convenience, I have limited baby shopping options. Buy Buy Baby is the shit and I would spend ALL my money there if I could, but it is well over an hour away and if you have read any of my other reviews, you know I don't like to drive much further than 3 miles to get somewhere....so even BRU is out of my way. BRU has the basics and a lot of crap you do NOT need or will EVER need for your child. Everything is comparable to what you would get anywhere else, but it does tend (from what i have heard) to be more expensive than Wal-mart (but that is one devil store I refuse to shop). For registering, I think it's a must do, b/c BRU is everywhere and Buy Buy Baby is still building their name and don't have nearly as many locations. The plus side about BRU is that everyone has heard of it and it's a trusted name...the downside is that it is a "trusted" name and generally is a terrible store. The staff is not well educated in products. They only (barely) know how to run the cash register. The return policy is outrageously annoying (SPECIAL TIP FOR ALL THOSE REGISTERING: Put everything you might never want on your registry and if you want, take it back for an in store credit. If it's NOT on your registry and you have no receipt. they will not give you any sort of credit. If you receive something that is not on your registry, you can EDIT it before you go into the store and get the credit, but if you don't, you are SOL). This is all a lot of information for a pregnant girl and seemingly unnecessary in my opinion. What is wrong with having a flexible policy especially for new moms?!?! Everything is difficult enough...by all means, make it as un-user friendly as possible. BRU's rewards program is also bunk. Supposedly the more you spend, the more coupons and treats you get. Not so much! It's just another way to over-spam your email account. Options are FAIRLY limited. Don't expect to find the likes of more upscale baby accessories like the Bugaboo or Uppa Baby Vista. They only carry more typical name brands....and typically extremely cheap product as well. That all being said, they have much of what you want/need. While the store may be disorganized and their staff is indifferent and useless, if you are in there long enough, you'll keep them in business and probably find what you are looking for. Yes, I keep going back, but only b/c my options are so limited in the Indy area....and I continually receive BRU gift cards which I cannot exchange for cash (dammit!).

text: All Anthropologies are nice. This one has character. It even has a grand staircase. The Anthropologie building has a spiral staircase leading to many levels. The displays are lovely from chalkboards with tea cup images built out of chalk to tables of wedges and coffee table books to tickle your fancy. The shirts and dresses are hanging on racks with space to breathe. The only spot where everything was crowded was in the basement sale area. I'll rummage through any sale. That's how you get the best deals. My $10 slacks were found on Rockefeller Center but here on Walnut I found the cutest bird shaped dispenser. I won't use it to hold food. I'm going to display it as a pop of color in my room. Plus the bird's bright yellow whistling face makes me happy. Anthropologie is the type of store that will make you ponder purchasing a $30 headband, inspire you to wear a French frock, and even turn you on to quilted blankets when clearly you are into silk. I love Anthropologie and I am in love with this location. They have an elevator with a couch in it. A couch! I thought secret couches were limited to Nordstrom bathrooms. text: A wealthy friend introduced me to Rescue about 5 years ago. I've gone every couple of months for every service they offer except massage. It's best described as an urban spa, which means exactly that. Do not expect a series of rooms to chill in the dark before and after the service. The space is dressed in white and is quietly and appropriately busy. Generally, it delivers what it promises to deliver. For those coming from the West Coast and all of its water-centric Asian spas and onsens, you will find none of it here. It's taken me years to find a Korean spa nearby and I drive 45 min to get to it. For facials, I really like Monica. Like Danuta (the owner) and Nives (the make-up and brow tech), Monica is originally from Eastern Europe. She does a very, very good job. I have my first appt with Danuta in March (she is usually booked months in advance) and have high expectations for the results. For waxing, I like Tirzah. I've had waxes with every person on staff I think. Recently, I've noticed that when I get a Brazilian, I actually have to ask them to do anything "in the back." What's happening here? Isn't that what differentiates a regular bikini wax from a Brazilian wax? I really don't want to have to *ask* for it. Like, ever. I've had my eyebrows shaped (not waxed; I break out) by Nives and Erica. Nives has a fabulous sense of style and her make up application is worth paying for, just to learn what's what. I came in a couple of times for brows, and she did an amazing job, commanding my brows to grow in and reshape themselves. 6 months later, Erica essentially destroyed what Nives had done. I will not go back to Erica. For nails, the only tech I like is Anna Maria. She's really good. My only gripe is that the benches are not comfortable to sit on, but I think they've just remodeled that space. Going for a pedicure in February, so we'll see.

text: I'd been here twice before and I dig their happy hour (except that they admittedly water down their margaritas. grrr), but lunch today was frustrating. Here's what their lunch menu insert looks like: "Served with beans, rice, and guacamole -Chile relleno -2 taquitos -Camarones empanizados -Enchiladas Served with rice and tortillas -4 -other -things -here Served with something somethign and vegetables -4 -other -things -here" I saw this menu and saw the first column of stuff and went YES. RICE BEANS AND GUACAMOLE. I WANT THOSE SO BAD. I wanted the side dishes more than anything else, so when I picked the entree it was almost arbitrary. I picked the shrimp. I didn't even care, I was more interested in the "beans, rice and guacamole" the menu said came with it. AWESOME. My boyfriend ordered from the same column, the taquitos. When we ordered, I proudly declared I wanted the shrimp, and that I wanted the green rice (they have red too. Just clarifying for the waitress). She nodded and took my boyfriend's order and then came back to me to ask "mumblemumble rice?" "Green rice!" I said back, all excited for this carb-fest I was about to get. And then it came. With just rice. 4 breaded shrimp and no beans, no guacamole. My boyfriend's taquitos (from the same 'served with' heading) DID come with beans and guacamole and a bunch of sour cream and 2 kinds of cheese that the menu didn't mention, which sucks for him because he hates cheese and sour cream. I went 'wait wait doesn't this come with beans and guacamole?' Waitress: "I asked if you wanted beans or rice and you said 'green rice' ". Me: "The menu said it comes with both." Waitress: "No. Just rice." She left and I felt like I couldn't argue, because she had kinda looked at me like I was a snotty bitch, but my friend ran and grabbed a menu to prove to me that I was right and I should argue. Then she came back and we showed her the menu and she just responded with "Do you want guacamole?" YES SILLY I WANT GUACAMOLE AND BEANS LIKE ON THE MENU. She did bring me some guacamole, but no beans, so I ate my boyfriend's because they were covered with cheese. Then he was still hungry so I gave him my shrimp. Here's the run-down basically: Either the menu is inaccurate or the waitress was really dumb The portions were less than fair for being in the $9 range. If you don't like cheese/crema or you're allergic or something, you should ask about it. The menu will simultaneously lie about what it will give you (cheese and sour cream) and what it won't (beans and guacamole). And I don't think it was a language barrier either, because in Spanish "incluye frijoles, arroz y guacamole" would still mean it came with all 3. I'm mad at you, Palapa.
label: NEG

text: I was a member of LA Fitness for about four years, only in another (smaller) location. When I moved to a new area, the Cherry Hill location was more than happy to transfer my membership over. I was thrilled; the gym had more amenities than my prior LA Fitness, such as racquetball courts, an Olympic-sized swimming pool (with aqua sports classes), and twice the amount of equipment available. I was also told that with my membership, I had a few guest passes each year to give to people who wanted to come with me to work out. Every time I brought a guest, the guest passes were never honored. In fact, no matter who was in charge, I was told that there was no such thing as guest pass, and that my guests would either have to pay $15 to work out that day, or go through about a half-hour of a gym tour, meet with a salesperson to assess what membership may work for them, and make a commitment that day to join the gym - or else they can't work out. When I moved out of the area, I canceled my membership with LA Fitness, and joined a new gym in my new state. I was a frequent visitor to my old digs, though, and decided to return to this LA Fitness, using an actual paper guest pass that was provided to a long-time member. Of course, when I arrived, I was given the same song and dance that guest passes don't exist. When I presented my "LA Fitness Guest Pass", I was rushed into a separate area where I was questioned for a long time. I explained I did not live there, but the rep didn't listen. I then made the mistake of telling the representative that I was once a member of that very LA Fitness. I was escorted out. Apparently, once you quit, you either sign up for another membership, or you don't go in there at all. With that knowledge, I returned a few months later to work out and told the person in charge that day that I just want to pay the money, not meet with anyone, and go work out. I was told there was no change for a $20 bill. This has happened MANY times. Sometimes the people in charge are so perplexed by the fact that I come in armed with $15 to pay (and not sit through a sales meeting) that they just let me work out for free because they have no idea what to do with me. Generally, I get the strange feeling that something a little weird is going on behind the scenes there, and unless you plan on staying with LA Fitness for the rest of your gym-going career, perhaps you should look at a gym that has similar amenities but is more managerially sound. If the point of a guest pass is to introduce potential new members to their services, why make guest passes such a tumultuous process? I was just looking to work out for a day, but for every person like me who comes in with no strings attached, there's about five people who actually are shopping around for gyms. Maybe like you are. And from a former member turned guest, I can tell you, it's not really worth it.

text: City Diner is another old established eatery in South St. Louis just one block south of Tower Grove Park. The atmosphere is definitely from the '50s & '60s, and the background music proves it. I had 2 eggs, hash browns, sausage, wheat toast & of course coffee. All of this for a mere $5.40 not including the tip. CHEAP. However, I asked for my eggs "over-easy" and they came out next to "over-hard". I sent them back. On the other hand, the server was always there to top off the coffee. Friday & Saturday they are open 24 hours. Normal hours are Mon. - Thur. 7 AM to 11 PM. Tuesday evenings feature 1950s prices from 5 PM to 9 PM. How does $3.99 for dinner sound? Naturally, non-specials run quite a bit higher, but not outrageous. For example: City Diner Meatloaf, $8.50 served with home-made mashed potatoes, gravy and choice of vegetable. Or, 1/2 Smoked Chicken $9.50 smoked in-house to a rosy hue, served with your choice of potato and vegetable. All-in-all, I'll probably go there again. text: We looked forward to The Landing because friends in the area recommended it, but they were as disappointed as we were. First, we were met by no fewer than five hostesses, several of whom were clad in Daisy Dukes, tank tops and flip flops. We pondered why so many girls were being paid to stand at the front and sip Dunkin' Donuts coffee coolers, but were unable to come to a consensus. Arranging two tables to accommodate four adults and three kids (all under age 4) took several staffers a few minutes, but they had fun shouting insults at each other and sharing tales of last night's adventures. The Landing has no high chairs, so we balanced the youngest baby on our laps. The food was poor overall. The gazpacho, (perfect for a hot day, right?) had grapes and canned pineapple in it. It was bizarre and inedible, but the server removed it from our tab. On the plus side, two of our friends enjoyed chicken wraps very much. The pear salad had a very heavy dressing. The kids' grilled cheese sandwiches were doughy and barely cooked. My one year old ate the beets and pear from my salad but wouldn't touch the sandwich. We asked for more iced tea and the server said, "I have to charge you for another bottle." I'm no restauranteur, but wouldn't it be cheaper to brew a big pot of iced tea than to stock bottles of the stuff? Service was slow and inaccurate, with the teenaged wait staff laughing and shouting at each other over diners' heads. They can't be blamed, really. We never saw a manager type appear, so they're probably just in need of supervision, training and a dress code. To top it all off, we were hit with an 18% gratuity because our party was more than six (we had seven.) We'd pay it without complaint if the service was good, but had trouble stomaching it considering that three of our diners are one, one and three years old! We ordered food for them, so I guess I can see it, but it was hard to fork it over when we were tempted to tip nada. There are several other cute places in New Hope. We wished we'd gone to Triumph Brewing Company instead.

text: Now before anyone gets glove slapping, let me say this place will most likely garner five stars after a few more successful visits. A fantastic variety of sushi is worth the short drive from downtown Philly to this quiet, elegant restaurant in Haddonfield. It's a BYO, so pick up a favorite Sake or bottle o'vino on the way. I started with the baby octopus, lightly roasted and tender, the taste was reminiscent of bacon with the smoky, rich flavor that was pulled out of these tiny tasty treats. Fresh Live Abalone!! OMG yes please. I'm fairly certain this is one of the only places in the area that serves this. Crunchy yet tender, nutty and sweet., wow. Fresh live scallop? Sweet as candy. Kumomoto oysters are fresh and served with a lovely mignoette interpretation. Crab cocktail was filled with huge pieced of crab, super fresh, perfectly cooked. Not a hint of anything but firm meaty goodness. The white tuna ceviche was crazy good. grapefruit wedges separated slices of white tuna. A sprinkle of crunchy fleur de sel was on top of each wedge of grapefruit, a small sliver of jalapeno on top of each slice of fish. with a very light citrus drizzle. This dish was amazing, and I would never have thought to salt grapefruit, it worked perfectly, and the light pop of the jalapeno was a great burst of green on your palate. Sunomono is served in multiple styles, I went with the simple cold version, which had the lovely addition of udon noodles. Crisp light flavors were a perfect interlude on this hot June evening. Two white tuna handrolls were served in nori so fresh it crackled and shattered in your mouth. I can't remember the last time I've had food this fresh short of Morimoto or Nobu. Our final dish this evening was a shashimi plate for two that was crazy good. Salmon so rich the thin slivers of lemon were practically a mandatory addition to prevent the richness from overwhelming your palate. Yellowtail that still tasted of the sun and sea. Amazing fish. So why not five stars? Three reasons. First, I asked for a bottle of water for the table. I received a soda glass with a straw. My guest received nothing, and had to order his own separate serving. When my glass was empty, it was not refilled, even when I slid it to the edge of the table to clearly indicate I wanted more. By the time staff returned to acknowledge the glass, I was done eating. Second, while we were there, a family in shorts and tshirts arrived. Now I think it's great bringing your kids out to try new things, but shame on Fuji for not putting them in a separate area of the dining room where their incessant prattle, booth kicking, and constant trips to the bathroom would not entertain the guests who were out for a Saturday night classy dinner. Elitist? Screw you and wear a tie hippie. It's Saturday night and if I'm paying $100 or more a person for a meal, wear a damn collared shirt and get a babysitter. Third? If an item is no longer available on your menu, remove it or let me know when you hand me the menu. Two main course items and one dessert item I requested were not available. Price? For the quality of the fish it was an excellent value. Definitely the best Sushi in South Jersey and in the top three in the region. Call ahead for seating at the Sushi bar of for either of the Chef's special tastings. I'm planning an Omikase here soon! I'm heading back tonight for another serving of abalone and to try a few more dishes. Hope to see you there!

text: I cannot in good conscience actually suggest Halloween to anyone I know. This is particularly disappointing as prior to my absolutely horrible experience I had told everyone I know to already go there. I have been rectifying that situation ever since. If you are looking to purchase something already displayed in the shop then please do not be swayed by my review. I have only experienced the handmade part of the business and so cannot account for the premade experience. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- I tend to dislike engagement rings in general. So when my boyfriend and I found ourselves getting closer to an engagement, he asked if we could go look at some rings. I had heard about this little shop that made handmade items, Halloween, and so we decided to go there. I found two rings I loved and my boyfriend got the information and we left. About 5 months later my boyfriend pops the question with a beautiful handmade ring based on one of the rings I found that day from Halloween. And then the nightmare begins... A few days after popping the question my boyfriend had to leave town for a few weeks. Unfortunately, this means that the ensuing poor customer service, shocking lack of professionalism and appalling level of craftsmanship that I encountered was left entirely in my hands. The ring had to be brought back twice. Once because a diamond fell out, there were a significant number of scratches on the gold due to jewelers tools and because the ring was in fact a shoddy mess with multiple holes where there shouldn't be. I brought the ring back and was told it wouldn't be a problem and that they would replace the missing diamond with no charge and have it back to me in 5 days (I had it on my finger for 3). I was fairly pleased at this point that they were so confident it would be perfect when I came back. Then I came back. I arrived with a friend and we took the ring and headed out. The jewelers didn't show it to me under a light or anything just handed it to me and sent me on my way. Not a problem in most shops but in the dark cavern that is Halloween you can't see anything. Sure enough we arrived home 20 minutes later and I find that while "fixing" the ring they have seriously damaged another portion and none of the scratches were polished out nor were the holes fixed. Essentially, they replaced the missing diamond and didn't touch it otherwise. My friend accompanied me back to the store and that's when it got really strange. The owner was extremely rude and unprofessional. He starts by trying to blame me for arriving so early in the day as if another hour would make the difference when they have had it for five days. The owner had this air of, "how could I dare to question his work and have the audacity to bring it back even!" Even to the point where I had to ask my friend when we left, "did I do something wrong here?" After another 3 days I returned and the ring was mostly perfect. The owner tried to tell me that the same scratches that I told him about the first day were my fault (although it was physically impossible for that to be true given the placement and that I had the ring for three days while he had had it for the remaining eight) and there is still a small hole where there shouldn't be one. I also brought the ring to another jeweler and was told that the work that was done on my ring was really sub par. I asked if I should return (a third time) to have the ring fixed and this other jeweler told me not to. He said that given how they had fixed the first problem (with a poor craftsmanship fix) there was too high a chance that they would further damage it if I brought it back. I cannot tell you how truly awful this experience was. If you are considering purchasing a handmade engagement ring at Halloween PLEASE I urge you not to. I am not writing this review for any purpose other than the hope that someone else will not have to deal with the same situation I did in the first weeks of my engagement. I had read other similar reviews on other sites but was so excited about the prospect of a handmade ring that I didn't heed their warnings. Please be sure to search the internet for all reviews about Halloween. You will quickly find that I am only one of a number of newly engaged women who spent much of the first weeks of their engagement without a ring on their finger and with the horror show of service and quality that is Halloween.
label: NEG
