text: Mole. Mole? MOLE. Huuuuh? I had no idea! Ok, I think I did have an idea that this little shop was also a taqueria, but it was the slightest little sliver of a memory from high school which was a long time ago, like uncountable layers of paint on the cow long ago. I came to the little shopping center that la Tapatia is in for other reasons, but one member of my party declared she was going to grab some pan dulce and we all pushed into the tiny little bakery where the vivid cornucopia of savory menu items were displayed 8x10 color glossy glory along the wall. I should say that they weren't *good* photos, someone commented that it looked like they were shot from a moving car, but it was enough to get the idea of coming back planted in our heads. It was nearly 7 at night, not heaving with people, but the small handful of dining patrons were undoubtedly thinking "crap, the gringos have found us. At least it's not Julia." One wall is shelves of pan dulce, all sorts including my favorite, the butterfly curly thingie. We selected about half a dozen assorted, 75c each. That's all we got this time, but I looked long and hard that the food menu and asked questions. I would totally be back to sample the tacos. I'm on a taqueria tour, after all. Meanwhile, the pastries. I couldn't dive into them until the following morning but my god they were so delicious. Really, the best butteryfly thingie I've ever had at a panaderia! Lightly crisp, yet dense and a little chewy. Did not fall apart in a big crumbly mess with each bite! I sampled an assortment, and my meager handful of all the pan dulce available were all great. A great balance of fluffiness, denseness, a subtle sweet to the pastries. They'd be awesome to have with a sweet coffee. I know I'm not the only person brainwashed by mass produced grocery store sugar bomb cakes that has taken a bite of a gorgeous looking pan dulce and wondered where the hell the sweet was. First, pastries need not be sugar bombs to be good, I finally figured that out. Second, these pan dulce weren't bland, they're Goldilock's "just right" middle ground and before I knew it, I'd eaten the whole thing up. I went back two days later for lunch. Two of us ordered a small carnitas taco and the mole con pollo to share. The taco does indeed come with a freshly made tortilla. It's soft and chewy and holds up to the filling that only one tortilla is necessary, and provided. The taco is simple and good, served with cilantro and onion, with wedge of lime and a green salsa on the side. The winning item, though, was the mole con pollo. Whooooa, really good! It may have beat the top spot in my heart for chicken mole. The sauce was sweet and spicy, rich, complex. The chicken was perfect - one large thigh with such tender meat falling off the bone that you only need to pull it apart with pieces of tortilla. And the tortillas! The dish came with more fresh, soft tortillas, the largest I'd ever seen for homemade corn tortillas. This dish also comes with a small portion of rice and beans. Some notes: * seriously hole in the wall. But they've packed a lot of stuff in. * Small tables have been pushed together to make longer communal tables. If it's busy you can share the benches running along one of the walls. * cash only * no prices listed on the hot foods. Gotta ask. The chicken mole was probably in the $8 range. The small tacos were in the $2.50 range, larger ones in the $3.50 range. Seems high, you might think, but it's because they make their tortillas fresh to order. Which brings me to my last point. * tortillas made fresh to order! I've uploaded photos, but like any food using dark sauces, it doesn't look that good. In words of IT Crowd, "It's chocolate! It's not shit."

text: I have been going to the Delaware County SPCA off and on for the last year or so because I was interested in adopting a dog. I went there early on a Saturday, about 15 minutes before their opening time and joined the small group of people who had gathered outside waiting for the shelter to open. Some people were there to look/adopt, and there were a few with cat carriers who were there to turn in cats. I want to mention there was a college age girl with a tear streaked face with a carrier and then also separately there were an older couple with a few cat filled cages. Now I started talking to the girl and she mentioned that she was about to head off to college to live in the dorms and her parents ( who sound pretty evil) refused to take care of the cat while she was away. She couldn't take the cat into the dorms with her and after trying to get friends or family to take her cat, she realized she was going to have to give it up. As someone who recently graduated college after living in the dorms, I knew how amazing it felt to come home during the holidays/breaks and be greeted with purrs by my cats. Now the older couple were bringing in cats that they had trapped in their backyard. So the shelter opens and because the staff wouldn't let anyone go in the dog hallway, everyone was pretty much stuck in the small lobby of the shelter. I could overhear the girl recant her story to the staff, and the lady behind the desk asks her if her cat was her pet, and not a stray. The girl confirms that the cat was her pet. The lady tells the girl "well, we can't take cats that were owned by someone at this time, we have no room. We can only put down the cat for you, and that will be $35.00." The girl burst into tears and the staff just went on with their business. Meanwhile the staff happily accepts the elderly couple's stray cats in traps because they were strays and thats ok. So people in the lobby start questioning the staff's reasoning behind rejecting a perfectly healthy, up to date on shots cat and the lady at the desk gets defensive and keeps saying "because that's our policy." So a nice family who was there to look for a dog takes the girl aside and after asking a few questions, lets everyone know that they will take the cat. I was truly appalled at the way that the "caring and animal loving" staff/voulenteers at the SPCA would just coldly tell someone who was giving up their beloved cat and it obviously pained them that "oh, we're going to put it down and it will cost you $35.00"

text: As I mentioned in my review of the Sheraton, I needed a place to watch the England vs. Algeria World Cup game while my lovely wife shopped with her daughter and grandkids. We timed our trip down there perfectly and I was sitting at the bar with time to spare! There were lots of TVs in this place and they had music playing that gave the bar a very cool vibe to it. I came to learn that Ernesto, the bartender, was very cool. He greeted me right away and wanted to get me set up as best as humanly possible. I picked my best vantage point and while I wasn't all that hungry, looked over the menu. Everything looked and sounded tasty, but I was in game mode and all I really wanted was a GOOD Bloody Maria. Long ago I accepted the fact that not all bars make good Bloody Marys/Marias. Would I be as lucky today as the US was against England in their first game of the World Cup or would I be victimized like we were in the Slovenian match? Ernesto was fired up to make me one and I was buoyed by his enthusiasm. It took a few minutes and when he was done, I have to say Ernesto has Fire + Spice in the plus column! My Bloody was so good I had to tell myself to slow down and savor it... I didn't want to be wasted by the time the Mrs. showed up. While England looked very uninspired during their match against Algeria, Ernesto & Co. were taking up the slack. People started to filter in for lunch, but I was the only one at the bar. Even though he started to get busy with orders for the lunch crowd he made sure to take care of me. Ernesto set out some very spicy chex mix for me. This mouth charring, endorphin pumping variant did not come out of a Chex Mix bag. It was "this is freakin' hot but I can't stop eating it" good. I meant to ask where it came from, but again I was in game mode and Ernesto could sense it. He was friendly, but not disruptive (and ended up giving me the remote so I could turn the volume up). He poured me a Dos Equis and kept tabs on me. At half time, I ordered a Sonoran Quesadilla. Not because I was super hungry, but it just looked so good: Roasted poblano's, oaxaca cheese, salsa fresca,crema ...for a buck they add beef machaca and it rolled out at $8. It came with salsa but it was so tasty, I didn't want to spoil it in any fashion. I wished I would have been starving, because I wanted to try a whole lot more on the menu. Anyway, the second half came and went uneventfully. England failed to produce, yet Ernesto & Fire + Spice came up big! I settled my tab and told Ernesto I would be back for a margarita to take back poolside. Everyone claims they have good margs...if life was only that simple. I tried two, just to make sure! They were as good as he claimed they were going to be. I wasn't completely bombed when the Mrs. returned. She tried to catch up and pitched in an order of cherry vodka & soda water. She tried two ..they tasted like cherry vodka & soda water. LOL! Our last report is on breakfast. We mosied on down there for breakfast thinking our breakfast vouchers were going to be for some prepacked bagels or honey buns and maybe a small carton of milk or Donald Duck OJ. The waitress informed us that they were good for the All- American breakfast. Mrs. asked if we could substitute it for the Breakfast Burrito..she is so good at that! They hooked us up and we both enjoyed one of the best breakfast burritos ever. It is not a humongous stomach stretching burrito, but a respectfully sized burrito. Some say that it is not the size of your burrito that matters , but what is inside. I believe it...in this case. Not only was the burrito delish....the hash browns were some of the best tasting shredded spuds we have ever had. The Mrs. couldn't finish hers and I was too full to help out. Guess it was big enough! The Sheraton is lucky to have this place on the property! I would go there even if I wasn't staying at the hotel.

The low price ($55/hour) made it affordable enough for me to pick up the tab for both of us: Pros: * excellent massage! My masseuse found every knot in my back, and some I didn't even know I had in my legs, and demolished them. I ordered a deep tissue massage and she used a combination of massage and acupressure to get everything fixed. I left feeling like new. * super nice staff. Really, really nice and friendly. * low price! For $55, I'll be able to come here 1-2x/month, instead of the 2-3x/year I normally afford at the foofy spa I go to. * the hot stones and hot towels are a nice touch, especially the towels. It was the first time I ever dressed after a massage and didn't have to worry about my clothes getting completely gooped in oil. * you don't need an appointment, so you can drive by and go "hey! I'm going to treat myself!" and just stop in. No having to wait 2 weeks for an appointment like at some of the fancy places. Cons: * yeah, the super-basic decor is a bit unnerving at first. The place is in the basement of a building, so when you walk into the massage area it's just a big dark basement room with stalls separated by a pipe-and-drape setup. This is not the kind of place you go with your girlfriends to have a spa day, it's a place to have someone beat the crap out of your back for cheap. The atmosphere is the reason I'm not giving this place 5 stars. * the hot towels and hot stones are down the hall from the "stalls", so the masseuses have to leave you on the table to go get them. My masseuse left at least 4 times, which in total probably took close to 5 minutes off my massage time while I laid there mostly exposed with the curtain open a crack. My BF had the same experience. It would be better if each stall had its own towel and stone heater in there, but I guess sharing supplies is one of the things that keeps their costs down. All in all, we give it 2 thumbs up. text: Named for the stream that once flowed where 43rd St. is today and is now contained in a giant sewer pipe, the Millcreek Tavern has a swampy, fetid quality much like its namesake. There's no reason to go here unless: 1. You have a friend in a band that's playing here. 2. You live within two blocks. So for those of us who find ourselves still supporting our aspiring rock star friends, or for those who live in this lovely little corner of West Philly and are too lazy to hike a few extra blocks to get drunk (alas! how I miss my old apartment), here's a brief survival guide to the Millcreek. First, you should know that Millcreek has managed to duck the smoking ban, perhaps because it meets the criteria or perhaps because it's owned by an ex-cop. Be prepared to be hit with a wall of USA GOLD smoke. You should also know that it's really two connected bars. The east side (entrance on 42 and Chester) is newer and superficially less dingy. This is where your friend's band is playing, on a shitty little stage way in the back corner. The sound will be both ear-splitting and incomprehensible at the same time. The sightlines and acoustics are dreadful, so you might want to show up early to get a better seat. Don't order the food. You'll save money and get your food quicker if you pick up something a door down Chester at the Five-Star Deli. That said, if it's late (the Five-Star closes at 11), the chicken fingers will suffice. The western side (entrance on Chester) is an older bar once known as the Track and Turf. (That's why USP kids in the know call it "The Track.") This side has more character. Character is a euphemism for wood paneling, dart boards, and a colorful cast of neighborhood alcoholics. You'll also find Larry on this side. Larry is a Southwest-Philly-born-and-raised bartender with a thick Philly accent. Larry can smoke a whole Winston without once removing it from his lips. Larry will encourage you to get the pitcher. Larry may not notice that something is floating in your beer. Larry likes you more if you have breasts. I like Larry. A few other tips. The jukebox will eat your money. Larry may or may not offer a refund. The Millcreek no longer serves actual Yuengling Lager. Instead, they carry a generic lager with a phony, cheesy tap that says "Millcreek Lager." I think they pump it up directly from the 43rd St. sewer pipe.

text: I made a quick trip down to the Tampa Bay area for a friend's wedding last weekend. While in town, I decided to drop by Cigar City Brewing to see their brewery and sample some of their brews. Their site indicates they had a lot of different and interesting concoctions, so I couldn't wait to stop by. The Building: The building where Cigar City Brewing resides is very unassuming. It's a large metal building off Spruce Street, about 5 minutes from Tampa International Airport. Anyone not looking for a brewery here would probably be very surprised to learn it was there - in fact, the friend I had lunch with and subsequently took to CCB had never heard of it before. It seems as though this fledgling brewery is somewhat of a secret among the general population of Tampa (though I'd also venture to say that "craft beer" is not on the average beer drinker's radar quite yet). It turns out there were two doors that said "Entrance" on the side of the building. Upon trying one, it was locked and my heart sank. Surely they were open - the website said they were. My hopes were raised again when I tried the other door and it opened into their tap/tasting room. Turns out the first door was the brewery entrance and they were not brewing that day. Tap Room: The tap room was clean and inviting. The deep earthy colored paint on the walls was complimentary to the wood bar, as well as their logo and the general "feel" I got of their brand-tobacco, cigars, Cuban life, etc. There was cool music being pumped through the speakers by a vintage stereo system (circa 1975). I was pleased that the music wasn't so loud that our conversation was drowned out. I was really surprised at how many people there were. The bar was almost full and I had to sit all the way at the end (by the time we left, there were people sitting at tables because the bar was full). The bar tender was friendly, though busy at times filling growlers and cleaning glassware. They didn't seem to have enough glassware to let it just all accumulate and do a big wash at the end of the day, so the employees were constantly going over to the sink, washing the glasses in a 3-step sink system and then setting on a towel to air-dry. The beers: I got their 4-glass sampler ($6), where you could choose any 4 beers they had on tap, including the higher gravity, and thus, more expensive brews. I had a friend with me, so that doubled the number of possible beers to try, though he got a few of the same ones as I did. Here's what I tried, along with what I remember about them. Jai Alai IPA Overall, a great IPA. Probably my favorite out of the beers I tried. It had a wonderful subtle grapefruit flavors and was not too earthy (I believe they use Simcoe hops). I think that the aroma was a little lacking but the flavor made up for it. Rye Porter I have had a Rye IPA (HeBrew) and now I've had a Rye Porter. I can say with all certainty that I do not like ales made with rye. I did not finish the glass. Cuban Espresso Maduro Porter I think that this was my second favorite, after the IPA. The espresso smell was divine! The coffee flavors were pronounced, but not too strong as to be overpowering. Apple Saison This was probably my least favorite. I know not everyone likes saisons, but I've had a few that I really liked. BJCP Guidelines for a saison (16C) state that, "Low to moderate sourness or acidity may be present, but should not overwhelm other characteristics." This beer was overwhelmingly sour to me - mouth puckering sour. It hit you right in the back of the cheeks when you drank it. While true to it's "apple" claim, it was pretty undrinkable because of the tartness and sourness. This was another that I did not finish. Peach Cream Ale I don't remember a lot about this beer, other than it was "peachy." The peach flavor and aroma was present, but it wasn't my favorite. Then again, I'm not a big fan of cream ales in general, though I like to try new things to expand my horizons. Seabass Black Saison This was a great saison! It still had the tartness of the other CCB saison we tried, though because of the darker malt that was used, It was not nearly as overwhelming. This was my friend's favorite beer, though he was kind enough to let me take a few sips and enjoy. The Brewery: The brewery area was large and open. We had to go into that are to use the restroom, and though they weren't brewing today, I took the opportunity to grab a few snapshots and a video of their facility. On my way out, I purchased a pint glass ($5) and a 750ml bottle of their "Humidor Series IPA" ($9) . I had a great time at the tasting room. The staff were friendly and overall I'd say the beers were good. If you're ever in Tampa and you're interested in craft microbreweries, this is a required stop.

So, after some discussion, John said he'd be back out that week to remove the rest of the tree. That was 5 weeks ago. Now, John from White Horse Tree Care, LLC refuses to take our calls (I'm sure he has caller ID, who doesn't?), he refuses to reply to our repeated voice mail messages and we have had to resort to using anonymous phones to get him to answer. When he does, he gives us a bunch of bullshit lines, saying he'll be out the next day, which never happens. We paid $1600 to have these trees removed and it will now cost us another $800 to have the rest of the tree that was supposed to be removed cut down. Lesson learned?... 1. DO NOT ACCEPT A CONTRACT THAT DOES NOT HAVE THE BUSINESS ADDRESS ON IT. 2. DO NOT ACCEPT A CONTRACT THAT DOES NOT HAVE THE OWNERS NAME CLEARLY PRINTED AND SIGNED ON IT. 3. CHECK TO SEE IF THE BUSINESS HAS A PHYSICAL ADDRESS AND VISIT IT PRIOR TO HIRING ANY COMPANY. 4. DO NOT PAY IN FULL UNTIL THE JOB IS COMPLETE! The company is a complete sham and the business "owner" is a scam artist. The next call we make will be to our attorney! UPDATE: The actual owner of the company is Kelly, not John. Oh, that's not all...there is still a 3 foot stump sticking out of my yard AND another 3 foot tall, ten foot around section of the trunk laying beside it. I do not possess the physical strength or equipment to remove that section of tree from my yard so I guess it will remain there until eternity (or termites) determine it no longer needs to be there! There are several cut marks into that stump so I know there was an attempt and a knowledge that it had to go but apparently John from WHTC just gave up and left it there for us to deal with. I sent a picture message to Kelly on her phone but I got no response. I called and spoke to her and asked if she would please come out to investigate the "finished" product but 10 days later, no luck. I'll give her until the end of this week to show up and if not, I'll place another call to Channel 10.

text: My Climb Nashville visit started off with a few Lucy and Ethel moments and ended with a new-found obsession. If you are looking for an amazing workout or are looking for an interesting experience and haven't been to Climb Nashville yet...HEAD THERE NOW. Muscles that I didn't even know existed bulged as I maneuvered myself on the indoor rock climbing walls at Climb Nashville. A day pass with equipment rental is only $19 which includes full access to the gym, workout area, and remittance if you decide to leave for a bit. This gym is nestled in the Sylvan Park area, so you can be seduced by lunch at many of the area dining spots. Hel-lo Local Taco! This gym was pretty packed when my brave buddy and I showed up but we were assisted right away. Our day started off with a 20 minute Belay class which teaches the technique of how to safely hold the rope for a climber. Um. Kind of important. The climbing part was actually the easy part for me. This lesson is the difference between a victorious climb or SPLAT. After a few awkward attempts at strapping myself in...I caught on and got into the rhythm. What can I say? I am a natural... This class is $15 but you can get refresher courses for free once you have taken it. I felt like Frogger as I climbed up the walls and felt such an adrenaline rush each time I made my way to the top. Belaying for my partner while it was her turn was just as much of a workout due to the constant movement of your arms too. I made a few attempts at the bouldering walls but will have to work up my upper body strength a bit more. These don't look like they would be tough due to the lack of height but in reality, you are working more muscles because there is no rope to help elevate your body weight. I felt each and every pound as I attempted to climb these walls. I am going on a diet as we speak. There are many levels of climbing available. It was amazing to watch families and people of all ages climbing and crawling throughout the afternoon. I woke up this morning and although most of my body is sore, I am actually craving my next visit back. TIP: Monthly memberships and packages are available ranging from $80-$540. You may also take yoga and other fitness classes or host parties here too.

text: Oh Em Gee. Why have I not been to Buddakan before?? Atmosphere is pretty fantastic - love the wall of water and the giant Buddha. Our server told us that the portions were shareable, but not gigantic - I beg to differ - They were HUGE! Definitely worth the prices! Appetizers: Pork Belly Hot Pot (10): Pork belly in a miso broth with a fried egg. Yum!!! Like having a breakfast soup (bacon and eggs... ya know?). Shrimp and Scallop Spring Rolls (11): Giant spring rolls bursting with shrimp and scallops - very little filler! Each bite was full of seafood! Comes with a mustard sauce and a plum sauce (my fave). Entrees: Aged Char Grilled Beef (Small - 32): HOLY COW! My boyf ordered the small portion and I cannot imagine what the large looks like! About 20 slices of beef, perfectly cooked, with a MOUNTAIN of crispy potato strings. The beef is topped with a red-wineish sauce and the potatoes are drizzled with spicy mustard. MMMM. Pan Seared Duck Breast (26): Ordered this (instead of the Pork Tenderloin which I considered) because of the promise of corn and scallion spoon bread. Best decision I ever made. The duck was perfectly cooked in a sweet plum sauce and the spoon bread was absolutely amazing - Kind of like a corn bread with the center not totally cooked. LOVE. Dessert: Carrot Cake (9): Delicious layers of spiced carrot cake and malted milk panna cotta. With a cinnamon ice cream on the side, I was absolutely in heaven!!! P. S. The table next to us got the dessert bento box, and that looked amazing as well. Might have to try that next time! Overall, pricy, but reasonable once you see the portion sizes! Come with an appetite!

One caution - the menu is written on a chalk board (entrees on one side, appetizers on the other), and your waiter will describe each entree to you. There is no other written description. This can be difficult if you go to Sidney Street with someone who is hard of hearing (I eventually just told my grandmother what I thought she would like) and it can become monotonous if you visit the restuarant on a semi-regular basis (not often enough for the waiters to recognize you). For non-weekends, the back room of the restuarant can be rented out for large groups. They don't rent it out for Fridays or Saturdays, but it can make a great venue for a weekday evening work event. text: Go to the weekend buffet for some of the most authentic Chinese food in Nashville. Food: A+ for weekend buffet, B for all other food/times There is never a huge/excessive selection of food for the buffet, but there's always two buffet counters. During the weekend buffet, you can have your fill of authentic Chinese food (maybe with the caveat that none of it is very spicy) and there's enough vegetarian options for vegetarians out there. I particularly like the dumplings/buns and seafood dishes. Also, there's fresh soymilk and bubble tea on the buffet (no extra charge) during the weekends, and I'd highly recommend trying both. I've always stuffed myself silly with the weekend buffets. The rest of the time (i.e. not weekend buffet), it's an average Chinese restaurant in Nashville. Price: B+ It's not a bargain, but $10-$12 should cover weekend lunch buffet costs. The non-buffet prices are typical for a sit-down Chinese restaurant. Non-alcoholic drinks are available at the usual prices; a pot of tea is available for $1.50. Service: A- The service isn't particularly memorable or fast, but is decent. The owner/manager often asks if you've enjoyed your meal. Hygiene: A There is nothing to suggest that the place is anything other than clean. At worst, the less popular buffet food sometimes sits out for a while on the buffet line. Facilities: A- Not luxurious or fashionable by any stretch of the imagination, but quite serviceable and utilitarian. Parking can get tight on the weekends. Overall: A for weekend buffet, B for all other food/times, A- composite There's not much of a point in going out of your way for their ordinary food, but they're weekend buffet is definitely something you should try if you're in the West End area. The weekend buffet features some of the best authentic Chinese food in Nashville.

text: We'd read good reviews of this place on Tripadvisor.com and thought it would be a good place to eat dinner, since we both love tapas. What a mistake! We were the only people in the restaurant on a Saturday night, which should have told us something, considering that other restaurants in the area had full parking lots. It actually reminded us a lot of the show Kitchen Nightmares, where the restaurant was deserted and the standards had slowly slipped over time (we're giving them the benefit of the doubt that they weren't always this awful). We arrived during "happy hour," which ostensibly should have entitled us to $5 tapas. After we were given the check, with full priced tapas on it, we overheard another server (not ours) tell the second group in the dining room that the $5 tapas was tapas that was not on the menu. Unfortunately, our server did NOT tell us this. He was very nice and friendly, but seemed quite callow, given the absence of his notification about the tapas specials and the fact that he didn't offer us dessert or to order more tapas, even though we said that we'd start with 3 and would probably order more. There were other strange things about the service like, with an entirely empty dining room, they gave us the table next to the bathroom. The woman who seated us didn't pull out our chairs or spread out our napkins, which was another indication of the unpolished service that we received here. The food, though, was the big problem. We wanted to start with three different tapas, but they were out of the one that sounded most appealing to us, the fried green tomatoes with crab meat. We ordered the ceviche, four crab croquettes, and the shrimp al ajillo. The ceviche turned out to be a garden salal with precisely TWO shrimp, sliced lengthwise, and a half of a bay scallop, which was cut into two pieces. Not exactly what is usually indicated by the term "ceviche," especially for $7.50. The crab croquettes, which were described as "filled with crab and cheese," turned out to be plain potato croquettes. Neither crab nor cheese was in evidence here. The shrimp al ajillo, at $7.95, was a giant rip off. This, of the three dishes, turned out to be the only one that was what it said it was: shrimp with garlic sauce. However, $7.95 at Tapas Garden buys you 6 medium-sized (26-30/lb) shrimp. Woo hoo! I'm posting a photo, though it's only got 5 shrimp, since I forgot that we were photographing the food and had eaten one of the shrimp before I remembered this. I was so irritated at this point by the misinformation and misleading descriptions that we just paid the check and left. I didn't even finish my glass of wine because I was so irked. I would definitely advise avoiding this restaurant unless you would like to pay too much for mediocre food with either excessively small portion sizes or misleading ingredients like "ceviche" or "crab" croquettes.

I had a very laid-back waiter who sat down at the chair across from me and asked me what I was thinking about for dinner, and I basically said "do your best - whatever you think." That was the ticket - he came back in a bit with the special not on the menu: two huge mahi-mahi, sushi-grade steaks of tuna, blackened on the outside to give them a good crust, but rare inside. I talked to the waiter about it a bit more, and he said they catch those tuna off the gulf shore. This guy came right off the boat, gently seared, and to my plate. It also came with a great spicy wasabi sauce, and some corn on the cob and fries, which were all great, but that tuna... Oh man, it was the best piece of seafood I've ever had in my life. It easily flaked, but was thick as a Texas oil baron's wallet. The tuna had no flavor or taste at all - it did not smell like tuna or fish or anything, it was so damn fresh. I barely used the sauce, but it wasn't bad, either. I devoured that stuff, went into protein overload, and talked to Eric, the waiter, about local fishing, scuba diving, and more. He gave me a check that was a joke it was so cheap. I think I left a 100% tip. There's lots of other choices, which I can't vouch for, but are probably decent. It's a step above a TGI Friday, a chain, but maybe a bit more authentic, and a good place to bring your drinking buddies for a few buckets of brew. But man, that whole experience was so incredible, I'm very scared to ever go back and jinx things.

text: I agree that the Mad Platter is VERY expensive, and maybe not quite spectacular enough to be priced at what it is. Still, it's a lovely place in Germantown, a very un-Nashville neighborhood. It's casual enough for lunch and perfect for a date. I loved the ambiance. It was small, rustic, with one wall acting as a semi-library. An old fashioned stove remains in the dining hall. It's dark, extremely romantic. You can supply your own bottle of wine, and there is a $15 corkage fee. We indulged in the 5-course prixe fixe, a savings of... well, a lot. You get to have one of everything - a soup, appetizer, salad, entree, and dessert. Holy moly. Everything was very well done and tasted excellent. The sweet corn chowder was a little spicy thanks to the bitty red peppers floating in it. The gumbo was smoky and thick, one of the more unusual things we ate that night. Salads were salads, with a few special ingredients to gourmet-ify them. The beet salad included flavorful goat cheese and pine nuts. We had the fried green tomato, which was topped with a mayonnaise-y frisee of greens. I realize mayonnaise-y isn't exactly the most positive of connotations, but that really does described it. In any case, it was great. We also had the tuna carpaccio, a hammered thin raw tuna filet that took up the entire plate. It was topped with an Asian-soy flavoring and avocado. Nice. Entrees: We had the crusted rack of lamb and the salmon. The lamb was rare, very well done and three 360 degrees characteristic of the dish made each bite complete. What do I mean? Well, if you scooped up everything on the plate in one fork-full - the crust, the lamb, the rissoto, etc. - that was the way to really get the full experience. The salmon was another very well cooked piece of fish I've in Nashville (everybody tells me not to eat fish in a landlocked state, but I have experienced some wonderfully prepared fish here), and was served on top of stewed spinach, honeydew and cucumber. I don't like honeydew, but when served in a hot compote-like thing it was really nice. The salmon was glazed with rum and mango. And finally for dessert, we had creme brulee and bananas foster. The bananas foster was exceptional. How could it not be, really? Butter, brown sugar, bananas, and ice cream. Sounds like a winner. The creme brulee was surprisingly thick, and enhanced with lemon zest. The crust was maybe a little under crispy, possibly due to the inclusion of lemon in the dish?? In any case, I would absolutely go back to the Mad Platter for another meal, but it would have to be a special occasion meal. Its name implies to me that the food should be more adventurous, abnormal. It's not quite strange enough for me. Yes it's pricey and your dollar could go a little further elsewhere. Still, I enjoyed being and eating there so much that there is no doubt I will return.

They offer several popular Korean dishes such as galbi, korean chicken, bulgogi, seafood, to name a few. The employees also work at the Sa Ri One on Cypress and the recipes are the same, so USF and Temple Terrace residents can now enjoy some tasty Korean without jumping on I-275 and driving 20-30 minutes away. Prices are also very reasonable since the style is made for to-go instead of a dine-in concept. There are still some dishes soup the soups that you can only have in a full Korean restaurant. The workers were friendly and we chatted about their new location. They plan to add frozen ice cream soon, something they used to have at the other location. They really have many plans to expand Sa Ri One and its great to hear the ambition. The inside is similar to a Chinese take-out spot with a more modern and clean look. There is free wi-fi which is pretty cool, but limited seating so I'd probably only come with one or two friends if I was going to eat it there. The area on Busch/56th is always under construction so driving there might be a little hassle (fyi it's next to Little Caesars), but it's well worth it. I ordered Bulgogi Beef with steamed rice, vegetables, two dumpings, and a soda for around $8 (talk about a bargain) and the beef came out still nice and hot, freshly made. I look forward to coming back and trying out other things on the menu and I'm sure this place will be a regular spot for me.

Finally, since the prices are so low, we decided to order three entrees for the two of us. The butternut squash risotto has a pretty strong sage flavor to it. Don't get me wrong, there wasn't anything wrong with it. It's just that there wasn't anything special about it either. I did like the crushed sweet potatoes that came with it. The humidity affects the amount of liquid, the strength of that days' lemon- all of these variables are so significant. In a hurry? You can't rush excellent. text: The four stars is based on the lunch buffet they offer. It's strictly a Monday-Friday deal, 11 a.m.-1:30. Outside of the lunch buffet, I've had a couple of the combo deals (pizza, wings, chicken fingers, fried vegetables, celery, carrot sticks, etc.) and found them to be a bit overpriced for what was offered. This isn't spectacular pizza, but at $6.99 for adults on the lunch buffet, it's a pretty darn good deal. Comparing it to the lunch buffet they used to offer at Godfather's, Pizza Plus is much better, both quality wise and in terms of selection. I took the youngster with me on the last trip, and was pleased that children under 11 were only $3.99, including a drink! Drinks are not included in the adult price, so the total bill for the two of us, including tax, was about $13.50. Still quite reasonable. One slight disappointment as far as the beverages (on the ayce): it's strictly a soda machine or coffee, there's no iced tea. I did notice iced tea was on the "to go" menu, so they must have it in bottles or cans. Beer is available on tap and in bottles as well. I started out with a plate of salad. It's a small salad bar with all your basic ingredients, nothing fancy but it gets the job done. The most important part of the salad bar, to me, would be the bleu cheese dressing to dip the chicken wings in. The wings, dear Yelp reader, are the big reason to hit the lunch buffet, and IMO the primary reason to visit Pizza Plus at all. The pizza's OK, nothing to write home about, but the wings are big, juicy, and, as a friend of mine observed, saucier than a lot of local wings. I'd say they're the best chicken wings in the Reno area. The buffet only includes mild and medium wings, so I always ask for a side of the nitro sauce, which is the ultra-spicy chili sauce. I like to double-dip my wings in bleu cheese dressing and the chili sauce, and since I have my own individual sauces on the side, double-dipping is not a sin, in fact it's encouraged!! Pizza Plus also has a side room that they rent out for parties--I once attended a birthday party there thrown by a Mexican family, who had ordered wings that were actually COOKED in the nitro sauce. They warned me that they were spicy, and I scoffed "no problem, I use the nitro sauce all the time." Seconds later I was wiping the sweat off my brow and reaching for my beer as tears started to well up in my eyes, much to the amusement of my friends... The pizza in the buffet, while not the best ever, gets definite points for variety. On the last visit, they had 3-4 different kinds out at all times, including sausage & veggie combo, pepperoni/olive, pepperoni/jalapeno, ham/pineapple, etc. Besides pizza and wings, the buffet also includes steak fries and BBQ chicken. Steak fries are pretty good, depending on how long they've been under the heat lamp. BBQ chicken were those boneless chunks of pressed chicken coated in a sweet BBQ sauce, I think some places call them "boneless buffalo wings." Not bad, they looked a little dry but were actually pretty juicy inside. It's just hard for me to justify eating them, though, when you've got the real hot wings sitting right there... For an inexpensive buffet, this is a great deal. I noticed that when certain items were getting low, and looking dry and worse for wear under the heat lamps, the staff would remove them and replace with a fresh batch. If you don't mind paying a little more, the specialty pizzas are pretty good, but not up to the level of a place like Blue Moon or the Blind Onion. They offer traditional red sauce, along with "our signature garlic ranch," which I have as yet to try. A fairly recent addition is the "Super Monster Mondo" pizza, which is costly ($29.99 for plain cheese or one topping, $39.99 for four toppings or more). It may be worth it, however, because it's a 24" pizza and (from the photos at least) looks like it's piled high with handfuls of toppings. There's even a "Super Monster Mondo Challenge," where you and a friend have 60 minutes to finish off a 24" Super Monster Mondo "fully loaded." If you finish, Pizza Plus picks up the tab...I'm not sure what "fully loaded" means in terms of what/how many toppings are included, but I'm sure I'd have to be "fully loaded" to try that dare. I'll stick with the lunch buffet for now... There are some arcade games, vending machines with stickers and toys, etc., so this place is definitely geared towards families. It's been packed with people every time I've gone in, and there are usually a few kids running around and loudly terrorizing the place, so if you're seeking a quiet lunch you should probably look elsewhere. I've also noticed that the one on Oddie (in the Kmart shopping center) usually has less business, and can sometimes be a little on the grimy side. Nothing really horrible, it just seems like the Prater location is better maintained. And don't forget the wings...they're a definite "plus" if you ask me!!

text: It is a long and stupid story about how I got dragged here, but I'll sum it up: I am a nice friend. So Vegetarian Suz and friend arrive at Voodoo. It's 9p on a Thursday night. The NOPD has taken up half of the front room, and they would be eye candy if I were in the market for dudes. (So this is probably good.) Friend and I try to figure what to eat by squinting at the menu board above the counter. Wait, menu board? This place doesn't have table service? WHAT?!? Problem #1: Voodoo is camped out on St. Charles, in a Nice Neighborhood™. This is primo real estate. People in this neighborhood will overpay for just about anything, just because it's a Nice Neighborhood™. But Voodoo has a menu board and no table service? No. If you are going to charge St. Charles prices (and they do) in the LGD (because they are), then you need table service. Or lower prices. Or both. So we're squinting at the menu board, trying to find things that Vegetarian Suz can consume. We've been at it for about 30 seconds, and we're standing over in the corner, out of the way and away from the register so we can figure out our order before bothering the counter girl. The counter girl, however, has begun bothering us. Problem #2: Someone went to a cheap management course and decided that staff at Voodoo need to be PROACTIVE!!!!! in their customer service. Which led to the counter girl yelling at us from 10 feet away, asking if we wanted our food for here or to-go. When we told her that we had no idea what we were going to order, she made a pinch face at us. Instead of yelling across the room to get our order, she should have waited until we approached her. Lay off the coffee juice, lady. Okay. We know what we're going to eat now, and we try to order. Try being the operative word. First, the girl doesn't know if the potato salad has bacon in it (yes). Nor does she even ask. Then she doesn't ask friend about the white vs. dark meat chicken thing. Instead, the cook yells--from the kitchen--about it. Does friend want white or dark meat? Friend doesn't care. Cook thinks this is odd. Friend doesn't care; friend wants chicken instead of awkward conversation about chicken. Why isn't the counter girl having this conversation with friend, re: chicken? Because of... Problem #3: The counter girl didn't finish dealing with her previous customers before taking our order. So while another couple was kicking up a fuss at not getting enough brisket ("I ORDERED HALF A POUND OF BRISKET!"), counter girl was transfixed and ignoring us. For someone who was so interested in "customer service" two minutes ago, this is a swift and unexpected change. So we get to watch the unfolding soap opera about brisket that involves two customers, the manager, and the counter girl. No cups. No little number-on-a-stick. I finally ask for them, receive cups and number-on-a-stick, and retreat to the drink machine. While at the drink machine, another nice young woman approaches friend and I with our food. Would we like it here, at the drink machine? (No, you dipshit, we would like to sit in chairs.) So the food beats us to our table. This is probably a good thing. The food itself wasn't too bad, but I'm pretty sure the potato salad had bacon in it. (Two bites left me with a tummy ache.) The fries and garlic bread were both top notch, and friend reports that her chicken was worth at least four stars. Voodoo reminds me of those trust-fund hipster kids...I'm sure you know the type: ratty clothes in cheap, dingy apartments swilling PBR and bemoaning the demise of their favorite dive bar while getting a four-figure allowance every month from daddy's accountants. Accessibility notes: Dining rooms are accessible for mobility devices, but the bar is a step up. No braille menu or signage. Can get loud at peak hours so potential difficulties for hard-of-hearing customers.

You go in further and there is a area upstairs with couches and a stage and some tables and chairs. We ordered there from a super nice girl named Julie. We didn't really know where to go so she said we can eat upstairs or down. Aside from Julie, another guy working there and the chef, we were alone. We were the only ones dining. We ordered: Pita & Hummus, broccoli salad, a spinach melt and a veggie burger, water, a chai latte, and a cranberry orange tea. EVERYTHING WAS EXCELLENT. The pita bread was flat like a tortilla. I actually prefer the flat pita. Growing up, my family had both and I personally like the flat one. The hummus was hand made. It was NOT like the typical peanut-butter smooth hummus you get everywhere else. It was grainy as when you grind the chickpeas yourself. It was spiced mild and perfectly. It was almost a falafel taste. Very good. The broccoli salad was similar to the one you find and various pot-luck gatherings. It was vinegary and quite excellent. The veggie burger was perfectly done on toasted bread. It came with tomato and lettuce. It really was awesome. The spinach melt was perfect spinich/cheese/spice blend on toasted bread. Again, wonderful food. The chai latte was perfect and had a huge latte head of foam. Loved it. The cranberry orange tea was good. We sweetened it with raw sugar. The whole experience was excellent except we wished there were more people there. It really needs to be frequented. I was wondering how they stayed in business. I left a large tip and the staff seemed blown away and very appreciative. I was going to give it four stars only because this was my first time at a vegetarian restaurant and I didn't know what to compare it with. But after thinking about it, the place fulfilled our every need. It was inviting, awesome food, cool atmosphere and friendly help. It deserved the five stars. -Darren

Honestly, I was just unimpressed by the Cuban sandwich. It was pretty weak. It was missing pickles...it was skinny...am I missing something? I wanted a big fatty melty cheesy thing full of pickles and grease. Hmmm. This thing would have embarrassed Subway. The Fried Grouper sandwich was actually pretty good, came out nice and hot and fried just right so it melted in your mouth. Maybe I should give it three stars but I just can't. Damn you, Cuban sandwich...

text: If you are planning a wedding or big celebration I would NOT book it here. The service is HORRIBLE, the food is horrible and the place is a mess. I was here for a wedding and they gave us the wrong seating chart a week before the wedding. Not only that some of the tables were asking for water and they told us that that they do not have water and they already provided soda so we dont need water. text: After lurking on Yelp for ages, I finally decided to contribute. We've (my wife and I) been here many times over the years. We even had our wedding rehearsal dinner here back in 2005. This is the most authentic place we've found in the Reno area for Chinese food. BTW, I'm Chinese, so I know what good Chinese food is. They were good back in the day (2005ish) but then the food quality went down hill, so we stopped going for a couple years. Looks like they got it back together again! We always start with the Seafood Tofu soup which we like a lot. I recommend trying it! I like it on the spicy side, so I always ask for some white pepper (it's not on the tables). The waiter (Sing) knows us and always brings the white pepper for me w/o me asking now. That's the kind of service we like! Also recommend the steamed whole fish, salt & spicy shrimp, and salt & spicy spare ribs. The staff is always friendly and attentive. This is back in our Reno restaurant rotation! If you're looking for a fancy shmancy fusion type place, this ain't it...but if you want some good Chinese food (especially in the Reno area) this will do the trick!

text: May the Gods of Brunch be blessed!! I love brunch it's a perfect eating opportunity on the weekend when waking up late and too lazy to do anything in your own kitchen. M & S offers an awesome Brunch menu and they hold back at nothing. My personal favorite the Crab Cakes Benedict. A fluffy perfectly poached egg sits upon a nice and plump crab cake this item does come with two eggs and two crab cakes!! The crab cakes are well seasoned and all crab, not mostly bread crumbs like some places. The spiked blueberry lemonade is tasty, but I'm a sucker for the Blood Orange Mimosa! The prices are reasonable considering it's not your mom and pop's diner.

text: Checked in at La Viola on Sunday night on a reccomendation. Living in the Bronx for 4 years, I grew quite fond of the casual Italian restaurants in the neighborhood. La Viola had that feel. This place proves that you don;t need fancy dishes and cutlery to get the point across. What's the point? Serve homestyle Italian comfort food. This place was a little pricey, but in my eyes worth it. Another CASH ONLY BYOB, i'm willing to pay a few extra bucks to stuff my face if i dont have to pay for the vino. We started with the antipasta and the mushrooms. The mushrooms were delicious, several different types cooked in a savory brown butter sauce. For my primera i had the Ravioli alla Viola, which was a Lobster Ravioli in a pink sauce. It was great, not too heavy, not too fishy, but could still taste the lobster in the sauce. My date had the Orriechete, which came in a brown butter and mushroom sauce with sausage, and that was very savory and filling. For the secundi we split the special, which was a rack of lamb covered in fontina cheese over polenta and zucchini. This was SO GOOD. Smothered in cheese, drizzled with a red wine demi-glace, It was perfect. For dessert we split a tiramisu, and i could barely walk out to the cab. Definitely pulled a Tony Soprano after this meal and unbuttoned the top button of my pants when i sat down to watch tv.
label: POS

text: The Thai food here is great and this place is somehow connected to Aroy Thai in O'Fallon - I think they have the same owner. So, if you like Aroy, you'll like this place. This location used to have a Chinese buffet, so I think a lot of people are disappointed when they find out there is no longer a buffet available here. I don't like buffets or Chinese food though. Basil Thai has never been crowded when I've been there...I hope this place survives, as it's nice to have a non-chain restaurant in The Heights! I recommend you try the Pad Eggplant - 4 star! Update: A friend provided this link confirming the relationship amongst the Thai restaurants in the MetroEast area: http://www.saucemagazine.com/blog/?p=7134 Excerpt: "The owner of Basil Thai Cuisine in Fairview Heights, Sala Thai in Belleville and Aroy Thai in O'Fallon will be opening his fourth Thai restaurant soon. Zapp Noodle & Market will be located in O'Fallon at 1407 W. Highway 50, Suite 106 and 107."

text: Sabrina's Café for brunch is worth a visit.. both times we have been here I've known to call ahead and get myself put on the waiting list. However, if I did not know to do that, I don't know if the 1hour plus wait that have been quoted to some new arrivals would really be worth it. But brunch here is very nice. I had the special 'It's Always Sunny' brunch special without bacon.. it still arrived with bacon. The waiter was really nice though and had it taken back and new eggs (the bacon was on the eggs) made for me. One thing - if you get the organic eggs, they won't make that for you runny. The rationale behind that is that organic eggs aren't irradiated nor are the chickens treated with routine antibiotics, so Salmonella poisoning was one of their concerns. I'll just say that although I eat organic eggs completely raw all the time and will continue to do so, I understand their liability and decision. I've also been able to try the polenta fries here (YUM!) and the French Toast (not stuffed).. Anyway, I'd recommend going.. Just be sure to call ahead though. text: Wow not much to complain about here but I wouldn't expect anything less from my favorite Iron Chef. I grew up watching this guy on the original show--before it was dubbed, subtitles only--on PBS. I loved that guy, I wanted to be him, or at least meet him, but I guess eating at his restaurant is the next best thing. Sad to say, he was not there, but I think my meal there made up for his absence. Grace and I started with the Morimoto tempura (fish, prawns, seasonal veggies, and a bacon-wrapped mozzarella ball deep fried in tempura batter with 3 dippning sauces) and a rice porridge topped with braised pork belly. Beautiful. Then for the main course I had the miso black cod and she had the sea bream served whole and de-boned. Both perfectly cooked and packed with flavor. The sea bream came with this miso beurre blanc that was pretty amazing. And my black cod (aka butterfish) just melted in my mouth. Favorite dish? the braised pork belly jook. simple, elegant, and delicious. It was a beautiful dish really. Least Favorite? the Morimoto tempura. Although bacon wrapped anything will fix pretty much any dish, it didn't change the fact that this tempura was a little heavy on the batter and was just kinda doughy and greasy instead of light and crispy as it should be. Come on, even Todai can produce well-fried tempura! All in all, it was an excellent experience and I will definitely be coming back here as soon as I can get a cheap flight out there. Now if only Morimoto could do something about the color-changing-neon-lights and the phallic-shaped table lamps then this place would be killer. Also, Iron Chef America is a joke.
label: POS

The sushi is very fairly priced and the portions are extremely generous. My friends had two rolls each and could barely finish what was on their plate. I had the deluxe sushi and received a number of premium cuts of fish along with the standards. Our service was friendly and on point. We did not have to wait long for anything, and our server, Daniel, was happy to talk to us about the food and the restaurant. All in all, a very satisfying experience!

text: I have been to Ceviche's several times, but each time the service has gotten worse and worse. The food is decent, but when your server never brings you a drink it's very hard to enjoy the food. I had to ask 6 times before the server brought me a glass of water. The sangria is ok, basically they just pour a bottle of wine in a pitcher with fruit...nothing special. The last time I went was on a Thursday night with 3 of my friends, it was busy, but most people were just hanging out and drinking. The server charged our table of 4 people a 20% gratuity! I have never been charged a gratuity here before, so I checked the menu to see the policy. The menu stated that an 18% gratuity would be added to parties of 6 or more. So why did our party of 4 get charged 20%??? I used to be a server, so I usually tip around 20-30%, but it is not a server's right to add grat on in a dishonest way. He didn't even tell us that grat was added and the place is so dark, we almost left a double tip, which is probably what the server was hoping for. So dishonest! I will not be back!

text: I would call my husband and myself sushi experts. Before moving to Tucson we would gorge ourself on fresh options in Portland, Or. We were worried we wouldn't find anything to compare here in Tucson and were happy to try Tatsu Sushi. The atmosphere is going for an modern look and misses the mark a bit, but the excellent menu distracts from that. There are a plethora of your standard rolls. I would complain that there are too many based on the traditional California Roll--fake crab isn't seafood in my book. Our meal came with miso soup and edamame (not to salty). I highly recommend the Key, the Lollipop and the Lemon Fresh rolls. All were are very creative with great sweet and hot flavors. Everything we ordered was fresh and all the staff were friendly. Prices are comparable to quality sushi restaurants everywhere. Some good happy hour options as well--running from 3 to 6pm M-F and 3 to 9 pm on Sunday. We will be back for sure.

text: I've eaten Ferearo's twice: Once on a lazy summer's eve, and again during Mardi Gras. At neither time, nor now, could I recommend Feraro's as a decent choice for hungry stomachs. During Mardi Gras, the difference between price and quality widened to canyon-levels. St. Louis offers many incarnations of excellent food, so if your stomach can hold out on those Mardi Gras afternoons, I urge you to seek out alternatives to Feraro's.

I've been trying to forget my experiences here and hope that maybe I can ward off some others in time. text: One of my regular Sunday morning spots. The Soft Tacos are my favorite, fresh with a little bit of spice against the eggs. The French Toast is thick and tasty, pancakes are stacked high, and the omelets come mixed with great ingredients (my girlfriend is a big fan of the spinach and feta). The waitresses at the counter are friendly and remembered us after going in just for a couple of Sundays (always a big plus for me). Prices are reasonable, if not cheap. My only complaint, and it's a nature of the beast thing, is that they are always packed for breakfast. I mean, people sitting on the curb outside packed. As long as tables are moving along (we watched a guy slowly work through half an omelet over a half hour period after his friends had finish) the tables flip in a hurry, but don't expect to get seated right away. My suggestion would be to take a counter spot...more fun that way anyway. Great food, good service. It's unfortunate it's not bigger, because they could fill it up.

text: Given the design and all white brightness of this second floor restaurant, one could be overlooking the Mediterranean on Positano itself. The place is worth multiple visits for a variety of reasons but certainly for the menu with the crudo, and the artichoke, ricotta and lemon soup which are extraordinary as are the fresh sardines. House made squid ink pasta more often than not a disappointment here made with crab and redolent of a briny breeze. text: Shopping for a corset is like picking that one good suit that will serve you for years to come - it had better, for the investment you're making! text: The best thing I can say about FCCC is that there are some wonderful caring individuals here. That said, they have an open door policy that maxes out the capacity and allows for many people to fall through cracks in the system. A strong feeling that the left hand doesn't know what the right hand is doing here. A few examples: Becoming diabetic is a common side effect of pancreatic cancer and despite it being clearly marked in my mother's chart, the staff would forget to check her glucose/administer insulin/or remember to offer her the diabetic menu daily! I set a radiology appointment for a Thursday, only to be called the Tuesday before asking why we missed our Monday appointment? When I explained we had a Thursday not a Monday, she blamed my mother's medication and that she must have forgot she changed it...at this point I was setting all appointments! It wasn't until after one of their interns wrote the wrong drug on a prescription that almost caused my mom to OD (rush to the ER Narcam shot!) and my threatening lawsuits all the way up to the president of the Hospital did they A) put the port that she needed a month ago in, B) get her a second Chemo treatment, C) actually see her team of doctors in one room at the same time. Those were just a few of our problems... My mother's was a terminal diagnoses and I make no illusions that they could have cured her. What I do know is that her final months could have been a lot better if we didn't go here. I've heard similar from other patients and sadly a story that mirrored my mom's own awful experience happened, a month after my mom passed, to my father's childhood best friend there at FCCC I've struggled with the idea of posting this here, but in the end if you or someone you know is considering going here don't. text: "Real Mexican Tacos." So says the sign out front. Please let me express up front that in no way do I have an aversion towards chains. With that said, El Taco Tote is a chain. Interestingly, it is a chain that spans both sides of the border. Naturally, I'm speaking of Mexico and the United States. As far as I'm concerned, El Pollo Feliz is a way better bi-national chain. Mmmmmm, happy chicken...... In terms of the food, I really don't have any strong feelings one way or another. It is merely all right. What gets me about this place is the price. I wouldn't mind paying upwards of $8 for a combination taco platter if it was of high quality, but it is somewhat lacking in that department. The pork adobada, as someone else had previously noted, was on the fatty and chewy side. On the bright side, the adobada spices gives it a good kick that attempts to mask the fattiness of the the pork. The sirloin is merely so-so here. I'm not exactly sure whether they grill their meat like other taquerias do. Mmmmm, mesquite grilled meat.... It simply is missing that unmistakable off-the-grill taste. Given a choice of how my meat is prepared, I'd take grilled or charbroiled over fried any day. That's why I almost solely patronize Carl's Jr. or Burger King when I crave fast-food hamburger. Other than meat, the other necessity for a good taco is the tortilla, and El Taco Tote abjectly fails in this regard. I liken the tortilla quality to those you can buy at a grocery store. In other words, the tortillas are a bit chewy on the chewy side and taste like they came from a bag. This is where the chain part becomes a negative. Tortillas at El Taco Tote are likely mass purchased for all franchises from one location. That is just plain wrong when you consider that there are a ton of places in town where you can purchase soft, tasty, and fresh tortillas from tortillarias. Ironically, I like my tortillas how I like my ladies.... There is a salsa bar, and it's fine and dandy and all. There was one salsa, however, that was inexcusable, as it was as thin as water. Red onions and radishes are available in the salsa bar, which is a standard in any self-respecting taqueria. The only thing really missing is sliced cucumbers to make it 100% truly authentic. I personally enjoy munching on a cucumber to cool off and balance out the spiciness of the salsa I dump in my tacos. Perhaps what rubs me the wrong way the most is just the physical location. The place used to be a Carrow's way back in the day, and I've had one of my most horrible, but hilarious, dining experiences there. Yes, I'm embarrassed to admit in full disclosure that I've dined at a place like Carrow's in the past. Never again, though. Seriously, I really do enjoy eating at places like Taqueria Juanito's, BK's or off a roadside, rather than a sterile, cookie-cutter generic former chain restaurant such as Carrow's. To reiterate myself, the tacos weren't inedible per se, but at three bucks each, they aren't simply worth it in my opinion. They are fairly big in size, however, and the translation of the restaurant's name implies a large taco. The salsa bar is nice, but isn't enough to cover up the chewiness and blandness of the tortillas. No offense to those who prefer quantity over quality, you can find better tacos in Tucson. You're also better off finding "real Mexican food" elsewhere as well. As a last resort, or maybe if you're recovering from surgery at nearby El Dorado Hospital, El Taco Tote may suffice as a real Mexican food restaurant.

text: Nice view and gorgeous space---check. Solid attentive service---check. Outstanding and inventive food worthy of the price tag---Hold it. I really really really wanted to have a great meal at Vin de Set. Sadly, it was not meant to be. Partially may have been because we went on a Sunday evening; perhaps the A team had the night off. We started with the steak tenderloin tartare with truffle oil and flatbread. It came out with nicely arranged radish sprouts and seeded flatbreads (bit of a skimpy supply of skinny thin points) over the tartare/truffle oil/??? mixture that was wrapped in a thinly sliced cucumber. The tartare looked like a dog's breakfast but fortunately tasted somewhat better. They were heavy handed with the truffle oil and the meat quality didn't wow me. It was only ok. Hubby liked this one more than I did. For entrees, I got the Steak and Frites, a reasonable test of a solid but not overly challenging french bistro dish, and my husband got the duck breast with fingerling potatoes and blueberry port reduction. First, for a place that sells itself as a french bistro, to me that entails some attractive presentation, classic knife skills demonstrated in the food, etc. Not the case here; there was no dish presented to us that I with my mediocre knife skills and lack of eye hand coordination could not have done myself at home. Furthermore, the lack of texture variation in the food was also notable. For fine dining, I not only expect great tasting food, but presentation also plays a role, and they didn't attend to this at all. For my dish, to their credit, it was actually cooked medium rare as asked; there are too few restaurants in Saint Louis who can actually correctly make a medium rare steak. It was not particularly flavorful however; I took about 3/4 of it home for my husband to have for lunch the next day. The fries were a huge disappointment. Unevenly cut, soggy undersalted fries. Not at all crispy and slightly cold. I, who am the queen of all carbs and the empress of french fries, only ate maybe 5 of them before I decided they were not worth the calories and did not take them home. The stuffed tomato with this dish was nice if a bit greasy and mushy; I didn't really taste the bacon that was supposedly in it. Some nicely crisped bacon or pancetta on top would have been great for taste and texture. My husband's duck was properly cooked as well. The potatoes were pretty average (except the undercooked one) and the "reduction" didn't seem very reduced---it tasted strongly of port with no blueberry to note and not much else. Nothing on the dessert menu tempted us, so we got a cheese plate which was tasty, though the cheese selection is somewhat limited. Love the fig spread, pickled onions and pickled brussel sprouts on this. They also had some nice wines by the glass, including a nice chenin blanc. For what we paid for this meal, I thought it was pretty disappointing. When the cheese plate is your sole highlight, there is a problem. Had I paid a third of what we paid, I still wouldn't have called it stellar food, but I would have not felt as cheated. We will likely try the food here in a less extensive meal again on a Friday to see if this evening was an anomaly, but this may end up being a bar and drinks only kind of place for us.
label: NEG

text: After a co-worker raved about the all-you-can-eat crab, I decided that I had to check this place out. I went ahead and got the Comps+ card so I could get the deal for $7.77 and headed out on a Friday night. (Without the member's card, the buffet is about $16.) The boyfriend and I got into line about 6:15 PM, and despite the number of people ahead of us, still managed to get into the buffet fairly quickly. The cashier who greeted us was a fun and vibrant lady, but the girl who seated us was dour and tired-looking. She barely said two words to us. While the BF waited on our server (I asked for a glass of water), I went ahead and checked out the food. To say that it was disappointing would be a bit of an understatement. Each "station" only has one or two offerings, and none of them looked particularly appealing. I decided to start with the crab and shrimp, which was the reason why I came in the first place. Unlike the Atlantis, the snow crab was sort of piled haphazardly next to the shrimp under a strange plastic dome. There was a scary, fishy smell coming from under there which almost made me turn away. Still, I didn't want to leave empty handed, so I grabbed a little of both, some cocktail sauce, and returned to the table. While I'd been gone, the waiter brought me iced tea instead of water, which was okay, I guess. The shrimp was warm and rubbery, but didn't taste too bad. The crab legs were thin and wimpy, not the large, robust legs I've seen at other buffets. The meat was also rather dry and salty, so I get the impression that they were overcooked. The boyfriend tried the chicken madeira, which looked appetizing enough. To hear him describe the flavor, however, "It's bland and salty at the same time." After trying a bite, I had to agree. There were no exceptional tastes jumping out at me, and it seemed like the chef thought dumping a whole lot of salt would make up for that. The Mexican station was a near bust; the only decent thing was the Spanish rice, and it still would have been better with the addition of some fresh salsas. The Chinese station was pathetic; undercooked egg rolls, bland fried rice, and I didn't bother with the steamed rice or the chicken stir-fry. There were a couple of cold noodle dishes at the salad station that were okay, and the boyfriend said the pizza slices were edible, if doughy. The linguine with clam sauce tasted like watered down alfredo sauce, the clam chowder was extremely thin but surprisingly tasty, and the seafood dish with penne pasta was all right, but I found a bone in one of the fish chunks. (Though, I guess that's bound to happen, sometimes.) The supposed "steamed" veggies were drowning in butter, and the roasted red potatoes were too salty. By the time we were finished wading through that nonsense, neither of us really felt like dessert. (In fact, I got an upset stomach a little after eating the crab and shrimp. It wasn't bad enough for me to think of it as food poisoning, or anything, but it does make me a little leery to go back.) For $7.77, I guess it's not so bad, but I wouldn't pay a dollar more for this fare. Charging $16 for it normally is a rip-off! For shame, Grand Sierra.

text: My extended family has used Otto's as a convenient meeting place for big breakfasts for years. The breakfast menu is large, kid-friendly, the coffee keeps coming, and service is usually quite efficient and friendly. However, the place takes on an entirely different flavor for dinner. We went for dinner one rainy Friday night recently. Before we even walked through the second set of doors, we were assaulted by an overpowering smell of broiled fish and maple syrup. Fish should not smell that bad. It just shouldn't. I read somewhere that, given time, the nose accustoms itself to bad smells so you can stomach them. This did not happen for me, sadly. It seemed to emanate from the dark wooden paneling and bad paintings of bucolic farmhouses. Accompanying the stench and decor was the music. Dear god, the music. I think it was Home on the Range on an accordian. At that exact moment, my husband turned to me and said something like, "You know, we really need more fun in our lives. We're getting old." As I looked at the sea of gray-haired customers in sensible shoes and sweaters with dogs on them, I had a vision of our future and pretty much lost it. I giggled for about ten minutes. Ok..the food. That's what we're here to talk about. I had pretty much lost my appetite due to the fish smell, but I persevered and ordered a wiener schnitzel sandwich and a chocolate milkshake. Note the word "shake," because the waitress proudly presented me with a blended, foamy chocolate milk, clearly made with powdered chocolate and told me that she had never made a milkshake before. The sandwich was a pale, rather soggy slab of breaded veal on a dry piece of untoasted rye bread. That's it. Jeez, throw in some mustard or mayo...or even a tomato! The good-hearted waitress seemed genuinely befuddled when I told her I didn't want to wrap the sandwich to take home. As the accordian music turned from a gentle Home on the Range to a demented circus theme, my husband and I wound our way through the lederhosen and walkers to the fresh air of a busy 611. I had the stench of fish in my nose for an hour afterwards and just thinking about it now makes my stomach turn.
label: NEG

text: I stopped in at the Claddagh twice during my 4-day stay in Indianapolis, once for drinks and once for lunch. Overall, it's a great bar and restaurant, with a laid-back crowd and staff. I found the same typically super-friendly service here that I saw in most of the establishments in this town, and the locals soon invited me and my boy to join their party. Good times! The most awesome thing about the Claddagh, though, is the incredible fish and chips lunch we enjoyed on a Monday afternoon. The fish and chips special is two-for-one all day on Mondays, and it is so worth it! This was easily the best fish and chips I've ever had, with a huge tasty portion of deliciously battered cod and excellent crispy-fried wedges of potato cooked in a light batter. This special is to die for! The decor of the Claddagh is pleasant and dark with your typical Irish-y feel, and lots of little nooks and crannies to hang out in. This is a very solid place to check out in downtown Indianapolis.

text: I moved to New Orleans earlier this year from San Francisco, the Tenderloin to be exact. Therefore, my weekly trips for Indian food to Jones & O'Farrell (Lahore, Chutney, Shalimar, Sultan, even Naan n Curry on Van Ness) consisted of my favorite weekly comfort food of my life. When I moved to NOLA, I knew comfort food would switch to cajun/creole - but I had no idea it would be so hard to get an adequate Indian meal. When you come here, don't expect traditional Indian. It bills itself as "New Orleans Indian". And, for what it claims to be it, it delivers. I have been in many times for the extensive and varied wine selection in the store, but had not tried the Indian food. I ordered the lamb spicy vindaloo. Like others, I was a little disappointed in the lack of sheer heat at first. But the flavor, while unlike any other Indian I tried, was outstanding. It was a little sweet - my wife's chicken curry was a lot sweet. No potatoes (is that everyday?), but that was always my secret least favorite part of vindaloo (more lamb!). Naan was pretty good. Papar was a little greasy but a perfect compliment to the Vindaloo. Portions were perfect for a dinner and prices were outstanding. This wouldn't be a 4 star Indian restaurant in San Francisco, but in New Orleans - as a super-funky place in the middle of one of the best neighborhoods in all the world - it's close to a 5.

text: Ok, first of all, enough with the comparisons between Burger Monger and Five Guys. They are entirely different establishments. Five Guys is a glorified fast food shop with over-hyped, over-priced burgers and shitty fries. Burger Monger, on the other hand, for essentially the same price offers an incredibly tasty, gourmet burger with a nice assortment of gourmet toppings. Accordingly, the comparison with Square One is apt, but overall I give the edge to Burger Monger. Burger Monger's kobe beef burger was actually jucier and more flavorful than Square One's, at approximately half the cost! Not surprising when you consider Square One's typical South Tampa vibe and Burger Monger's more pedestrian Carrollwood existence. Granted, you can't get buffalo at Burger Monger (and it is quite tasty at Square One), but for straight up burger goodness, Burger Monger wins on both taste and value. In terms of desserts, Burger Monger's shakes are amazing, and absolutely destroy Square One's sorry excuse for cupcakes (you are better off going down the road to the Cupcake Spot for dessert). At Burger Monger, try the onion slaw and chipotle ketchup, and ask for your burger cooked medium, as opposed to the default medium well. Then prepare for messy burger nirvana. Kudos, Burger Monger, for getting me excited again about burgers!

text: TERRIBLE, DO NOT GO THERE. If I could give this place no stars, I would. Having said that, here's the review. First of all, I moved here a few months ago and did not yet have a dentist. Last week I suddenly had a terrible toothache which was definitely an abscess. I called around (on a Friday) but barely anyone was open. I called this place and they gave me a Monday appt. This is the only reason why I went there. Got to the consult and the receptionists weren't very friendly. Not a huge deal but then I waited at least an hour before my appointment. When I did get called in, they did a panoramic x-ray and a few other x-rays even though it is only one spot that was bothering me. The multiple x-rays were NOT necessary. The dentist finally came in, looked at my tooth and declared I needed a root canal (well duh, I knew that already) and later a crown. He then gave me a prescription for a (very mild) antibiotic. I should also mention that the right side of my face was swollen from the infection so I should have received a much stronger one. I then was scheduled for a root canal 4 days later. Oh and the antibiotic did NOT finish clearing the infection. I also did not receive a quote for the root canal or crown. I should have asked but I was in so much pain. Root canal day. I waited about 30 mins and was then put in a room and left waiting for 1.5 hours! I would have walked out had I not needed the root canal (and more antibiotics). When the dentist finally came in, she't wasn willing to answer simple routine questions like, how long I'd be on new antibiotics, etc., as if I was bothering her with my questions. She also was a little jabby with the needles. The root canal itself didn't take that long but her and her assisant were not very friendly.
